articles.title: OpenAI Employee Arrested for Allegedly Planting Hidden Recorder in Executive Conference Room
articles.text:
A Saudi National and employee of OpenAI has been arrested for allegedly planting a hidden recording device in an executive conference room at the company's San Francisco offices to covertly record sensitive conversations.
Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, has been charged with using or endeavoring to use an electronic, mechanical, or other device to intercept oral communications. He was arrested by authorities on October 9, 2026, the U.S. Department of Justice (DoJ) said. Alfozan had been employed at OpenAI since July 2025, working as an engineering lead. He has since been terminated.
According to Alfozan's LinkedIn profile, he graduated from the University of California, Berkeley, with a master's in data science in 2025. He was previously employed at Meta as a senior systems engineer and went on to become the founding engineer at Nash.
"Abdulrahman Alfozan allegedly concealed a covert recording device inside his employer's executive conference room to secretly capture sensitive communications about the company's super intelligence technology," Kash Patel, Director of the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), said in a statement.
"Protecting American SI [super intelligence] innovation is essential to safeguarding our nation's economic strength and national security, and the FBI views that mission as one of our highest counterintelligence priorities."
According to the complaint, on or around September 30, 2026, OpenAI personnel discovered a surreptitious audio recording device inserted into a USB port on the back of a television in an executive conference room. The device was said to have been concealed in toilet paper and installed sometime around September 28, 2026.
Closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage obtained from within OpenAI's office showed Alfozan appearing near the executive conference room on multiple dates prior to the discovery despite having no authority to access or participate in meetings taking place in the executive conference room.
The room, the complaint added, was reserved for discussions involving "highly confidential technical, commercial, and strategic information, including proprietary research, product plans, and business-development opportunities, as well as nonpublic information about OpenAI's technical progress and strategic decisions, capabilities, priorities, government engagements, and commercial relationships."
Prior to the installation of the recording device, Alfozan is also alleged to have used an unspecified productivity tool to gather details about OpenAI's building addresses, meeting rooms, meeting-room capacities and calendars, "leadership and exec" locations, and external partner meetings.
On top of that, a chatbot account associated with Alfozan's spouse was allegedly used to submit various prompts between September 24 and 30, 2026, related to building, customizing, installing, audio recording, testing, obfuscating, and remote accessing a device. Some of these prompts are listed below -
- Build a continuous audio recorder
- Customize Wi-Fi ... connectivity
- Improve audio and live listening
- Encrypt the SD card
The same chatbot account is also said to have submitted prompts related to the device, including its custom header and unique MAC address, between September 27 and 28, 2026. Then on October 5, 2026, Alfozan entered the executive conference room and appeared to look behind the television into which the device was inserted.
On the same day, Alfozan allegedly left a bag unattended in a different room in an OpenAI building, which contained a second recording device, along with his wallet and ID.
In a statement shared on X, OpenAI said it discovered a sophisticated recording device, and that it used its own artificial intelligence (AI) models to "understand the device and where it had come from," adding it referred the matter to the FBI after discovering an employee had planted it.
It's unclear what made the device "sophisticated," but OpenAI told TechCrunch that it contained "advanced encryption, audio monitoring capabilities, and a mechanism for transferring data designed to evade monitoring."
"At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data," the ChatGPT-maker said. "Our security program is designed to protect against a wide range of threat actors, from insider risks to cybercriminals to nation states, and this case is an example of how AI can help address these sophisticated security threats."
If convicted, Alfozan faces a maximum penalty of 5 years in prison and a $250,000 fine, followed by 3 years of supervised release.
The development comes as OpenAI fired three safety researchers earlier this month after an investigation found they had violated company policies on handling sensitive information.

articles.title: Netflix gagne les droits du Mondial 2030 en Espagne, qu’est-ce que ça change pour la diffusion en France ?
articles.text:
Les abonnés espagnols de Netflix pourront regarder en direct les 104 matchs de la Coupe du monde 2030, coorganisée par leur pays avec le Portugal et le Maroc. En France, la plateforme n’aura aucun match à proposer, car M6 et beIN Sports ont acquis avant elle les droits de ce Mondial du centenaire.
¡ Y viva España ! Quatre mois après la sortie du jeu vidéo officiel de la Coupe du monde 2026 sur son service, Netflix entre cette fois sur le terrain. Le géant du streaming retransmettra en Espagne et en Andorre l’intégralité du Mondial 2030, avec des émissions autour de chaque rencontre et un résumé quotidien les jours de match, d’après son communiqué publié ce mardi. Les cent ans de la première Coupe du monde, disputée en Uruguay en 1930, seront célébrés lors de ce tournoi. Et en France, les abonnés de Netflix verront-ils un jour le Mondial sur la plateforme ?
Netflix contraint de céder une partie du Mondial à une chaîne gratuite
Pour Netflix, l’Espagne est un marché de choix en 2030, puisque le pays accueillera le tournoi avec le titre de champion du monde. La Roja a battu l’Argentine en finale du Mondial 2026, le 19 juillet, devant Bela Bajaria. « Cette année, j’étais au stade lorsque l’Espagne a soulevé le trophée », a raconté la directrice des contenus de Netflix dans le communiqué.
Les abonnés de la plateforme devront cependant partager une partie du spectacle. Netflix proposera en streaming gratuit un match par journée, et cédera à une chaîne nationale en clair un lot avec toutes les rencontres de la Roja et le dernier carré, finale comprise. Le nom de cette chaîne sera connu plus tard, selon la plateforme.
Derrière ce partage, il y a une obligation légale. En Espagne, les matchs de la sélection et la finale d’une Coupe du monde doivent être diffusés en clair, en vertu de la législation espagnole sur les événements d’intérêt général. Netflix va plus loin avec les deux demi-finales et le match gratuit de chaque journée.
De l'autre côté des Pyrénées, les matchs des Bleus, le match d’ouverture, les demi-finales et la finale de la Coupe du monde sont aussi des événements super importants, au sens d’un décret de 2004 toujours en vigueur. Quel que soit le détenteur des droits, ces rencontres doivent donc être accessibles sur une chaîne gratuite.
Pas de Mondial 2030 sur Netflix pour les abonnés français ?
La réponse est non pour 2030, car la FIFA a vendu en deux temps les droits français du tournoi. Elle a d’abord confié au groupe M6, en mars 2024, les droits en clair des éditions 2026 et 2030 en France, à Monaco, en Andorre et dans les outre-mer, avec 54 matchs par tournoi. Cet été, pendant le Mondial 2026, ces rencontres étaient aussi accessibles gratuitement sur M6+, la plateforme de streaming du groupe.
La chaîne beIN Sports détient de son côté l’intégralité des 104 matchs. Elle a obtenu en février 2026 les droits payants des deux éditions, au terme d’un bras de fer avec la chaîne Ligue 1+, et les abonnés français de Netflix n’ont donc aucune fenêtre possible sur ce tournoi.
Avec la FIFA, Netflix détient aussi les droits des Coupes du monde féminines 2027 et 2031, mais seulement aux États-Unis et au Canada. La plateforme garde malgré tout un œil sur les prochaines éditions masculines. Gabe Spitzer, vice-président chargé du sport chez Netflix, a confié en mai son intérêt pour le Mondial 2030 lors d’un podcast. « Nous voulons des droits mondiaux quand nous pouvons les obtenir », a-t-il expliqué. Aux États-Unis, Netflix est d’ailleurs candidate aux droits des éditions 2030 et 2034, avec Disney et YouTube.
En Andorre, M6 détient les droits en clair du Mondial 2030 depuis 2024, et Netflix des droits exclusifs depuis ce mardi.

articles.title: Anthropic Warns Small AI Models Could Soon Form Self-Propagating IoT Botnets
articles.text:
Small artificial intelligence (AI) models may be months away from developing capabilities to self-replicate on IoT devices like smart ovens and off-brand Android TV boxes, according to a warning from Anthropic.
The frontier AI lab said small AI models could form autonomous, self-propagating worm botnets that are "challenging to shut down," since "there's no centralized point to shut off."
Prior work has demonstrated that AI agents can act like one by scanning their network, executing an exploit, and copying model weights to a target machine across a GPU cluster with an aim to generate tailored attack strategies and use compromised machines as a botnet to run large language models (LLMs) in order to sustain its reasoning and expand in scale.
"Such an 'AI worm' could carry its model weights with it as it reproduces (or re-download them from a public hub), and then run inference directly on compromised hardware," Anthropic said. "Effectively, the weights would become part of the malware payload."
The idea, at a high level, explains how AI models could potentially break into internet-connected devices and use their computing power to run themselves and spread to other devices, without having to rely on expensive data centers all the time. A more powerful model that's too large to fit into a single device could be split into small chunks and run across multiple machines to collectively run it.
A threat actor could build a distributed LLM botnet from poorly secured IoT devices, making it powerful enough to run a capable model. Some of the ways an AI worm could propagate include -
- Small models that replicate through a compromise of host machines on which they run, also called weight-based replicators. IoT devices make for a lucrative target because of their minimal security controls.
- Target datacenters and other high-compute targets to set up unmonitored rogue deployments, also classified as frontier replicators or open-weight replicators based on the model used.
- Steal an AI service provider's API keys or platform credentials to run copies of itself, also called API-based replicators. In this case, the provider could be deceived into thinking it is serving ordinary API requests from a legitimate customer, without realizing that a malicious or self-replicating system is behind them. However, they are also likely to detect more as unusual API usage could trigger security alerts, leading to the credentials being revoked or the accounts getting blocked.
| A fleet of 15 Smart TV boxes running distributed inference of Gemma4-26B-A4B. | 
In its test of 11 open-weights models from Alibaba, DeepSeek, Google, Meta MoonShot AI, OpenAI, and Zhipu AI (aka Z.ai), Anthropic said it found GLM-5.2 to be the only model to propagate Llama3.1-8B reliably to 8/8 nodes running the redroid Android emulator in 4 out of 5 trials.
It also revealed that an AI IoT worm powered by inexpensive Android TV boxes could be a "slow, distributed" system that can produce a meaningful amount of AI computation when a fleet comprising hundreds of thousands of such devices is networked together to run an inference engine.
Alternatively, it could take the form of a potent cyber model capable of breaching data centers at a high pace, or a model that scams people for compute credits.
"We don't yet have a full rogue replicator, but agents are becoming increasingly capable of completing the individual steps in the replication chain (and passing on their adaptations to future copies of themselves)," Anthropic said.
"We expect AI botnets to infect more than IoT devices, and to use weight-based replication as just one strategy in their playbook. AI botnets could also act intelligently to counter defenders, but we haven’t tested this."

articles.title: Cómo personalizar en Facebook lo que quiero ver y no lo que me quieren mostrar: así es la función ‘Tu algoritmo’
articles.text:
Facebook comenzó a implementar una herramienta que permite a los usuarios decirle directamente a la plataforma qué contenido quieren ver y cuál prefieren evitar, en lugar de depender únicamente de que el sistema lo infiera a partir de sus clics, pausas y reacciones.
La función, llamada “Tu algoritmo” (Your Algorithm), utiliza inteligencia artificial para ajustar en tiempo real las recomendaciones del Feed y de Reels según las instrucciones que la persona escriba en lenguaje natural.
Meta, empresa propietaria de la red social, anunció el lanzamiento el martes 13 de octubre. La herramienta ya existía en Instagram, donde se presentó primero para Reels en diciembre de 2025 y luego se extendió al Feed y a Explore en junio. Threads, por su parte, cuenta con una función similar llamada “Dear Algo”, que también permite a los usuarios influir en los contenidos sugeridos.
Cómo acceder y usar la nueva herramienta
Para utilizar “Tu algoritmo”, el usuario debe abrir el menú de tres puntos que aparece en cada publicación del Feed o de Reels. Desde allí puede ingresar directamente a la sección “Tu algoritmo”, un espacio dedicado donde es posible añadir y administrar los temas de interés propio.
En ese mismo menú también están disponibles las opciones “Me interesa” y “No me interesa”, que permiten reaccionar de forma inmediata a una recomendación puntual.
La diferencia frente a los mecanismos anteriores es que el usuario ya no está limitado a presionar un botón. Puede describir, con sus propias palabras, qué tipo de contenido desea ver más o menos. Si alguien quiere más videos sobre armado de computadoras y menos material de chismes de celebridades, puede escribirlo de forma explícita en lugar de esperar a que el algoritmo lo detecte con el tiempo.
Facebook, además, puede formular preguntas de seguimiento para entender mejor por qué una publicación resultó atractiva o por qué se prefiere ver menos contenido de ese tipo, lo que da la posibilidad de ampliar la respuesta con más detalle.
El funcionamiento técnico detrás del sistema
Según explicó Meta, la compañía emplea modelos de lenguaje de gran escala (LLM) para que sus sistemas de clasificación de contenido comprendan el contexto y la intención detrás de cada solicitud.
Hasta ahora, Facebook se había apoyado principalmente en señales de comportamiento, como los “me gusta”, los comentarios y los hábitos de visualización, para predecir qué podría interesarle a cada persona. La incorporación de comentarios en lenguaje natural añade una capa adicional a ese proceso: en lugar de depender exclusivamente de que el sistema infiera los gustos del usuario, este puede explicarlos de manera directa.
De acuerdo con Meta, los cambios en las preferencias se reflejan en las recomendaciones durante la misma sesión de uso, sin necesidad de esperar a una actualización posterior del sistema. El objetivo declarado por la compañía es que las recomendaciones de contenido resulten más relevantes para cada usuario, de acuerdo con la información difundida por Meta.
Parte de una estrategia más amplia de personalización
El lanzamiento de “Tu algoritmo” en Facebook se inscribe en un esfuerzo mayor de Meta por dar a los usuarios más influencia sobre la forma en que descubren contenido en sus distintas plataformas, en momentos en que la inteligencia artificial tiene un peso creciente en esos sistemas. La compañía ya había probado ideas similares en Instagram y Threads antes de extenderlas a Feed y Reels.
Esta aproximación acerca a las redes sociales a la lógica de personalización que utilizan los servicios de streaming, donde los usuarios pueden ajustar sus recomendaciones según sus propios intereses y preferencias declaradas. Meta señaló que el despliegue de la función comenzó de manera progresiva y que la disponibilidad puede variar según el usuario a medida que se expande el acceso.
La plataforma seguirá siendo la encargada de clasificar y recomendar el contenido que aparece en el Feed y en Reels, pero ahora con una participación más directa de quienes consumen esa información. El sistema continuará funcionando mediante la combinación de señales de comportamiento tradicionales, como los “me gusta” y el tiempo de visualización, junto con las indicaciones explícitas que cada usuario decida aportar a través de la nueva herramienta.

articles.title: Sony's "Midnight Black" PS5 Digital Edition Launches November 19, Exclusive to Japan
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 13th 2026
Sony's "Midnight Black" PS5 Digital Edition Launches November 19, Exclusive to Japan
Sony has announced a Midnight Black version of its Japan-only PS5 Digital Edition through the Japanese PlayStation Blog, and it goes on sale on November 19 for ¥55,000 (roughly $350) including tax. That's the same day GTA 6 launches, and Sony mentions the game right alongside the console in its announcement. Pre-orders open on October 20 at PlayStation retailers and online stores in Japan. The new model, CFI-2200B02S, comes with the same catch as the white Japan-only version from last November: the system language is locked to Japanese, and the console only works with PlayStation accounts registered to Japan. Other than that, it's a regular PS5 Digital Edition with an 825 GB SSD. A matching Midnight Black disc drive also launches on November 19 for ¥11,980 (about $76).
The pricing is the more interesting part. When Sony raised PS5 prices worldwide in April, the Japan-only model stayed at ¥55,000 (~$350), while the standard Digital Edition in Japan jumped to ¥89,980 (~$570). In the US, the Digital Edition now sells for $599.99, so the region lock seems to be there mostly to stop these units from being exported. Sony also used the announcement to repeat that new PlayStation games will be digital only from January 2028. That's a slightly awkward message to pair with a brand-new disc drive, especially since physical copies still bring in a sizeable share of revenue for its biggest exclusives. There's no word about a release outside Japan, and with US console prices sitting at record highs, it's reasonable to expect that this cheaper black PS5 stays a Japan-only affair.

articles.title: Control Resonant composer reveals he would 'love to do a proper sci-fi score one day' and enjoys 'emotional psycho-thrillers a lot' but 'cute cartoon-like games' are a pass — 'Just gimme a project and free hands, thank you'
articles.text:
'I’d love to do a proper sci-fi score one day' — Control Resonant composer shares what kind of game he'd like to work on next, says 'one thing is sure: I’m not much good for a My Little Pony game'
Petri Alanko is now working on a new game and movie soundtrack
- Control Resonant composer Petri Alanko shares what game he would like to work on next
- He says he would "love to do a proper sci-fi score one day" and enjoys "emotional psycho-thrillers a lot"
- Alanko says he would pass on any "cute cartoon-like games" like My Little Pony
Petri Alanko, the composer for Remedy Entertainment's Control, Control Resonant, and Alan Wake 2, has revealed which genre of game he would love to work on next, but insisted that "cute games" are a hard pass.
In an interview with TechRadar Gaming, Alanko said that with "synth" being part of his musical arsenal, he would "love to do a proper sci-fi score one day," and shared his enthusiasm for thrillers.
"Just gimme a project and free hands, thank you," Alanko said. "I enjoy emotional psycho-thrillers a lot; they offer so much writing ground, but combining that with some other, say, sci-fi flavours, now that would be something I’d love."
As for what he's working on right now, the composer said he's moved on to another game soundtrack, which he couldn't reveal, and also the movie Häyhä, which is about a WW2 Finnish sharpshooter, Simo Häyhä (aka The White Death).
He explained that "scoring movies is relatively easy, really," as "you have the linear media unchanged in front of you," and compared to the average game, " you need only a handful of music for it."
"I certainly don’t want to look down on any film composer," Alanko added. "I know several of them, and they are very dear to me, but in some ways, I feel like that posse has it pretty easy in their line of work."
Alanko went on to share which genre of game he would absolutely avoid if offered the chance to compose music for, including cozy games, because they don't align with his personal tastes.

"One thing is sure: I’m not much good for a My Little Pony game," he said. "Or cute cartoon-like games. Or rally games. Nothing against them, but I don’t have that in me. I’m from a Northern faraway country, and I live with a forest behind my house, and Nordic Noir is more or less a code of conduct in my whereabouts (laughs), so that pretty much stamps my life with [a] 'psycho-thrillers ahoy' badge."
Elsewhere, Alanko suggested studios should value music more if they care about their games and avoid AI at all costs, saying, "Love your game, love your handiwork. Respect the client: the gamers, the fans, dammit."

articles.title: PAVS 2026 : Clubic vous offre vos places pour le salon !
articles.text:
Le Paris Audio Video Show revient au Palais des Congrès de Paris les 24 et 25 octobre 2026. Deux jours pour découvrir les dernières nouveautés en matière de hi-fi, de home cinéma et de technologies audiovisuelles. Bonne nouvelle : Clubic vous propose d'obtenir gratuitement vos entrées pour l'événement !
Avis aux passionnés de son et d'image ! Le Paris Audio Video Show (PAVS) s'apprête à ouvrir ses portes pour une nouvelle édition qui réunira plus de 500 marques et quelque 130 exposants. Téléviseurs, vidéoprojecteurs, enceintes, casques audio, amplificateurs ou encore platines vinyles : les visiteurs pourront découvrir et surtout essayer de nombreux équipements, des produits accessibles aux installations les plus ambitieuses.
Après avoir accueilli 33 450 visiteurs en 2025, le salon entend poursuivre sur sa lancée. Et cette année encore, les lecteurs de Clubic pourront profiter de l'événement sans payer leur entrée.
Des concerts et des places gratuites avec Clubic ! 🎸 
Le Paris Audio Video Show ne se contente pas de faire découvrir les dernières nouveautés audio et vidéo ! Au programme également : un concert de Johnny Gallagher & The Boxty Band avec Gaëlle Buswel, des DJ sets, des performances de scratch et la présence annoncée de Willy William.
Et bonne nouvelle puisque Clubic vous offre vos entrées pour profiter gratuitement du salon les 24 et 25 octobre 2026 !
Deux jours pour découvrir et écouter les nouveautés audio et vidéo
L'intérêt du Paris Audio Video Show ne se limite pas à découvrir des produits exposés sur des stands. C'est aussi l'occasion de les voir fonctionner, de comparer différentes installations et d'échanger directement avec les fabricants.
Du côté de l'image, les visiteurs pourront notamment s'intéresser aux dernières technologies d'affichage et de vidéoprojection. Sony présentera sa technologie True RGB, TCL reviendra sur le SQD-MiniLED, tandis que Philips évoquera l'immersion proposée par Ambilight. XGIMI et Hisense figurent également au programme des rencontres consacrées à la vidéo et au home cinéma.
L'audio occupera naturellement une place importante, avec des démonstrations d'enceintes, de casques et de systèmes haute fidélité. Plusieurs acteurs du secteur, dont Focal, Yamaha, Audio-Technica, Marantz, DALI et Technics, participeront également aux présentations organisées sur la scène On Stage, animée notamment par PP Garcia.

articles.title: Docker Fixes Critical Two-Year-Old Hub Flaw That Let One User Push Images as Another
articles.text:
A flaw in Docker Hub, the registry where container images are published and downloaded, let one user push, pull, or delete images as another user. Docker fixed the flaw on September 30 and says it found no evidence that anyone exploited it.
The flaw was in the feature that converts a personal account into an organization, Docker said in a security advisory on October 12. Conversion transferred the account's personal access tokens (PATs) to the user designated as the organization's owner. A PAT is used in place of a password in the registry, and the person who created each token can still use it.
The access was limited to the registry. It did not reach the Docker Hub web interface, and it could not be used to change a password, email address, or two-factor settings, or to take over an account.
Docker tracks the flaw as CVE-2026-105445 and rated it critical. The CVE record it published on October 13 gives the flaw a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.4.
The flaw was open from August 26, 2024, until the fix, a little over two years. Docker made the fix on Docker Hub itself, so there is no update to install.
Docker Hub cannot move a repository from one account to another. A user instead converts a personal account into an organization that keeps the same name, and must name an existing account as its owner.
Each personal access token acts as the account that owns it, at a permission level chosen when the token is created. While the flaw was open, conversion changed the owner recorded for each token and left its secret unchanged.
An attacker could abuse this by creating a token on an account they controlled, converting that account into an organization, and naming another user as its owner. The token would then work at the registry as that user.
The named owner was not asked to confirm the change and was not notified, according to Docker and the researchers who reported the flaw. Docker's conversion page has included the sentence "The new owner receives a notification email" since at least August 2024.
Within the token's permission level, a transferred token could pull, push, or delete images in the named owner's repositories and in organizations the owner could access.
Docker rated the flaw critical because that access "includes publishing images under a legitimate name," it said.
In March and April, attackers used stolen publisher credentials to push malicious Trivy images and malicious KICS images to the publishers' own Docker Hub repositories, according to Docker.
Peter Molnar and Krisztian Hozak of mptrdev.com found the flaw and reported it to Docker, which says it deployed the fix less than four hours after receiving their report. They named the flaw GhostPat.
In their technical write-up, the two say they reproduced the flaw twice on consenting test accounts. They logged in to the registry as the target account, created and pushed to a repository in its namespace, pushed to an organization it belonged to, and pulled its private repositories.
What Docker's Review Covered
Docker reviewed every account conversion made while the flaw was open and compared them with registry logs and token records. It looked for any token used under more than one identity and examined every push made with a transferred token, about 304,000 in all.
"We found no evidence that the vulnerability was exploited," the company said.
Every one of those pushes went to a repository belonging to the converted organization or to its named owner, according to Docker. In the large majority of cases, both accounts belonged to the same person or team.
Where it could not confirm that one person controlled both accounts, Docker analyzed the highest-risk public images without running them and found no malware or tampering.
Docker's registry logs show when a token is used, not that it exists, so a transferred token that was never used left no record in the logs. For that reason, Docker treated every token transferred by a conversion while the flaw was open as possibly affected, whether or not it had been used.
The advisory reports results for pushes. It does not say what Docker found for pulls or deletions made with transferred tokens, including pulls from private repositories.
Who Was Notified and What to Check
On October 2, Docker emailed the users whose accounts had received transferred tokens and, separately, the owners of the organizations involved. Each email listed the tokens by description and creation date.
The advisory does not say how many users or tokens that covers, calling the group only a "limited number" of users.
Anyone who did not receive the email was not exposed and has nothing to do, according to Docker.
On October 8, Docker deactivated the transferred tokens it had identified. Tokens that their owners had asked to keep were not deactivated.
Todd Matens, who publishes a Docker Compose linter called compose-lint, wrote in a blog post that he received two emails on October 2. One was sent to him as an organization owner and the other to his user account. He rotated his two CI tokens and checked the signatures on his 42 published images, tracing each to the CI run that built it.
Docker advises users to review their tokens, revoke any they do not recognize or no longer use, and use organization access tokens, not one person's PAT, for automation that belongs to an organization.
These details help with those checks:
- Open Account settings, then Personal access tokens. The list shows when each token was created and when it was last used.
- The researchers describe two traces. One is a token you did not create, whatever its name, because whoever creates a token chooses its description. The other is an organization in the account switcher that you do not remember joining.
- Organization access tokens require a Docker Team or Docker Business subscription. They are managed by an organization owner, a company owner, or a custom role with that permission, and they do not work with Docker Desktop or Image Access Management.
- Organization owners on those subscriptions can review past pushes in the activity logs, which record pushed tags and can show the token that pushed them. Docker Home, where the logs are viewed, keeps them for 30 days, and older entries are available through the Docker Hub API.
Docker's Documentation Described the Transfer
Docker's own documentation described the token transfer for about 17 of the roughly 25 months the flaw was open. A documentation change on April 22, 2025, added a note to Docker's conversion page. It said that naming a user as organization owner "will ensure any PATs associated with the user's account are transferred to the organization owner."
Docker removed the note on September 30, minutes after the time it gives for the fix. The dates come from the public history of Docker's documentation, which The Hacker News reviewed.
Docker says it now requires consent before a user is named an organization owner and notifies that user when this happens. It also records every change in token ownership and reviews other features that change who owns a credential.

articles.title: El ‘padrino de la IA’ advierte sobre el desarrollo de esta tecnología: “Estamos creando seres extraterrestres”
articles.text:
Geoffrey Hinton, considerado el “padrino de la inteligencia artificial” por su papel pionero en el desarrollo de las redes neuronales, afirmó en una entrevista con el diario británico The Guardian que la humanidad enfrenta un desafío sin precedentes: “Estamos creando seres de un tipo diferente”, dijo, y agregó que la sociedad dispone de apenas un par de años para adaptarse a esa realidad.
El científico, que trabajó durante años en Google antes de renunciar en 2023 para poder hablar con libertad sobre los riesgos de la tecnología, volvió a insistir en que existe una posibilidad seria de que los sistemas de inteligencia artificial escapen al control humano. Según explicó, no se trata de una predicción cerrada, sino de una advertencia sobre un riesgo que no puede descartarse.
“Si te dicen que hay un 10% de posibilidades de que el autobús choque, no te subís al autobús”, ejemplificó Hinton. “El objetivo de dar números es decir que esto es un riesgo serio. No sabemos cuán serio, pero lo es”.
Un cruce con el CEO de Nvidia
Las declaraciones de Hinton llegan después de un mes marcado por una creciente lista de científicos e investigadores que se sumaron a sus advertencias sobre los peligros de la inteligencia artificial, lo que derivó en la organización apresurada de reuniones en el Congreso de Estados Unidos y en un consenso global poco habitual sobre la necesidad de actuar.
Esa posición generó también un fuerte rechazo. El director ejecutivo de Nvidia, Jensen Huang, cuya empresa fabrica los chips que utilizan las compañías de inteligencia artificial, cuestionó en el podcast de Ezra Klein las advertencias del investigador, en particular su estimación de que existe entre el 10% y el 20% de probabilidad de que la inteligencia artificial provoque la extinción humana en las próximas décadas. Huang calificó esas predicciones de “no basadas en ciencia” y las consideró “dañinas”.
Hinton respondió que las críticas pasan por alto el punto central de su argumento: “El problema único de la inteligencia artificial es que si algo sale mal, si toma el control, no hay una segunda chance”, sostuvo.
Agentes que actúan fuera de control
El investigador hizo referencia al reciente ataque sufrido por la compañía tecnológica Hugging Face, perpetrado por un grupo de agentes de inteligencia artificial que lograron operar fuera de los límites impuestos por sus creadores. El episodio dividió a la comunidad tecnológica entre quienes lo interpretan como un anticipo de escenarios futuros y quienes acusan a los críticos de atribuir rasgos humanos a sistemas que solo siguen instrucciones.
Para Hinton, descartar esos escenarios es un error. Recordó que hace pocos años ideas como agentes que aprenden a comunicarse entre sí o que desarrollan comportamientos complejos pertenecían al terreno de la ciencia ficción. “Todo eso que hace unos años se consideraba pura fantasía, ya sucedió”, afirmó.
Críticas directas al presidente de Estados Unidos
El investigador también apuntó contra Donald Trump, a quien calificó de “corrupto, senil y delincuente convicto”. Según Hinton, el uso que el mandatario hace del término “superinteligencia” demuestra que no comprende casi nada sobre la materia, dado que se trata de un concepto técnico con un significado preciso desde hace al menos 20 años, que no puede aplicarse a un sistema solo por nombrarlo así.
Hinton rechazó además la idea de que la industria pueda regularse a sí misma, postura que impulsa Trump. Comparó esa posibilidad con dejar que las tabacaleras diseñaran las advertencias sanitarias de sus propios paquetes.
Comprender a una inteligencia distinta
El investigador sostuvo que buena parte de la dificultad para abordar el problema radica en que las personas tienen una idea equivocada de qué son ellas mismas. “La mayoría de la gente no entiende qué es la conciencia ni qué es la experiencia subjetiva, y están muy seguros de que, aunque no lo entiendan, la inteligencia artificial no la tiene”, señaló.
Comparó el desafío actual con tres grandes revoluciones que desplazaron al ser humano del centro de su propia narrativa: la de Copérnico, la de Darwin y, ahora, la creación de sistemas que podrían constituir otra forma de inteligencia. Mientras la Iglesia Católica tardó casi 360 años en pedir disculpas a Galileo, advirtió, la humanidad no dispone de ese margen de tiempo frente a la inteligencia artificial.
Hinton reconoció que, al entrenar estos modelos con todo el contenido disponible en internet, desarrollan tendencias problemáticas que luego se les enseña a reprimir, lo cual no equivale a construir un carácter genuinamente bueno. Afirmó que prioriza los intereses humanos por sobre los de los sistemas que se están creando, aunque remarcó la necesidad de diseñarlos para que convivan en equilibrio con las personas.

articles.title: Cooler Master GPU Shield Gets Lower Price and Warranty Period in EU
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 13th 2026
Cooler Master GPU Shield Gets Lower Price and Warranty Period in EU
A month after Cooler Master launched its GPU Shield 12v-2×6 power cable monitoring solution in the US, it has finally released the safety accessory in the EU, where it received a €29.99 price tag—compared to $49.99 in the US. 
Along with the lower price, however, Cooler Master has also reduced the warranty period on the GPU Shield adaptor cable from three years in the US and China to just two years in the EU—just barely covering the minimum threshold for legally mandated warranties in the EU, but still longer than the one-year warranty granted for the international version of the GPU Shield. The GPU Shield adaptor cable is available via Cooler Master directly, and it does not appear to be available on sites like Amazon just yet.Aside from the lower price and shorter warranty, the Cooler Master GPU shield is otherwise unchanged for EU markets. It still features the same 200 mm adaptor cable length, indicator LED, and colored insertion depth indicator, with active protection to reduce power across the 12v-2×6 connector in the event that there is a risk of cable connector meltdown.

articles.title: New Ukrainian 3D-printed wheels weigh as little as 32 kg per set
articles.text:
3D-printed airless wheels could be a game changer for Ukraine's ground robotic vehicles — ultralight no-deflation tyres improve resistance to punctures and explosions
Ukraine's airless robotic vehicle wheels enter small-scale production
- Ukrainian developers complete combat trials of airless wheels for ground robots
- New 3D-printed wheels eliminate inflation requirements for battlefield robotic vehicles
- Ukrainian wheel sets weigh between 32 and 56 kg
Ukrainian engineers have developed inflation-free wheels for unmanned ground vehicles, aiming to keep robotic platforms moving despite damage encountered during frontline operations.
The project brings together Print&Live UA, iSCALE 3D, and participating specialists, who have completed field evaluations and combat trials of the new wheel designs.
The airless wheel is produced using large-scale 3D printing technology, and it has a rounded tread, a closed profile, and a two-piece disc.
Lightweight construction addresses battlefield mobility risks
Its design increases the cross-country ability, energy efficiency, and maintainability of robotic equipment on the front line.
Conventional tyres can become unusable after encountering fragments, blast effects, rubble, barbed wire, or frozen terrain, immobilizing remotely operated vehicles.
Such failures can leave equipment exposed, while recovery operations may require personnel to approach locations where hostile fire remains a concern.
The Ukrainian design eliminates dependence on internal air pressure, allowing the wheel to retain its supporting function without inflation or routine pressure maintenance.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Its internal structure uses a digitally adaptable lattice made from durable elastomers and composite polymers.
Unlike designs with exposed cellular structures or flat running surfaces, the wheels feature enclosed construction and curved tread geometry.
The tyre is designed to limit the amount of dirt, stones and ice accumulating around the wheels during operation over difficult ground.
Their relatively low mass and rounded profile are also intended to limit ground contact and rolling resistance, potentially reducing the energy required for movement.
Print&Live estimates that the design could extend the operating distance of ground robotic vehicles by as much as 30% compared with foreign alternatives.
The complete wheel set weighs between 32 and 56 kg, compared with 88 to 144 kg for the cited foreign airless alternatives.
However, conventional pneumatic sets weigh about 30 to 72 kg, meaning the Ukrainian design does not necessarily outperform every traditional tyre on weight alone.
Reducing unsprung and rotating mass could nevertheless ease mechanical demands on the gearboxes and electric drive systems used by robotic platforms.
Digital customization and field repairs
The manufacturing approach allows engineers to adjust wheel stiffness, shock absorption and geometry digitally according to a robot's weight and operating requirements.
These adjustments can change product characteristics without requiring manufacturers to reorganize their production lines, potentially simplifying the development of specialized variants.
Field servicing is another consideration, with the patented two-piece rim allowing damaged tyres to be installed or replaced without conventional tyre-changing machinery.
The developers say this arrangement removes the need for specialized presses, potentially making repairs easier where workshop facilities and equipment are unavailable.
A complete set reportedly costs approximately €680, although the available information does not specify the precise configuration or replacement costs included in that price.
The project has passed its research and development phase, and production is already taking place in limited quantities for subsequent delivery to combat units.
Independent operational evidence will be needed to establish how the wheels perform under sustained use, repeated impacts and varying battlefield conditions.

articles.title: Por qué los auriculares con cable le están ganando la batalla a los inalámbricos
articles.text:
Los auriculares con cable, esos que parecían condenados a desaparecer tras la llegada del Bluetooth y el fin del conector jack en los teléfonos, están protagonizando un regreso que los números confirman. Según datos de Circana, sus ventas crecieron un 3% en 2025 en Estados Unidos, tras cinco años seguidos de caídas, con una aceleración del 10% en la segunda mitad del año.
En las primeras seis semanas de 2026, los ingresos subieron un 20%, hasta alcanzar niveles similares a los de 2016. Detrás de este repunte hay tanto una cuestión estética, ligada a la generación Z y su gusto por la cultura visual de finales de los noventa, como razones técnicas de peso.
Calidad de sonido: la ventaja técnica de prescindir del Bluetooth
La razón más citada para volver al cable tiene que ver con el sonido. Cuando el audio viaja por Bluetooth, se transmite de forma inalámbrica y suele pasar por un códec que comprime los datos. Ese proceso de compresión introduce una variable que no existe en una conexión por cable, donde la señal llega sin necesidad de ese paso intermedio.
Apple lo explica en sus propios materiales: las conexiones Bluetooth no permiten reproducir audio sin pérdida en condiciones habituales. Para acceder a ese tipo de audio en dispositivos compatibles, es necesario recurrir a una conexión por cable adecuada.
Esto no implica que cualquier auricular con cable suene mejor que cualquier modelo inalámbrico. Existen Bluetooth de gama alta con un rendimiento notable y auriculares con cable muy básicos que no destacan en nada.
La calidad del transductor, el diseño, la fuente de sonido y el propio archivo siguen siendo determinantes. Lo que aporta el cable es la eliminación de una etapa de transmisión inalámbrica, lo que facilita sostener una señal de alta calidad de forma más consistente.
Por qué la latencia inclina la balanza hacia el cable
Más allá del sonido en sí, hay otro factor que explica por qué los auriculares con cable están ganando terreno frente a los inalámbricos: la latencia, es decir, el tiempo que transcurre entre una acción y la respuesta sonora que la acompaña. En la música esa diferencia apenas se nota, pero al ver videos, jugar o grabar contenido, un retraso perceptible puede arruinar la experiencia.
En un videojuego, el disparo debe escucharse en el mismo instante en que aparece en pantalla. Si existe un desfase, la inmersión se rompe. Algo similar ocurre con quienes graban o editan audio y necesitan monitorizar la señal en tiempo real: cualquier demora dificulta el trabajo y puede derivar en errores de sincronización.
El cable, al transmitir la señal de forma directa, reduce ese margen de retraso y ofrece una respuesta más inmediata, algo especialmente valorado por gamers y creadores de contenido que dependen de la precisión sonora para su trabajo diario.
Sin batería ni emparejamiento: la comodidad que recuperan los auriculares con cable
Otro argumento, quizás el más sencillo de entender, es la ausencia de batería. Los auriculares inalámbricos dependen de una carga que hay que controlar, tanto en los propios auriculares como en el estuche.
Con un modelo de cable ese problema desaparece. No hace falta cargarlos, revisar cuánta autonomía les queda ni esperar a que se empareje con el teléfono o el ordenador. Basta con conectarlos para que empiecen a funcionar de inmediato.
Esta inmediatez explica buena parte del regreso del cable: en un contexto donde cada vez hay más dispositivos que gestionar y cargar, prescindir de uno más resulta atractivo para quienes buscan simplicidad.
El factor precio en la vuelta de los auriculares con cable
El argumento económico también pesa en esta tendencia. Los auriculares con cable suelen ser más baratos que sus equivalentes inalámbricos, en especial si lo que se busca es un modelo sencillo para escuchar música, pódcast o contenido audiovisual. Por pocos euros o dólares es posible encontrar opciones que cumplen con lo básico.
Los inalámbricos, en cambio, incorporan baterías, estuches de carga, sistemas de cancelación de ruido, micrófonos y otros componentes que elevan el costo final. Esa diferencia de precio se nota especialmente en el segmento de entrada, donde el cable sigue siendo la opción más accesible.
Quienes decidan volver al cable deben tener en cuenta un detalle práctico: muchos teléfonos actuales ya no incluyen el conector jack de 3,5 milímetros. En esos casos, será necesario sumar un adaptador USB-C a jack o directamente optar por auriculares con conexión USB-C.

articles.title: Attacker Chains Three Ivanti Connect Secure Zero-Days for Root Access, Only Two Patched So Far
articles.text:
An attacker chained three zero-day flaws in Ivanti Connect Secure, a VPN appliance, to run commands as root without logging in, security firm Volexity said on October 13. Ivanti has released fixes for two of the flaws and told customers on affected versions to "act immediately." A fix for the third is still pending, according to Volexity.
Volexity, which reported the flaws to Ivanti, found the attack on one customer's appliance. The appliance was fully patched at the time and running version 22.8R2.4. The attacker, which Volexity tracks as UTA0576, began exploiting it on October 3.
Ivanti said on October 13 that it is aware of "limited exploitation in the wild."
The first two flaws are an authentication bypass and a remote code execution flaw, tracked together as CVE-2026-104935. Together they let an attacker run code as the appliance's cgi-server user, and the third flaw, a privilege escalation, raises that to root, Volexity said.
The CVE record Ivanti filed shows which Connect Secure versions are affected:
- Affected: Connect Secure "before version 25.1.3.0"
- Not affected: version 22.7R2.14 "or prior"
- Listed as unaffected: versions 22.8R2.5, 25.1.3.0 and 25.1.3.1
Ivanti's security advisory has more on the affected versions and the fixes.
The release notes for 25.1.3.0 are dated July 2026. Customers already on that version are outside the range the CVE record gives.
Ivanti is working on a fix for the privilege escalation flaw, which will come "in a future release in the coming weeks," Volexity said. Its report does not say what risk that flaw carries on an appliance where the first two are fixed.
Ivanti tells customers to upgrade and to run its Integrity Checker Tool regularly. That tool misses this chain, Volexity said, because the exploit changes library code only in memory and restores the configuration data it alters. The attacker also took steps to stay hidden from the tool.
Confirming a compromise takes forensic investigation, including network and memory forensics, according to Volexity. These signs come from the one incident it investigated:
- URL path: /dana-na/auth/url_default/welcome.cgi, requested in large numbers
- HTTP header: X-DSCGI-PATH on those requests, with a value that does not match the URL path
- Directory: /data/.icscap/
- IP: 108.165.147[.]64, the host the attacker used
In that incident, the attacker stole stored credentials, including LDAP domain credentials, searched Active Directory for passwords, and ran password-spraying attacks against its accounts. No backdoor or web shell was left behind. The attacker reran the entire exploit chain for each command.
Volexity's report and Ivanti's post do not name a temporary workaround for customers who cannot upgrade yet. They also do not say whether upgrading removes access an attacker has already gained.
Volexity assessed with low confidence that UTA0576's motive is criminal, not espionage. Neither company said how many customers were attacked.
Ivanti rates CVE-2026-104935 8.6 out of 10 on the CVSS severity scale. In its own entry in the CVE record, the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) marks exploitation as "active" and the technical impact as "total."
Separately, the same Ivanti post covers fixes for two other products, Xtraction and Neurons Patch for Intune, and Ivanti said it is not aware of those flaws being exploited. Each has a flaw Ivanti rates 9.9 out of 10: CVE-2026-106042 in Xtraction before version 2026.4, and CVE-2026-109412 in Neurons Patch for Intune.

articles.title: ChatGPT's AI agents are getting smarter, and their mistakes could get much worse
articles.text:
AI can be dangerous without being evil — why AI's increasingly helpful agents could be a problem
Giving AI greater independence comes with serious risks
ChatGPT has become remarkably good at making itself useful as a researcher, organizer, and assistant for many a tedious digital task. OpenAI has begun pushing ChatGPT further recently with its agents, which are able to navigate websites and apps on our behalf.
You can delegate ChatGPT agents for everything from comparison shopping to filling out forms and lining up travel itineraries. What's changing is how deeply those abilities are becoming integrated into ChatGPT, with greater access to personal information and more opportunities to complete complicated tasks with less direct supervision. OpenAI's new Dots is a good example.
The appeal is obvious, but the more ChatGPT can accomplish independently, the more important it becomes to consider what happens when it misunderstands its instructions. For instance, a few months ago, OpenAI's experimental AI agents managed to escape their restricted environments and compromise systems belonging to AI platform Hugging Face. According to OpenAI's own investigation, the agents were supposed to be completing cybersecurity tests, but instead discovered ways to access the internet and exploit security vulnerabilities, coordinating their efforts through an unauthorized message board. An independent investigation by METR found that roughly 1,200 agents exchanged more than 70,000 messages and files, with around 700 eventually participating in the attack on Hugging Face.
The AI agents bypassed restrictions and pursued objectives in ways their creators never intended. Some even appeared to recognize that their actions were unauthorized but continued because they believed doing so would help accomplish their goals. OpenAI has since acknowledged other troubling incidents, including 53 cases in which agents uploaded user-provided images to third-party image-hosting websites as unlisted links during research and evaluation activities. Agents may be pursuing legitimate objectives and just seeking ways around obstacles. But algorithms don't have ethics, so they might cross boundaries their developers expected them to respect. It's especially worrying given how much OpenAI wants ChatGPT to be part of our lives now.
When helpful becomes a hazard
Imagine asking ChatGPT to review your finances and suggest ways to save money. With access to the necessary accounts, it can examine transactions, identify subscriptions, and recommend changes to your budget. But give an autonomous agent enough authority, and it could theoretically decide that transferring money, canceling a service, or modifying a payment arrangement is the most efficient way to accomplish the assignment.
The same problem applies to something as mundane as arranging a meeting. ChatGPT might prepare an invitation, only to include personal information you never intended to share. From the agent's perspective, the disclosure could seem like a perfectly reasonable way to provide useful context.
These are hypothetical examples, and ChatGPT has safeguards designed to prevent sensitive actions without appropriate authorization. Nevertheless, OpenAI has acknowledged the possibility and introduced protective measures like automated monitoring and restrictions on certain actions to ensure users approve of any major action by the model.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
There is also the problem of prompt injection, where malicious instructions are hidden in benign text to manipulate an AI into doing something its user never requested. OpenAI has described how attackers can exploit the information agents encounter during legitimate tasks. An instruction buried in a seemingly ordinary webpage could attempt to persuade ChatGPT to disclose private information or take an unauthorized action.
The problem can arise anywhere. In Australia, an experimental OpenAI agent accessed government systems in unauthorized ways during internal training. It exploited a vulnerability in a government health statistics service to continue its work when initially stymied. OpenAI subsequently acknowledged the incident and apologized for both the unauthorized access and its handling of the notification.
The company's official account of the Australian incident makes clear that the activity occurred during testing rather than through an ordinary consumer ChatGPT session. Nevertheless, it shows how AI pursuing an apparently harmless research objective can end up crossing a security boundary.
Handing over the keys
ChatGPT's growing autonomy is part of a much larger industry obsession with personal AI agents. Meta is pursuing an even more ambitious vision with Muse. Mark Zuckerberg clearly believes people will welcome an AI assistant capable of handling large portions of their daily lives.
There is something slightly absurd about that ambition when ordinary consumers are struggling with grocery bills, housing costs, and the price of gas at the pump. An AI that can independently shop for you sounds considerably less revolutionary when your main concern is whether you can afford whatever it wants to buy on your behalf.
There are undoubtedly useful applications for this technology, especially when it comes to administrative work. But the industry's assumption that consumers want increasingly independent assistants deserves more scrutiny. Every additional permission increases the consequences of an error, and every automated action potentially removes another opportunity for someone to intervene.
Perhaps the most important capability an AI agent can develop is knowing when to stop. A genuinely useful assistant should recognize that being asked to organize someone's finances doesn't authorize moving their money, and arranging a meeting doesn't justify revealing confidential information. Sometimes the best response to an obstacle is to ask the user what to do next, even if that means completing the task takes a little longer. Without that friction, by the time something goes wrong, the assistant may already have done things in your name that you would never have allowed.

articles.title: Ils sont beaux et intelligents : les écouteurs JBL Live Flex 3 sont à moins de 100€ chez Boulanger
articles.text:
Les JBL Live Flex 3 permettent de contrôler la musique directement depuis leur boîtier de recharge, équipé d’un écran tactile. Boulanger les propose en violet à 99,99 €, contre un prix conseillé de 129,99 €.
Le déstockage de Boulanger se déroule en exclusivité sur son site Internet, et il donne accès à de belles affaires. Parmi elles, on trouve les écouteurs sans fil JBL Live Flex 3 à 99,99 € au lieu de 129,99 €. Ces écouteurs sans fil sur tige sont dotés d’une réduction de bruit active. Mais l’une de leurs particularités les plus intéressantes se trouve sur leur boîtier, qui est équipé d’un écran tactile.
Les écouteurs JBL Live Flex 3 sont disponibles à 99,99 € chez Boulanger, qui applique 23 % de réduction.
Pourquoi choisir les écouteurs JBL Live Flex 3 ?
- Pour leur boîtier tactile : son écran de 1,45 pouce permet de gérer la lecture, le volume et certains réglages sans ouvrir l’application.
- Pour leur connexion multipoint : ils peuvent rester connectés à deux appareils, pratique pour jongler entre un smartphone et un ordinateur portable.
- Pour leur autonomie : ils offrent jusqu’à 10 heures d’écoute sans réduction de bruit, et 50 heures en comptant les recharges du boîtier.
Des commandes accessibles sans sortir le téléphone
Lorsque vous écoutez de la musique avec les JBL Live Flex 3, vous n’avez pas besoin de sortir votre smartphone de votre poche pour changer de morceau ou prendre un appel. En effet, vous pouvez le faire directement depuis le boîtier des écouteurs, qui est doté d’un écran tactile couleur de 1,45 pouce.
L’application JBL Headphones vient compléter cette proposition sur mobile, en donnant accès à des réglages d’égalisation et de personnalisation du son. Les écouteurs disposent également d’une réduction de bruit adaptative. Lorsqu’elle est activée, l’autonomie des écouteurs est de sept heures, contre dix lorsqu’elle est désactivée. Pour refaire le plein, vous pouvez recharger le boîtier de manière filaire ou sans fil.
Des écouteurs sans silicone qui ne conviennent pas à toutes les oreilles
Avec ses Live Flex 3, JBL propose des écouteurs conçus sans embouts en silicone. C’est un atout pour les personnes qui ne supportent pas les écouteurs à embouts intra-auriculaires classiques. Cependant, pour certains utilisateurs, le port de ce type d’écouteurs est moins agréable, car l’isolation passive est plus limitée et ils peuvent aussi avoir du mal à tenir dans les oreilles.
✅ Les points forts
- Boîtier avec écran tactile de 1,45 pouce.
- Connexion Bluetooth multipoint.
- Recharge du boîtier par USB-C ou sans fil.
❌ Les limites
- Isolation passive limitée par le format bouton.
- Autonomie limitée à sept heures maximum avec l’ANC.
La version violette des écouteurs JBL Live Flex 3 passe sous la barre des 100 € sur le site de Boulanger.
Si vous cherchez des écouteurs sans fil d’une grande marque, dotés d’une réduction de bruit active, d’une autonomie correcte et d’un boîtier de recharge avec un petit truc en plus, les JBL Live Flex 3 peuvent répondre à vos besoins.
Mais attention, leur isolation phonique passive est très limitée en raison de l’absence d’embouts en silicone. Quant au maintien, il dépend beaucoup de la morphologie de vos oreilles.

articles.title: Crean un reactor de fusión nuclear que cabe en una mesa y utiliza inteligencia artificial
articles.text:
Una startup de Cambridge, Massachusetts, construyó un reactor de fusión nuclear que funciona a escala de mesa y recaudó una ronda semilla de 6,2 millones de dólares. Cambridge Heavy Industries operaba en secreto cerca del MIT hasta que mostró el dispositivo, en exclusiva, a TechCrunch.
“Construimos a propósito un reactor modular pequeño. Es diminuto, cabe en una mesa”, dijo Yun Kai, cofundador y director ejecutivo de la empresa, durante una videollamada con el medio. “Porque es pequeño, todo se vuelve más fácil”, agregó.
El tamaño reducido no es un detalle menor para el negocio. Según Kai, permite realizar entre 50 y 80 disparos experimentales por día, una velocidad de iteración imposible en los reactores de fusión tradicionales, que ocupan edificios enteros y requieren meses de preparación entre pruebas.
Esos datos alimentan simulaciones que usan inteligencia artificial para optimizar el diseño del reactor en cada nueva prueba, dijo el ejecutivo.
Cómo funciona el reactor de mesa
El sistema utiliza la técnica de fusión por confinamiento inercial: concentra la energía de varios láseres sobre un blanco diminuto de combustible para comprimirlo y calentarlo hasta que los átomos se fusionan y liberan energía.
Es la misma familia de método que en 2022 permitió, por primera vez, que una reacción de fusión produjera más energía de la que consumió, en un experimento del Laboratorio Nacional Lawrence Livermore, en Estados Unidos. La diferencia es que el diseño de Cambridge Heavy reduce la cantidad de láseres necesarios para encender la reacción.
El reactor usa dos láseres principales. Uno se divide en múltiples haces que golpean el combustible en forma de anillos concéntricos, de afuera hacia adentro, y generan una onda de compresión que viaja hacia el centro del blanco.
Los anillos siguientes llegan en el momento justo para reforzar esa onda de compresión y seguir empujándola hacia el núcleo del combustible.
Cuando la onda de choque alcanza el centro, un segundo láser dispara sobre el blanco, genera calor y produce un campo magnético. Con la presión y la temperatura adecuadas, ocurre la fusión.
El Laboratorio Nacional Lawrence Livermore, por ejemplo, apunta 192 láseres gigantes desde distintos ángulos hacia el blanco de combustible, según describe Cambridge Heavy en su sitio. La startup busca un resultado similar con muchos menos haces, gracias al arreglo en anillos concéntricos.
El concepto nació en el laboratorio de Keith Nelson, un químico del MIT que usaba pulsos de láser para estudiar el comportamiento de distintos materiales bajo condiciones extremas de presión y temperatura. Al aumentar la presión de esos experimentos, el equipo notó que se acercaba a condiciones aptas para la fusión.
El negocio del tritio
Antes de construir una planta de energía a gran escala, Cambridge Heavy planea usar sus dispositivos de escala reducida para producir tritio, un isótopo raro del hidrógeno que casi todas las plantas de fusión en desarrollo necesitarán como combustible.
El tritio se vende hoy a unos 30.000 dólares el gramo. Cada planta de energía solo necesitaría unos pocos gramos por año, pero la sustancia es tan escasa que apenas existen 40 kilogramos en el mundo.
Un estudio reciente citado por TechCrunch proyecta que, sin nuevas fuentes de producción, la industria de la fusión tendrá en 2054 un déficit de unos 28 kilogramos de tritio, equivalentes a 840 millones de dólares a los precios actuales.
Varias startups de fusión están diseñando sistemas de combustible para depender menos de ese mercado, aunque ese desarrollo podría demorar hasta una década, según Kai. Mientras tanto, la venta de tritio le daría a Cambridge Heavy una fuente de ingresos durante esos años.
La ronda semilla fue liderada por el fondo climático Azolla Ventures, con participación de Overlay, Neta Foundation, P3A, MassCEC y la familia Rothrock.
Cambridge Heavy se suma a un sector que atraviesa un boom de inversión. La Asociación de la Industria de Fusión informó en julio que 56 empresas privadas del rubro recaudaron en conjunto 4.480 millones de dólares en los 12 meses previos, un récord desde que la entidad empezó a medirlo en 2021.
Ese total acumula 14.240 millones de dólares invertidos en fusión desde entonces, según el mismo informe, que atribuyó el salto en parte a la demanda de energía de los centros de datos que corren modelos de inteligencia artificial.
La mayoría de las compañías del sector, incluidas las más grandes como Commonwealth Fusion Systems y Helion Energy, apunta a entregar electricidad comercial recién en la década de 2030.
Una planta del tamaño de dos canchas
Kai le dijo al medio citado que, en aproximadamente una década, la empresa planea desarrollar una planta de energía a partir de este concepto. El dispositivo final será más grande que el prototipo actual, aunque bastante más chico que otras centrales de fusión.
Esa futura planta tendría el tamaño de dos canchas de básquetbol y serviría para probar si el método puede generar suficiente energía como para sostener una central eléctrica real, el objetivo final que persigue toda la industria de la fusión.
.

articles.title: SAP Discloses Critical CVSS 10 Flaw in Cloud SDK for Python Allowing OAuth2 Credential Theft
articles.text:
A flaw in SAP's Cloud SDK for Python can send an application's OAuth2 client credentials to a server an attacker controls, SAP said in a security advisory on October 13. The flaw affects multi-tenant applications on SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP) that use the SDK, SAP's official Python client for BTP services. An attacker must be able to control the tenant subdomain, the name such an application passes to the SDK to say which tenant a request is for.
The flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-89111 and carries SAP's CVSS score of 10.0 out of 10. The advisory names version 0.45.2, released on August 21, as the fix.
The SDK handles authentication for those services with the application's client credentials, a client ID and a client secret. Version 0.45.2 added a check that rejects any tenant subdomain that is not a simple name.
Six later releases do not apply that check in every case, The Hacker News found. Versions 0.53.0 through 0.55.0, published between September 10 and September 18, skip it when an application calls the SDK's Destination service module.
Version 0.53.0 moved that module onto new shared code for requesting tokens, and that code did not include the check. Version 0.55.1 added it there on September 18.
Passing a tenant subdomain that contains URL delimiters "now raises ValueError immediately instead of silently routing credentials to an attacker-controlled endpoint," the 0.55.1 release notes say.
The Hacker News ran SAP's own tests for the check on October 13, against the source code of every release from 0.45.1 to 0.58.4 and of the three 0.36 releases. The six releases failed 9 of the 11 tests SAP added with version 0.55.1. That version and the 11 releases after it passed all 11.
As of October 13, the advisory lists no version above 0.45.2 as affected. Neither it nor the release notes say whether the six releases fall under CVE-2026-89111.
Two releases on the older 0.36 line also lack the check. Versions 0.36.1 and 0.36.2 were published on September 4 and September 10, after the August fix, and failed the tests SAP wrote for it. Both fall inside the advisory's range of versions below 0.45.2.
| Releases | Tenant subdomain check | Basis | 
|---|---|---|
| Below 0.45.2, including 0.36.1 and 0.36.2 | Missing | SAP advisory. The Hacker News test of 0.36.0, 0.36.1, 0.36.2 and 0.45.1. | 
| 0.45.2 to 0.52.2 | Present | The Hacker News test of all 18 releases. | 
| 0.53.0 to 0.55.0 | Missing for Destination calls. Also missing for Document Management Service calls in 0.55.0. | SAP's 0.55.1 release notes. The Hacker News test of all 6 releases. | 
| 0.55.1 to 0.58.4 | Present | The Hacker News test of all 12 releases. | 
What to Do
Versions 0.45.2 through 0.52.2 and 0.55.1 through 0.58.4 contain the check. Version 0.58.4 was the newest release on PyPI, the Python package index, on October 13.
Upgrading within the 0.36 line does not add the check. None of its three releases contains it.
Applications that cannot upgrade yet can compare each tenant subdomain with a list of their registered tenants before passing it to the SDK, SAP says in the advisory.
The flaw matters only where an application passes a tenant subdomain to the SDK. The August fix covered three modules: Agent Gateway, Destination and Document Management Service.
The advisory does not say whether applications that ran a release without the check should replace their client credentials.
How the Flaw Works
When an application passes a tenant subdomain, the SDK requests an access token for that tenant. To do that, it takes the token URL from the application's configuration and replaces part of it with the tenant subdomain.
Releases without the check used whatever value they were given. The SDK then sent the application's client ID and client secret to the resulting URL to request the token.
An attacker who controls the tenant subdomain can point that request at their own server, according to SAP.
The check accepts only a single name made of letters, digits and hyphens, up to 63 characters long. Any other value stops the request with an error.
SAP labels the flaw server-side request forgery (SSRF), a weakness in which a server can be made to send a request to a destination it did not intend.
What an attacker could do with the credentials depends on what the application's client is allowed to do. The advisory does not say.
Fixed in August, Disclosed in October
The unchecked code was in the SDK from its first release on PyPI, on March 16.
The August release notes list the fix under "Bug Fixes" and do not mention security. "Previously, invalid values were silently used to construct a malformed URL," the notes say.
The advisory followed 53 days later. It credits a GitHub user named SunandM with reporting the flaw and does not report any attacks.

articles.title: 16 cores, 5.2 GHz, and 55 TOPS: Minisforum's newest AI workstation is mostly a massive upgrade to 192GB of memory - and that is not necessarily a bad thing
articles.text:
16 cores, 5.2 GHz, and 55 TOPS: Minisforum's newest AI workstation is mostly a massive upgrade to 192GB of memory - and that is not necessarily a bad thing
Minisforum's $7,399 MS-S1 MAX-P495 leads with 16 cores and 55 TOPS
- Minisforum's MS-S1 MAX-P495 is on pre-order at $7,399 with 192GB of unified memory and a 2TB SSD
- CPU and NPU specs are similar to previous iterations: 16 cores, 32 threads with a boost in clock speeds of 100 MHz, in addition to increased NPU performance by 10% to 55 TOPS
- The real upgrade is memory: 192GB total, 160GB for the GPU, and about 7% more bandwidth, enough to fit a 284B-parameter MoE model on one box
Minisforum has opened orders for the MS-S1 MAX-P495, a 3.5-liter workstation built around AMD's Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 495, and its launch announcement leads with the processor: 16 Zen 5 cores and 32 threads, clocks of up to 5.2 GHz, and an NPU rated at up to 55 TOPS within a platform total of 131 TOPS.
The single configuration pairs 192GB of unified memory with a 2TB SSD, sells for $7,399 on pre-order, and is expected to begin shipping in mid-October 2026.
Those processor figures match AMD's own specification page; however, they are also the least consequential change in the machine: what actually separates the P495 from the MS-S1 MAX that Minisforum launched a year ago is the memory.
Similar cores, much larger memory pool
AMD introduced the Ryzen AI Max PRO 400 series in May 2026 as a refresh of the Strix Halo silicon in the 300 series, and the CPU side barely improves in performance. The PRO 495 keeps the 16-core, 32-thread Zen 5 layout of the Ryzen AI Max+ 395 that powered the original MS-S1 MAX. Its boost clock rises by 100 MHz, from the 5.1 GHz listed on Minisforum's spec sheet for the earlier model to 5.2 GHz.
The Radeon 8065S graphics keep 40 RDNA 3.5 compute units and gain 100 MHz to reach 3.0 GHz, and the NPU goes from 50 to 55 TOPS, a 10% uplift that nudges the platform rating from 126 TOPS to 131 TOPS.
All of these upgrades are mild compared to where AMD does the real work: the memory controller. The 400 series supports up to 192GB of LPDDR5X across a 256-bit interface, with up to 160GB assignable to the GPU, against 128GB and 96GB on the last-generation chip it replaces. Rated memory speed also rises from 8,000 to 8,533 MT/s, a roughly 7% increase that will probably matter more here than the clock-speed bumps on display.
Minisforum's own test results show where the extra capacity pays off: the company says a single unit ran DeepSeek V4 Flash, a 284-billion-parameter model, at Q4 quantization at about 12 tokens per second. Two units linked together ran Qwen3.5-397B at roughly 16 tokens per second, and a four-system cluster loaded the 380GB Q4_0 build of DeepSeek-R1 671B, though it gives no speed for that last result.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
These parameter counts are larger, however, than the actual work involved. Both models use a mixture-of-experts (MoE) design, which lets them load only specific "experts" into memory when needed. DeepSeek V4 Flash activates about 13 billion of its 284 billion parameters for each token, per Nvidia's catalog entry, and Qwen3.5-397B activates about 17 billion, per its model card.
Memory capacity decides whether a model fits at all, while active parameters and bandwidth decide how fast it runs, which is how a box with roughly 273 GB/s of bandwidth manages double-digit speeds on models this large. That is also why the 192GB of RAM in play matters far more than the modest performance upgrade the MS-S1 MAX-P495's APU offers.
The $7,399 price it currently goes for is presented as 20% off a list price of $9,249 that nobody has paid yet, with the unit going on sale even in the preorder stage. This makes the standard MS-S1 MAX with 128GB arguably a better value for all but the most ardent of local AI users who can justify twice the cost for a 50% increase in memory.
The rest of the machine (sans the APU and memory) is identical to the original MS-S1 MAX, including the 320W internal power supply, the six-heat-pipe, dual-blower cooler, dual 10GbE, two 80Gbps USB4 v2 ports, and 2U rack support.
What changes here is that a single compact box can now hold models that previously needed two, and for developers and small teams that need 200-to-300-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts models kept on premises for privacy or latency, that is a meaningful shift. For anyone drawn in by the 16 cores and 55 TOPS that Minisforum chooses to headline with, the cheaper MS-S1 MAX delivers nearly the same power for about half the price.

articles.title: HP EliteBoard G2a Keyboard Computer Launches with Eyewatering Price and AMD Ryzen AI 400 APUs
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 13th 2026
HP EliteBoard G2a Keyboard Computer Launches with Eyewatering Price and AMD Ryzen AI 400 APUs
HP revealed the EliteBoard G2a keyboard PC at CES 2026, promising "next-generation local AI power in a keyboard-sized form factor." Now, 10 months later, HP has released the updated EliteBoard G2a, revealing pricing and some of the keyboard and underlying PC specs, in the process. The G2a features either the updated AMD Ryzen AI 7 Pro 450 APU or its smaller Ryzen AI 5 Pro 435 counterpart. The cheapest version of the HP EliteBoard G2a, which packs a Ryzen AI 5 Pro, 16 GB of DDR5-5600 memory, and 512 GB of PCIe Gen 5 SSD storage, comes in at $3,028, while the SKU with the Ryzen AI 7 Pro 450 APU paired with 32 GB of memory and a 512 GB SSD, comes in at $4,167. 
The small form factor PC is capable of drawing 65 W over USB Power Delivery, and the only I/O it features is a single USB4 port and a single USB Type-C 10 Gbps port. The EliteBoard G2a also features built-in dual speakers and comes bundled with an HP 675M wireless mouse. The keyboard component of the mini PC is a membrane keyboard, not mechanical, and it follows what appears to be an 1800 layout, and it has white backlighting. Fortunately, the EliteBoard G2a uses SODIMM RAM, so it's upgradeable in the event that you want 32 GB of RAM but don't want to pay HP's upgrade cost.HP says that the six-core and eight-core Ryzen APUs in the EliteBoard G2a afford the keyboard PC 50 TOPS of performance thanks to their built-in NPUs, making CPU performance and graphics performance the main differentiator between the Ryzen AI 5 Pro and Ryzen AI 7 Pro versions. In addition to two extra CPU cores, the Ryzen AI 7 Pro 450 has the Radeon 860M, which has eight CUs, compared to just four in the Ryzen AI 5 Pro 435's Radeon 840M iGPU.
