articles.title: Product Walkthrough: Bitdefender AI Visibility and Control
articles.text:
A user opens a browser tab, pastes data into a chat assistant, and nothing is installed.
A developer adds a coding assistant as an editor extension, and nothing shows up in the installed programs list.
Someone downloads a local model runtime, a program that runs models directly on the machine instead of sending data to an external service, because they were told not to send company data outside.
None of this reaches your software inventory. Tasked with controlling AI, an administrator often resorts to blocking well-known AI websites and taking enforcement action without knowing what is actually running.
Bitdefender GravityZone AI Visibility and Control (AIVC) is the discovery and risk layer that answers the questions you have, first: Which AI software is present on your protected Windows endpoints, who is running it, and how much risk does each one carry.
What Your Software Inventory Was Never Built to Watch
AI Visibility and Control covers four classes of exposure, and each one sits outside a control you already own.
- AI services reached through the browser. Hosted assistants are the path most organizations already worry about. The inventory identifies which services are running, on which machines, and whether you have marked them as approved. A service with no findings is not automatically approved; a clean result on a tool your organization never sanctioned is still shadow AI. This ensures filtering decisions are based on real user activity rather than hand-picked domain lists.
- AI inside the development environment. Coding assistants run inside editors that already hold source repositories, and often credentials and configuration files in the same working directory. They are rarely covered by whatever you decided about chat assistants, because nobody classified them as the same kind of tool.
- AI running locally on the endpoint. Local model runtimes, MCP servers, and agent frameworks execute on the machine itself. A control that governs which websites an endpoint may reach does not see them at all. The MCP server is the sharpest case: its entire purpose is to hand a model access to something else, and it usually arrives as a configuration entry rather than as an install.
- AI with reach into other systems. Where a tool is configured to connect to a database, a code repository, an internal API, or a third-party model service, that connection is part of your attack surface. AI Visibility and Control records the configured scope of those connections, not the data moving across them.
How AIVC Finds and Categorizes What It Finds
GravityZone AI Visibility and Control discovery takes place during the risk scan. The GravityZone BEST agent collects metadata from each endpoint and keeps that collection minimized: it records what AI software is present and how it is configured, not what anyone does with it. AIVC does not inspect prompts, chat history, model weights, credentials, or full file content.
AI Visibility and Control recognizes more than 50 AI agents and more than 70,000 skills, the modular code packages that extend an agent's capabilities and that arrive from public registries. Because agents exercise permissions through these skills, considering only agents while ignoring skills would account for only a fraction of the total exposure.
Every discovered service is assigned to one of 17 functional categories based on its primary function (e.g., LLMs, coding, productivity, and others). The category makes the inventory actionable at the policy level because it maps to the question the reviewer arrived with. A security team investigating data-handling risk, filters to LLMs and chatbots plus Platforms and infrastructure. A development manager auditing what touches source code goes straight to Coding and Tools and skills. A governance review covering automation risk works from Agents, Automation, and MCP.
Two Views, and a Connector Nobody Installed
AI Visibility and Control appears in Bitdefender GravityZone Console as two views, each answering a different question.
AI Services answers "what AI is running in my environment?" It is the inventory: every discovered service with its risk score. This includes the function category, the related AI assets it depends on or exposes, its count of open findings, the affected resources and endpoints it was found on, its state of Active or Ignored, and whether it sits on the watchlist. Opening a service shows its details alongside mitigation guidance.
AI Findings answers "what should I look at first?" It is the prioritized risk view. Each finding includes a risk score, the service it relates to, the affected resources it was observed on, a link to mitigation guidance, and the endpoint-specific evidence behind it.
This enables you to see why a finding was raised on one machine and not another before deciding what to do. Most administrators work in AI Findings day to day and drop into AI Services for the full picture of a particular tool.
A score of 0 means AI Visibility and Control found nothing risky in how a tool is configured, not that your organization approved it. Review AI Services against your list of sanctioned tools, not just AI Findings.
Consider a developer who connects their AI assistant to the company ticketing system using a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, which is a small connector that gives a model access to external tools. The setup requires only a few lines in a configuration file: there is no installer, no entry in the installed programs list, and no network traffic for controls to inspect. It simply surfaces in AI Services alongside the assets it exposes.
The finding answers not just whether the connector exists, but what it reaches. A connector tied to a read-only reporting view presents a vastly different risk from one holding write credentials to a production database. This distinction lives entirely in its configuration. Meanwhile, the affected-host list clarifies the broader scope: whether this is an isolated shortcut or a pattern copied across the entire team.
That endpoint-specific evidence is also what makes findings usable by a SOC analyst rather than only as a posture metric. A finding tied to a local model runtime or an MCP server identifies a process executing on a specific host outside the browser sandbox, and the affected-resources list gives the host set to pivot from, in Search and Incident Advisor.
From Inventory to Enforcement
GravityZone AI Visibility and Control establishes which AI is present and what about its configuration is risky. The score orders your queue; it does not decide the outcome. A high score is not an order to remove the tool, and a score of 0 is not an approval. It does not block access, remove software, or modify program permissions. Those actions are handled separately by existing controls within the GravityZone console.
Blocking access to a prohibited service is Web Content Filtering. Most AI services are accessed through the browser, so once AIVC identifies which ones are in use, you block the domains.
Blocking a specific tool wherever it turns up is what custom detection rules do: once AIVC has named the tool, you define a rule that matches it on process name, attach Kill process as an automatic action, and every later appearance is handled without an administrator in the loop, and is company-wide or scoped to endpoints carrying a given tag.
Reducing what an installed tool is permitted to do belongs to hardening policies and to PHASR. PHASR for AI agents evaluates the agent separately from the person using the machine: processes started by a known agent binary are attributed to that agent's own behavioral profile rather than to the user's session, so the agent gets the tools its tasks require while the user's restrictions stay tied to the user's role.
Turning on AI Visibility and Control does not require a rollout project. It runs on your existing Bitdefender Endpoint Security Tools agent and can be enabled by editing a current policy. The setting sits in the General section under Risk Management and applies to all endpoints targeted by that policy. Results will appear after the next risk scan.
Summary
Bitdefender GravityZone AI Visibility and Control provides the AI inventory your traditional software inventory cannot: browser-reached assistants, editor extensions, local runtimes, MCP servers, and agent frameworks; each with a risk score, one of 17 functional categories, and a list of impacted endpoints. It covers more 50 agents and 70,000 skills, and it records what is present and how it is configured, rather than user prompts.
The two console views align with your existing workflow: AI Findings highlight what to address first, while AI Services gives a complete picture of any specific tool. A risk score tells you how exposed a tool is, not whether it is sanctioned; that decision, and the enforcement that follows, stays with you. Enforcement remains where it already lives: Web Content Filtering, custom detection rules, and PHASR, so your policy decisions stop being guesses, and you can gain greater confidence in the control you have over AI use within your organization.

articles.title: El FBI arrestó a un ingeniero de OpenAI por esconder un micrófono en una sala ejecutiva
articles.text:
Un ingeniero de OpenAI identificado como Abdulrahman Alfozan, de 35 años y nacionalidad saudita, fue arrestado el 9 de octubre acusado de instalar en secreto un dispositivo de grabación de audio en una sala de reuniones ejecutiva de la empresa en San Francisco, según un comunicado del Departamento de Justicia de Estados Unidos.
Alfozan fue imputado por usar o intentar usar un aparato electrónico para interceptar comunicaciones orales. Compareció por primera vez ante un tribunal federal el martes y permanece detenido. Si es condenado, enfrenta hasta cinco años de prisión y una multa de USD 250.000, además de tres años de libertad supervisada.
Alfozan trabajaba como ingeniero en OpenAI desde julio de 2025. El 30 de septiembre, personal de la empresa descubrió un dispositivo de grabación insertado en un puerto USB detrás de un televisor, dentro de una sala de reuniones ejecutiva de una de las oficinas de la compañía en San Francisco.
El aparato estaba oculto entre papel higiénico y su contenido estaba encriptado. Según la fiscalía, había sido instalado alrededor del 28 de septiembre, y las reuniones que se realizaban en esa sala solían incluir información confidencial sobre investigación, planes de producto y acuerdos comerciales de la empresa.
Cómo detectaron al sospechoso
Las cámaras de seguridad del edificio mostraron que Alfozan merodeó cerca de la sala en varias fechas previas al hallazgo, aunque no tenía autorización para ingresar ni para participar de las reuniones que se realizaban allí, señala la denuncia penal.
Antes de instalar el dispositivo, Alfozan usó una herramienta interna de la empresa para hacer consultas sobre direcciones de los edificios, salas de reuniones, capacidades y agendas, y sobre la ubicación del “liderazgo y los ejecutivos”, de acuerdo con la fiscalía.
Una cuenta de chatbot vinculada al cónyuge de Alfozan, que compartía varios identificadores con la suya, envió entre el 24 y el 30 de septiembre consultas sobre cómo construir, personalizar, instalar y ocultar un grabador de audio, y cómo encriptar la tarjeta de memoria del aparato.
La misma cuenta preguntó, entre el 27 y el 28 de septiembre, por las características técnicas del dispositivo hallado en la sala, incluida su dirección de identificación única, según el documento judicial.
El 5 de octubre, Alfozan ingresó a la sala y miró detrás del televisor donde estaba escondido el grabador, en una escena captada por una cámara que la empresa había instalado tras el hallazgo inicial.
Ese mismo día dejó una mochila sin vigilancia en otro sector de las oficinas. El personal de seguridad la abrió y encontró su billetera, su identificación y un segundo dispositivo de grabación similar al primero, de acuerdo con la denuncia.
La respuesta de OpenAI
OpenAI confirmó el hallazgo en un comunicado publicado en la red social X. “Descubrimos un sofisticado dispositivo de grabación escondido dentro de una de nuestras oficinas. Usamos nuestros modelos para entender el aparato y de dónde había salido, identificando que un empleado específico lo había colocado días antes”, señaló la empresa.
La compañía agregó que remitió el caso al FBI y que no tiene indicios de que Alfozan haya accedido o sustraído el peso de sus modelos de inteligencia artificial, el código fuente de sus productos o datos de clientes.
Entre el 30 de septiembre y el 9 de octubre, OpenAI restringió de manera progresiva los accesos de Alfozan a sistemas y espacios físicos, hasta suspenderlo y despedirlo el mismo día de su arresto, siempre en coordinación con la investigación federal.
Una prioridad de seguridad nacional
El director de Inteligencia Nacional de Estados Unidos, Jay Clayton, calificó el episodio como un asunto de seguridad nacional. “Esta situación grave confirma por qué ganar la carrera global de la superinteligencia es una prioridad de seguridad nacional”, afirmó.
Clayton encabeza desde principios de octubre la Fuerza de Superinteligencia, un grupo de trabajo que el gobierno de Donald Trump creó para coordinar la política del Estado frente al avance de la inteligencia artificial y la competencia tecnológica con otros países.
El director del FBI, Kash Patel, dijo que proteger la innovación estadounidense en inteligencia artificial es una de las prioridades más altas de la agencia en materia de contrainteligencia, y agradeció a los fiscales que lograron un arresto rápido.
El fiscal federal Craig Missakian, a cargo del distrito norte de California, sostuvo que su oficina “seguirá al frente de la protección de esa innovación estadounidense” frente a quienes buscan robar tecnología del sector.
OpenAI detalló que su equipo técnico analizó imágenes forenses del almacenamiento del dispositivo para entender qué datos había capturado y cómo habían cambiado con el tiempo, un trabajo que la empresa atribuyó al uso de sus propios modelos de inteligencia artificial.
El caso quedó a cargo de la sección de contrainteligencia y control de exportaciones de la División de Seguridad Nacional del Departamento de Justicia. Alfozan permanece detenido y la fiscalía no difundió información sobre un abogado que lo represente.
.

articles.title: Xbox Won't Survive Without New IP, Warns CEO Asha Sharma
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 13th 2026
Xbox Won't Survive Without New IP, Warns CEO Asha Sharma
Xbox CEO Asha Sharma told staff at an internal town hall last week that the division needs new IP to survive, according to transcripts obtained by Windows Central from multiple sources. Sharma apparently said Xbox will keep betting on its biggest franchises, though she also wants the studios to keep making new games, and she framed that second part as a matter of survival. Sharma did tell The New York Times earlier this month that Xbox is not for sale, so it seems the plan is a smaller Xbox that still takes some creative risks. Here's what she reportedly said:
We're backing our strongest franchises. I want our great games to become great global billion-dollar franchises. I would also like to see us continue to create enduring new IP. We will not survive if we only revive on the past. We have to find new ways, and courage, to have invention on new IP, that reaches new sets of audiences.
The comments arrive three months after Xbox announced it would cut around 3,200 jobs through FY27, with Double Fine and Compulsion Games going independent as part of the "reset." Ninja Theory staff have since reported layoffs as the Hellblade studio moves toward closure, and Obsidian has reportedly had several projects canceled. People were quick to point out how odd the message sounds, given that Double Fine and Compulsion, two studios that recently shipped new IP for Xbox, are no longer part of it. How many new games actually get greenlit is something readers can judge over the coming year.
Source:
				Windows Central			
	
	
	
		
	
		
17 Comments on Xbox Won't Survive Without New IP, Warns CEO Asha Sharma
Just look around, the best selling games are 1-6 person indie jobs and the really hard hitting AA and AAA titles mostly came from studios of industry veterans and fanatics of their craft.
Mid-life crisis strikes a few decades later and they take up cocaine, fast cars, golf, or build a gaming PC.
I only just now realized that the article is about XBOX Gaming Studios, and not the XBOX Console Division... I think? I honestly don't think there's any way to salvage the Gaming Studios.
Nice jacket. I'm not even being sarcastic.
It's a good green and says "Xbox", "Halo" and "military" without actually saying any of it.
Nice choice Asha.
Likely, they want to foster their own pseudo-indie teams that could quickly make a new IP on a budget, and just let it loose on the world. If it does half as well as say, Expedition 33 or Balatro or Hollow Knight or Schedule I, at 20 USD or less, then that would be an easy victory. At least, that seems to be the goal with Asha's previous statements on leaner teams and faster game development, combined with this new statement.
The "talent", as it turns out, was a one trick pony.
Would rather have a 100 low to mid budget genre agnostic games than 1 billion dollar CoD franchise.
Yeah thanks Captain Obvious, It's not like both of your competitors have been doing exactly this even on a lower-budget scale for a decade. Good thing you laid off most of the mid-tier developers who actually would have thrived in a lower-budget, less-pressured, highly creative role.
Guess those C-level executives bought themselves a few more years of bloated salaries. Now they get to spend the next 3 years preaching 'innovation' and 'portfolio diversification' to the board, completely ignoring the fact that these new IPs will suffer from the exact same thing that killed the old ones: a total lack of flawless execution and deep player trust from this management team.
Textbook definition of a clown showYou have to love Xboxs Incredible strategy: step 1, spend $69 billion on old IP. Step 2, fire all the mid-tier creative studios capable of making new IP. Step 3, warn everyone that the company won't survive without new IP. A masterclass in corporate geometry, truly coming full circle
Sony did the same when they began cancelling a number of live service projects as well as several games under the previous PlayStation head, and only kept projects that were close enough to a live release to just complete and see what happens, even the game turns out like Concord.
I'm not defending her beyond that though; the real results of her changes will need a year or more to be seen. As it is though, I'm more inclined to support the cuts because it's not like we had any major, worthwhile games out of most of those studios in the past few years.

articles.title: Shadow AI : faut-il interdire l'IA fantôme en entreprise ? Les experts de la cyber ne sont pas d'accord
articles.text:
ChatGPT ouvert en douce, des agents bricolés avec Copilot et d'autres : le Shadow AI, ou IA fantôme, s'installe dans les entreprises et crée la pagaille. Six experts nous ont expliqué comment le dompter, sans tous appeler à son interdiction.
Le Shadow AI, cette IA fantôme que les salariés utilisent en entreprise sans l'aval de leur service informatique, s'est imposé comme l'un des grands casse-têtes de la cybersécurité en 2026. Au fil de nos rencontres aux Assises de la cybersécurité à Monaco ces derniers jours, les spécialistes de Sekoia, Check Point, Illumio, Nomios et KnowBe4, ainsi que le responsable sécurité de SNCF Connect & Tech, ont décrit un phénomène bien plus vaste que le simple rapport sensible de la boîte copié-collé dans un chatbot. Comment répondre à ce phénomène ? Faut-il l'interdire ou l'encadrer ? Vous allez voir que les avis divergent.
Le Shadow AI, ce collègue invisible dont on préfère ne pas parler
Lorsque vous avez devant les yeux un rapport à synthétiser avant une réunion, quelques lignes de code à faire relire, ou un document trop long à résumer, le robot conversationnel de type Claude, Gemini ou ChatGPT est devenu l'allié de nombreux salariés, souvent sans demander l'avis de personne. Ce réflexe porte un nom, le Shadow AI, et Anthony Hervé, ingénieur avant-vente chez Illumio, nous en donne une définition. Il s'agit d'utiliser « des outils IA de manière générale, qui ne sont pas contrôlés, validés par les équipes IT de l'entreprise », au risque d'y partager des données sensibles. Plus de trois salariés sur dix utiliseraient déjà des assistants que leur direction informatique n'a jamais approuvés. Et chacun a son anecdote, car forcément, nous connaissons tous quelqu'un qui a collé le dernier rapport de sa boîte dans ChatGPT pour en tirer une synthèse express.
Ce scénario, François Deruty le connaît par cœur. Passé par l'ANSSI, le gendarme français de la cybersécurité, avant de prendre la direction des opérations de Sekoia, il nous explique le problème. Faute d'accompagnement, les salariés les moins à l'aise avec les nouvelles technologies découvrent souvent ces outils chez eux, ils y glissent des données de l'entreprise pour soigner un rapport, et « ils n'osent pas le dire ». Le danger tient en fait moins à l'outil qu'à ce qu'on lui confie. Par principe, le spécialiste se méfie de tout service externe, évoquant une évidente question de confiance, tant pour l'envoi du contenu que ce que les entreprises qui le traitent en font. Car une fois partis vers ces outils, les documents échappent à l'entreprise, qui ne sait plus très bien où ils sont stockés, ni qui peut y accéder.
Francis Bergey, responsable de la sécurité des systèmes d'information (RSSI) de SNCF Connect & Tech, que nous avons interrogé à l'issue de son atelier avec AWS à Monaco, pointe le piège des offres gratuites. « Dans les conditions générales, il y a écrit que ce que vous allez envoyer au LLM (Ndlr : par exemple GPT-4o, Claude 5 Sonnet ou autres) va servir à entraîner la génération d'après. » Un document interne peut ainsi finir dans le modèle dont profitent tous les autres utilisateurs. La frontière se brouille encore avec l'abonnement Mistral payé à titre personnel puis utilisé pour le travail. « La difficulté qu'on peut avoir, c'est dans l'usage pro/perso », explique le technicien.
IA fantôme : la menace se cache aussi dans les outils officiels
Puisqu'on parle de fantôme, celui-ci ne rôde pas toujours là où on l'attend. Le directeur technique France de Check Point, Adrien Merveille, rappelle qu'un logiciel acheté en bonne et due forme peut embarquer de l'IA sans que l'entreprise le sache, jusqu'à découvrir, en grattant un peu, que « derrière, c'est du DeepSeek qui tourne ». Voilà qui est fâcheux pour les nombreuses sociétés qui bannissent les modèles chinois. « On ne peut pas contrôler ce qu'on ne voit pas », insiste celui qui enchaîne les rendez-vous avec des entreprises privées de toute visibilité sur leurs propres usages de l'IA.
Chez Nomios, intégrateur de solutions de sécurité de 500 salariés, Eric Bohec a mesuré la vitesse du phénomène sur ses propres troupes, pourtant encadrées. « On a formé 500 personnes, et pourtant dans les trois semaines, il y avait 800 agents » IA. Ces assistants justement, n'importe quel salarié peut désormais les créer avec des outils fournis par l'entreprise, comme Copilot, l'assistant IA de Microsoft, et les faire agir sous sa propre identité. Pour le directeur technique, laisser chacun bricoler dans son coin, « c'est créer autant d'entrepreneurs que vous avez d'employés et à la fin autant de process dans votre boîte ».
Parlons des privilèges aussi, au sens informatique du terme. Car le vrai danger surgit quand ces agents IA reçoivent des droits sur des applications internes. Eric Bohec imagine un commercial qui, au volant, dicte à son assistant de créer une commande dans Salesforce, son logiciel de gestion client. C'est pratique, évidemment, jusqu'à la consigne mal comprise qui déclenche une action non désirée, voire efface des données clients. « Le risque est juste gigantesque. » Anthony Hervé évoque le développeur pressé qui branche un modèle non validé sur le système d'information, sans voir que « lui, il est le pont vers l'extérieur ». Car avec ces interconnexions, prévient François Deruty, « tu peux avoir un chemin jusqu'à tes données critiques ».
Ce pont, les pirates savent aussi l'emprunter. Anthony Hervé précise que chaque outil branché sans contrôle multiplie les portes d'entrée dans l'entreprise. Un pirate qui met la main sur un agent IA décroche un passe-partout, puisque cet assistant, pour être utile, est relié à tout, souvent sans garde-fou parce qu'on l'a déployé trop vite. Là où il fallait autrefois un groupe de pirates chevronnés, l'IA change la donne, en ce qu'il « suffit d'une seule personne vraiment motivée ».
Interdire ou encadrer l’IA fantôme, le grand débat
Faut-il tout simplement interdire le Shadow AI ? Eric Bohec ne tergiverse pas sur le cas le plus courant, celui du salarié qui confie des données de l'entreprise à un chatbot grand public, « ça, c'est à interdire purement et simplement ». Selon lui, la plupart des entreprises disposent déjà d'un proxy, un poste de contrôle par lequel transite la navigation internet des salariés. Il suffit d'y activer la surveillance des IA publiques pour voir, et bloquer, ces usages. Anthony Hervé balaie pourtant l'idée, pour lui, c'est « impossible. » Car le salarié privé d'IA, qui voit ses collègues ou ses amis en profiter, passera par son téléphone ou un Wi-Fi public, voire par son compte personnel, ce qui est encore pire. Interdire, prévient-il, ne fera que créer de la frustration, et engendrera ainsi des comportements toujours plus critiques.
Florian Malecki, directeur Europe du Sud de KnowBe4, fait la comparaison avec une ère plus ancienne, celle du Shadow IT, quand des services entiers contournaient la direction informatique (DSI), puis celle de l'arrivée des smartphones personnels au bureau. Son avis est que « bloquer, ce n'est pas la bonne réponse, les gens trouveront toujours un moyen de l'utiliser dans tous les cas et de le ramener au monde du travail ». Francis Bergey, dont les équipes repèrent pourtant ces usages sur le réseau et les postes de travail, et qui a déjà vu des collègues utiliser des outils non validés, ne dit pas autre chose, même s'il est concède que tout ça, « c'est hyper dur de contrôler. »
Couper l'accès aux chatbots publics ne règle pas tout. Eric Bohec s'attaque surtout à l'IA fantôme interne, donc aux agents que les salariés créent eux-mêmes sur les outils de l'entreprise. Pour garder ces agents à l’œil, il empile trois garde-fous, à commencer par une passerelle de sécurité, sorte de douanier qui lit chaque demande avant qu’elle n’atteigne l’agent et la bloque si elle sort des clous. Ensuite, un journal de bord qui enregistre tout (qui a sollicité l'IA, avec quelle demande, via quel modèle). En cas de pépin ou d'audit, l'entreprise peut ainsi retracer et prouver ce que l'agent a réellement fait. Enfin, un humain garde le dernier mot sur les actions sensibles. Le commercial qui, en sortant d'un rendez-vous, demande à son agent de créer une commande ne la voit pas partir directement : elle arrive d'abord chez l'assistante commerciale, qui la valide, ou la bloque si l'agent, ayant mal compris, réclame d'effacer des comptes clients. « La première chose, c'est de rendre visible l'action de l'IA », assure Eric Bohec.
Il y a une piste qui rallie presque tout le monde, à savoir proposer mieux que le fantôme. Francis Bergey aimerait des outils internes qui « soient les meilleurs du marché pour que les gens se disent, pourquoi j'irais chercher ailleurs ? ». Car « le Shadow AI peut naître du fait que l'entreprise n'offre pas un catalogue de services IA », souligne Anthony Hervé, partisan d'une méthode qui consiste à « éduquer, communiquer, former ». Chez Sekoia, il a fallu six mois pour rédiger une doctrine d'usage interne. Florian Malecki préconise, lui, une charte simple, partant du principe qu'à la fin, « il y aura toujours des erreurs. » Adrien Merveille, enfin, l'avoue : « Je ne sais pas où est le security by design dans l'ère de l'IA, honnêtement. » Après le Shadow IT et l’arrivée des téléphones personnels au bureau, l’histoire se répète, mais à la vitesse de l’IA. Dans cette course, l’entreprise qui tarde à proposer ses propres outils risque surtout de voir ses salariés trouver les leurs. Pour le meilleur et pour le pire.

articles.title: God of War Laufey Collector Box Costs £129.99, Game Not Included
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 13th 2026
God of War Laufey Collector Box Costs £129.99, Game Not Included
Sony has opened pre-orders for the God of War Laufey Collector Box on its UK PlayStation Store, priced at £129.99. Despite the name, the box does not include the game in any form, and the store page states plainly that God of War Laufey is sold separately. Buyers instead get a light-up resin statue of Faye, a 51-card Oracle Deck with custom illustrations on every card, and a mini artbook of concept art put together by the development team. Orders are capped at one per customer, and the listing carries a February 16, 2027 date, the same day the game launches on PlayStation 5.
The Faye-led spin-off was first tipped back in April, and Santa Monica Studio confirmed the February release at San Diego Comic-Con in July. The Standard Edition sells for $69.99 and the Digital Deluxe Edition for $79.99, and there is no word of a traditional collector's edition that bundles the game. That is quite a change from God of War Ragnarök, whose $199.99 Collector's Edition came with access to the game on both PS4 and PS5. Of course, Sony isn't alone here, since Rockstar's $399.99 Vice City Collection box for GTA 6 also leaves the game out. It looks like players who want both the statue and the game will have to buy them separately.
Sources:
				PlayStation UK on X, 				PlayStation Store UK

$170 for a mini artbook, a cheap statue, and a deck of cards, at minimum for that price it should include a full sized artbook, larger high quality statue, and the game on disk in a steelbook case.
For me personally, these "goodiebags" are the clearest indication that the title is intended to be multiplatform at some point so YAAY!

articles.title: Attackers Heat French Supermarket Fridges Up to 50°C by Hijacking Danfoss Controllers
articles.text:
Attackers took remote control of fridges and freezers at hundreds of French supermarkets on the night of October 11 and warmed them, forcing stores to throw food away, several retail chains said.
The attackers reached them through the controller that runs all of a store's fridges and freezers, a device made by Danish company Danfoss that maintenance firms can manage remotely. Les Mousquetaires, which owns the Intermarché chain, said its fridges and freezers were put into defrost and heated to as much as 50°C.
CERT-FR, the French government's computer emergency response team, said in an alert published in French on October 12 that it is aware of numerous compromises affecting two Danfoss controller series, the AK-SM and the AK-SC. It told operators to disconnect the controllers or filter access to them.
CERT-FR is part of ANSSI, France's national cybersecurity agency. ANSSI's head, Vincent Strubel, called it urgent to take the two series off the internet or filter access very tightly, AFP reported.
Neither French authorities nor Danfoss has so far said who carried out the attack or how the attackers got into the controllers. Danfoss said most of the units hit were older models that it no longer updates.
Which Chains Were Hit
The chains gave their own figures to AFP, Reuters and broadcaster RTL. Each counts the stores the attack reached.
| Retailer | Stores Reported Hit | Source | 
|---|---|---|
| Intermarché and Netto (Les Mousquetaires) | At least 300 across both brands, per AFP. About 150 stores, per Reuters | Company statements, October 12 | 
| Coopérative U | 80 of 2,000 | Chief executive Dominique Schelcher, on RTL, October 13 | 
| Carrefour | 80 supermarkets | Company statements to AFP and Reuters, October 12 | 
| Monoprix | About 30 | Company statement to AFP, October 12 | 
| E.Leclerc | Several stores | Company statement to AFP, October 12 | 
A store on that list did not always lose its stock. Schelcher told RTL that the cold chain held in most of the 80 Coopérative U stores hit, and that only a minority could not react fast enough and lost goods, according to AFP. He praised the quick reaction of store staff and refrigeration contractors.
Intermarché, by contrast, said its affected stores had to throw away all the products concerned.
Thierry Cotillard, who heads Les Mousquetaires, told broadcaster BFMTV he expected losses of tens of millions of euros across France, according to Reuters.
In its statements on October 12, Danfoss gave no figure for how many systems were hit. It told Reuters it was "aware of incidents in France affecting a limited number of refrigeration management systems."
Which Controllers, and Whether They Can Be Patched
Danfoss told AFP that most of the units hit were older products that no longer get software or security updates, and it named two: the AK-SM 800 and the AK-SC 355.
Danfoss declared the AK-SM 800 end-of-life in May 2021 and phased out the AK-SC 355 in 2016. In an October 2025 newsletter, it said it would end all services for such older products and urged customers to plan replacements.
Some units of the current model, the AK-SM 800A, were also hit. Those were running outdated firmware, according to Danfoss's statement to trade publication Cooling Post, which did not name the versions.
| Controller | Status, According to Danfoss | Advice From CERT-FR and Danfoss | 
|---|---|---|
| AK-SM 800 | End of life since May 2021. No software or security updates | Disconnect it or filter access. Danfoss urges replacement | 
| AK-SC 355 | Phased out in 2016. No software or security updates | Disconnect it or filter access. Danfoss urges replacement | 
| AK-SM 800A | Current model. Package 5.3.x, dated October 2026, was the latest listed on October 13 | Disconnect it or filter access. Danfoss advises keeping firmware up to date | 
As of October 13, Danfoss's security advisories page listed no advisory about the attack or about either older model.
What Operators Should Do
CERT-FR's first instruction covers every AK-SM and AK-SC controller: disconnect it or filter access to it. Exposing a management interface to the internet goes against good practice, the alert says.
Where remote administration cannot be avoided, limiting access to trusted IP addresses is a first, temporary step. Beyond that, the alert advises following CERT-FR's hardening recommendations, which were written for the energy and water sector.
Where a controller may have been compromised, the alert lists six steps, in this order:
- Limit network access to the controllers to service providers only.
- Do a factory reset.
- Apply all available security fixes.
- Change the device's secrets, such as passwords.
- Check the existing accounts.
- Reconfigure the device completely.
Danfoss no longer issues fixes for the AK-SM 800 and the AK-SC 355, so the third step offers their owners no new fix.
For the AK-SM 800A, the latest software package Danfoss listed on October 13 was 5.3.x. A system on version 3.x should move to 4.x first, and a controller cannot be downgraded once it runs 5.3.x, according to the package's readme.
Starting with version 4.0, a setting called Strict Session Control is enabled by default and makes HTTPS mandatory. Danfoss's pages do not say whether the 5.3.x package was released in response to the attack.
Danfoss told Cooling Post it was working with customers on "firmware updates where available, stronger network protections and removing direct internet exposure where applicable."
Its general security guidance, published in French, also tells operators to keep controllers unreachable from the internet, change default passwords when a system is installed, and require remote users to log in through a single managed entry point.
CERT-FR had published no indicators of compromise as of October 13, so operators have no official signs to check for.
Coopérative U's stores do not buy directly from Danfoss. They are customers of refrigeration contractors that supply them with the Danfoss system, Schelcher said.
How the Attackers Got In Is Not Established
As of October 13, CERT-FR had named no vulnerability, no firmware version, and no way in. Its alert warns against exposing management interfaces to the internet without saying that was the route.
A person close to French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu told AFP that ANSSI had identified a vulnerability in software supplied by a Danish company and had contacted the vendor. No CVE was named, and the statement does not say the vulnerability was used in the attack.
E.Leclerc told AFP that a cyberattack had affected one of its refrigeration equipment suppliers, with effects on cold equipment in several of its stores. The supplier was not named.
Danfoss issued fixes for three flaws in the newer AK-SM 800A in 2025. Neither French authorities nor Danfoss has linked them to this attack.
CVE-2025-41450 is an authentication bypass, a way past the login, in versions before 4.2. CVE-2025-41451 is a command injection flaw that could lead to remote code execution, and CVE-2025-41452 could allow a denial-of-service attack. Both need a login and were fixed in version 4.3.1.
Researchers at Claroty described the three flaws in August, said they could be combined into attack chains, and reported finding thousands of AK-SM 800A management interfaces reachable from the internet. Their tests of the flaws were laboratory work on the newer model. The report describes no attacks and does not mention the two older models.
Danfoss's October 2025 newsletter records earlier attacks on the AK-SM 800: 16 Russian supermarkets using the model were targeted in 2022, and 40 Israeli stores were hacked the same year. All 40 lacked proper firewall or VPN protection, and the newsletter names no vulnerability in either case.
The Inquiry and Reports From Other Countries
The Paris prosecutor's office has opened an inquiry on its own initiative, it told AFP. Its cybercrime section leads the inquiry, which is assigned to the anti-cybercrime office known as OFAC.
The inquiry is to count the victims and establish the link between the attack and the damage they reported, which includes lost food and equipment that began to catch fire.
ANSSI is in contact with cybersecurity agencies in other European countries because those countries may be affected, the person close to the Prime Minister said.
Félix Aimé, a senior threat intelligence analyst at Sekoia, told Reuters that Spain, Portugal, Poland, Germany and Belgium had also been affected. Reuters gave no details on those cases.

Bon plan – La barre de son Sennheiser Ambeo Soundbar Mini à 499,00 € (-19%)
La barre de son Sennheiser Ambeo Soundbar Mini passe sous les 500 € chez Son-Video.com soit une baisse d'environ 19% sur le prix habituellement constaté.
Habitué aux barres de son de grande taille, Sennheiser s’essaie au marché des barres de son compactes avec l’Ambeo Soundbar Mini. Mais ne vous laissez pas abuser par sa petite taille, car elle cache un potentiel digne de celui des meilleures barres de son du marché.

Points forts
- Virtualisation surround Ambeo toujours aussi bluffante.
- Rendu sonore clair, équilibré et précis.
- Très belle reproduction des voix/dialogues.
- Calibration acoustique efficace.
- Compatible avec de nombreux formats sonores 3D (Dolby Atmos, DTS:X, MPEG-H, 360 Reality Audio).
- Qualité de fabrication exemplaire.
Points faibles

Sennheiser n’en finit plus de nous étonner avec ses barres de son. Malgré sa taille contenue, l’Ambeo Soundbar Mini surprend par son habileté à reproduire une scène sonore large et très immersive. Elle jouit d’un rendu sonore précis et maîtrisé qui lui permet d’être aussi à l’aise sur les contenus musicaux que cinématographiques. Sa grande polyvalence et le nombre foisonnant de fonctionnalités connectées sont également de sérieux atouts qui feraient presque oublier la pauvreté de la connectique embarquée. Au bout du compte, l’Ambeo Soundbar Mini n’a pas à rougir des barres de son plus imposantes et s’impose comme la reine de barres de son compactes.

articles.title: Puces IA : Nvidia perd rapidement du terrain en Chine face à un Huawei conquérant
articles.text:
Le marché chinois des puces IA est important pour NVIDIA. Mais avec les contraintes imposées par Washington, la firme de Jensen Huang recule logiquement en 2026.
Faut-il ou non laisser la Chine acheter les puissants GPU de NVIDIA, destinés à entraîner les modèles d'IA ? Pour Jensen Huang, patron de NVIDIA, la réponse a toujours été évidemment oui, le milliardaire arguant que couper l'accès à la Chine ne ferait que la rendre plus indépendante, avec le développement de solutions alternatives locales. Et les derniers chiffres que l'on a sur les ventes semblent confirmer en partie sa prédiction.
La part de marché de NVIDIA dans les accélérateurs IA en Chine chute fortement en un an
Les contraintes géopolitiques issues de la rivalité entre la Chine et les États-Unis rendent les affaires de NVIDIA dans l'empire du Milieu toujours plus compliquée. Ce qui a aussi un impact sur ses ventes d'accélérateurs IA dans ce pays, comme nous le montrent les chiffres d'IDC, rapportés par Reuters.
Les ventes de puces IA NVIDIA en Chine ont ainsi, durant le premier semestre 2026, reculé de 44% par rapport à la même période l'an dernier. Résultat, sa part de marché dans le pays pour ce type de produit a réculé à 36%.
Huawei est de son côté en plein essor
De l'autre côté, par contre, c'est une ascension fulgurante que l'on peut observer pour l'entreprise locale la plus susceptible de remplacer un jour NVIDIA en Chine : Huawei. Le géant, qui a encore présenté en septembre dernier de nouvelles puces IA promettant une hausse sensible de puissance, voit en effet sa part de marché se rapprocher de NVIDIA, pour s'établir sur les six premiers mois de 2026 à 28%.
En parallèle, on peut observer que les ventes de GPU parmi les accélérateurs IA ont reculé de 26%, pour atteindre 991 000 unités vendues lors de la période observée. Les accélérateurs IA qui ne sont pas des GPU se sont ainsi plus vendus, grâce à une croissance de 80% sur un an, représentant 1,016 million d'unités écoulés.
Huawei, T-Head (Alibaba), Kunlunxin (Baidu) et Cambricon ont représenté 95% des ventes de ces accélérateurs IA non-GPU. Un format qui aurait été adopté en Chine, selon IDC, par les administrations publiques, les géants du Web et les opérateurs des télécoms. Alors, le découplage USA-Chine est-il en marche ?

articles.title: Ucrania golpeó tres centros de datos de Yandex y desató apagones digitales en toda Rusia
articles.text:
Drones ucranianos destruyeron o dejaron fuera de servicio tres centros de datos de la empresa rusa Yandex entre el 8 y el 11 de octubre, un ataque que provocó fallas en bancos, aplicaciones de reparto, taxis y plataformas de streaming en buena parte de Rusia, según confirmaron la compañía y medios locales.
La primera ofensiva alcanzó el centro de Sasovo, en la región de Riazán, en la madrugada del 8 de octubre. El ataque provocó un incendio y obligó a suspender por completo las operaciones del predio, que alberga dos de las tres supercomputadoras que Yandex usa para entrenar sus modelos de inteligencia artificial.
Un segundo ataque, el 9 de octubre, dañó parte de la infraestructura del centro de Kaluga, al suroeste de Moscú, uno de los más grandes del país. Nueve personas resultaron heridas en la zona, aunque las autoridades regionales no vincularon de forma directa las lesiones con las instalaciones de Yandex.
El tercer golpe llegó el fin de semana sobre el centro de Vladimir, al este de la capital rusa. Allí funcionaba Galushkin, otra supercomputadora de la empresa que ocupaba el puesto 134 del ranking mundial Top500 con una capacidad de 20,64 petaflops. Unos 1.600 usuarios quedaron sin electricidad en la zona, según sus autoridades locales.
Un monopolio que lo controla casi todo
Yandex suele compararse con Google por el tamaño de su ecosistema: un buscador con cerca del 70% del mercado ruso, según datos citados por Ars Technica, además de mapas, correo electrónico, pagos, taxis y reparto de comida bajo una misma marca. Su servicio de nube, Yandex Cloud, contaba con más de 64.000 clientes empresariales a mediados de 2026.
La aplicación Yandex Go, que combina las funciones de Uber y de un servicio de reparto como DoorDash, es un ejemplo del peso cotidiano de la empresa: para millones de rusos resultó, de un día para el otro, más difícil pedir un taxi o encargar comida.
Los cortes alcanzaron bancos digitales, supermercados, cadenas de comida rápida y una cadena de electrodomésticos que dependen de esa infraestructura, de acuerdo con el diario independiente The Moscow Times. También se reportaron fallas fuera de Rusia, en Kazajistán, Kirguistán y Armenia.
Yandex admitió que reponer el equipamiento dañado podría demorar hasta seis meses, según una fuente citada por el diario ruso Kommersant.
Una guerra que empezó Moscú
Rusia había lanzado en septiembre una campaña de ataques contra centros de datos y redes de telefonía móvil ucranianas, parte de una ofensiva más amplia con misiles y drones que también alcanzó la red eléctrica, nudos de transporte y edificios residenciales, según relató Ars Technica.
El presidente ucraniano Volodymyr Zelensky presentó los ataques como una respuesta simétrica a los bombardeos rusos contra centros de datos en Kiev ocurridos en septiembre. “Siempre respondemos de la misma manera. Ustedes saben que ellos atacan y siguen atacando nuestros centros de datos”, dijo ante la prensa, según citó Al Jazeera.
Según el medio especializado The Record, Rusia había atacado antes al menos seis centros de datos ucranianos, entre ellos los operados por las firmas MiroHost, Parkovy y Data Group, además de infraestructura de las operadoras Kyivstar y Ukrtelecom. Un bombardeo del 23 de septiembre dejó sin conexión fija a unos 100.000 hogares en la región de Kiev.
A diferencia de Rusia, la red ucraniana está más descentralizada y recibe apoyo de compañías extranjeras: Amazon Web Services aloja más de 15 petabytes de datos de más de 60 organismos del gobierno ucraniano, entre ellos la energética DTEK, según reportó Ars Technica.
Blogueros militares rusos cercanos al Kremlin advirtieron que la ley de “internet soberano”, sancionada en 2019, complica que compañías como Yandex construyan respaldos fuera del país en plena guerra, de acuerdo con traducciones difundidas por el investigador independiente conocido como ChrisO_wiki.
Una disputa sobre los bots
Zelensky sostuvo además que los ataques habían reducido la actividad de cuentas rusas vinculadas a operaciones de desinformación, incluidas publicaciones de apoyo al movimiento estadounidense MAGA y al partido alemán AfD.
Pero la cadena BBC consultó a investigadores especializados que no hallaron pruebas de ese freno. El grupo dTeam, que monitorea redes de bots prorrusas, afirmó que no detectó “ningún cambio de tráfico” en las cuentas rusas conocidas. La oficina de Zelensky explicó luego que el mandatario se refería al clima general en las redes sociales y no a una caída medible en la actividad de los bots, según precisó la propia cadena británica.
El ministro ruso de Desarrollo Digital, Maksut Shadayev, confirmó que su cartera trabaja junto al Ministerio de Defensa para reforzar la protección del resto de los centros de datos del país, mientras persisten fallas parciales en los servicios de Yandex.

articles.title: Nvidia RTX Spark challenges Dell Pro Max 18 Plus for local AI crown
articles.text:
Fastest AI laptop ever built keeps its crown for now as Nvidia unleashes RTX mobile workstations — $18,600 Dell Pro Max 18 Plus laptop doubled in price in 14 months, and it could be unseated within days
Dell's fastest AI laptop faces its biggest challenge in the coming days
- Dell Pro Max 18 Plus leads current local AI rankings, yet Nvidia's launch could unsettle results
- RTX Spark offers 128 GB shared memory for larger locally run models
- Spark's 300 GB/s bandwidth trails Dell's graphics memory at 896 GB/s
The Dell Pro Max 18 Plus still holds the title of fastest AI laptop, topping local AI rankings ahead of every other machine tested.
Its RTX PRO 5000 chip reached 185.1 tokens/s on the Phi model, 140.5 tokens/s on Mistral, and 119.7 tokens/s on Llama 3.
However this lead faces a test on October 16 2026, when Nvidia's RTX Spark laptops go on sale from several manufacturers, with preorders already open.
RTX Spark arrival
Microsoft is expected to field the Surface Laptop Ultra from $2,599, while Dell is bringing the XPS 16 Creator Edition from $3,799.99.
Asus, HP, Lenovo and MSI are also launch partners, while Acer and Gigabyte are expected to add models later.
Nvidia rates RTX Spark at up to 1 petaflop of FP4 AI performance, with 6,144 CUDA cores and up to 128 GB of shared memory.
The 1 petaflop figure covers only FP4 calculations that exploit sparsity, an upper limit that everyday workloads may not reach.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
The company also claims the chip can run large language models of about 120 billion parameters locally, with a context window of one million tokens.
That is slightly above the 109 billion parameters that the Dell Pro Max 18 Plus can reportedly handle locally.
This does not automatically mean that RTX Spark will outperform Dell's workstation in AI workloads, as model capacity alone does not determine inference speed.
The price Dell buyers paid for the lead
The Pro Max 18 Plus offers Core Ultra 5, 7, or 9 processors and RTX PRO 1000 to 5000 graphics, with prices starting at $3,488.
Dell's top configuration, equipped with an RTX PRO 5000, 128 GB of memory and two 1 TB drives, cost $9,245.52 when the laptop launched.
A similar configuration later appeared at roughly $14,000, while the laptop now sells for almost $18,600, double its launch price after 14 months.
The top model is built around the Intel Core Ultra 9 285HX processor with 24 cores, a 5.5 GHz boost clock and a 55 W rating.
Its RTX PRO 5000 graphics chip has 24 GB of GDDR7, a 175 W power ceiling and a graphics clock of 1,807 MHz.
Memory comes from a single 128 GB CAMM2 module running at 6,400 MT/s, while storage consists of two 1 TB Gen5 SSDs configured in RAID 0.
The 18-inch QHD+ display runs at 2560 × 1600 and 120 Hz, covers 100% of the DCI-P3 colour space and contributes to a minimum chassis weight of 7.17 lb.
Nvidia's case for displacing Dell rests partly on RTX Spark's shared memory, which can accommodate AI models exceeding Dell's 24 GB graphics capacity.
However, Spark's shared memory delivers about 300 GB/s of bandwidth, compared with 896 GB/s for Dell's RTX PRO 5000. Spark also has 6,144 CUDA cores, fewer than Dell's 10,496
To overtake Dell, an RTX Spark laptop must beat its token-generation rates for Phi, Mistral and Llama 3 under the same UL Procyon tests.
Matching those results while consuming 45 W to 80 W of chip power could also improve battery endurance beyond Dell's recorded three hours and 39 minutes.
Via StorageReview
