articles.title: Cisco's OCP message: The network is now AI's critical path, and openness is the price of admission - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Cisco’s OCP message: The network is now AI’s critical path, and openness is the price of admission
For most of its history, Cisco Systems Inc. won by building vertically integrated network products and asking customers to buy all of it. The company did very well with that model. Security, meanwhile, was something Cisco sold as a separate product line rather than something that was inherent to its infrastructure. Patching a core switch meant scheduling a maintenance window, crossing your fingers and hoping nothing broke.
Under Chief Product Officer Jeetu Patel, Cisco has moved away from that model and embraced openness. That’s why I found Cisco’s announcements at this week’s Open Compute Project Global Summit in San Jose more interesting for what they reveal about the company than for the products themselves.
As Mike Wheatley outlined in his SiliconANGLE post, Cisco rolled out a new pluggable optics form factor with Nvidia Corp., shipped its first Silicon One G300 systems, introduced the G302 top-of-rack chip and a new out-of-band management platform, and brought its Live Protect runtime security capability to SONiC. His post detailed the announcements, but it’s worth a deeper look at why these matter for artificial intelligence and what they say about a Cisco trying to be both open and secure, neither of which were strengths before Patel.
The network is now in the critical path of AI
During the event’s pre-briefing, Cisco Senior Vice President of Engineering Will Eatherton discussed the problem the company is trying to solve. A few years ago, a large training run used hundreds of graphics processing units. Today, the largest clusters use hundreds of thousands of GPUs. Cisco cited Epoch AI data showing that projects that once fit in one or two buildings now span campuses, metros and regions, largely because that’s where power and real estate are available.
This changes the role of the network. In a traditional data center interconnect, the wide-area network carries many small, independent flows, and a network hiccup affects a single application or user. In large-scale deployments, the network needs to “scale-across” and carry a small number of massive, synchronized flows between accelerators working on the same job.
As Rakesh Chopra, Cisco Fellow and senior vice president of silicon and systems architecture, explained on the call, scale-across puts the long-haul network “directly in line with the workload performance.” If a link slows down, GPUs sit idle, and idle GPUs are the most expensive waste in information technology today.
That’s the context for Cisco’s OCP news. The Ultra-Dense Small Form Factor Pluggable, or USFP (pictured), is the first pluggable module designed for 400-gigabit-per-lane signaling, delivering up to 12.8 Tbps and about four times the bandwidth density of today’s leading modules. The key word is pluggable.
Cisco’s optics team made a fair point on the call: the competing XPO approach requires liquid cooling, which no optic in the industry needs today, and it creates real headaches when handling, replacing and validating modules. Keeping the operational model familiar while doubling the lane rate is the kind of pragmatic engineering that speeds adoption.
Equally important, USFP is being standardized as a multisource agreement with TE Connectivity and Amphenol. Optics is one of the highest cost and supply-chain constraints in AI buildouts, and a multivendor spec should drive higher volumes, greater competition,and lower prices.
Open at every layer is a big shift for Cisco
Cisco used the phrase “open at every layer of the stack” throughout the briefing, and Eatherton was clear that this “is not just a SONiC story.” That spans P4 programmability at the chip level, Nvidia Reference Architecture compliance in systems, OpenZR+ in optics, a choice of SONiC, FBOSS, a custom NOS, NX-OS, or IOS XR, third-party controllers, and the CNCF-governed Cilium ecosystem at the Kubernetes layer.
Eatherton called SONiC a first-class network operating system at Cisco and admitted that is “unusual for Cisco in the context of our 20- or 30-year history.” SONiC was once viewed within Cisco circles as a threat, a way for hyperscalers to commoditize switching. Now Cisco offers community builds, custom builds using its software development kit, and a turnkey Cisco-validated version under the Nexus One controller. Though this may seem inconsistent with Cisco’s past strategy, it aligns with Patel’s commitment to make Cisco unrecognizable from what it was two years ago.
The openness also extends to Cisco. Intelligent Collective Networking, the G300 capability that detects remote congestion and link failures and signals back to the ingress leaf in hardware time, is being standardized by the Internet Engineering Task Force rather than kept proprietary. Five years ago, I’m not sure Cisco would have given away something it considers a competitive advantage.
Why the change? Because the customers driving AI infrastructure spending will not accept lock-in. Hyperscalers have built their own operating systems and controllers, and the more mature neoclouds are now closely examining SONiC. Cisco is betting it can win on silicon, optics, systems engineering and support while letting customers choose what runs on top. Microsoft running Silicon One P200 systems in production and Alibaba deploying its in-house router on the P200 at massive scale suggest that bet is paying off.
Being open doesn’t hurt Cisco; it expands its addressable market. A Cisco that requires its full stack can sell only to customers that want it. A Cisco that is open at every layer can sell silicon to one customer, optics to another, and validated SONiC to a third.
Security that keeps the network running
The announcement I believe is most underappreciated is Live Protect for Cisco SONiC. Cisco cited data showing that the mean time to exploit a vulnerability has dropped from about nine months to roughly 10 hours. Eatherton noted that attackers now feed newly published CVEs into large language models and attempt exploits within hours.
That creates an impossible situation for AI network operators. Patching a switch typically requires a reboot, and rebooting a switch in a fabric running a multiweek training job across thousands of GPUs is not something anyone wants to do on short notice. So operators either risk an outage or a breach.
Live Protect addresses this by applying a “shield,” a compensating control, to the live system at the kernel level without downtime or rebooting. The switch is protected immediately, and the patch can be applied during a planned window. Cisco has had this capability in NX-OS for about a year and is bringing it to Cisco-validated SONiC on Nexus One, with availability targeted for the second quarter of 2027.
There are two important aspects to this. First, it reflects Cisco’s move to build security into the infrastructure rather than bolt it on, a shift the company has long discussed but often struggled to deliver, and now appears to be delivering. Second, it brings Cisco’s security engineering to an open operating system.
One criticism of SONiC has been its lack of enterprise-grade security and support, and closing that gap makes SONiC viable beyond the largest hyperscalers. With line-rate, quantum-resilient encryption built into the P200, Cisco now has a security story for AI infrastructure it simply didn’t have a few years ago.
Final thoughts
AI infrastructure is being built under conditions that punish both lock-in and downtime. Cisco’s OCP announcements address both issues and show that the company understands the AI market won’t be won the way the enterprise campus was.
For infrastructure leaders building AI capacity, my advice is to evaluate the network on job completion time and GPU utilization, not port speeds alone; to require open interfaces at the operating system and controller layers so you keep your options; and to ask every vendor how it will protect production fabrics during the hours between a CVE disclosure and a maintenance window.
Zeus Kerravala is a principal analyst at ZK Research, a division of Kerravala Consulting. He wrote this article for SiliconANGLE.

articles.title: Governo autoriza bloqueio de celulares em presídios sem ordem judicial • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Governo autoriza bloqueio de celulares em presídios sem ordem judicial
Decreto permite interromper sinais de comunicação em áreas delimitadas e restringir aparelhos pelo IMEI.
O Governo Federal publicou nesta terça-feira (13/10) um decreto que permite bloquear celulares em presídios sem uma ordem judicial. A medida prevê a cooperação entre União, estados, Distrito Federal e Anatel para acelerar o bloqueio de celulares e de outros meios de comunicação usados ilegalmente.
O programa, assinado pelo presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), já está valendo e vai atuar em duas frentes: restringir aparelhos identificados individualmente e interromper sinais de radiocomunicação em perímetros de segurança ao redor das unidades prisionais. A segunda opção depende de equipamentos bloqueadores e deverá seguir as condições técnicas definidas pela Agência Nacional de Telecomunicações.
As administrações penitenciárias estaduais e distrital serão responsáveis por identificar os casos e encaminhar informações técnicas. Os pedidos serão enviados por uma plataforma digital do Ministério da Justiça e Segurança Pública, integrada ao Sistema Nacional de Informações Penais (Sisdepen).
Segundo o Art. 6º do decreto, quando um celular for identificado individualmente, a solicitação será encaminhada ao fluxo do Banco Nacional de Celulares com Restrição, com o código IMEI do aparelho. Nos casos que envolvam bloqueio de sinais em áreas delimitadas, as informações serão direcionadas à Anatel.
As autoridades penitenciárias poderão solicitar o bloqueio de celulares à Anatel sem prever a apresentação de uma ordem judicial como requisito. Pelo procedimento, a autoridade deve elaborar um informe técnico e encaminhá-la à Anatel ou ao sistema nacional de restrição de celulares, conforme o tipo de bloqueio.
O decreto também cria o Cadastro Nacional de Perímetros de Segurança Penitenciária. Os estados e o Distrito Federal que aderirem ao programa deverão registrar as coordenadas das áreas de segurança de cada unidade, além de informações sobre o entorno, incluindo núcleos habitacionais e equipamentos públicos próximos.
Essa exigência busca evitar que os bloqueios prejudiquem os serviços de telecomunicações nas áreas vizinhas aos presídios. A Anatel terá acesso ao cadastro para planejar, coordenar e fiscalizar o uso dos bloqueadores de sinais.
O texto prevê ainda mecanismos para revisar bloqueios feitos por engano. Caso seja comprovado erro na identificação de um aparelho ou que não houve uso irregular dentro do presídio, o procedimento de cooperação deverá permitir a correção ou a retirada da restrição.
A plataforma digital que centralizará os pedidos deve ficar disponível em até 180 dias após a publicação do decreto. Até lá, os órgãos poderão utilizar os sistemas existentes e encaminhar determinadas solicitações diretamente à Anatel, com comunicação simultânea ao Ministério da Justiça.
A medida se soma a outra iniciativa para combater o uso ilegal de celulares em presídios. Em junho, a Anatel firmou uma parceria com os principais marketplaces do país para coibir a venda de minicelulares não homologados. Embora a comercialização desses aparelhos seja proibida no Brasil desde 2017, eles continuam à venda em anúncios com outros nomes, como mostramos aqui no Tecnoblog.

articles.title: Biostar Introduces the BIWCL-PAT Industrial Motherboard for Edge Computing and AIoT Applications
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 13th 2026
Biostar Introduces the BIWCL-PAT Industrial Motherboard for Edge Computing and AIoT Applications
BIOSTAR, a leading manufacturer of consumer and industrial motherboards, edge computing solutions, graphics cards, and storage devices, today introduced the BIWCL-PAT industrial motherboard. Powered by Intel Core Series 3 (Wildcat Lake) processors, the BIWCL-PAT brings triple independent displays, high-speed NVMe storage expansion, and versatile wired and wireless connectivity into a small-form-factor platform. Designed for system integrators, it supports applications across industrial automation, AIoT, and edge computing, as well as human-machine interfaces (HMI), POS systems, and self-service kiosks.
With a 148 × 102 mm footprint, the BIWCL-PAT is built for integration into space-constrained equipment. It supports processor options from Intel Core 3 to Intel Core 7, and its single DDR5-6400 SO-DIMM slot supports up to 64 GB of memory, providing capacity for multitasking and local data processing. This combination gives developers a solid foundation for systems that bring computing closer to factory equipment, retail terminals, and networked devices.Triple independent display support through LVDS, HDMI, and DisplayPort lets one platform drive multiple screens with different content. HDMI 2.1 and DisplayPort 1.4 each support 4K resolution at 60 Hz, while the LVDS interface drives embedded panels at up to 1920 × 1200. Industrial operators can use separate displays for control interfaces, equipment status, and operational data, while POS and kiosk developers can combine operator screens with customer-facing information.
Three dedicated M.2 slots support storage, cellular, and wireless expansion. The M.2 Key-M slot accommodates 2242/2280 NVMe SSDs through PCIe 4.0 x2, enabling high-speed access to applications and locally stored data. An M.2 Key-B slot supports 3042/3052 4G/5G modules over PCIe 4.0 x1 and USB 3.2, with an onboard SIM slot for cellular network access. An M.2 Key-E 2230 slot supports Wi-Fi and Bluetooth modules. Together, these options let integrators configure storage and wireless access for each deployment.
For always-on networking, the BIWCL-PAT features dual Intel 2.5GbE LAN ports powered by Intel I226-LM and I226-V controllers. The two interfaces let developers connect local equipment and upstream networks through separate ports, supporting reliable data exchange between embedded devices and wider infrastructure. Cellular and Wi-Fi expansion add further options for installations with different network access requirements.
The BIWCL-PAT also offers a practical mix of modern and industrial interfaces, with two USB 3.2 Gen 2 ports, four USB 2.0 connections, two RS232/422/485 interfaces, two RS232 interfaces, and an 8-bit digital I/O header. These connections accommodate peripherals such as barcode scanners and industrial controllers.
Onboard TPM 2.0 provides hardware-based security capabilities, while supported operating systems include Windows 11 IoT Enterprise 24H2 or later and Ubuntu 24.04. A 9-24 V DC input range and an operating temperature range of 0°C to 60°C further support deployment across industrial and commercial environments.
With the BIWCL-PAT, BIOSTAR gives system integrators the tools to build compact, connected systems for factory terminals, interactive kiosks, and retail installations. Its combination of multiple displays, dedicated M.2 expansion, and dual 2.5GbE networking helps power the edge across practical embedded applications.

articles.title: Kein Claude Code mehr? Darum ziehen Microsoft und Meta die Reißleine
articles.text:
Von 60.000 auf 30.000 Nutzer halbiert: Meta drängt Entwickler weg von Claude Code
Anthropics KI-Agent Claude Code ist nicht nur bei Privatanwender:innen beliebt. Auch im Unternehmens- und Arbeitsumfeld wird der Coding-Helfer rege genutzt. Zu rege sogar, wenn es nach Microsoft und Meta geht. Beide haben laut einem Bericht von The Information damit begonnen, die Nutzung von Claude Code intern herunterzufahren. Entwickler:innen werden dazu angehalten, weniger mit Anthropics KI zu arbeiten.
Warum Meta und Microsoft Claude Code einschränken
Solche Schritte hatte Microsoft schon im Mai 2026 angestoßen und damals seinen Entwickler:innen mitgeteilt, dass zahlreiche Claude-Code-Lizenzen im Laufe der kommenden Monate gekündigt werden sollen. Laut internen Berichten sollen sich auch deshalb die Prognosen für die KI-Ausgaben ebenfalls drastisch reduziert haben. Anfang des Jahres hatte Microsoft noch geplant, eine Milliarde US-Dollar für Anthropics KI auszugeben. Jetzt ist es in etwa ein Drittel weniger.
Bei Meta soll sich ein ähnliches Bild abzeichnen. Mittlerweile arbeiten deutlich weniger Entwickler:innen mit Claude Code als es noch Anfang des Jahres der Fall war. Damals waren es rund 60.000 Meta-Mitarbeiter:innen, die Anthropics KI in den Arbeitsalltag integrierten. Die Zahl soll jetzt auf etwa 30.000 gesunken sein. Ein Teil dieses Rückgangs kann mit Metas Stellenabbau erklärt werden. Aber das soll laut internen Quellen nicht der primäre Treiber sein.
Stattdessen wollen beide Unternehmen, dass ihre Entwickler:innen vermehrt die hauseigenen KI-Tools nutzen. Bei Microsoft soll Copilot den Mitarbeiter:innen weiterhelfen, während bei Meta das vergleichsweise neue KI-Modell Muse Spark zum Einsatz kommt. Bei Meta kommt zudem noch Muse Code, ein Coding-Agent, der aktuell intern getestet wird, hinzu. Er soll wohl künftig als Konkurrenz zu Claude Code erscheinen. Für den internen Gebrauch setzt Meta noch auf einen weiteren Agenten namens Meta Code.
Kund:innen von Microsoft sind im Übrigen von diesen Änderungen nicht betroffen. Sie können auch weiterhin über die Microsoft-Dienste auf Anthropic-Modelle zurückgreifen und unterliegen dabei keinen neuen Limits. Fraglich bleibt, ob sich die Änderung mittel- bis langfristig auf Anthropic selbst auswirkt. Gerade Microsoft gehört mit zu den größten Investor:innen des KI-Unternehmens.

articles.title: Philips renueva su cepillo más avanzado: así es el nuevo Sonicare DiamondClean 9900 Prestige
articles.text:
Philips acaba de actualizar la gama alta de su catálogo de higiene bucal con la llegada del nuevo Philips Sonicare DiamondClean 9900 Prestige. La firma neerlandesa vuelve a apostar por un dispositivo tope de gama que combina tecnología sónica de alta frecuencia con sensores de presión y guiado en tiempo real mediante inteligencia artificial. Su precio oficial de partida es de 379,99 euros, aunque en Amazon ya está en oferta por 229,95 euros.
Philips Sonicare DiamondClean 9900 Prestige
Retroalimentación en tiempo real y ajuste automático de potencia
El principal argumento tecnológico del nuevo DiamondClean 9900 Prestige de Philips radica en la integración de la tecnología SenseIQ. Este sistema monitoriza el cepillado hasta 100 veces por segundo para analizar la fuerza aplicada y la zona cubierta.
A diferencia de modelos de gamas más accesibles que se limitan a emitir una alerta lumínica, este cepillo incorpora una función de intensidad adaptativa: si detecta que el usuario ejerce una presión excesiva que pueda dañar el esmalte o las encías, reduce de forma automática la potencia del motor.
La orientación durante la limpieza se apoya en dos elementos visuales directos en el cuerpo del cepillo de dientes:
- Indicador de presión mediante código de colores: un anillo de luz avisa en verde si la presión es idónea, parpadea en morado si es excesiva o se atenúa si resulta insuficiente.
- Mapa bucal y sensor de cobertura: la base cambia de color (amarillo si falta insistir, azul cuando el área está limpia) y la pantalla integrada proyecta al finalizar un resumen de las zonas que han quedado sin repasar.
En cuanto al rendimiento del motor, la tecnología sónica de la marca alcanza los 62.000 movimientos de cerdas por minuto, manteniendo una potencia constante en todo momento para evitar caídas de rendimiento durante la sesión.
Modos de uso, conectividad y accesorios
A través de la pantalla táctil a color integrada en el mango, es posible alternar entre tres niveles de intensidad y ocho modos de cepillado específicos (entre los que destacan opciones para encías sensibles, limpieza profunda o eliminación de manchas superficiales). Para quienes busquen un seguimiento más detallado a largo plazo, el cepillo se vincula vía Bluetooth con la app móvil de Philips.
En el apartado de diseño y autonomía, ofrece hasta 14 días de uso continuo por carga. Incluye una base de carga con vaso de cristal por inducción para el baño y un estuche de viaje rígido que también permite recargar el dispositivo de forma directa.

articles.title: TechSparks 2026: Here’s all that’s happening on Day 2
articles.text:
TechSparks 2026: Here’s all that’s happening on Day 2
From Bengaluru’s urban future and Vibecode30 to deeptech capital and the convenience economy, here’s everything you can expect on day two of TechSparks 2026.
Namaskara Bengaluru!
Day one of TechSparks 2026 set the tone for the 17th edition and its theme, ‘The New Tech Order’. On day two, the conversation goes deeper into AI agents, deeptech capital, creativity and the brands of tomorrow.
On October 14, the day opens with YourStory launching Vibecode30 2026, unveiling a cohort that celebrates exceptional technology builders.
Next, Dr Shivkumar Kalyanaraman, CEO, Anusandhan National Research Foundation, Government of India, will share what needs to change for Indian inventions to move from papers and patents into products.
Later, Dr Vignesh Subrahmaniam, Principal AI Scientist, Intuit, will explore what builders need to rethink as AI moves from responding to prompts to reasoning, deciding and acting.
In the afternoon, Chandrika Deb, Country Manager – India, Canva, will reflect on how AI is becoming a co-creator in the creative process. Sanjeev Kumar, CTO, Pine Labs Payment, will unveil three launches built for the agent economy, including an Agent Store for third-party developers.
In a fireside chat, Manish Maheshwari, Managing Director, India, Stripe, will decode how Indian startups can go from early traction to global scale.
Don’t miss the panel representing nearly Rs 2,000 crore in deeptech capital, featuring Vishesh Rajaram (Speciale Invest), Abhishek Srivastava (Kae Capital), Mayuresh Raut (Seafund) and Anirudh Singh (Avataar Venture Partners). They will discuss which technologies investors are most willing to back and where India’s funding ladder breaks.
Rohit Kapoor, CEO, Swiggy Food Marketplace, will talk about the future of India’s convenience economy. In the evening, Mohit Bhatnagar, Managing Director, Peak XV, will discuss how India’s startups can move from valuation to value creation.
On the Focus Stage, Tejas Goenka and Nupur Goenka of Tally Solutions will share how the company has stayed relevant for 40 years. Dr Nagendra Nagaraja, Founder, CEO, and Chairman of QpiAI, will ask whether India is early enough for quantum this time.
The D2C Stage brings together founders and operators on building brands that last, with Natasha Tuli, Founder, Soulflower, and Ananth Narayanan, Founder and CEO, BRND.ME, among them.
Other speakers for the day include Prof Satya Chakravarthy, Founder, The ePlane Company; Deepit Purkayastha, Co-founder and CEO, InShorts; Srijon Biswas, CTO, PhonePe; Dr Geetha Manjunath, Founder and CEO, Niramai Health Analytix; Matt Yi, Co-founder and Tech VP, VeloDB; and Mihir Shah, CBO, Shopflo, among others.
The day also features hands-on Action Labs and executive roundtables with Oppex AI and Stripe.
So, are you ready for round two?

articles.title: Ce détecteur d'IA confronte 23 moteurs avant de trancher !
articles.text:
Malgré les progrès des détecteurs, il est toujours difficile de savoir si un texte a été rédigé par une IA. SlopTotal adopte une méthode prudente : il soumet le contenu à 23 détecteurs différents et affiche leurs résultats séparément. Un fonctionnement qui permet de repérer les désaccords plutôt que de transformer un simple pourcentage en verdict définitif.
Les détecteurs d'IA présentent tous des limites : leurs résultats dépendent notamment du texte analysé, de sa longueur et de la méthode employée. Un contenu court, très formel ou légèrement retouché peut ainsi compliquer leur travail. SlopTotal combine plusieurs approches de détection et publie également les résultats de ses propres évaluations pour permettre aux utilisateurs de mieux interpréter les scores obtenus.
23 analyses pour voir quand les détecteurs ne sont pas d’accord
Il suffit de coller un texte, de renseigner l'URL d'une page Web ou d'importer un document pour lancer l'analyse. SlopTotal mobilise 23 moteurs répartis en trois catégories : 9 classifieurs neuronaux, 7 tests statistiques et 7 analyses linguistiques. Certains s'appuient sur des modèles entraînés à distinguer les textes humains des contenus générés par IA, tandis que d'autres examinent notamment la perplexité, la structure des phrases ou différents marqueurs linguistiques.
Chaque moteur fournit son propre résultat, que SlopTotal rassemble ensuite pour produire un score global. Celui-ci ne correspond pas à une simple moyenne des 23 analyses : le service utilise un modèle de calibration qui combine leurs résultats en tenant compte de leurs performances mesurées.
L'intérêt réside surtout dans la possibilité d'examiner les désaccords. Un même texte peut être fortement signalé par certains moteurs et considéré comme humain par d'autres. Plutôt que de masquer ces écarts derrière un chiffre unique, SlopTotal permet de consulter les résultats individuels et de mieux comprendre les incertitudes de la détection.
Le service est accessible gratuitement, sans création de compte et sans limite d'analyses annoncée pour le moment.
- Vingt-trois moteurs de détection
- Analyse de textes et URL
- Gratuit, open source et auto-hébergeable
Des tests publics pour mesurer les performances et les erreurs
SlopTotal ne se contente pas de réunir plusieurs détecteurs : son développeur publie également les résultats de ses propres évaluations. Son benchmark, baptisé SlopBench, comprend 3 252 textes, répartis à parts égales entre contenus humains et textes générés par 14 modèles d'intelligence artificielle.
Parmi les contenus humains figurent notamment 87 passages littéraires publiés entre 1532 et 1915. Leur présence permet d'évaluer les risques de faux positifs, notamment lorsque les détecteurs rencontrent des styles d'écriture anciens ou inhabituels.
Sur ce jeu de tests, le développeur annonce un taux de faux positifs de 1,7 % au seuil « Likely AI », mais seulement 67 % des textes générés par IA sont détectés à ce même seuil. Autrement dit, le système cherche à limiter les accusations injustifiées, quitte à laisser passer une partie des contenus artificiels. Ces chiffres proviennent toutefois des évaluations du projet lui-même et ne garantissent pas des performances identiques dans toutes les situations.
Le projet est open source et peut être auto-hébergé, ce qui permet d'analyser des textes localement sans les transmettre au service en ligne. L'installation depuis les sources nécessite Python 3.10 au minimum, environ 2 Go d'espace pour les modèles et au moins 4 Go de mémoire vive. Une installation via Docker est également proposée, sans nécessiter de carte graphique dédiée.
SlopTotal reste néanmoins un outil d'aide à l'analyse, pas une solution capable de prouver qu'un texte a été généré par une IA. Les résultats sont notamment moins fiables sur les contenus très courts ou réécrits par un humain. La langue constitue également un facteur important : le français est pris en charge, mais les performances peuvent varier selon les langues et les types de contenus.
Pour un enseignant, un recruteur ou un éditeur, les 23 analyses constituent donc avant tout un point de départ pour examiner un texte. Même lorsque plusieurs détecteurs s'accordent, leur verdict ne saurait suffire, à lui seul, à établir l'origine d'un contenu.

articles.title: Video | Así es el exoesqueleto robótico que permite “caminar” a personas con paraplejia
articles.text:
Jessica Tawil volvió a dar sus primeros pasos en más de una década con la ayuda de un exoesqueleto portátil. (Tomado de Instagram)
Jessica Tawil dio sus primeros pasos en más de una década con un exoesqueleto portátil, luego de que un accidente automovilístico ocurrido en Nueva Jersey, Estados Unidos, en noviembre de 2014 le provocara una lesión medular y la dejara paralizada de la parte inferior del cuerpo.
El video superó las 200 millones de reproducciones en Instagram, donde la joven de 27 años reúne más de 800 mil seguidores. La publicación acumuló más de 8 millones de me gusta y 140.000 comentarios.
Tawil tenía 16 años cuando sufrió el accidente. Desde entonces usa una silla de ruedas a diario y fue diagnosticada como parapléjica T6, una condición que le impide mover las piernas y la parte inferior de su cuerpo.
Aunque considera que posiblemente no vuelva a caminar de forma natural, el dispositivo le permitió ponerse de pie y avanzar. Al incorporarse, reaccionó con incredulidad: “Oh, Dios mío... está bien, está bien, está bien”.
Cómo es la tecnología detrás del exoesqueleto
Los exoesqueletos son estructuras que se colocan sobre el cuerpo y utilizan energía para asistir el movimiento de personas con parálisis. Suelen fabricarse con metal y fibra de carbono, e incorporan sensores que registran los desplazamientos del usuario.
En quienes no pueden mover las piernas, estos sistemas interpretan señales de la parte superior del cuerpo. Inclinarse hacia adelante o desplazar las caderas puede activar el inicio de un paso.
Algunos modelos, incluido el que utilizó Tawil, cuentan con controles situados en las muñecas para dirigir el movimiento. Otros incorporan botones desde los que el usuario puede ordenar cada acción.
La tecnología fue desarrollada durante años por científicos e ingenieros con el objetivo de ampliar la movilidad de personas con paraplejia. Sumado a permitirles caminar con asistencia, los investigadores han asociado su uso con efectos físicos y psicológicos.
Qué beneficios de salud traen los exoesqueletos
Un estudio publicado en 2022 en el Journal of Personalized Medicine señaló que caminar con un exoesqueleto puede fortalecer músculos afectados, mejorar la velocidad y la eficiencia de la marcha, y actuar sobre consecuencias secundarias de una lesión medular.
Los autores incluyeron entre esos posibles efectos la espasticidad, la densidad ósea, la masa corporal magra, el tono muscular, el dolor y cambios en las funciones cardiovasculares, de la vejiga y del intestino. A su vez, indicaron que se registraron mejoras en el estado de ánimo, la salud mental y la calidad de vida.
Cómo le fue a la creadora de contenido probando el exoesqueleto
En el video se observa el procedimiento mediante el cual la máquina eleva a la joven desde una banqueta hasta la postura erguida. Durante la sesión, dos especialistas permanecieron a su lado para supervisar la prueba e impartir instrucciones sobre la operación de los mandos del dispositivo.
A lo largo del ensayo, los técnicos explicaron a Tawil la manera de dirigir los controles para realizar giros a la izquierda y avanzar en línea recta por el recinto. El exoesqueleto sostiene el torso y las extremidades inferiores mediante correas y soportes rígidos, permitiendo el movimiento asistido de las piernas.
Hacia el final de la prueba, la creadora de contenido se desplazó hacia un espejo ubicado frente a los ventanales del establecimiento para observar la posición erguida con la estructura robótica colocada.
Asimismo, este tipo de tecnología médica basada en robótica, se utiliza en procesos de rehabilitación e investigación para proporcionar soporte físico y movilidad asistida a pacientes con parálisis o afectaciones en la columna vertebral.
Actualmente, el desarrollo de estos sistemas tecnológicos continúa en fase de evaluación clínica, con el objetivo de mejorar la autonomía funcional de los usuarios y analizar la viabilidad de su integración progresiva en espacios de uso personal y cotidiano.

articles.title: Top 10 notebooks com placa de vídeo dedicada para comprar em 2026 • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Top 10 notebooks com placa de vídeo dedicada para comprar em 2026
Selecionamos os melhores notebooks com GPU dedicada para jogos, edição de vídeo e tarefas de alto processamento gráfico em diversas faixas de preço
Notebooks com placa de vídeo dedicada são voltados principalmente a quem precisa de mais recursos do que os oferecidos pelas GPUs integradas aos processadores. Esses modelos são recomendados para designers, editores de vídeo, arquitetos, gamers e outros usuários que lidam com processamento gráfico intenso.
Mas ao escolher o melhor computador com GPU dedicada, é importante entender o nível de exigência das suas atividades. Modelos de entrada e intermediários, com RTX 3050 ou RTX 4050, são ideais para atividade gráfica leve e moderada, enquanto máquinas com RTX 5060, RTX 5070 e até RTX PRO 1000 são recomendadas para quem quer máxima performance.
Além disso, a escolha não depende apenas da GPU: processador, quantidade e tipo de memória e armazenamento também influenciam o perfil de cada equipamento.
A seguir, o Tecnoblog apresenta 10 notebooks com placa de vídeo dedicada para comprar em 2026. Veja prós e contras de cada modelo.
O Acer Predator Helios Neo 16 é um notebook avançado para jogos, edição de vídeo, criação gráfica e outras atividades que aproveitam processamento e aceleração gráfica. Ele combina o Intel Core Ultra 9 275HX, com 24 núcleos, à GeForce RTX 5070 com 8 GB de memória GDDR7 e recursos de IA.
Seu painel IPS tem 16″, resolução WQXGA de 2560 x 1600, 240 Hz de taxa de atualização, brilho de até 500 nits e cobertura de 100% do espaço DCI-P3 — que pode ser útil para trabalhos de imagem e vídeo.
O conjunto ainda traz 32 GB de RAM DDR5 e SSD NVMe de 1 TB, com possibilidade de expansão de memória e armazenamento nessa configuração. Por ser um equipamento voltado a desempenho gráfico, o Helios Neo 16 tem dimensões e peso maiores que os notebooks comuns e a conectividade inclui Wi-Fi 6E, Ethernet, além de USB e HDMI.
O Galaxy Book6 Ultra é o notebook da Samsung recomendado para quem trabalha com edição de vídeo, criação gráfica, projetos em 3D e outras tarefas que podem aproveitar uma GPU dedicada, mas também precisa de um notebook fino: são 15,4 mm de espessura e 1,89 kg.
No hardware, o conjunto reúne o Intel Core Ultra 7 356H, 32 GB de memória LPDDR5X, SSD NVMe de 1 TB e GeForce RTX 5060 com 8 GB de GDDR7. A NPU do processador pode ser utilizada por aplicações compatíveis com recursos de IA executados localmente.
O principal diferencial físico está na tela. O painel Dynamic AMOLED 2X de 16 polegadas tem resolução de 2880 x 1800, é sensível ao toque e trabalha com taxa adaptativa de 30 a 120 Hz. O brilho chega a 500 nits em SDR e 1.000 nits em HDR, enquanto o acabamento antirreflexo ajuda na visualização em ambientes iluminados.
A bateria é acompanhada de carregador USB-C de 140 W, e a Samsung informa autonomia de até 30 horas em condições específicas de reprodução de vídeo. Há ainda Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 5.4, duas portas Thunderbolt 4, USB-A, HDMI 2.1 e leitor SD.
O ASUS ROG Strix G16 é recomendado para quem prioriza jogos e aplicações gráficas e quer combinar uma GPU dedicada com uma tela de alta resolução e frequência. Ele traz chip Intel Core i9-14900HX, com 24 núcleos e 32 threads, acompanhado da GeForce RTX 5060 com 8 GB de GDDR7.
A tela ROG Nebula é um dos componentes centrais do modelo. O painel de 16 polegadas usa proporção 16:10, resolução 2.5K, taxa de atualização de 240 Hz e tempo de resposta de 3 ms. Também há G-Sync, MUX Switch e Nvidia Advanced Optimus, recursos voltados ao gerenciamento gráfico e à sincronização da imagem.
O modelo traz 16 GB de RAM DDR5 e SSD PCIe 4.0 de 512 GB, capacidade que pode exigir gerenciamento de arquivos para quem mantém muitos jogos ou projetos grandes instalados simultaneamente. O sistema operacional é Windows 11 Home, com Wi-Fi 6E e teclado ABNT2 retroiluminado.
O Lenovo Legion 5i é voltado a quem pretende usar o notebook para jogos, criação de conteúdo e multitarefa, mas prefere investir em um painel OLED. Esse modelo traz chip Intel Core Ultra 7 255HX e uma GeForce RTX 5060 com 8 GB de GDDR7.
Seu painel OLED de 15,1″ tem resolução de 2560 x 1600, proporção 16:10, taxa de atualização de 165 Hz, brilho de até 500 nits e cobertura de 100% do DCI-P3, além de suporte a HDR.
Na prática, a resolução favorece maior área de trabalho que um painel Full HD tradicional, enquanto o OLED é relevante principalmente para quem valoriza contraste e reprodução de conteúdo.
São 16 GB de RAM DDR5 e SSD de 1 TB, além de Wi-Fi 7 e Bluetooth 5.4. O teclado em português possui retroiluminação RGB e a webcam de 5 MP inclui obturador eletrônico. É uma configuração que equilibra uso em jogos com características que também interessam a quem trabalha com criação visual.
O Dell Pro Max 16 é voltado ao público profissional, que precisa de uma GPU dedicada para aplicações gráficas, projeto e criação, em vez de um notebook desenvolvido exclusivamente para jogos. A RTX PRO 1000 Blackwell disponível no modelo possui 8 GB de GDDR7 e pertence à linha profissional da Nvidia.
A Dell oferece o modelo com Core Ultra 7 265H ou Ultra 9 285H, diferentes quantidades de memória e opções de SSD, portanto, a configuração exata deve ser conferida no anúncio antes da compra. Na versão com Ultra 7, por exemplo, há opções com 16 ou 32 GB de RAM DDR5 em módulos expansíveis.
Na configuração exibida pela Dell, a tela tem 16 polegadas, resolução FHD+ e 300 nits, com opções de touchscreen, enquanto a conectividade inclui duas Thunderbolt 4 com Power Delivery e DisplayPort, USB-A, HDMI 2.1, Ethernet e leitor de cartão SD.
O Alienware 16 é recomendado para quem procura um notebook gamer com tela de alta resolução e uma configuração intermediária de GPU dedicada. A versão reúne o Intel Core 7 240H, de 10 núcleos, com a GeForce RTX 4050 de 6 GB GDDR6, 16 GB de memória DDR5 e SSD de 512 GB.
A GPU dedicada acrescenta capacidade para jogos e aplicações gráficas que dependem de processamento paralelo, enquanto os 16 GB de RAM atendem a um cenário de multitarefa mais exigente que o de notebooks básicos.
A tela é de 16 polegadas com resolução de 2560 x 1600, 120 Hz de taxa de atualização, 300 nits e cobertura de 100% do sRGB para melhor visualização de cores. Essa resolução oferece mais pixels do que o Full HD, enquanto os 120 Hz favorecem movimentações mais fluidas do que em notebooks comuns.
O modelo tem Wi-Fi 7 e Bluetooth, Ethernet RJ-45, HDMI 2.1 e duas portas USB-A, além de duas USB-C com DisplayPort, e seu peso fica na faixa de 2,5 kg.
O Lenovo LOQ 15IRX9 é um modelo para quem quer um notebook gamer com uma GPU de entrada/intermediária, mas não pretende abrir mão de um processador Core i7. Ele tem o chip de 13ª geração da Intel, com 14 núcleos e 20 threads, 16 GB de DDR5 e GeForce RTX 4050 de 6 GB.
A tela de 15,6 polegadas utiliza resolução Full HD, painel WVA, 144 Hz, 300 nits e cobertura de 100% do sRGB. Para jogos, essa frequência favorece a fluidez quando o hardware consegue gerar taxas de quadros compatíveis; para trabalho com edição de imagens, a cobertura de sRGB pode ser interessante para maior gama de cores.
O conjunto ainda traz teclado retroiluminado, webcam Full HD com obturador eletrônico, Wi-Fi 6 e Ethernet. Entre as conexões estão três USB-A, USB-C com DisplayPort e Power Delivery, HDMI 2.1 e RJ-45.
O ASUS TUF Gaming F16 é um notebook com GPU dedicada mais acessível. Ele combina o Intel Core i7-13620H, de 10 núcleos e 16 threads, com a GeForce RTX 4050 de 6 GB GDDR6 e SSD de 512 GB, além do sistema KeepOS baseado em Linux.
Como a memória instalada é de apenas 8 GB, esse é um ponto que merece atenção para quem pretende utilizar simultaneamente jogos, navegadores e programas mais pesados; a plataforma, por outro lado, possui dois slots de RAM e suporta expansão.
A tela de 16 polegadas é de alta resolução, com revestimento antirreflexo e taxa de atualização de 144 Hz. A ASUS também informa suporte a G-Sync, MUX Switch e Advanced Optimus na plataforma. O TUF Gaming F16 também tem Wi-Fi 6, Ethernet, HDMI e Thunderbolt 4.
O Acer Nitro V15 é recomendado para quem procura um notebook gamer de entrada com GPU dedicada para jogos e aplicações gráficas, sem partir para as configurações mais caras da linha Nitro.
A versão com Intel Core i5-13420H combina um processador de 13ª geração com 8 núcleos e 12 threads, à GeForce RTX 4050 de 6 GB GDDR6. Há versões com 8 GB de RAM e SSD de 512 GB, enquanto outras configurações utilizam 16 GB; por isso, a memória instalada deve ser conferida no momento da compra.
Na configuração i5/RTX 4050, a tela tem 15,6 polegadas, resolução Full HD e taxa de atualização que pode chegar a 165 Hz. A família Nitro também traz Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth e Thunderbolt 4, além de HDMI e conexões USB. O peso fica próximo de 2,1 kg.
O LOQ-e é o notebook da Lenovo para quem quer entrar na categoria com GPU dedicada gastando menos em componentes do que nas configurações mais avançadas da linha LOQ. O modelo combina o Intel Core i5-12450HX, de 12ª geração, com a GeForce RTX 3050 de 6 GB, 8 GB de RAM e SSD de 512 GB.
Essa GPU é mais antiga, mas ainda permite utilizar aceleração gráfica dedicada em jogos e aplicações que aproveitam processamento paralelo, mas os 8 GB de RAM merecem atenção em cenários de multitarefa mais pesada.
A tela de 15,6 polegadas trabalha em Full HD, com painel antirreflexo e taxa de atualização de 144 Hz. O conjunto também inclui teclado retroiluminado e numérico, características que podem ser úteis tanto para jogos quanto para quem utiliza o equipamento em tarefas de produtividade.
Diferentemente de boa parte dos notebooks gamers deste guia, essa configuração é comercializada com Linux, o que pode ser um ponto negativo para quem não é acostumado com esse sistema operacional. O modelo possui Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth, USB-C, USB, HDMI, Ethernet e leitor de cartões.
A escolha deve considerar o conjunto de componentes e o tipo de atividade que será realizada. Entre os principais pontos estão:
A GeForce RTX 5090 ocupa o topo da linha em especificações, com 10.496 núcleos CUDA e 24 GB de GDDR7. A RTX 5080, RTX 5070 Ti e RTX 5070 aparecem em níveis inferiores, enquanto a RTX 5060 é uma opção intermediária da geração.
O Acer Nitro V15 aparece como uma opção de custo-benefício na categoria notebook gamer. Ele traz configuração com Core i7-13620H, RTX 4050, 16 GB de RAM e SSD de 512 GB na faixa de R$ 7 mil no varejo brasileiro.

articles.title: AMD Showcases Its Next-Gen EPYC "Verano" CPU, Up to 192 Cores and LPDDR5X Memory
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 13th 2026
AMD Showcases Its Next-Gen EPYC "Verano" CPU, Up to 192 Cores and LPDDR5X Memory
AMD showed off its next-generation EPYC "Verano" server CPUs during CEO Dr. Lisa Su opening keynote at the 2026 OCP Global Summit. The new CPU is the first EPYC processor to support LPDDR5X memory via SOCAMM2 modules. Now AMD is mirroring rival NVIDIA's Vera CPU that already uses SOCAMM2 modules. The "Verano" processor sits within the EPYC 9006 "LP" family and is built on the same TSMC 2 nm process as the already-launched EPYC "Venice". While AMD "Venice" is the first EPYC processor based on Zen 6 architecture, "Verano" is optimized for AI tasks in agentic AI racks. For this, AMD plans to pair them with its own Instinct MI500 GPUs via xGMI connectivity at up to 112 Gbps. It will run on the new SP8 platform rather than Venice's SP7. When we first heard about "Verano", AMD indicated that the upcoming CPUs will feature up to 72 cores on a single-socket platform. However, that has now been updated to up to 192 cores.
From the initial information available, this could mean either a single large chip or a dual 96-core configuration. More details came from System360Cheese on X, who reported that the chip shown featured eight Zen 6 CCDs alongside two large IO dies and four LPDDR5X memory controllers. The CCDs appear smaller than those in Venice's Zen 6C design, suggesting these are the standard 12-core Zen 6 dies rather than the denser 32-core Zen 6C variants. The announcement follows AMD's earlier reveal of the Helion agentic AI rack, an Open Compute Project spec-designed system that Verano is expected to be integrated. Availability is targeted for 2027.
Sources:
				AMD, 				Wccftech, 				System360Cheese on X

articles.title: Avec des partenaires de renom, Apple s'attaque à la sécurisation et au pilotage de votre maison
articles.text:
Avec des partenaires de renom, Apple s'attaque à la sécurisation et au pilotage de votre maison
Apple étend son écosystème domotique avec une gamme complète d'appareils connectés, baptisée Home Collection. Conçue par ses partenaires LG et Schneider, elle compte des caméras, thermostats et serrures connectés, le tout pilotable depuis son tout nouvel écran intelligent HomeView.
C'est une petite révolution à Cupertino. Apple ne se contente plus de ses segments historiques (informatique, téléphonie, audio, montres et clés TV) et investit désormais bien plus largement l'univers de la maison. Le constructeur ne se limite pas à l'annonce d'un écran connecté, le HomeView, servant de hub domotique au cœur de la maison, mais dévoile un écosystème complet d'accessoires permettant de piloter et sécuriser le domicile. Cette gamme est conçue en partenariat avec des spécialistes du genre que sont LG et Schneider. L'occasion pour le Californien de lancer ce qu'il appelle son Apple Home Collection.
Conçus pour fonctionner avec l'application Apple Home (Maison dans notre tumultueuse contrée), les appareils en question sont pensés pour être reliés au HomeView, lequel met à profit Siri AI, sur lequel nous ne vous ferons pas l'affront de revenir. Nous nous contenterons de rappeler que si l'assistant dopé à l'intelligence artificielle est bien disponible en français, il n'est pas accessible sur le Vieux Continent pour cause de bisbille avec les instances européennes. Cela explique que l'intégralité de la nouvelle gamme de produits soit uniquement attendue aux États-Unis et au Canada, où le HomeView est annoncé.
Caméras, serrure et thermostats : le détail des nouveaux accessoires connectés
Ces produits se déclinent en une gamme complète. On y trouve la bagatelle de quatre caméras connectées, dont le flux peut évidemment être consulté depuis l'écran intelligent HomeView fraîchement présenté par le fabricant. La Video Doorbell prend la forme d'une sonnette connectée dotée d'une caméra 2,5 K, la Floodlight Cam est une caméra extérieure pensée pour la vision nocturne et la détection de mouvements, l'Outdoor Cam en est une déclinaison simplifiée et l'Indoor Cam se destine à l'intérieur du domicile. L'ensemble de ces caméras est conçu par LG. Le Sud-Coréen livre en outre un Smart Deadbolt Lock, soit une serrure connectée pouvant être déverrouillée à l'aide d'un iPhone ou d'une Apple Watch, mais aussi d'un code numérique.
Deux thermostats s'ajoutent à cette gamme déjà complète. On doit le premier à LG et le second à Schneider Electric ; ils permettent tous deux de piloter un chauffage connecté ou encore de vérifier l'humidité ambiante du domicile.
Prix et disponibilité des équipements Apple Home Collection
Côté tarifs, il faut compter entre 199 et 399 $ pour les caméras connectées, tandis que les thermostats de LG et Schneider sont tous deux facturés 199 $ (avec un capteur de température additionnel à 39 $ pour LG). La serrure est pour sa part facturée 349 $. L'ensemble de ces produits sera commercialisé à compter de décembre 2026.

articles.title: Einst milliardenschwer, jetzt Pleite: Gehyptes KI-Startup Character AI muss Insolvenz anmelden
articles.text:
Einst milliardenschwer, jetzt Pleite: Gehyptes KI-Startup Character AI muss Insolvenz anmelden
2021 von den Ex-Googlern Noam Shazeer und Daniel De Freitas gegründet, ermöglicht es Character AI Nutzerinnen, mit verschiedenen echten oder fiktiven Persönlichkeiten wie Elon Musk, Albert Einstein oder Super Mario zu chatten. Zudem können Nutzer:innen sich eine eigene KI-Persönlichkeit programmieren, um sich mit ihr zu unterhalten.
Milliardenbewertung ganz ohne Einnahmen
2023 erreichte die KI-Plattform monatlich 100 Millionen Besuche, hatte aber bis dahin noch keinen einzigen Cent eingenommen. Trotz fehlenden Umsatzes sammelte Character.ai in einer von Andreessen Horowitz angeführten Finanzierungsrunde 150 Millionen Dollar ein. Damit erreichte das Startup eine Bewertung von gut einer Milliarde Dollar.
Jetzt muss Character.ai Insolvenz nach dem Chapter-11-Verfahren anmelden. Es drücken Verbindlichkeiten in Höhe von 50 bis 100 Millionen Dollar. Das ist aber noch nicht alles. Als Grund für das Scheitern gab das Unternehmen „erhebliche rechtliche, regulatorische und operative Gegenwinde“ im vergangenen Jahr an.
Character AI: Finanzielle und rechtliche Probleme
Neben den finanziellen Schwierigkeiten musste sich Character.ai mit zahlreichen rechtlichen Problemen auseinandersetzen. So hatte Disney das KI-Startup im September 2025 per Unterlassungsaufforderung dazu gebracht, Chatbots mit Disney-Figuren aus dem Angebot zu entfernen.
Zudem gab es eine Reihe von Klagen von Familien in den USA. 2024 soll ein 14-Jähriger aus Florida nach langen Gesprächen mit einem Character-AI-Chatbot Suizid begangen haben. Eine entsprechende Klage der Mutter endete Anfang 2026 mit einem Vergleich. Außerdem hatten Familien aus Texas dem Unternehmen vor, mit seinen KI-Chatbots Jugendliche zu Gewalt und Selbstverletzung ermutigt zu haben, wie Trendingtopics schreibt.
Daraufhin hatte Character AI Altersprüfungen eingeführt. Seit Ende 2025 war es Nutzer:innen unter 18 Jahren außerdem verboten, offene Chats zu führen. Darüber hinaus hatte Character.ai 2024 seine Gründer Shazeer und De Freitas sowie weitere rund 30 Mitarbeiter:innen an Google Deepmind verloren. Erst im September 2026 war CEO Karandeep Anand als CTO zu Disney gewechselt.
Disney soll Startup-Teile kaufen wollen
Der Konzern soll auch das Vorkaufsrecht für zum Verkauf angebotene Teile des insolventen KI-Startups haben – das entsprechende Paket soll 20 Millionen Dollar in die klammen Kassen spülen. Weitere Interessenten könnten diesen Grundpreis aber noch überbieten. Der Verkauf soll bis Dezember 2026 abgeschlossen sein.
Mindestens bis dahin soll der Betrieb der Plattform weiterlaufen. Die Abos bleiben von der Insolvenz vorerst unberührt. Bei Änderung kostenpflichtiger Funktionen will das Unternehmen die Nutzer:innen informieren. Nutzer:innen können aber auch ihre Konten löschen und/oder die Daten exportieren.

articles.title: Workday makes Sana its new home for AI-driven HR and finance - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Workday makes Sana its new home for AI-driven HR and finance
Enterprise management software company Workday Inc. today announced that it wants to turn its existing knowledge of people, money and business rules into an operational foundation for agentic artificial intelligence tools.
At Workday Rising, the company’s annual global conference, the company said Sana, an agentic experience that brings together tasks, experiences, decisions, meetings and agent activity in one place, is becoming the new Workday Home. Employees will now work directly with Sana to get everything done.
The company also introduced Sana Concierge, a new service agent for human resources and information technology teams, which can resolve employee requests. It can handle onboarding, leave and password requests without passing these tedious twenty-minute tasks that can be automated to people, so they can focus on issues that require actual intuition.
The company also said Sana now adapts to each employee with a “Home” experience that can tailor itself to each employee role. This includes a user interface that can generate interactive applications using Jev, a cutting-edge model from TypeSafe AI that can create forms, calendars, approval cards, visualizations and interactive experiences in real time.
“AI is the new UI,” said Chief AI Officer Joel Hellermark. “Users shouldn’t have to decide which agent to use, just as they shouldn’t have to click between dozens of different systems. We’re giving our customers an agentic experience that opens up a whole new way to work.”
Included in this new experience, Workday’s executives demonstrated a shift from “copilot to autopilot” during a press briefing. This follows an industry trend alongside agentic automation, where many enterprises are giving employees access to AI agents that can act behind the scenes without needing to be touched and can be triggered when data changes or comes their way, instead of needing a chat interface.
For example, a recruiter autopilot agent prepares for a user’s day by checking open requisitions without waiting for the recruiter to log in, prepares outreach and surfaces candidates. Then the employee reviews outreach and chooses whether to advance candidates from the Sana interface; interview scheduling then runs autonomously. When the interview happens, the agent joins to listen in, prepare notes and uses recruiter feedback to influence future recommendations.
Work Intelligence and Decision Intelligence
As more teams begin to incorporate AI agents, models and tools, Workday announced two new platforms that help teams interact with AI experiences: Work Intelligence and Decision Intelligence.
Work Intelligence helps businesses build for AI by showing enterprise teams how AI tools and agents change work. Workday said AI rarely changes a whole job at once; it can change tasks, and as those tasks change, the underlying skills that matter also change. Every worker that interacts with AI is a data point for how the company can grow.
“Work Intelligence gives leaders the data to thoughtfully redesign roles, build careers and help people grow into what’s next,” said Vice President of Talent Management and Insights Nikki Helmer.
Workday said it can use its deep understanding of skills, delivered through its Skills Cloud, which is now used by more than 3,450 customers and built on an ontology of more than 75,000 canonical skills, to help leadership plan how to grow people as work changes. AI won’t just change existing roles; it will create new ones too.
Decision Intelligence lets HR and finance teams operate in the same space without curating and trading information across clunky communication channels, which often rely on dry reports pulled on a periodic basis. Too often, hiring decisions and procurement are based on analyst-produced reports that slowly go out of date; with an AI analyst on hand, those decisions are based on real-time business data. When the HR or finance team needs to look over a hiring plan, explain shifts in margins or respond to changes in business, they need trustworthy workforce and financial data but this data is often siloed.
As a result, Decision Intelligence performs analysis for both HR and Finance, allowing them to make “decisions,” thus the name, and compare using actionable, real-time data based on business needs.
For example, if HR wants to hire 50 people, it can ask whether the business still needs 50 based on the current workforce makeup. Decision Intelligence can look at the composition, skills that exist, roles that can be filled and how the hiring plan affects costs. Hiring managers and leadership can look at current workforce data instead of staring at a static report.
C1.ai joins Workday
In addition to the Sana updates, Workday announced that it agreed to acquire ConductorOne Inc., also known as C1.ai, an agentic identity platform for people and agents.
C1.ai provides a platform that governs people and agents so that they have the right access at the right time. This means that when a new agent or person is onboarded, they receive the roles they need, and only the roles they need, to get the job done, and then when they no longer need those permissions, they are turned off. This removes the stress of constantly monitoring every part of the system for potential rogue activity.
Without these kinds of controls, AI agents can become lawless, creating security and compliance risks across the entire enterprise.
“Today’s companies run on a combined workforce of people and AI agents,” said Workday President of Product and Technology Gerrit Kazmaier. “With C1.ai, we’ll help secure that workforce by managing and enforcing exactly who – and what – has access to connected apps and systems…”
C1.ai will combine with the Workday Agent System of Record, which already provides a place to see and manage agents. It will go beyond registering agents to also govern what they can access across Workday and other enterprise systems.

articles.title: Apple TV 4K : un nouveau boitier TV que les Européens ne pourront pas vraiment utiliser
articles.text:
Une nouvelle version de l’Apple TV, ça se fête ! C’est un produit de niche mais adoré de ses utilisateurs et qu’Apple ne met à jour que très occasionnellement. La dernière fois c’était en 2022, une autre époque à l’échelle des nouvelles technologies. Quatre ans plus tard, Apple prend donc la peine de revoir son boîtier TV et la marque de Cupertino a un objectif précis : transformer ce simple cube dédié au streaming en véritable hub domotique.
C’est donc tout sauf un hasard si l’annonce de cette nouvelle Apple TV 4K (4ᵉ génération) intervient au même moment que l’officialisation des premiers produits domotiques signés Apple ou encore du HomeView. À l’instar de l’enceinte connectée, l’Apple TV 4K veut devenir un relais pour contrôler SiriAI et les produits qui y sont liés.
Deux nouveautés matérielles
Pour transformer un simple boîtier TV en hub domotique, il convient d’apporter quelques ajustements matériels. C’est ainsi que l’Apple TV 4K se voit modifiée aussi bien au niveau du boîtier que de la télécommande. Sur le premier, les ingénieurs d’Apple sont venus ajouter trois micros longue portée (Far-field) avec annulation d’écho avancée. Celui-ci se déclenche avec la commande vocale « Dis Siri ».
Côté télécommande, c’est un haut-parleur qui permet désormais de la faire sonner pour la retrouver rapidement. C’est tout simplement la fonctionnalité « Find My » qui est appliquée à la télécommande.
Enfin, à l’intérieur de l’Apple TV il y a aussi un chamboulement notable avec une nouvelle puce, l’A19 en l’occurrence. La puce de l’iPhone 17 et de l’iPhone 17e devrait être largement en mesure d’effectuer les tâches classiques demandées à l’Apple TV, mais aussi, dans les pays où la législation le permet, d’accéder à SiriAI. Rappelons à toutes fins utiles que la dernière version de l’assistant vocal d’Apple n’est pas encore disponible en Europe.
Le gain de puissance annoncée est de 50% pour le CPU et une vitesse de traitement doublée côté GPU. Enfin Apple intègre un décodeur AV1 pour améliorer la fluidité du streaming.
En revanche, côté design, il n’y a que très peu de changements à noter côté boîtier. En revanche, côté télécommande on revient à une version métallique et donc bien plus solide, sans changer de form factor.
Des fonctionnalités étendues
Intégrer l’Apple TV 4K dans un système domotique Apple a un autre avantage : créer un réel écosystème. Ainsi, il sera possible de combiner son boîtier TV avec des HomePod mini 2 (jusqu’à 4) pour un effet surround. Dans ce cas de figure, l’Apple TV se chargera de calibrer automatiquement le son en fonction de la position des enceintes dans la pièce.
Prix et date de commercialisation de l’Apple TV 4K (2026)
La nouvelle version de l’Apple TV 4K est déjà disponible en ligne, les premières livraisons sont prévues pour le 13 novembre prochain. Son prix : 349 euros.

articles.title: OpenAI engineer arrested for allegedly planting spy device in office
articles.text:
A Saudi OpenAI engineer has been arrested for allegedly planting a hidden recording device in an executive conference room at the company's San Francisco offices to secretly record sensitive conversations.
The U.S. Department of Justice announced Tuesday that Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, who had worked at OpenAI since July 2025, was arrested on October 9 and charged with illegally intercepting oral communications.
The DOJ says OpenAI security personnel discovered the recording device on September 30, plugged into a USB port behind a television in an executive conference room.
According to the DOJ, OpenAI determined that the device had been concealed in toilet paper, was installed around September 28, and contained encrypted data.
"On or about Sept. 30, OpenAI personnel discovered a surreptitious audio recording device (Recording Device 1) inserted into a USB port on the back of a television in an executive conference room inside one of their buildings in San Francisco," says the DOJ press release.
The DOJ says the conference room was regularly used for meetings involving confidential information about OpenAI's proprietary research, product plans, technical capabilities, business relationships, and government engagements.
Security camera footage allegedly showed Alfozan near the conference room on multiple occasions, despite not being authorized to attend meetings held there.
According to the complaint, Alfozan also used a productivity tool to search for information about OpenAI's offices, meeting rooms, executive locations, and meeting schedules.
The complaint also says a chatbot account associated with Alfozan's spouse was used to ask questions about building and concealing recording devices.
These included inquiries about creating a continuous audio recorder, modifying Wi-Fi connectivity, improving live listening capabilities, and encrypting an SD card.
"The same chatbot account also submitted prompts specifically related to Recording Device 1, including its custom header and unique MAC address, between Sept. 27 and Sept. 28," alleges the DOJ.
On October 5, surveillance footage allegedly captured Alfozan returning to the conference room and looking behind the television where the device had been installed.
The complaint says that on that same day, OpenAI security employees discovered a second, similar recording device inside a bag Alfozan had left unattended in another room.
In a statement posted on X, OpenAI said it used its own AI models to investigate the suspicious device and help identify the employee responsible.
"We used our models to understand the device and where it had come from, identifying that a specific employee had planted it a few days earlier," OpenAI said.
The company said it terminated the employee and referred the incident to the FBI.
"At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data," OpenAI added.
If convicted, Alfozan faces up to five years in prison and a $250,000 fine.

articles.title: While WoW: Forever's Collector's Edition offers a game code, God of War Laufey's 'Collector's Box' is taking the GTA 6 approach and doesn't come with a copy of the game — 'Eventually the statue is going to be digital as well'
articles.text:
Like GTA 6, God of War Laufey's 'Collector's Box' doesn't come with a copy of the game, and fans are outraged — 'I see Rockstar is an inspiration for everyone'
The Collector's Box is priced at £130 / $149.99
- The God of War Laufey - Collector's Box has been revealed for £130 / $149.99
- The box doesn't include a copy of the game, just like Grand Theft Auto 6's collector's edition
- Fans are frustrated with the exclusion of the game from the collection, with some calling it "greedy"
Santa Monica Studio has revealed its God of War Laufey Collector's Box, and just like Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 collector's edition, the pricey package doesn't include the game.
The studio shared the "Collector's Box" in a social media post, confirming that the £130 / $149.99 package includes a light-up Faye statue, 51-card Oracle Deck, and a mini art book, noting that the God of War Laufey game is "sold separately."
That's the part of the announcement that has fans talking, with many sharing their frustration over yet another collector's edition that doesn't offer a physical or digital copy of the game.
"I remember when collector's editions used to come with games. Not liking this new trend," one user responded, as another wrote, "'Game sold separately?' ...man, [the] gaming industry is getting greedier and greedier."
The lack of physical games has been a point of contention ever since Sony announced its plans to stop producing game discs by January 2028. The PlayStation company isn't alone; Rockstar Games is also skipping physical discs for GTA 6, the biggest game launch of all time, and players will instead receive a code in the box, a decision that initially caused an uproar.
On top of that, the studio recently announced The Goodtime State – Vice City Collection, a £349 / $399 premium collector's box featuring exclusive merchandise and no game.
"I see Rockstar is an inspiration for everyone," one redditor said about the Laufey - Collector's Box.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Another said, "We need to stop calling these collectors edition when they dont include the game and start calling them over priced cash grabs."
For now, it doesn't look like every company is cutting out games from their expensive collector's editions; Blizzard, for example, is selling its World of Warcraft: Forever's Collector's Edition with a digital download code included, and Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis's version will also offer a physical copy and steelbook alongside other goodies.
Still, fans are particularly worried about the future of collector's editions, which used to typically offer more than just a pretty statue and artbook.
"They [Santa Monica Studio] soft launched this back in Ragnarok, when the collector's edition only had a download code, same for Horizon Forbidden West. Eventually the statue is going to be digital as well," remarked a fan.

articles.title: Google transforme Gemini : discuter ne suffit plus, l’IA veut désormais agir à votre place
articles.text:
Le géant du Web commence à intégrer plus étroitement Spark dans l’application Gemini sur Android. L’objectif est de permettre de basculer plus facilement d’une conversation à une tâche confiée à l’IA, puis d’en suivre l’avancement au même endroit.
Jusqu’ici, discuter avec Gemini et lui confier une vraie mission restaient deux expériences assez séparées. Google commence à les rapprocher. Selon 9to5Google, une nouvelle interface apparaît progressivement sur Android afin de faire remonter Spark au cœur de l’assistant, plutôt que de le laisser vivre dans un coin du menu.
Le changement semble être activé côté serveur. Aucun équivalent n’a encore été repéré sur iOS ou sur le Web, ce qui laisse penser à un déploiement progressif plutôt qu’à une simple expérimentation interne.
Discuter ou déléguer sans changer d’espace
Deux boutons prennent désormais place au-dessus du champ de saisie. Chat conserve le fonctionnement classique de Gemini, tandis que Task ouvre directement Spark.
L’ancienne entrée dédiée disparaît du menu latéral et les conversations comme les tâches se retrouvent dans un historique commun. Des filtres permettent ensuite de retrouver les tâches prêtes, celles encore en cours et celles qui réclament une intervention de l’utilisateur.
À gauche (ou en haut sur mobile), l’interface de Gemini avec l’agent Spark et, à droite, la version française.
Google regroupe également les actions programmées dans une rubrique Scheduled. L’utilisateur peut ainsi lancer une conversation ou une tâche depuis le même écran, puis retrouver les deux dans un historique commun.
Spark peut continuer à travailler sans vous
Il peut, par exemple, trier des newsletters, préparer une veille récurrente ou aller chercher des informations dans Gmail, Drive et Agenda. Son navigateur lui permet également d’interagir avec certains sites.
Cette intégration aux services Google constitue évidemment l’un de ses principaux atouts, mais elle implique aussi de lui ouvrir l’accès aux données nécessaires. Certaines actions sensibles réclament donc une confirmation, notamment lorsqu’il s’agit d’envoyer un message ou d’effectuer un achat.
En France, il faudra encore patienter pour utiliser Spark. L’agent n’y est pas disponible, même avec un abonnement Google AI Pro ou Ultra, et cette refonte n’annonce pas son arrivée chez nous. Dans les pays où il est proposé, il faut souscrire l’une de ces formules et avoir au moins 18 ans pour y accéder.
Claude et ChatGPT suivent la même direction
Google n’est évidemment pas seul à vouloir transformer son assistant en exécutant numérique. Claude Cowork peut déjà mener des tâches en plusieurs étapes, travailler sur des fichiers autorisés et produire des documents tout en laissant l’utilisateur suivre son avancement.
OpenAI pousse une logique comparable avec ses dots, conçus pour poursuivre des projets dans la durée sur leur propre environnement cloud et revenir vers l’utilisateur lorsqu’une décision humaine devient nécessaire.
Mistral avance également sur ce terrain avec Vibe qui rassemble assistance au travail, programmation et automatisations récurrentes, avec des capacités plus avancées réservées aux offres payantes.
Tous cherchent finalement à franchir la même étape. Après avoir appris à répondre à nos questions, les assistants veulent maintenant faire le travail à notre place, vraiment ?
- Multimodalité texte, voix et fichiers
- Intégration poussée aux services Google
- Applications Web, mobile et bureau

articles.title: Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse is a successful resurrection, but not without faults
articles.text:
This year has been quite the story for dormant platformer franchises, especially Castlevania.
It’s been nearly 20 years since we’ve had a single-player Metroidvania-style Castlevania game. My introduction to the franchise was with Symphony of the Night over a decade ago, and since then, I was hooked. It’s a prime example of a sublime platformer game, with perfect controls, interesting world-building and a rich atmosphere.
Since then, I’ve played through the various Castlevania games led by Koji Igarashi, who spearheaded the Metroidvania titles, including his spiritual successor, Bloodstained: Ritual of the Night. Despite the lack of Castlevania video game releases, though, the franchise itself was still active through various other media, including the fantastic Netflix TV series and video game collaborations.
The most famous of these collaborations was with Dead Cells, a roguelite (where players get randomized gear during each run) game inspired by the Metroidvania genre. After rave reviews (though I personally haven’t played it), it felt fitting for Konami to give Castlevania the “Sonic Mania” treatment with the creators of Dead Cells taking the helm for the newest iteration, Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse.
How does it compare to its previous iterations or even the endless Metroidvania games out there now? Well, it has its highs and lows that will ultimately determine whether you really jive with it.
A rose has its thorns
Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse stars Rose Belmont, daughter of Trevor Belmont from Castlevania III: Dracula’s Curse. This game is a continuation of that story, taking place in 1499 after the events that transpired in Curse of Darkness. While Belmont’s Curse is a Metroidvania, it is structured differently compared to the previous Igarashi-led titles.
Rose Belmont is more than a capable fighter. Outside of the usual moveset, she can also wall climb and perform a double dodge. Rose can later unlock more movement capabilities, including the featured grapple hook (or rather, grapple whip).
Adding to her arsenal are three healing potions that can be used with a simple button press. These refill after using a save point, and you can collect three additional potions as an item drop. Gone is the traditional inventory system where you can keep various items to use throughout your journey. Instead, drops are immediate recovery items for health and mana.
This also applies to collecting weapons and accessories, which is a positive. One of the more frustrating design choices with the older games was that there were various items or abilities that you could only get through a specific enemy with a one per cent drop rate.
Belmont’s Curse takes a different approach by having seven unique weapon types that you can find throughout the game. Each weapon also has its own abilities that can be combined with your grapple whip. On top of this, Rose also has access to magic through her tarot cards. These are acquired by defeating bosses and can be further improved by completing various challenges throughout the game.
However, if you thought Rose’s enhanced loadout would lead to an easy experience, you would be wrong. Belmont’s Curse is tough.
For starters, bosses and common enemies hit a lot harder, echoing classic Castlevania titles where you have to be more methodical with your actions. If you try to furiously attack like a blithering idiot, your chances of surviving are slim to none unless you level grind. This added difficulty is also incorporated in the level design with various platforming challenges and puzzles that are genuinely testing.
This is where Belmont’s Curse could be divisive since platforming challenges are forced onto the player, especially after receiving movement upgrades. I liked that it tested your platforming skills, and the game does provide shortcuts once you complete the platforming challenges at hand. However, if these are too difficult, you can solve some of these issues with accessibility features that can scale your journey to be easier or harder if you’re a masochist.
Despite this, fans of the series will adore the world-building as told through the level design and tarot card system. Besides the main story and references in Dracula’s Castle, Belmont’s Curse incorporates lots of dialogue through Rose’s interaction with these tarot cards, not only adding to her own development but also contextualizing certain characters in the Castlevania lore.
While the story itself isn’t particularly complex, Rose’s interactions with characters in this game were outstanding and always left a smile on my face.
Both a blessing and a curse
One of my issues with Belmont’s Curse isn’t with the platforming, but rather the lack of movement upgrades in its first half. This leads to my overall problem with this game: the map is simply too big.
Paris (which includes the streets, catacombs and cemetery) is a slog on your first playthrough, taking around three hours because of the platforming challenges, boss fights and no movement upgrade besides the whip. Blind exploration is also encouraged, especially since the tarot card hint system doesn’t entirely point you in the right direction.
I appreciate Belmont’s Curse being more open-ended. However, without more movement upgrades, traversing around the map ends up being tiresome. Belmont’s Curse’s pacing would’ve drastically improved if the catacombs and cemetery were cut, with the streets of Paris serving as the intro stage. Since the game truly hits its stride after entering Dracula’s Castle (where you start getting more movement upgrades), it wouldn’t have been a big loss.
Belmont’s Curse is a good game that I really wish I loved more.
On one hand, I really enjoy the challenging platforming and combat because it’s a fresh yet familiar experience that combines both the Metroidvania genre and the original classic Castlevania gameplay. But on the other hand, Belmont’s Curse is bloated, with puzzles that can feel grating or downright unsolvable because of its open-ended design.
Before you cue the obvious “bad gaming journalist” joke, let me explain two puzzles that soured my experience towards the end.
The first puzzle is about a hidden mystery in an area after completing the main objective. My entire map is nearly 100 per cent complete except for that one segment. I’ve spent literally hours combing through the map again for any missing hints and overanalyzing past tarot card hints just to trigger something. This remains unsolved. The other puzzle involves a tarot card where you seemingly need to interact with specific safe rooms. Except, there’s no indication on what to do, despite me trying literally everything.
This is increasingly frustrating when this tarot card is linked to the third ending, leading to an overall half-baked finale. This is one that I’m convinced is bugged because there is no way the developers would make it this convoluted for a tarot card. However, there’s no way to tell since the tarot card hints and a less-than-useful ring accessory are the only tip systems the game offers.
Overall, Belmont’s Curse is best described as a game that delivers incredibly high moments but underlying issues can sour your experience depending on what you get out of a Metroidvania. Still, I’m incredibly happy that this game exists and hopefully, we continue to get more Castlevania games in the future.
Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse launches on Oct. 15 for Nintendo Switch, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S and PC through Steam.
