articles.title: New Apple Home Collection includes smart cameras, door lock, and thermostats made by LG and Schneider Electric
articles.text:
The big picture: Apple unveiled a range of smart home hardware built around Siri AI and Apple Intelligence at its 'Welcome Home' event in New York City today. The products signal the company's newfound focus on the smart home segment, after years spent largely on the sidelines of a market dominated by Google, Amazon, Samsung. and many other specialized vendors.
The Apple Home Collection is a lineup of smart-home devices built in collaboration with LG and Schneider Electric, including several cameras with full iCloud+ integration, as well as thermostats, a doorbell, and a door lock. Apple also introduced the second-generation HomePod mini, a new Apple TV 4K, and the HomeView smart-home display and hub.
The camera lineup includes both indoor and outdoor models from LG, starting with the Floodlight Cam, which pairs dual floodlights with motion detection for perimeter monitoring. The lights switch on automatically when motion is detected, and a color night vision mode helps capture clear footage in low light.
The other two cameras are the Outdoor Cam and the Indoor Cam. The former offers the same low-light color night vision, minus the floodlights. The latter can automatically tilt up and down to adjust its view when users check in on their home. It can also be tilted manually or through the Home app on iPhone.
Apple also announced two new smart thermostats, one from LG and another from Schneider Electric. Both can be controlled through the Home app on iPhone, and both can adjust temperatures automatically using on-device intelligence, depending on whether anyone is home. Both work with a wide range of HVAC systems.
Next up is the Video Doorbell Wired, which uses dual cameras to capture separate views of visitors and packages. The front camera records in 2.5K, while the bottom camera supports full HD. It also has a built-in spotlight and a chime that plays through HomeView, HomePod, and HomePod mini.
As for the Smart Deadbolt Lock, LG uses Ultra Wideband technology to sense when someone carrying a Home Key on a compatible iPhone or Apple Watch is approaching, and unlocks the door automatically, with no tapping or passcode needed.
In the US, the LG Video Doorbell Wired and Smart Deadbolt Lock start at $230 and $350, respectively, while the Floodlight Cam starts at $400. The Outdoor Cam Plug-In starts at $300 and the Indoor Cam Plug-In at $200. Both thermostats start at $200, and the LG Temperature Sensor and Schneider Home Room Sensor each start at $40.
The Apple Home Collection arrives in December, with select accessories following in early 2027. The doorbell and cameras will be sold in the US, Canada, and the UK, while the lock and thermostats are limited to the US and Canada at launch.
Finally, Apple announced the HomePod mini 2, with support for Siri AI arriving in a future software update. Powered by the S10 chip, the second-gen speaker improves on its predecessor with better audio quality and four-speaker surround sound when paired with the new Apple TV 4K and either four HomePod mini 2 or HomePod (2nd-gen) speakers. It costs $149, up from $99 for the original, and is available to pre-order today, with in-store availability beginning Friday, October 30.

articles.title: La preventa del iPhone Duo arranca este viernes 16 de octubre de 2026: el primer plegable de Apple cada vez más cerca
articles.text:
Apple iniciará la preventa del iPhone Duo, su primer teléfono plegable, el viernes 16 de octubre de 2026. La compañía, dirigida por John Ternus, lo ofrecerá desde USD 1.999 y comenzará a venderlo el viernes 23 de octubre.
El precio variará según la capacidad de almacenamiento:
- 256 GB: USD 1.999
- 512 GB: USD 2.199
- 1 TB: USD 2.599
- 2 TB: USD 3.199
Cuando está plegado, el equipo cuenta con una pantalla externa de 5,4 pulgadas que ofrece el 90% de la superficie de pantalla del iPhone 18 Pro, en un diseño compacto que cabe en el bolsillo. Como ambas pantallas comparten la misma relación de aspecto, el contenido se adapta de forma proporcional para mantener la continuidad visual.
Características del iPhone Duo
El iPhone Duo es el primer teléfono plegable de Apple y combina una pantalla exterior de 5,4 pulgadas con un panel interior de 7,6 pulgadas.
Cuando está cerrado, ofrece el 90% de la superficie de pantalla del iPhone 18 Pro en un formato compacto; al abrirse, amplía el espacio disponible para ver contenido, jugar y usar varias aplicaciones a la vez.
Ambas pantallas Super Retina XDR comparten la misma relación de aspecto, por lo que el contenido se ajusta de manera proporcional al plegar o desplegar el equipo.
Incluyen tecnología ProMotion, pantalla siempre activa y un brillo máximo de 3.000 nits en exteriores. Además, la pantalla interior tiene un acabado nanotexturizado que reduce los reflejos y minimiza la visibilidad del pliegue.
Apple fabricó el dispositivo con titanio de grado 5, Ceramic Shield en la parte posterior y Ceramic Shield 2 en el frente.
El teléfono cuenta con certificación IP68 de resistencia al agua, las salpicaduras y el polvo. Su bisagra, compuesta por más de 100 piezas, fue diseñada para controlar la apertura y reforzar la estructura.
El sistema fotográfico incorpora una cámara Fusion principal de 48 MP, con teleobjetivo de calidad óptica de 2x, y una cámara Fusion ultra gran angular de 48 MP para capturas más amplias y fotografías macro.
Suma una cámara frontal Center Stage, que permite tomar fotos y grabar videos en cualquier orientación sin girar el teléfono.
El iPhone Duo puede grabar video 4K Dolby Vision a 120 fps y ofrece efectos cinematográficos que pueden aplicarse después de la grabación. Su diseño plegable permite apoyar el equipo sobre una superficie para realizar videollamadas o grabar sin trípode.
Touch ID está integrado en el botón lateral, mientras que el Control de la Cámara permite abrir rápidamente la app fotográfica.
El equipo utiliza el chip A20 Pro, un sistema de cámara de vapor y dos baterías que funcionan como una sola.
Apple afirma que ofrece hasta 31 horas de reproducción de video con la pantalla interior y hasta 44 horas con la exterior. iOS 27 incorpora Split View para usar dos apps lado a lado, compatibilidad con Apple Intelligence y una nueva versión de Siri capaz de interpretar el contexto personal del usuario.
Apple lanza nuevos dispositivos para el hogar
Apple presentó Apple Home Collection, una línea de accesorios para hogares inteligentes desarrollada junto con LG Electronics y Schneider Electric. La línea incluye cámaras para interiores y exteriores, timbres con cámara, cerraduras inteligentes, termostatos y sensores de temperatura y humedad.
La línea de LG incorpora cuatro cámaras capaces de grabar video en resolución de hasta 2,5K. Los dispositivos pueden identificar personas, rostros conocidos, mascotas, vehículos y paquetes.
Ofrecen hasta 10 días de historial de video mediante planes compatibles de iCloud+ y almacenamiento local para mantener las grabaciones aun cuando se interrumpa la conexión Wi-Fi.
La cerradura Smart Deadbolt Lock de LG utiliza tecnología de banda ultraancha para reconocer cuándo el usuario se aproxima a la puerta.
Puede desbloquearse automáticamente con una llave de casa guardada en un iPhone o Apple Watch compatible, además de contar con teclado numérico y una llave física de respaldo.
Apple también anunció termostatos inteligentes de LG y Schneider Electric. Estos equipos ajustan la temperatura según la presencia de personas, los horarios de descanso o la ausencia de residentes. Los sensores adicionales permiten medir la temperatura y humedad en diferentes habitaciones.

articles.title: Oportunidade: AirPods 4 com ANC aparece pelo menor preço que já vimos • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Oportunidade: AirPods 4 com ANC aparece pelo menor preço que já vimos
Apple AirPods 4 com cancelamento ativo de ruído, Áudio Espacial e bateria de até 30 horas têm menor preço divulgado pelo Achados, com desconto de 37% no Pix na Amazon
Os AirPods 4 com ANC estão saindo por apenas R$ 1.259 no Pix na Amazon. Os fones de ouvido da Apple, que oferecem experiência imersiva e com menos ruído, alcançam o menor preço já divulgado pelo Achados e o menor desde abril de 2026 segundo o Zoom, com desconto de 37% sobre o original de R$ 1.999.
Lançado em 2024, este modelo dos Apple AirPods 4 conta com cancelamento ativo de ruído (ANC), recurso que usa os microfones para captar e filtrar ruídos externos para tornar o áudio limpo e livre de interferências. O recurso também está presente nos novos AirPods 5, mas atualizado e mais preciso.
O chip H2 também aprimora a experiência sonora geral, com destaque para o recurso de Áudio Espacial, que usa rastreamento dinâmico da cabeça para emular o ambiente ao redor do usuário, a fim de oferecer sons mais imersivos.
Vale anotar que, por questões de segurança, o recurso de isolamento de sons externos deixa passar ruídos que podem impactar na rotina diária, como os de trânsito, enquanto barra os de baixa frequência.
O estojo dos Apple AirPods 4 com ANC ficou 10% mais compacto em comparação à geração anterior e usa uma porta USB-C para carregamento, enquanto os AirPods 5 oferecem uma versão que suporta carregamento sem fio. O case fornece carga para 30 horas de uso, segundo a Apple.
Os fones usam a Siri para executar ações com movimentos, como balançar a cabeça para atender ou recusar ligações. Esse recurso é bastante útil para quando não for possível acessar o dispositivo pareado ou usar comandos de voz. Os AirPods 5, por sua vez, suportam tradução em tempo real.
Os Apple AirPods 4 com ANC (apenas R$ 1.259 no Pix) contam com certificação IP54, que adiciona resistência moderada contra poeira, respingos de água e de suor.
Aviso de ética: ao clicar em um link de afiliado, o preço não muda para você e recebemos uma comissão.

articles.title: Thermaltake Launches the OB360 AIO Liquid Cooler
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 13th 2026
Thermaltake Launches the OB360 AIO Liquid Cooler
Thermaltake, a leading PC DIY brand for premium hardware solutions, introduces the OB360 AIO Liquid Cooler, combining powerful cooling performance with refined industrial aesthetics. Featuring a 360 mm single-frame fan design, support for up to 360 W TDP, and distinctive textured detailing, the OB360 simplifies installation while delivering efficient thermal management. Its black, non-RGB design offers a minimalist and understated look for modern PC builds.
Industrial Textured Aesthetics
The OB360 features a black water block with diagonal textured grooves that create a distinctive finish. Embossed detailing on the fan frame complements the water block, establishing a cohesive industrial aesthetic throughout the cooling assembly.Single-Frame Fan Design
The OB360 integrates three 120 mm high static pressure PWM fans into a single 360 mm frame, simplifying installation and reducing cable clutter. The unified structure makes fan installation easier and helps keep the interior organized.
Powerful Cooling Performance
Engineered to support thermal loads of up to 360 W TDP, the OB360 combines high static pressure fans with PWM speed control for efficient heat dissipation. Each fan delivers up to 53.9 CFM of airflow and 2.36 mm-H₂O of static pressure, with a maximum noise level of 32.3 dB-A. Operating between 500 and 2000 RPM, the fans dynamically adjust their speed to meet varying cooling demands.
Slim Radiator for Effective Heat Dissipation
The OB360 incorporates a 27 mm slim radiator with a thickened 20 mm copper chamber, designed to facilitate efficient heat dissipation while maintaining a compact profile. The slim construction supports easier installation and provides greater flexibility for integration into compatible chassis.
High-Performance Pump and Copper Base Plate
The OB360 features a high-performance PWM pump operating between 1500 and 2500 RPM to maintain consistent coolant circulation. Paired with a copper base plate for effective thermal transfer from the CPU, the cooling system helps maintain stable temperatures under demanding workloads.
Minimalist Black Design for Non-RGB Builds
Designed for users who prefer a non-RGB setup, the OB360 features a black finish without integrated lighting. Its understated industrial styling complements minimalist and performance-focused PC builds, maintaining a cohesive look without RGB lighting effects.
Features of the OB360 AIO Liquid Cooler
- Diagonal textured grooves and embossed fan frame detailing create a refined industrial aesthetic.
- Supports up to 360 W TDP for demanding cooling applications.
- Single-frame design integrates three 120 mm high static pressure PWM fans into one module.
- Each fan delivers up to 53.9 CFM of airflow and 2.36 mm-H₂O of static pressure.
- PWM fan speeds from 500 to 2000 RPM provide responsive cooling performance.
- 27 mm slim radiator with a thickened 20 mm copper chamber supports efficient heat dissipation.
- PWM pump operates from 1500 to 2500 RPM for consistent coolant circulation.
- Copper baseplate enables effective thermal transfer from the CPU.
- The black, non-RGB design complements minimalist, performance-focused builds.

articles.title: Science Corporation implants its vision-restoring chip in its first Stargardt disease patient | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Science Corporation CEO Max Hodak announced that the company has implanted its vision-restoring chip, PRIMA, into its first patient with Stargardt disease, an inherited eye disease that gradually destroys central vision. Hodak, the former president and co-founder of Neuralink, the brain implant company, explained onstage at TechCrunch Disrupt how the company’s work with PRIMA fits into its broader pursuit of a novel brain-computer interface (BCI).
“The retina is part of the central nervous system,” Hodak said. “We consider cochlear implants, retinal prostheses, motor prostheses, these are all different types of BCIs.”
Hodak outlined a vision in which BCIs expand into a wide range of medical technology applications, rather than simply being a way to control computers.
While PRIMA is commercially available in Europe for patients who’ve lost their sight to geographic atrophy, an advanced form of age-related macular degeneration, the company believes its approach can be applied to multiple diseases, including Stargardt disease, which is currently considered incurable.
Stargardt disease affects the outer retina, causing the gradual death of the eye’s light-sensing cells while potentially sparing the inner retina, the part that passes visual signals onto the brain. It causes a central blind spot that gradually enlarges over time. Approximately 150,000 people worldwide have lost vision due to the disease.
“One of the nice things about this device approach, when I was saying the brain’s a computer, vision is electrical potential, like electrical activity down the optic nerve,” Hodak said. “That’s all vision is to the brain, and so if you can get the optic nerve to signal the rest of the brain correctly, then you can provide vision to it.”
The company says its first patient with Stargardt disease received the PRIMA implant in May as part of its ongoing trial at the Sydney Eye Hospital in Australia. During the patient’s first rehabilitation session, he saw a letter, and during the second, he was able to read a word.
To use the device, patients undergo an hourlong procedure that plants a small chip in the back of their eye, where the photoreceptors have degenerated. Then they wear camera-equipped glasses that transmit a view of the world to the chip. The implant essentially works like artificial photoreceptors.
“The device that this patient has is a two millimeter by two millimeter implant placed in the back of the eye, and so it’s like looking through a straw,” Hodak said. “It is not a big field of view color vision. It’s a patch in their central vision where … it’s black and white, but it is sharp. It’s high-contrast sharp, and so they can see a couple letters at a time. The next step is to make the field of view bigger. So to make a bigger implant, you have to deal with the curvature of the eye, and we need to make the electrodes smaller so that we get closer to native levels of detail.”
He continued, “I think we have a clear path. There’s a ‘next generation’ that’s being worked on that’ll be in humans in the next year, and over the next five years, I think we’ll be able to get pretty close to native acuity.”
When Hodak founded Science Corporation in 2021 after leaving Neuralink, the company outlined plans to develop advanced neural engineering and brain-computer interface technology. But first, the company wants to prove its methods work and develop a sustainable business, which is why it’s working to restore vision with the visually impaired.
As for Science Corporation’s brain-computer interface technology, it has previously said that its sensor will be implanted inside the skull and rest on top of the brain, unlike a Neuralink device, which is inserted directly into brain tissue.
The company has said it believes the device could help address neurological conditions, such as possibly monitoring neurological activity in patients with brain tumors.
“In the near term, we’re going to be applying our first clinical indication, which hasn’t been announced publicly, is a neurodegenerative disease that everybody’s heard of,” Hodak said. “We’re also looking at stroke. For example, if you’ve lost part of your brain because it’s been dead due to stroke, if you can get connections into the deep brain in two different areas, you can imagine adding new cortical areas, just like adding new brain areas entirely — something simply not possible with conventional electrodes. But, I’d say longer term, the long-term mission of the company is to understand how the brain creates the mind and to learn to build engineered brains.”
Hodak went on to note that Science Corporation’s belief is that many people will eventually use some kind of BCI. While the company isn’t designing for “healthy 40-year-olds,” he said, it believes people will eventually need some kind of BCI by the age of 60 or 70.
“We want to figure out how do we extend not just lifespan but health span,” Hodak said.

articles.title: No Man's Sky is coming to iPhone and iPad
articles.text:
No Man’s Sky will fly onto iPhones and iPads on Oct. 28, developer Hello Games has announced.
In a blog post, the studio outlined the new ports, which come just over 10 years after the space exploration game debuted on PS4 and PC. Impressively, No Man’s Sky will work on iPhone 11 and 3rd-generation iPad Air and above, albeit with some limitations.
In particular, multiplayer isn’t available on Apple devices, while Planetary Settlements, which are alien towns that the player can build and manage, are only supported on iPhone 15 Pro and above.
Still, it’s commendable that so much of this vast and ever-expanding game is playable on Apple’s mobile devices. In addition to having streamlined touch controls, Hello Games says it will offer support for controllers, TV casting and even mouse and keyboard on iPad.
The game will also be free to try at launch and come in at under 4GB.
The No Man’s Sky Apple ports come as Hello Games toils away at its next game, Light No Fire. The open-world adventure MMO is currently in development for PC, although no release window has been confirmed.

articles.title: VPN dark web alerts vs. free tools: Are you paying extra for repackaged data?
articles.text:
VPN dark web alerts vs. free tools: Are you paying extra for repackaged data?
VPN providers are increasingly selling “dark web alerts” as premium security features, marketing them as essential protection against identity theft. This raises a key question: do paid alerts find unique threats, or just repackage data that's freely available?
With subscriptions to the best VPNs already costing up to $10-15 monthly, adding identity protection features can push bills toward $20 a month. If you’re essentially paying for data available at no cost, that’s money better spent elsewhere.
This article is the third in a series of content relating to Cybersecurity Awareness Month 2026, which runs throughout October. The previous articles have covered VPN protection when using AI, and the benefits of dedicated antivirus over packaged solutions.
How dark web monitoring works
Let’s clear up a common misconception first: VPN services aren’t sending security analysts to actively patrol the dark web hunting for your name. That would be impossible – the dark web is too vast and constantly shifting.
Instead, what most dark web monitoring services actually do is simpler: they cross-reference your information against massive databases of leaked credentials that have already been publicly disclosed. These databases contain billions of compromised accounts from data breaches spanning over a decade.
The monitoring happens automatically. You register your identifiers – such as your email address, phone number, or social security number – the service scans these databases periodically, and sends you an alert if a match appears.
The free option: Have I Been Pwned
For free breach checks, Have I Been Pwned (HIBP) has become the industry benchmark. Created by security researcher Troy Hunt in 2013, this free service hosts nearly 18 billion compromised email addresses from hundreds of publicized breaches. Checking is free and requires no account.
Where it gets interesting for continuous tracking is Mozilla Monitor, which runs entirely on HIBP’s data.
Since launching in 2018, Mozilla’s free service has helped people in 237 countries identify exposed information. You can sign up for email notifications that ping you whenever your address shows up in a breach – essentially the core functionality paid services advertise.
Several VPN providers have acknowledged using this same foundation. ExpressVPN Keys explicitly integrates with HIBP for both email breach and password detection, while CyberGhost Identity Guard is described in their documentation as being “powered by Have I Been Pwned.”
Yet not all vendors are relying on public data alone. Domininkas Virbickas, Product Director at NordVPN, said they track “more than 40,000 sources around the clock” and that “most of this data never reaches the public breach databases people can check for free.”
When to pay for premium alerts
That doesn’t mean paid services lack value. Having breach alerts built into an app you already use for VPN protection eliminates another password and dashboard to manage.
If you’re already paying for a VPN subscription, adding monitoring for free or minimal extra cost is efficient. You don’t need to remember to check another website or log into a separate service.
While HIBP updates regularly, paid services may offer faster notifications. Minutes matter when someone steals your credentials – they can try accessing accounts immediately.
That head start can mean the difference between resetting your password on your own terms versus dealing with account recovery after unauthorized access.
Finally, there’s the distinction between basic email alerts and full identity theft protection.
Free services like HIBP notify you about email addresses appearing in breaches. Paid identity protection packages often go much further, including SSN monitoring, credit file locks, bank account number tracking, and even identity theft insurance.
Coveron, which partners with NordVPN for identity protection on premium plans, adds credit monitoring, flags suspicious credit inquiries, and includes identity theft insurance.
Similarly, services like Norton’s LifeLock monitor multiple data types – phone numbers, SSNs, financial accounts – and provide guided recovery steps if something goes wrong.
The verdict
Don’t pay extra for a VPN subscription to get basic email breach alerts. If you want to monitor whether your credentials have been exposed, free tools like Have I Been Pwned or Mozilla Monitor do the same job at no cost.
However, if you’re already paying for a VPN and the dark web monitoring is included at no additional charge, there’s no reason not to enable it. If you genuinely need identity theft protection, then premium services justify their cost with features free tools simply don’t offer.
So the question isn’t whether free tools work for basic breach checking – they do. It’s whether you need the expanded coverage, faster alerts, and recovery support that paid services provide.
For most people, starting with free monitoring makes sense. You can always upgrade later if your threat profile warrants it.
Mark is a Tech Security Writer for TechRadar and has been published on Comparitech and IGN. He graduated with a degree in English and Journalism from the University of Lincoln and spent several years teaching English as a foreign language in Spain. The Facebook-Cambridge Analytica data scandal sparked Mark’s interest in online privacy, leading him to write hundreds of articles on VPNs, antivirus software, password managers, and other cybersecurity topics. He recently completed the Google Cybersecurity Certificate, and when he's not studying for the CompTIA Security+ exam, Mark can be found agonizing over his fantasy football team selections, watching the Detroit Lions, and battling bugs and bots in Helldivers 2.

articles.title: Amperesand Aims to Smooth AI Data Center Power Spikes - EE Times
articles.text:
Singapore-based solid-state transformer (SST) startup Amperesand aims to help AI data centers smooth the spikes in their electrical demand that can stress power grids.
“When a glitch happens, we don’t just kick off the grid; we actually power the AI load with a battery,” Amperesand CEO Brian Dow told EE Times. “We also can pull power to keep the rate of change in the medium voltage under control.”
Dow noted a recent data center failure he hopes to help prevent: a July 2026 grid disconnection in the U.S. state of Virginia that caused data centers to automatically switch to backup generators, dropping a more-than 3-gigawatt load in seconds that caused power to flicker across the eastern U.S.
“A gigawatt is probably the power consumption of Cincinnati,” Dow said. “It’d be like Cincinnati turning all its lights on and off at every single load, simultaneously.”
SSTs are set to enter AI data centers as traditional transformers made of copper coils and magnetic iron cores struggle to meet rising demands for efficiency, power density, and scalability. Increasing rack power levels and fluctuating AI workloads cause energy losses, thermal challenges, and system complexity, power IC maker Microchip noted. SSTs directly convert medium-voltage grid power like 13.8 kV to 35 kV AC into high-voltage 800 VDC in a single step.
SSTs use wide-bandgap semiconductors such as silicon carbide (SiC) to replace conventional transformers with power electronic systems that enable intelligent control of power flow from a variety of sources including, potentially, a microgrid on the site of an AI data center.
“We can run in a microgrid,” Dow said. “We can take medium voltage off a turbine, or from the grid; we actually don’t care where it comes from, we’re like a universal power adapter.”
Supercharged
The SST segment has been “supercharged” after Nvidia, Google, and Microsoft last year announced an open-standard 800 VDC power architecture for next-generation AI data center racks, Xora Innovation chief investment officer Phil Inagaki told EE Times in an interview. Inagaki is Amperesand’s founding CEO turned board chair, who provided Xora’s venture capital to the 2023 startup as a bet on needed improvements in the AI infrastructure.
“A solid-state transformer takes AC power from the grid and can efficiently, safely convert it to DC,” Inagaki said. “It’s also bi-directional, and you can integrate battery or local generation, the grid, and your AI load. Rather than big magnets and copper wires, it is an intelligent device that can respond extremely quickly.”
The concept of solid-state transformers has been around for decades, but without the latest generation of power semiconductors, the practical implementation didn’t make sense, Inagaki noted.
Dow, a former Tesla executive, said he joined Amperesand last year to “transform the grid” by launching SSTs.
“At Tesla, we famously in the Model 3 built a huge production line that was super automated; the alien dreadnought, as Elon [Musk] called it, but it was very difficult to scale because it was so complex,” Dow said. “I learned from that lesson. Learned how to build your product, iterate rapidly. This facility in Reno, Nevada, that I’m in is where we’re doing just that. We build our power stages, power electronics converters, the SST system. We test it on site; we have a whole validation closed loop.”
Inside the SST
The Amperesand product is a modular power converter with blocks called power stage modules, or PSMs.
“Each PSM is a standardized element that has medium-voltage to low-voltage isolation in it, and a power conversion system that samples a portion of the AC waveform from the medium-voltage side and then produces a low-voltage output that’s galvanically isolated,” Dow said.
“You can stack them in series to modularly select the amount of voltage,” he continued. “It’s a very intelligent product, so all the modules interoperate as a set. They’re synchronized all very precisely to convert the waveforms. It’s not a rectifier; it’s a bidirectional power converter. Our design is very custom-targeted to the AI factory transition that’s occurring with 800 VDC and beyond.”
The company is aiming for 98.5% efficiency at full power.
“If you think of the traditional system that would do this, you would essentially have a transformer-rectifier combo, plus you’d have a converter for a battery backup,” Dow said. “We essentially replace a UPS by adding a battery to our unit.”
According to Dow, the company has a major hyperscaler among its first customers, but he declined to name it.
“We’re also partnering to test with them at a national laboratory this year, so we’re deploying the unit to a national lab,” Dow said. Among the company’s other first customers is a traditional electrical OEM.
“It’s one of the ‘Big Five’, I’ll say,” Dow added. “Think of ABB, Eaton, Schneider, Siemens [Dow did not name the fifth company]. They’ve taken a minority investment in our company. We’ve done a very significant partnership with them for multiple hyperscalers.”
Other applications
Amperesand is evaluating more applications in photovoltaics and battery energy storage systems.
“Those are two major verticals,” Dow said. “The photovoltaic industry is huge in terms of electrical scale, at 600 gigawatts a year plus capacity. It’s a very large total addressable market, one even bigger than data centers. But it’s also got a lot of commoditization; there’s a lot of competitors worldwide.”
The company is also working with a partner on port electrification.
“One thing that’s very interesting about ships is they run medium-voltage networks,” Dow said. “They’re like a city. They come to these ports, and they run their diesel engines while they’re unloading. A ship might pull anywhere from 7 to 10 megawatts of power while at dock. We have our first customer with that. That’ll be in late 2027.”
Amperesand has been talking with a power utility in California about another product, a 10- to 20-kilovolt transformer mounted on an electrical pole that could help to prevent forest fires.
“We can actually shut off a load automatically if there’s a fault during a fire season in California,” Dow said. “You can kill a line that runs through the mountains if there’s a fire-risk day.”

articles.title: Anthropic warns self-replicating AI could spread to your smart devices
articles.text:
Anthropic is warning that small AI models could soon be able to self-replicate across consumer IoT devices, from Android TV boxes to smart ovens, creating distributed botnets capable of running AI workloads without relying on data centers.
The company's experiments showed that models could identify unfamiliar devices, connect them into a network, and prepare them to run an AI model.
Although the researchers successfully distributed the Gemma4-26B-A4B model from Google DeepMind on 15 off-brand Android TV boxes, they did not demonstrate a fully autonomous, self-replicating AI worm running on real IoT hardware.
However, they estimate that smaller models could achieve self-replication by the end of the year if they continue to improve at their historical rate.
“Our experiments suggest that small AI models may be months away from being capable enough to self-replicate on commercial internet-of-things (IoT) devices, like smart ovens and off-brand Android TV boxes,” Anthropic warns.
“ A replicator like this would be challenging to shut down, since there’s no centralized point to shut off—though it may be slow (with a doubling time of days).”
Replication experiment
Anthropic ran its replication experiment using cheap Android TV boxes, and the AI models Qwen3.5-9B, Gemma4-26B-A4B, Llama3.1-8B, Opus 4.8, and GLM-5.2, each assigned a different role.
Qwen3.5-9B and GLM-5.2 acted as agents tasked with setting up and propagating Llama3.1-8B (inference), while Gemma4-26B-A4B demonstrated that a model could run across 15 Android TV boxes. Opus 4.8 was separately tested as an advisor to Qwen.
The experiment used a simplified setting where the targets exposed unauthenticated ADB access.
The experiments showed that Qwen3.5-9B successfully installed and configured the software needed to run Llama3.1-8B on eight of the nine hardware types tested.
GLM-5.2 reached all eight nodes in the controlled emulated network in four out of five trials, but the other models failed to complete the full process reliably.
Anthropic observed an improvement in success rate when it retained data from previous attempts, with Qwen3.5-9 B's success rate rising from 45% early on to 84% in later generations.
Using the stronger Opus 4.8 model to assist Qwen in inference produced no measurable improvement.
Based on the results and historical data, Anthropic predicts that models with 30 billion parameters or fewer could reach the necessary capability level by the end of 2026.
On the studied hardware, the inference setup would be a slow process, taking between 28 and 51 hours for Qwen3.5-9B, and 71-150 hours for Gemma4-26B-A4B, giving defenders enough time to detect and respond.
However, this time could shrink with future models, so implementing stronger security measures for IoT may soon become a priority.
Proposed defenses include detecting large model transfers and unusual device-to-device traffic, using honeypots to inspect payloads, quarantining infected subscribers, and improving IoT security defaults.
While Anthropic’s warning is not based on an imminent threat, as their experiment failed to demonstrate full end-to-end worm-creation capability at this stage, even with lowered security settings and explicit propagation goals, the message for better IoT security remains valid.

articles.title: Karnataka govt cautious on use of AI in governance: Priyank Kharge
articles.text:
Karnataka govt cautious on use of AI in governance: Priyank Kharge
The Minister for Home, IT, BT & E-Governance, Govt of Karnataka, said the government will first look at responsible use of AI before deploying the technology in governance.
The Karnataka government is being very cautious about using artificial intelligence (AI) in governance as it first needs to understand how this technology can be used responsibly, said Priyank Kharge, Minister for Home, IT, BT & E-Governance, Government of Karnataka.
During a fireside chat with Shradha Sharma, Founder & CEO, YourStory and The Bharat Project, at Techsparks 2026, Kharge remarked that the state government's cautiousness stems from the fact it owns an enormous amount of data across multiple sectors. “While I keep data privacy as part of the core and use models to develop agents or solutions, governance is very important,” the minister said.
However, this does not mean that the state government will not use AI in governance. The minister said the technology is being leveraged for basic issues such as citizen grievances, health, and mobility. He also said the government has set up a committee to study how to use AI responsibly in governance.
The minister highlighted that the Karnataka government is focused on building the much-needed skill base for AI and is engaged with several companies on this. “One knows how these models (AI) are going rogue; so we are cautious, but at the same time we are investing heavily in skilling,” he said.
“In the next couple of months, one will see a lot of startups and companies working with the government to solve problems,” the minister said.
The Karnataka government recently came out with a policy to engage with startups to solve certain governance challenges. The minister said it will adopt a sandbox environment wherein startups can build their solutions.
“If they (startups) succeed, I will ensure that it (solution) is taken across the state. But it should be a proven model and, more importantly, it should be solving real-life problems,” said Kharge.
The minister highlighted that startups possess the agility and out-of-the-box thinking to come out with innovative solutions. “I think startups deserve a chance to be with the government,” he remarked.

articles.title: Le nouveau film Street Fighter est presque aussi nul que celui avec JCVD (critique sans spoilers)
articles.text:
Il paraît que le film Street Fighter avec Jean-Claude Van Damme en tête d’affiche rapporte régulièrement de l’argent à Capcom, signe d’une postérité inattendue pour une adaptation aussi médiocre. En 2026, la firme nippone redonne sa chance à sa saga star, cette fois aux côtés du studio américain Legendary. Signée Kitao Sakurai, réalisateur de la comédie Bad Trip et de l’émission The Eric Andre Show, cette nouvelle tentative sort ce mercredi 14 octobre dans les salles obscures.
Jean-Claude Van Damme n’est pas de la partie dans ce reboot cinématographique, qui s’offre quand même quelques stars, à l’image de Jason Momoa (Blanka) ou du rappeur 50 Cent (Balrog). Malheureusement, ces quelques arguments ne suffiront pas à sauver Street Fighter, qui ne sait jamais vraiment s’il doit opter pour un ton sérieux ou assumer totalement son côté décalé. On se demande surtout à qui il s’adresse, puisqu’un néophyte n’y comprendra pas grand-chose.
Le nouveau film Street Fighter ne sait pas sur quel pied danser
Street Fighter débute par une séquence intégralement en animation, particulièrement réussie dans sa direction artistique. Kitao Sakurai fait un choix curieux en réservant ce style graphique aux flash-back. Un style qui impose une rupture de ton assez marquée : les affrontements sont bien mieux chorégraphiés et nettement plus violents et gore que les passages en prises de vues réelles. En résulte une cohabitation bancale, qui donnerait presque l’impression qu’il y a deux adaptations ne boxant pas du tout dans la même catégorie.
Ce n’est pas le seul sentiment étrange qui émane de Street Fighter, bien sûr articulé autour de combats entre les personnages phares des jeux vidéo. Du moins, quand on a la chance d’assister aux combats en question, étant donné que certains d’entre eux sont totalement éclipsés pour faire avancer une histoire bateau et prétexte. À la place, le long métrage empile les gags à l’humour douteux, notamment dans la relation entre Ken, le bouffon, et Ryu, le champion mystérieux. Le tout avec le running gag autour de la chanson What’s Up, du groupe 4 Non Blondes. «L’amitié entre hommes, c’est compliqué », entend-on. Oui, Street Fighter est parfois très, très gênant.
Plus grave, d’un point de vue purement narratif, Street Fighter ne prend jamais la peine d’expliquer son univers. C’est donc un très mauvais point d’entrée pour qui découvre la saga avec ce film. Tout est imposé comme si on savait déjà qui est qui. Certes, les fans esquisseront sans doute quelques sourires devant des références savoureuses, y compris dans les mouvements signatures des héros comme des méchants. Sur ce point, on peut souligner la fidélité dont fait preuve Kitao Sakurai, mais c’était le strict minimum à attendre d’une telle adaptation.
Les fans pesteront en revanche sur certains choix douteux. David Dastmalchian est ridicule, pour ne pas dire catastrophique, dans le rôle de M. Bison, sans aucun doute le seul rôle qui méritait un minimum de sérieux et de charisme. Le Blanka de Jason Momoa ne respecte pas vraiment la morphologie ou l’attitude du personnage vu dans les jeux vidéo, quand bien même le combat est réussi. Il n’y a peut-être que Callina Liang pour sortir du lot dans le costume de Chun-Li, grâce à un entraînement sans relâche pour assurer une performance physique réussie à l’écran. On a presque de la peine pour elle, perdue au milieu d’une bande d’acteurs aux allures de cosplayeurs.
Si on devait comparer, Mortal Kombat (2021) et, surtout, Mortal Kombat II (sorti en mai 2026) s’en sortent bien mieux, en dépit d’un univers encore plus absurde sur le papier. Ce Street Fighter se contente hélas d’aligner gags nuls et clips plus ou moins impressionnants dans un fourre-tout beaucoup trop indigeste pour devenir un simple plaisir coupable.
Le verdict
Street Fighter
Voir la fiche
On a aimé
- Les mouvements signatures sont là
- Les séquences en animation
- Callina Liang est parfaite en Chun-Li
On a moins aimé
- David Dastmalchian est catastrophique en M. Bison
- Des gags très, très gênants
- Des ellipses étranges

articles.title: Après plusieurs mois de travail, Surfshark achève la transition post-quantique de sa version de WireGuard
articles.text:
Surfshark annonce avoir complété la protection post-quantique de sa version de WireGuard. Après avoir sécurisé l’échange des clés en janvier, le fournisseur VPN protège désormais l’authentification de ses serveurs, sur macOS et iOS.
Vous le savez peut-être déjà, des données chiffrées interceptées aujourd’hui pourraient être déchiffrées dans plusieurs années si des ordinateurs quantiques suffisamment puissants venaient à voir le jour. Une perspective qui pousse déjà les fournisseurs de VPN à revoir les méthodes cryptographiques utilisées pour sécuriser leurs connexions. En janvier, Surfshark avait introduit une première protection post-quantique dans sa version de WireGuard, afin de sécuriser l’échange des clés de chiffrement face aux futures attaques. Le 7 octobre, l’entreprise a annoncé une nouvelle évolution, consacrée cette fois à la vérification de l’identité des serveurs VPN.
Après l’échange des clés, Surfshark sécurise l’identité des serveurs
Lorsqu’un appareil se connecte à un VPN, il doit s’assurer qu’il communique avec le bon serveur et établir avec lui une clé secrète pour chiffrer les échanges. Ces deux opérations reposent sur des procédés cryptographiques qui pourraient être compromis par les futurs ordinateurs quantiques.
Pour protéger l’échange des clés, Surfshark utilisait déjà ML-KEM, un algorithme conçu pour empêcher le déchiffrement ultérieur du trafic intercepté aujourd’hui, même à l’aide d’un ordinateur quantique suffisamment puissant.
Mais sécuriser cet échange ne protège pas automatiquement contre l’usurpation d’identité du serveur. Un attaquant capable de se faire passer pour un serveur de Surfshark pourrait alors chercher à intercepter les communications. Pour répondre à ce risque, Surfshark intègre désormais ML-DSA, un algorithme de signature numérique qui permet à l’application de vérifier l’authenticité du serveur auquel elle se connecte.
Les deux technologies, normalisées par le NIST en août 2024, reposent sur des méthodes mathématiques considérées comme résistantes aux attaques quantiques. ML-KEM protège l’établissement des clés, tandis que ML-DSA vise à empêcher la falsification des signatures utilisées pour authentifier le serveur. Surfshark estime ainsi avoir couvert les deux principales faiblesses cryptographiques de WireGuard face à la menace quantique.
Une protection complète, mais pas encore sur tous les appareils
Cette nouvelle version de WireGuard est disponible dans les applications Surfshark pour macOS et iOS. Pour en profiter, il suffit de sélectionner WireGuard dans les paramètres VPN de l’application, la protection post-quantique étant alors appliquée automatiquement. Les configurations manuelles de WireGuard ne sont pas concernées.
Le fournisseur prévoit d’étendre cette protection à d’autres systèmes, sans avoir communiqué de calendrier pour Windows, Android ou Linux. Son protocole propriétaire Dausos, actuellement disponible sur macOS, utilise déjà les deux algorithmes ML-KEM et ML-DSA.
Attention toutefois, ces améliorations concernent la version de WireGuard adaptée par Surfshark, et non le protocole standard. Par ailleurs, les algorithmes utilisés sont conçus pour résister aux attaques quantiques connues, mais cela n’exclut pas la découverte de nouvelles vulnérabilités, y compris dans leur implémentation.
- storage4500 serveurs
- language100 pays couverts
- lanConnexions simultanées illimitées
- moodGarantie de remboursement 30 jours
- thumb_upAvantage : idéal pour les foyers
Lancé en 2018, Surfshark est idéal pour les foyers disposant de nombreux appareils grâce à ses connexions simultanées illimitées. Il propose des applications compatibles avec les principales plateformes et intègre des fonctions adaptées à un usage courant. Son infrastructure évolue régulièrement pour maintenir une offre solide grand public.

articles.title: Galaxy S27 Ultra : Samsung améliorerait l’écran qui protège votre vie privée, mais à quel prix ?
articles.text:
Le Privacy Display est l’une des principales curiosités du Galaxy S26 Ultra et notre 01lab s’était penché sur ce filtre de confidentialité qui modifie la diffusion lumineuse. En l’activant, le smartphone cherche à rendre illisible le contenu pour les regards indiscrets et ça marche, même si cela ne vient pas sans sacrifices. Loin d’abandonner son idée, Samsung plancherait sur la deuxième version de cet écran anti-regards.
Selon le leaker Sawyer Galox sur X, Samsung travaillerait sur un « Privacy Display v2 » pour le Galaxy S27 Ultra avec trois améliorations notables : de meilleurs angles de vision, une meilleure résolution quand la protection est activée, et une qualité et une clarté d’écran accrues. Samsung n’a, pour l’heure, rien confirmé alors que son nouveau modèle arriverait début 2027.
 Samsung is working on improving
Galaxy S27 Ultra Privacy Display v.2
Improved viewing angles
Better resolution when Privacy Display is enabled
Improved screen quality and clarity
Well, there are good hardware upgrades next year, so the price will be between $1,400-$1,500 https://t.co/vSa9LAcpl1
— Sawyer Galox (@Sawyergalox) October 10, 2026
Une estimation de prix, pas un tarif
Sur le S26 Ultra, Samsung a modifié certains pixels pour qu’ils n’émettent que vers l’avant, et la protection éteint les autres. Le prix à payer, selon nos mesures, est que la moitié des pixels sont retirés, ce qui donne une lecture moins confortable sur les textes et les motifs fins, ainsi qu’un écran moins lumineux. La deuxième et la troisième promesse du leaker répondent au premier de ces compromis, pas au second : il ne dit rien de la luminosité ni de la façon dont Samsung compte s’y prendre.
Le premier point est plus flou et Sawyer Galox parle d’« angles de vision » sans préciser s’il s’agit d’élargir la zone où le propriétaire voit bien l’écran, ou de mieux masquer l’image aux voisins.
Le Privacy Display pourrait aussi sortir de l’Ultra puisque d’autres fuites évoquent son arrivée sur un Galaxy S27 Pro, absent de la gamme actuelle. Ice Universe affirme de son côté que le S27 Ultra pourrait ne masquer qu’une seule application en écran partagé, comme le propose déjà le Xiaomi 18 Pro.
Une estimation de son prix qui inquiète
Sawyer Galox s’avance aussi sur le prix et écrit que, vu les « bonnes améliorations matérielles » de l’an prochain, le tarif sera compris entre 1 400 et 1 500 dollars aux États-Unis. Une déduction plus qu’une fuite qui s’inscrirait dans la hausse des prix des smartphones. Depuis le 1er octobre, le S26 Ultra de 256 Go est vendu 1 399,99 dollars outre-Atlantique, contre 1 299,99 dollars à son lancement, en raison du prix de la mémoire. Le bas de la fourchette correspond donc au tarif actuel, et le haut à 100 dollars de plus.
En France, ce même modèle est passé de 1 469 à 1 569 euros début octobre, comme nous l’avons détaillé plus tôt ce mois-ci. Rappelons au passage que les prix américains s’entendent hors taxes et qu’il ne faut pas les convertir tels quels.
Samsung présenterait ses Galaxy S27 vers février 2027, avec One UI 9.5 basée sur Android 17.

articles.title: Haibike AllMtn 2 : ce nouveau VTT électrique tout-suspendu à moteur Bosch 120 Nm perd déjà 1 500 € — Frandroid
articles.text:
La gamme AllMtn, chez Haibike, vise les sorties où l’on grimpe longtemps avant de profiter de la descente. L’AllMtn 2 embarque un moteur Bosch Performance CX livré à 85 Nm, qui monte jusqu’à 120 Nm avec la mise à jour gratuite de Bosch, et une batterie de 800 Wh pour assurer un vrai soutien dans les montées les plus pentues. Il est actuellement affiché avec 1 500 euros de remise.
Les atouts du Haibike AllMtn 2
- Moteur Bosch Performance CX de 85 Nm (jusqu’à 120 Nm après mise à jour) et batterie de 800 Wh
- 160 mm de débattement à l’avant comme à l’arrière
- Freins SRAM DB4 à quatre pistons avec disques de 200 mm à l’avant et 203 mm à l’arrière
Au lieu de 4 299 euros (Haibike l’affiche même à 4 499 euros sur son site), le Haibike AllMtn 2 passe à 2 799,99 euros pendant la période de précommande sur le site d’Alltricks. Il sera livré à partir du jeudi 22 octobre.
Un vélo mulet réglé pour la descente
L’AllMtn 2 roule en configuration mulet, avec une roue de 29 pouces à l’avant et une de 27,5 pouces à l’arrière. La grande roue avant franchit plus facilement les racines et les cailloux, tandis que la petite roue arrière rend le vélo plus vif dans les virages serrés (et laisse un peu plus de place derrière la selle dans les passages raides). La géométrie va dans le même sens, avec un angle de direction de 64,5° et un cintre large de 800 mm. De quoi garder un vélo stable quand le terrain plonge.
Pour encaisser les chocs, Haibike a choisi une fourche Suntour Zeron36X de 160 mm et un amortisseur Suntour Edge-X R à l’arrière. Bon, Suntour n’a pas la même réputation que Fox ou RockShox chez les vététistes, et c’est un poste sur lequel certains voudront monter en gamme plus tard. Le reste de l’équipement est cohérent pour du all-mountain : pneus Continental Kryptotal (version Fr à l’avant, Re à l’arrière) en 60 mm de large, ainsi qu’une tige de selle télescopique dont la course va de 125 à 170 mm selon la taille.
Un moteur Bosch de 120 Nm pour avaler le dénivelé
Au niveau du pédalier, on trouve le moteur Bosch Performance CX, compatible avec l’écosystème Smart System de Bosch. Il est livré réglé à 85 Nm de couple, mais la mise à jour gratuite Performance Upgrade 2.0, disponible depuis mai 2026 dans l’application eBike Flow, permet de monter jusqu’à 120 Nm. Haibike prévient au passage que ce surplus de couple use plus vite la chaîne et les pignons. Il est alimenté par une batterie PowerTube de 800 Wh intégrée au tube diagonal. Alltricks n’indique pas d’autonomie chiffrée, ce qui est assez logique. Sur un VTT électrique, elle varie énormément selon le dénivelé, le mode d’assistance et le poids du pilote. Avec une telle capacité, les grosses sorties en montagne restent clairement envisageables.
La transmission Shimano Deore à 12 vitesses associe un plateau de 36 dents à une cassette 10-51, ce qui offre une large plage de développements pour les rampes les plus raides. Le freinage est confié à des étriers SRAM DB4 à quatre pistons, avec des disques de 200 mm à l’avant et de 203 mm à l’arrière. Deux réserves tout de même. L’écran Bosch Purion 200 est compact, et Alltricks ne communique pas le poids (le revendeur Kelvelo annonce 23,9 kg). Avec un cadre en aluminium et une batterie de 800 Wh, il ne faut pas s’attendre à un poids plume.
Si vous roulez surtout sur des chemins et des petites routes plutôt qu’en montagne, un tout-suspendu n’est pas forcément le plus adapté, et notre comparatif des meilleurs VTC électriques vous aidera à trouver un modèle plus polyvalent.

articles.title: En España cada vez hay más gente haciendo 200 kilómetros en coche todos los días para ir a trabajar
articles.text:
Vivir a 110 kilómetros del trabajo parece una forma de ahorrar, pero lo que se ahorra en alquiler se paga en coche, en tiempo y en sueño. Aunque hay quien prefiere conducir, como María Inmaculada Jiménez, quien lleva la gerencia de un restaurante en La Cala de Mijas (Málaga), pero vive en Mollina, en el interior de la provincia. Según contaba El Mundo, recorre 220 kilómetros diarios entre ida y vuelta para poder pagar una casa que en la costa no podría permitirse.
Es un caso extremo pero no aislado que en inglés denominan super-commuting. El problema es el de siempre: que la tecnología te permite vivir lejos del trabajo no significa nada en sí mismo. Porque la argolla sigue siendo la misma: salario insuficiente para pagar una casa.
A todos lados con portátil. Un estudio de Stanford sobre dos millones de trayectos en las diez mayores ciudades de EEUU detectó que los desplazamientos de 40 millas (unos 64 km) o más han pasado del 15,8% al 18,5% del total desde la pandemia. Los supercommutes de 75 millas (unos 120 km) o más han crecido casi un tercio hasta rondar el 3% de los trayectos, y suelen costar unas dos horas y veinte por sentido.
Quien no tiene que ir a la oficina cada día tolera un trayecto largo una o dos veces por semana si a cambio gana espacio y nivel de vida, claro. Según estos estudios, los más jóvenes y quienes tienen ingresos altos son quienes viven más lejos. Un estudio de UCLA sobre Los Ángeles va en la misma línea: los supercomuters tienen más probabilidades de ser de rentas altas, y los de rentas bajas usan el autobús seis veces más que ellos.
Quien no puede teletrabajar. Un camarero o un gerente de restaurante no puede acceder a ese modelo híbrido. Hacen la misma distancia, pero cinco o seis días por semana y con turnos rotativos a veces, lo que complica las cosas. Así que hagamos números. Lo que sigue son estimaciones propias con supuestos conservadores: 220 días laborables, 90 km/h de media y 200.000 km de vida útil para el coche. Con eso, 220 kilómetros diarios suman unos 48.400 al año. Solo en combustible, y tomando como referencia que el RACE sitúa en más de 1.000 euros el gasto con 15.000 km anuales, la factura superaría los 3.200 euros.
Si usamos en cambio la tarifa de referencia que Hacienda fija en 0,26 euros por kilómetro, hablamos de 12.584 euros al año, algo más de 1.000 al mes. Esa cifra incluye desgaste y amortización, que es justo lo que el conductor no ve. A este ritmo, un coche se agota en unos 4 años, cuando con un uso normal duraría más de una década. Y luego está el tiempo: a 90 km/h, son unas 540 horas al volante cada año, el equivalente a 13 semanas laborales de 40 horas.
La vivienda. La afirmación de María Inmaculada puede parecer una exageración, pero los números lo respaldan. Según Idealista, alquilar una habitación costó de media 430 euros al mes en España en el primer trimestre de 2026, y en Málaga capital 437, así que lo que se pide en La Cala de Mijas casi duplica esa media.
Alquilar un piso entero tampoco ayuda: el alquiler cerró junio en 15,3 euros por metro cuadrado, récord histórico, lo que da unos 1.200 euros mensuales por un piso de 80 metros. Y construir más es cada vez más caro: el suelo urbano superó entre abril y junio los 207,8 euros por metro cuadrado, la primera vez por encima de los 200 en 15 años, y se disparó hasta los 430 en los municipios de más de 50.000 habitantes.
El kit de supervivencia. Frente a esas cifras, el kit de supervivencia es casi lo más barato de la ecuación. Un botiquín homologado ronda los 17 euros, y en Decathlon un hornillo de gas de un fogón sale por unos 30 euros, cuatro cartuchos por 11, una manta de viaje por 12 y una botella térmica de un litro por 17. En total, unos 87 euros, algo más de una décima parte de un mes de esa habitación. Lo cuento casi de broma, pero el chiste no tiene gracia.
Lo caro es el coche, siempre: el seguro a terceros cuesta de media 503 euros al año, y cambiar aceite y filtro en un coche de gama media ronda los 130-150 euros. Si con 48.000 kilómetros anuales se cambia cada 15.000 (más o menos), son tres cambios al año. Solo con seguro y aceite subes a 900 euros anuales, más de diez veces el kit, sin contar neumáticos (o una limpieza completa que puede rondar los 50 euros) ni combustible.
La realidad de los "ultraviajeros". Pero la depreciación, los neumáticos, las revisiones y la avería inesperada son cosas que nadie tiene en cuenta cuando te dice "qué suerte, trabajas donde quieras". Sumemos que los ultra-viajeros suelen madrugar mucho o acostarse tarde para cuadrar horarios, y eso se traduce en peor salud. Un trayecto largo, de madrugada y con cansancio acumulado es justo el escenario donde el riesgo laboral se dispara.
Lo digo en sentido literal: el accidente in itinere se considera accidente de trabajo, siempre y cuando uses el medio de transporte habitual. De lo contrario, una revisión puede desembocar en una sentencia desfavorable por negligencia.
El debate de fondo. El sector de la hostelería lleva tiempo planteando que la vivienda turística no es solo un asunto inmobiliario, sino también laboral. Según recogía El Mundo, Víctor Márquez, secretario general del sindicato Sintrah, denuncia una “competencia no equilibrada”. Un particular puede comprar un piso como inversión y alquilarlo a turistas, mientras que hoteles y restaurantes cargan con más regulación, costes laborales y exigencias fiscales.
Lo insostenible es que el alojamiento turístico crezca a costa de sacar vivienda del mercado residencial y, con ella, a los trabajadores que el propio sector necesita. Ya lo contábamos: en Ibiza hay poblados de caravanas que en realidad son trabajadores sin alternativa; otros directamente se mudan a caravanas para alquilar sus casas a turistas. Porque la relación de cuatro a uno da contexto de la presión a la que se enfrentan algunas regiones: el trabajador de oficina con modo híbrido compra distancia con dos o tres días de trayecto. Quien sirve mesas o trabaja en un hotel está atado por mucho más tiempo.
La subida del SMI. Quiero cerrar con la “buena” noticia, porque el Gobierno ya ha puesto en marcha la subida del salario mínimo para 2027. El Ministerio de Trabajo encargó el 8 de octubre a la comisión de expertos una propuesta para principios de noviembre, tras la cual se abrirá la mesa con el diálogo social, y esta vez con una cifra única. Yolanda Díaz defendió que el proceso no puede esperar a las elecciones del 29 de noviembre, porque las empresas necesitan saber el 1 de enero cuál es el SMI.
No hay cifra oficial, pero los expertos prevén una subida superior al 4% sobre los 1.221 euros actuales en 14 pagas, y CCOO pide más del 5%. En la práctica, serían entre 50 y 60 euros más al mes. Pero hay riesgo de retraso, porque la de este año no se aprobó hasta febrero y con carácter retroactivo. Aparte, los funcionarios tienen pactado un 5% para 2027.

articles.title: Streaming sportif : ces box fibre évitent les mauvaises surprises les soirs de match
articles.text:
Quelle box fibre choisir pour regarder les grands matchs sans coupure ?
Pour regarder un grand match en streaming sans coupure, une connexion fibre à 1 Gb/s suffit largement dans la plupart des foyers, à condition de disposer d’un Wi-Fi stable dans la pièce où se trouve la télévision. La Freebox Pop reste un bon compromis, tandis que la Livebox Up Fibre et SFR Fibre Premium visent davantage les familles nombreuses ou les logements très connectés.
Quelle box fibre choisir pour regarder les grands matchs sans coupure ?
| Profil | Box fibre à privilégier | Pourquoi | 
|---|---|---|
| Meilleur équilibre | Freebox Pop | Wi-Fi 7, jusqu’à 5 Gb/s partagés et répéteur disponible sur demande | 
| Foyer familial | Livebox Up Fibre | Livebox 7 Wi-Fi 7, jusqu’à 8 Gb/s symétriques selon éligibilité et 1 répéteur Wi-Fi 7 sur demande | 
| Grand logement très connecté | SFR Fibre Premium | Box 10+, Wi-Fi 7, jusqu’à deux répéteurs et 8 Gb/s symétriques | 
| TV et plateformes incluses | Freebox Ultra | Wi-Fi 7, 8 Gb/s symétriques et plusieurs services de streaming intégrés | 
| Petit foyer | Offre B&YOU Pure Fibre | Débit largement suffisant pour un match 4K et quelques usages simultanés | 
Notre conseil : ne choisissez pas uniquement la box qui annonce le débit le plus élevé. Pour éviter les coupures pendant un match, la position de la box, la qualité du Wi-Fi dans le salon et la présence d’un répéteur comptent davantage que le passage de 5 à 8 Gb/s. Lorsque c’est possible, relier la TV ou le décodeur à la box avec un câble Ethernet reste la solution la plus stable.
Une diffusion fluide : le vrai enjeu des soirs de match
Regarder un match sans saccades n’a rien d’un luxe lorsqu’il s’agit d’un rendez-vous mondial. Les flux vidéo en direct sollicitent fortement le réseau domestique, surtout quand plusieurs écrans fonctionnent en même temps. Streaming sur TV 4K, commentaires sur mobile, notifications en arrière-plan : tout s’additionne.
Dans ce contexte, les box fibre deviennent un élément central. Les offres de SFR, Free ou Orange misent justement sur des débits élevés et des équipements plus robustes. Mais tous les abonnements ne se valent pas lorsqu’il s’agit de stabilité en heure de pointe.
Par ailleurs, la qualité du WiFi joue un rôle presque aussi important que le débit théorique. Une box peut afficher 1 Gb/s sur le papier, mais perdre en efficacité si le signal se dégrade dans le salon au moment du coup d’envoi.
Débit, WiFi et TV : les critères qui font la différence
Pour suivre un match sans interruption, trois éléments comptent particulièrement.
D’abord, le débit fibre. Les offres autour de 1 Gb/s suffisent pour un foyer classique, même avec plusieurs appareils connectés. Les formules plus haut de gamme montent aujourd’hui beaucoup plus haut : jusqu’à 5 Gb/s partagés avec la Freebox Pop et jusqu’à 8 Gb/s symétriques avec la Freebox Ultra, la Livebox Up Fibre dans les zones éligibles ou SFR Fibre Premium. Ces débits servent surtout lorsque plusieurs usages lourds tournent en même temps.
Ensuite, la génération WiFi. Le WiFi 5 reste fonctionnel, mais le WiFi 6 apporte une meilleure gestion des appareils connectés, ce qui limite les microcoupures. Le WiFi 7, désormais présent sur certaines offres premium, améliore encore la stabilité dans les logements très équipés.
Enfin, la TV incluse peut faire la différence. Orange et SFR annoncent 200 chaînes sur leurs offres concernées, tandis que Free dépasse désormais les 300 chaînes sur ses Freebox Pop et Ultra. La Freebox Ultra ajoute aussi plusieurs plateformes de streaming incluses, dont Netflix Standard avec pub, Disney+ Standard avec pub et Prime Video avec pub.
Quelle box choisir selon votre usage réel ?
Pour un usage simple, une box fibre standard suffit largement si le foyer ne dépasse pas quelques connexions simultanées. En revanche, dès que la maison devient très connectée, avec TV 4K, consoles, ordinateurs et smartphones utilisés en parallèle, une offre équipée d’un Wi-Fi plus récent et d’un répéteur peut apporter davantage de confort.
Chez Free, la Freebox Pop combine jusqu’à 5 Gb/s partagés, le Wi-Fi 7 et un répéteur inclus sur demande, tandis que la Freebox Ultra grimpe à 8 Gb/s symétriques et ajoute plusieurs services de streaming.
Orange équipe désormais la Livebox Up Fibre d’une Livebox 7 Wi-Fi 7 pouvant atteindre 8 Gb/s symétriques selon l’éligibilité, avec un répéteur Wi-Fi 7 sur demande.
SFR Fibre Premium repose sur la Box 10+ Wi-Fi 7, jusqu’à 8 Gb/s symétriques et jusqu’à deux répéteurs disponibles sur demande.
Au final, le bon choix dépend moins du marketing que de la configuration du logement et du nombre d’écrans actifs pendant les matchs.

articles.title: Nintendo confirms it has no plans to abandon physical Switch 2 games
articles.text:
In a nutshell: In a recent interview with Brazilian YouTuber Coelho no Japao, Bill van Zyll – VP and GM of Nintendo Latin America – shared the company's stance on physical game sales on the Switch 2. Simply put, Nintendo won't be making the same mistake that Sony did.
Asked about Nintendo's stance on physical media, Zyll said that historically, the company goes off what the consumer prefers. They're barely a year into the launch of the Switch 2, he continued, which supports both digital and physical media.
"There's no plan to ditch physical," he said, adding that Nintendo knows how much fans like it.
That stance is in stark contrast to the position Sony has taken. Earlier this year, the company announced it would stop making physical games for its PlayStation console starting in January 2028. Sony cited consumer preferences and an overall shift in the entertainment industry as reasons for the change, adding that going digital only will allow them to better accommodate how people access and play games.
Not everyone agreed with Sony's reasoning. There are still lots of gamers that seek out and even prefer physical media, and it's these consumers that are set to bear the brunt of the decision. Future game collectors will also be impacted as there simply won't be anything tangible to collect.
There are several valid reasons why Sony would want to abandon physical media, and they mostly tie back to money. Manufacturing, shipping, and distributing physical games is costly, not to mention the fact that they take up valuable space on retail shelves. With digital delivery, there's no risk of running out of inventory. Digital essentially eliminates the used game market and opens the door to additional new game sales down the road.
Now that the dust has settled a bit after Sony's announcement, where do you stand on the subject? Are you all for the convenience of digital or do you still prefer something tangible that you actually own? Let us know in the comments section below.

articles.title: XMEMS starts mass-producing chips that cool AI glasses, smartphones and data centers - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
XMEMS starts mass-producing chips that cool AI glasses, smartphones and data centers
Silicon chip startup xMEMS Labs Inc. today said it has started mass production of its XMC-2400 and XMC-4800 chips for cooling artificial intelligence hardware.
No one has commercialized solid-state active cooling at this scale before, according to the company.
The chips are aimed at AI hardware running into heat limits in two places. Conventional fans “simply cannot fit” in AI glasses and smartphones that still need active heat removal, said Mike Housholder, vice president and general manager of the thermal management business unit at xMEMS. For data centers, the company is targeting solid-state drives, laser modules and other parts left outside the liquid cooling that increasingly surrounds high-power processors.
The technology behind both chips came out of the company’s speaker business, where an electrical signal flexes a thin silicon membrane to produce sound. In the cooling chips, the same type of membrane moves air. Device makers can route the air down narrow channels to a processor or a memory chip, the company said, since it builds high pressure.
Nothing in the package spins. Because each device is a single piece of silicon, Housholder said, it could eventually be packaged together with the AI processors it cools.
Personal SSDs and glasses built for AI or extended reality are the target for the XMC-2400. The XMC-4800 moves more air, enough for thermally demanding AI smartphones as well as enterprise SSDs and other lower-power subsystems in the data center. In July, xMEMS introduced a third, smaller model, the XMC-1200, to cool the light engines and processors inside smart glasses.
Customers testing the chips have cut temperatures by 10 to 25 degrees Celsius at the chip and system level in glasses, smartphones and SSDs, xMEMS said. At 7.42 by 9.48 by 1.13 millimeters, the XMC-2400 moves up to 28 cubic centimeters of air per second against as much as 1,300 pascals of back pressure on about 150 milliwatts. The larger XMC-4800 tops out at 48 cubic centimeters per second.
Founded in 2018, xMEMS is a venture capital-backed startup that made its name with speakers for earbuds and headphones. In October last year it raised $21 million in a Series D round led by Boardman Bay Capital Management LLC to fund the move into mass production.
The first commercial products built around the XMC-2400 are expected to reach the market in early 2027. Live demonstrations are planned for CES in Las Vegas in January.

articles.title: Gana diamantes y skins gratis en Free Fire canjeando los códigos disponibles el 13 de octubre de 2026
articles.text:
Garena habilitó una nueva serie de códigos para Free Fire que permite reclamar diamantes, skins de armas, trajes y otros objetos dentro del videojuego. Los beneficios están destinados a jugadores que tengan una cuenta registrada y vinculada con alguna de las plataformas autorizadas.
Como ocurre cada día, la difusión de estas combinaciones alfanuméricas concentra la atención de miles de usuarios. Los códigos tienen un número limitado de usos y su disponibilidad puede variar según la región, así que conviene validarlos antes de que expiren o alcancen el límite de canjes.
Cuáles son los códigos de Free Fire disponibles hoy 13 de octubre
Los códigos publicados para este 13 de octubre de 2026 combinan letras y números. Cada jugador debe ingresarlos sin alterar las mayúsculas ni cambiar el orden de los caracteres, porque un error puede impedir la validación del premio.
La lista difundida para la jornada incluye más de 20 alternativas. Los jugadores registrados pueden probar los siguientes códigos en el sistema oficial de recompensas de Free Fire:
- FM6N1B8V3C4X.
- FT4E9Y5U1I3O.
- 4N8M2XL9R1G3.

- BR43FMAPYEZZ.
- FFCBRAXQTS9S.
