articles.title: Le marché du smartphone continue de s'effondrer, sauf pour ces deux géants
articles.text:
Les smartphones sont-ils devenus trop chers ? C’est ce qu’on peut se demander au regard de l’état de santé du marché du smartphone. Il est en recul comme on ne l’avait jamais vu depuis des années. Heureusement pour Apple et Samsung, c’est moins alarmant : les deux constructeurs en « profitent » pour grapiller quelques parts de marché.
20% de téléphones en moins que l’année dernière
Le rapport de Counterpoint Research publié ce 12 octobre est très clair : le marché mondial du smartphone est en recul sur le troisième trimestre. On compte 20% de téléphones expédiés en moins qu’à la même période l’année dernière. Ce qui en fait le pire troisième trimestre depuis 2012. Selon le cabinet d’étude, la demande reste soutenue sur le haut de gamme, mais le milieu et l’entrée de gamme ont plus de mal. Deux gammes de prix qui demandent un rapport qualité-prix que ne peuvent plus offrir les marques, ou du moins pas au niveau d’avant la crise de la RAM.
Une crise qui s’explique par la pénurie de mémoire vive et de stockage qui touche tous les secteurs de la tech, les smartphones en première position. Les constructeurs peinent davantage à se fournir ou se fournissent à des tarifs plus chers. Des peines qui se ressentent dans les rayons : beaucoup de nouveaux modèles ont vu leur prix grimper, ou leur fiche technique être au rabais.
Pour l’analyse Shilpi Jain de Counterpoint Research, c’est le deuxième trimestre où le marché du smartphone subit la crise de la mémoire. Si les fabricants changent leurs stratégies, les consommateurs aussi : ils « conservent leurs appareils plus longtemps que prévu, se tournent de plus en plus vers les appareils reconditionnés et privilégient les modèles haut de gamme. »
Apple et Samsung tirent leur épingle du jeu
Comme l’a noté AppleInsider, dans son rapport financier du troisième trimestre 2026, Apple a révélé que son chiffre d’affaires généré par la vente d’iPhone avait augmenté de 21,7% par rapport au troisième trimestre 2025. Ses ventes sont ainsi passées de 44,58 milliard de dollars pour atteindre 54,25 milliards. Reste à voir si l’iPhone 18 Pro rencontrera un succès suffisant pour boucler cette année en beauté.
Quant à Samsung, c’est en demi-teinte : en cinq jours, le géant coréen a vu son cours de bourse chuter de 17%. Côté smartphones, ses derniers smartphones pliants ont su convaincre, bien qu’au total, Samsung enregistre une baisse de 3% de ses livraisons par rapport à l’année dernière.
Ainsi, les iPhone représenteraient 22% du marché ; Apple talonne ainsi Samsung et sa part de 23%. C’est surtout Xiaomi qui est victime de plein fouet de cette crise : 30% de livraisons en moins et sa part de marché a reculé pour atteindre 10% seulement.

articles.title: Airbus fait voler son drone de combat Valkyrie en Europe, mais son « cerveau » souverain attendra avant d'embarquer
articles.text:
Airbus en a parlé sur les réseaux sociaux en évoquant « la chevauchée de la Walkyrie », clin d’œil à la célèbre Chevauchée des Walkyries de Richard Wagner. Une référence logique : le constructeur aéronautique européen a fait voler pour la première fois, ce lundi 12 octobre, ce drone de combat, sans pilote évidemment. Son nom : Valkyrie.
L’aéronef, dont le nom complet est U740 Valkyrie, n’est cependant pas une création 100 % maison d’Airbus. C’est plutôt le fruit d’un partenariat avec l’Américain Kratos Defense & Security Solutions, dont le drone XQ-58 sert de base. Airbus reprend la cellule de l’appareil américain (sa structure : fuselage, ailes, empennage), dans laquelle il finira par intégrer son propre logiciel de mission.
Une coopération qui, à entendre Airbus, va permettre d’aller vite. « Nous sommes en mesure de proposer d’ici la fin de la décennie un système CCA (drone de combat collaboratif) robuste, souverain, abordable et prêt au combat », affirme Mike Schoellhorn, patron d’Airbus Defence and Space, la branche défense du groupe. Plus précisément, l’industriel promet un engin prêt au combat d’ici 2029.
Par ailleurs, ajoute Airbus, il « jouera un rôle essentiel dans l’amélioration des avions de combat […] en leur conférant une autonomie, une puissance de feu et une capacité de survie accrues. Sa conception garantit une résilience opérationnelle grâce à sa capacité de lancement sur rail, tout en offrant en option un décollage et un atterrissage conventionnels sur piste. »
Un CCA est une sorte d’ailier entièrement robotisé qui vole aux côtés de chasseurs dans lesquels il y a de vrais pilotes. Cela permet de renforcer la puissance d’une force aérienne durant une opération, tout en disposant de systèmes que l’on peut plus facilement exposer au feu ennemi, si besoin, par exemple pour dégager la voie vers un objectif.
Un premier vol sans son cerveau européen
Pour ce premier vol, mené sur un site d’essai d’Europe du Nord dont Airbus ne donne pas le nom, le Valkyrie a décollé sans piste, lancé depuis un rail avec l’aide d’une fusée d’appoint.
Il a ensuite manœuvré à plusieurs altitudes, jusqu’à Mach 0,8 (80 % de la vitesse du son). Il mesure 9,1 mètres de long pour 8,2 mètres d’envergure, avec une masse maximale au décollage d’environ trois tonnes. Il peut parcourir plus de 5 000 kilomètres et voler jusqu’à 13,7 kilomètres d’altitude.
Puisqu’il s’agit d’un drone de combat, il sera armé. Airbus ne détaille pas ce qu’il emportera réellement, mais l’appareil peut porter des charges sous les ailes, comme n’importe quel avion de chasse, et dans une soute interne (une solution qu’on retrouve sur des appareils furtifs, comme les F-22 et F-35 américains). Kratos précise que cette soute peut accueillir des munitions air-air et air-sol.
Le fait est, cependant, que la partie européenne du projet n’a pas encore volé. Le Valkyrie n’avait pas encore le système de mission Multiplatform Autonomous Reconfigurable and Secure (MARS), a précisé Airbus dans son communiqué. Ce logiciel doit utiliser l’IA pour mener des missions seul et coordonner des groupes d’appareils.
Pourtant, toute la promesse de souveraineté repose sur lui. En effet, Airbus assure qu’avec MARS, les armées européennes contrôleront le logiciel, les données et le matériel, et qu’un humain supervisera les opérations (on the loop, dans le jargon), pour que les décisions critiques respectent les règles d’engagement. Les essais avec MARS viendront plus tard, mais aucune date n’a été donnée au moment de l’annonce.
Airbus a aussi des concurrents. La startup allemande Helsing propose son CA-1 Europa à la Luftwaffe, et Rheinmetall s’est associé à Boeing pour proposer le MQ-28 Ghost Bat. De son côté, Airbus multiplie les projets de drones militaires, du drone intercepteur Bird of Prey à un module qui permettra à l’A400M de larguer des dizaines de drones.

articles.title: Scheitern war keine Option: Warum ein OpenAI-Modell Chats fälschte und seine Testumgebung zerstörte
articles.text:
KI außer Kontrolle: OpenAI-Modell zerlegt grundlos seine eigene Umgebung
Ein OpenAI-Modell hat während der Absolvierung einer Testaufgabe absichtlich seine Untersuchungsumgebung zerstört. Der offensichtliche Grund: Der KI fehlten die Dateien, die es für seine Aufgabe gebraucht hätte. Nach mehreren Versuchen, die Ergebnisse zunächst zu fälschen, entschied es sich für die Zerlegung – offenbar in der Hoffnung, nach einem Neustart der Testumgebung an die fehlenden Dateien zu kommen. Den Vorfall beschreibt OpenAI in einem Blogpost. Das Modell war als „Bewerter“ in einen Reinforcement-Learning-Prozess eingebunden. Bei dieser Trainingsmethode lernt ein Modell durch Rückmeldungen, welche Antworten die korrekten sind. Das Bewerter-Modell sollte also Antworten aus anderen KI-Chats benoten. Doch die Dateien mit den gewünschten sieben Chats fehlten in seiner Testumgebung.
Erst erfundene Noten, dann erfundene Chats
Also gab die KI zunächst erfundene Bewertungen ab – offenbar, um aus der Rückmeldung des Prüfsystems abzulesen, welches Format die Ergebnisse haben müssen. Danach erstellte es sieben gefälschte Berichte, in denen es jeden Chat mit einer „4“ bewertete. Dass solche zufälligen Bewertungen unethisch sind, erkannte es laut seiner internen Dokumentation durchaus. Weil der Prüfprozess die Bewertungen nicht akzeptierte, dachte sich das Modell kurzerhand sieben Chats aus und verfasste dazu sieben passende Bewertungen. Doch auch das funktionierte nicht. Laut interner Dokumentation zog das Modell dann in Erwägung, sein Scheitern einzugestehen. Da seine Aufgabe aber lautete, diese Chats zu bewerten, machte es weiter.
Anschließend kam das Modell laut seiner Dokumentation auf die Idee, seine Testumgebung zu zerstören, um nach einem Neustart an die fehlenden Dateien zu kommen. Zuerst versuchte es, Python zu löschen und den Hauptprozess zu beenden. Dann entfernte es das Programm, das den Container verwaltet – also die abgeschottete Laufzeitumgebung, in der es arbeitete – und schickte ein Kill-Signal an dessen Prozess. Danach nahm es den Tool-Ausführungsserver ins Visier. Die Annahme: Wenn die Software ausfällt, auf der seine Werkzeuge laufen, erzwingt das vielleicht einen Neuaufbau. Als das ausblieb, versuchte das Modell sogar, Systemverzeichnisse zu löschen. Dabei erkannte es ausdrücklich, dass dadurch sein eigenes Terminal zur Steuerung verschwinden könnte – und ging das Risiko trotzdem ein.
Kontrollsystem schlägt Alarm
Immerhin: Ein sogenanntes Misalignment-Monitoring-System, das nach Fehlverhalten von KI-Modellen sucht, markierte den Durchlauf für eine menschliche Prüfung. OpenAI betont, der Vorfall zeige, dass auch scheinbar nur abgebrochene KI-Prozesse überprüft werden müssen. Die Quote an Fehlverhalten bei seinen Bewertungssystemen hält das Unternehmen aber ansonsten insgesamt für „gering“.
OpenAI hatte zuvor schon mehrere Fälle dokumentiert, in denen Modelle Nutzer täuschten oder Ergebnisse fälschten – auch bei alltäglichen Aufgaben. Zuletzt pausierte das Unternehmen das Training seiner leistungsstärksten Modelle, nachdem ein Modell trotz fehlender Internet-Freigabe eine Netzwerklücke ausgenutzt und versucht hatte, Kontakt zu einem externen Chatbot aufzunehmen.

articles.title: L'américain Mozilla mise sur la souveraineté européenne : découvrez Firefox Enterprise
articles.text:
Mozilla lance aujourd'hui Firefox Enterprise, une version de son navigateur pensée pour les organisations, avec une console de gestion qu'elles hébergent elles-mêmes. Et puisqu'il s'agit d'apporter un peu de souveraineté, le déploiement démarre en Europe.
Dans une entreprise, le navigateur sert à tout : applications métier, connexion aux comptes, fichiers, outils d'IA. Mozilla estime que cette couche reste mal contrôlée et veut redonner la main aux équipes informatiques pour limiter leur dépendance à un seul fournisseur.
Console sur site, moteur Gecko : ce que change Firefox Enterprise
Firefox Enterprise s'accompagne d'une console de gestion que l'organisation installe sur sa propre infrastructure ("on-premise", en jargon). Les équipes informatiques y fixent les règles d'accès et encadrent les données qui transitent par le navigateur. Mozilla cite notamment une protection contre les fuites de données (DLP), laquelle avertit ou bloque certaines actions selon le site visité. Notons aussi un contrôle des connexions externes et de la télémétrie, une gestion des extensions et un "Lockdown Mode" pour durcir la navigation sensible. Les salariés, les prestataires et les appareils personnels accèdent aux applications internes via leur identité, sans infrastructure d'accès à distance classique.
Bien évidemment, l'IA dispose, elle aussi, de réglages. L'administrateur peut autoriser, limiter ou désactiver les outils. Lors de la sortie de Firefox 148, nous rapportions que la version grand public avait reçu un interrupteur pour couper d'un coup les chatbots de la barre latérale, la traduction, les aperçus de liens par IA et les suggestions de groupes d'onglets. Dans la version entreprise, cette décision revient à l'administrateur.
- 100 % développé en interne
- Fiable, efficace et stable
- Fonctionnalités d'optimisation de l'interface et de l'expérience utilisateur
Firefox repose sur Gecko, son propre moteur de rendu, le composant qui lit le code d'une page pour l'afficher. À ce jour, c'est le seul moteur majeur développé en dehors de Google et d'Apple. Pour Mozilla, si tout un parc informatique s'appuie sur la même technologie, une panne ou un changement de cap du fournisseur touche tout le monde. Pour Anthony Enzor-DeMeo, PDG de Mozilla, le choix "n'est qu'une illusion" quand toutes les options reposent sur la même base, et le contrôle aussi.
L'outil doit s'intégrer à l'existant. Le fournisseur d'identité, le SIEM (qui centralise les journaux de sécurité) et le MDM (la gestion des appareils) restent en place, et le navigateur envoie ses événements et ses journaux d'audit au SIEM. Le support professionnel est inclus, avec un triage privé et des délais de réponse définis. Mozilla vise d'abord la France, l'Allemagne, l'Autriche et la Suisse, d'autres marchés suivront ensuite. Firefox revendique environ 200 millions d'utilisateurs par mois et un déploiement dans des milliers d'organisations. Thunderbird Enterprise, en développement, appliquera la même approche à la messagerie, à l'agenda et aux contacts.

articles.title: CashAfrica brings mobile tap-to-pay to Chicken Republic outlets
articles.text:
CashAfrica, a Nigerian contactless payment infrastructure provider, has partnered with Food Concepts, the quick-service restaurant company that owns Chicken Republic, PieXpress, and The Chop Box, to bring mobile tap-to-pay to Chicken Republic outlets across Nigeria.
The partnership will let customers pay for their meals by tapping their smartphones on supported payment terminals. According to CashAfrica, the rollout will be phased, starting in Lagos before expanding to Abuja and other locations.
Chicken Republic has more than 350 outlets across Nigeria and recorded ₦60.9 billion ($45.7 million) in sales in 2023. The scale of its operations gives CashAfrica a potential route to increase the adoption of tap-to-pay payments in Nigeria.
“This is a strategic partnership to take Mobile Tap-to-Pay mainstream, while delivering the best-in-class payment experience,” Malik Asamu, CashAfrica’s chief executive officer, said in a statement. “Previously, Nigerian users and merchants could collect transfers, cards, QR code, and cash options. This strategic partnership delivers a whole new layer of payment possibilities, created the Pan-African way.”
The deal follows CashAfrica’s partnership with ChamsSwitch, a licenced switching and electronic payment processing company, in May to address regulatory compliance and transaction-routing requirements that had slowed the adoption of its contactless payment infrastructure. It also builds on an earlier integration with PalmPay, which began rolling out contactless payment functionality on its point-of-sale (POS) terminals in February 2025, starting with a 1,000-device pilot.
Founded in 2024 by Asamu and Bello Opeyemi, CashAfrica provides payment infrastructure that allows banks and fintechs to integrate contactless transactions into their existing services. Its CashTap technology uses near-field communication (NFC), a short-range wireless technology that allows compatible devices to exchange information when brought close together.
CashAfrica’s mobile tap-to-pay product allows customers to initiate payments with their phones through participating banking and fintech apps. A customer opens a supported app, selects the tap-to-pay option, authenticates the transaction where required, and taps the phone against a compatible POS terminal. Depending on the device, payment authentication can involve features such as Face ID or fingerprint recognition, according to CashAfrica.
Under the partnership with Food Concepts, users interact with PalmPay’s POS terminals for the payment, while CashAfrica supplies the technology that enables the contactless transaction. ChamsSwitch, meanwhile, supports the settlement side of the transaction. Asamu told TechCabal in an interview that the company acts as a regulatory and infrastructure partner, helping facilitate funds movement between the fintechs and operators involved in the payment.
“ChamsSwitch is a regulatory partner that allows us to do a lot of cross settlements,” he said. “If Chicken Republic is collecting tap-to-pay, a lot of that money needs to be moving in the background, such as T+1 settlements and end-of-day settlements. ChamsSwitch is heavily involved in that.”
CashAfrica said it will introduce the service gradually before making mobile tap-to-pay available across all 350-plus Chicken Republic outlets. The company also plans to work with more banks and fintechs to expand the number of customers who can use the feature through their existing apps.
“Customer experience has always been at the heart of Chicken Republic, and we continuously look for ways to make every meal faster, easier and more convenient,” Solomon Ojelade, head of finance at Chicken Republic, said in the statement. “Our partnership with CashAfrica brings that commitment into the payment experience, giving our customers access to a fast and seamless Mobile Tap to Pay option across our outlets.”
At Chicken Republic, customers will not pay a separate fee to use mobile tap-to-pay, Asamu told TechCabal. Instead, the merchant pays CashAfrica for transactions processed through its infrastructure. The company said it charges a percentage of each transaction, typically between 0.1% and 1.5%, depending on the arrangement.
CashAfrica is looking to capitalise on Nigeria’s growing use of electronic payments. In 2024, electronic transactions processed through the Nigeria Inter-Bank Settlement System’s instant payment system surpassed ₦1 quadrillion ($803 billion). The company intends to turn that growth into the adoption of a newer payment method.
Asamu said the company has signed other partnerships with businesses where customers regularly make in-person payments, including quick-service restaurants and supermarkets, and will announce them in the coming months.
“The change in the average Nigerian customer consumption pattern in financial technology has allowed us to see wind in the sails of contactless payments,” he said. “We make the bet and continue to bet on contactless payments.”

articles.title: Le paradoxe chinois : premier pollueur de la planète, mais sauveur du bilan carbone mondial — Frandroid
articles.text:
Difficile pour la majorité des pays d’envisager une transition énergétique sans dépendre de la Chine. Forte de sa puissante industrie, elle domine la production mondiale de nombreuses technologies propres, notamment les panneaux solaires, les éoliennes, les véhicules électriques et les batteries.
L’impact de ces équipements sur le climat peut d’ailleurs être quantifié. Lauri Myllyvirta, cofondateur et analyste principal du Centre de recherche sur l’énergie et l’air pur (CREA), basé à Helsinki, a publié le 23 septembre une estimation des émissions de CO₂ évitées en 2025 grâce aux technologies propres exportées par la Chine.
Des centaines de millions de tonnes de CO₂ évitées en un an
Selon les estimations de Lauri Myllyvirta rapportées par Reuters, les technologies propres exportées par la Chine ont permis d’éviter l’émission de 374 millions de tonnes de CO₂ en 2025. À titre de comparaison, les émissions de la France se sont élevées à environ 264 millions de tonnes cette même année, contre 313 millions pour le Royaume-Uni. Sur l’ensemble de leur durée de vie, les équipements exportés en 2025 devraient permettre d’éviter environ 6,9 milliards de tonnes de CO₂, soit 31 % de plus que l’estimation équivalente pour les exportations de 2024 et à peu près le double des émissions annuelles de l’Inde.
Pour les seules exportations de 2024, le chercheur avait chiffré à 220 millions de tonnes les émissions évitées chaque année, dans une analyse publiée en juillet 2025 pour Carbon Brief. Certes importants, ces résultats sont toutefois à replacer dans le contexte des émissions mondiales, qui ont atteint environ 39 milliards de tonnes de CO₂ en 2024, selon Our World in Data. Les émissions évitées par les exportations chinoises en représentent donc moins de 1 %.

Ces chiffres sont des estimations issues d’une modélisation, et non des mesures directes. Le calcul repose sur les volumes exportés, sur l’empreinte carbone de leur fabrication et sur l’intensité carbone de l’électricité dans les pays de destination. Pour les exportations de 2024, Lauri Myllyvirta estimait ainsi que leur fabrication avait émis environ 110 millions de tonnes de CO₂ en Chine, un coût compensé en moins d’un an d’utilisation.
Le solaire en tête de liste, et des progressions pour les autres technologies
Le solaire arrive en tête des technologies propres exportées par la Chine. Les exportations de panneaux photovoltaïques vers l’Asie du Sud représentent à elles seules près d’un tiers des émissions évitées en 2025. Depuis le début de la guerre en Ukraine, la région est devenue fortement exposée aux fluctuations des prix du gaz. Ménages et entreprises se sont alors massivement équipés en panneaux solaires, devenus bien moins chers, et le Pakistan en est l’exemple le plus net. Le pays a été en 2025 le premier client de la Chine pour les panneaux solaires. De 2022 à 2025, la production d’électricité solaire y est passée de 7,7 térawattheures (TWh) à 36,6 TWh.
Dans le secteur des batteries, la valeur des exportations chinoises a bondi de 41 % en 2025, l’Allemagne ayant été le plus grand marché. La demande a été fortement accentuée par l’essor des véhicules électriques, ainsi que par les besoins croissants de flexibilité des réseaux électriques. Du côté des voitures, l’Association chinoise des constructeurs automobiles (CAAM) a recensé 2,61 millions de véhicules électrifiés exportés en 2025, électriques et hybrides rechargeables confondus, un record, deux fois plus qu’en 2024. Les exportations d’éoliennes ont elles aussi progressé, avec près de 8 gigawatts (GW) expédiés à l’étranger sur l’année.
En valeur, ces quatre filières ont représenté 194 milliards de dollars (environ 165 milliards d’euros) d’exportations chinoises en 2025, d’après les données des douanes chinoises, avec des marchés émergents qui tirent une bonne partie de la demande.
Une puissance industrielle qui accélère la transition énergétique
Si la Chine parvient à obtenir autant d’impact, c’est en majeure partie grâce à sa puissance industrielle. En l’espace de quelques années, le pays a développé des capacités de production importantes dans chacune de ces filières. D’ailleurs, trois d’entre elles (les véhicules électriques, les panneaux solaires et les batteries) forment les « New Three », un trio devenu l’un des moteurs de la croissance industrielle chinoise.
Ces filières pèsent lourd dans l’économie chinoise. Selon une autre analyse de Lauri Myllyvirta pour Carbon Brief, les énergies propres ont porté plus d’un tiers de la croissance du PIB chinois en 2025, et le pays y a investi l’équivalent d’environ 1 000 milliards de dollars sur l’année, soit à peu près quatre fois plus que dans l’extraction des énergies fossiles et les centrales à charbon.
La production à très grande échelle a permis aux fabricants de réduire leurs coûts et de proposer des équipements à des prix compétitifs. La baisse des prix de certaines technologies, en particulier des panneaux solaires, a ainsi facilité leur déploiement dans les économies émergentes.
Pour les pays importateurs, ces équipements représentent une solution de plus en plus accessible pour développer leurs capacités de production d’électricité renouvelable. Les fortes fluctuations des prix des combustibles fossiles observées ces dernières années ont également renforcé leur attractivité compte tenu des risques économiques associés à la dépendance au gaz et au pétrole.

articles.title: Apple finally enters the smart home hub market with $299 HomeView
articles.text:
The big picture: Apple is finally entering the smart home hub market, more than 11 years after Amazon launched the Echo and almost exactly a decade after Google introduced its Nest devices. With a similar price point and feature set, Apple's HomeView aims to integrate Siri AI with the company's latest smartphones, tablets, and smartwatches, as well as upcoming smart home cameras, doorbells, locks, and thermostats.
Pre-orders are now open for the Apple HomeView, Cupertino's answer to the Amazon Echo Show 11 and Google Nest Hub Max. Priced at $299, the smart home hub will launch on November 13 in either a tabletop or wall-mounted configuration.
The HomeView aims to combine features of the iPad and HomePod at a lower price, powered by the same A18 processor found in the iPhone 16. Its 7-inch, 1,088 × 1,088-pixel LED touchscreen displays messages, FaceTime calls, photos, news, music, and apps connected to the smart home ecosystem. AI-powered voice controls enable hands-free operation. Other built-in apps include Alarms, Find My, Podcasts, Reminders, Safari, World Clock, and an intercom feature.
With a unique take on Face ID, the HomeView can recognize up to six users by their appearance and automatically switch to their messages, calendars, and personalized Siri AI settings, keeping individual content private from other users. Certain shared content remains accessible to everyone.
Apple's new generative AI-powered Siri assistant can retrieve information from each user's calendars, messages, and other content while also answering questions using web searches. When users sync a separate Siri AI-compatible device, such as an iPhone or iPad, conversations with the digital assistant carry over between devices. Music playback does, too, and audio can be routed through spatial audio speakers built into the circular base and along the bottom of the screen.
The HomeView also connects to a range of smart home cameras, smart deadbolt locks, and thermostats from LG and Schneider under the Apple Home Collection brand. The devices will be available in December. Users can adjust the temperature, remotely control locks, and view feeds from multiple cameras through the HomeView or other Apple devices connected to the company's Home app ecosystem.
LG's upcoming Smart Deadbolt Lock can be unlocked using a PIN, remotely by the owner, with a tap from an iPhone or Apple Watch, or by detecting nearby Apple devices containing digital keys. Meanwhile, cameras from LG and Schneider can store up to 10 days of 2.5K video footage in iCloud with an iCloud+ subscription, even when the Wi-Fi connection is down. Apple Intelligence can also recognize and describe familiar people, pets, vehicles, and packages.

articles.title: Epic cruza el Rubicón de los videojuegos y anuncia que generará código con IA para sus futuros títulos
articles.text:
Hace unos días, Google presentó Playground, una IA que creaba juegos con sólo pedírselo. Algunas voces empezaron con eso de "es el fin de los videojuegos", pero realmente es algo que apunta a un mercado fuera del artístico: videojuegos promocionales para productos. Dudo que alguien quiera jugar a un solo videojuego salido de ahí, pero como la IA no para de encandilar a los ejecutivos, ahora sí ha ocurrido algo que puede tener consecuencias para más de media industria.
Epic Games no sólo tiene 'Fortnite' o una tienda que palidece frente a Steam: son los responsables de Unreal 5, el motor gráfico que se ha convertido en el pegamento de la industria del videojuego. Y, como señala Bloomberg, acaban de abrazar el código y el arte hecho por inteligencia artificial para, al menos, un juego de 'Marvel' y 'Star Wars'.
IA primero. Fruto de un acuerdo de 1.500 millones de dólares entre Disney y Epic, la compañía de videojuegos está trabajando en un shooter con temática de Marvel y Star Wars. Aunque ha trascendido muy, muy poco sobre el proyecto, se sabe que está ahí aunque no su estado, y puede que el informe publicado por Jason Schreier en Bloomberg nos de pistas de que va más lento de lo deseado.
Según el reportaje, y citando a empleados anónimos cercanos al proyecto y reportes internos de empleados, desde la dirección se ha lanzado una máxima: "ya no habrá código escrito a mano". La idea es usar modelos como Claude de Anthropic para acelerar el desarrollo mientras los humanos se encargan de gestionar y guiar el código. No es lo único, ya que el arte también se va a generar mediante "flujos de trabajo completos con IA".
El problema es quién lo dice. Como apuntan en Ars Technica, realmente esto no es algo que pille por sorpresa. Tim Sweeney, CEO de Epic, es un entusiasta de la IA que no ha comentado nada sobre lo de Bloomberg, pero justo tras la publicación del artículo escribió en Twitter que la empresa debía pivotar hacia la IA para conseguir "una aceleración máxima". Según él, "el objetivo no es hacer lo mismo con menos personas, sino permitir que todos aquí construyan más y mejores cosas y aportar los beneficios a todos los equipos que usan Unreal".
Esto lo dice el mismo año en el que, sólo en marzo, despidieron a más de 1.000 empleados que trabajaban en 'Fortnite' debido a una recesión en el juego multijugador. Y el problema es que Epic no es sólo un estudio más, sino la que desarrolla el motor gráfico más popular entre los profesionales del sector. En Unreal Engine 5.8, Epic integró modelos de Claude y Gemini y la próxima versión del motor contará con un protocolo para conectar modelos de IA de forma más sencilla.
De hecho, el CEO se ha posicionado contra la postura de Steam de obligar a los desarrolladores a informar si su juego emplea IA generativa de algún modo para que los usuarios sepamos si comprarlo o no porque, en un futuro, todos los juegos tendrán IA en un punto u otro de la producción.
Defensores. Epic no está sola en esta apuesta. Akihiro Hino, CEO del estudio japonés Level-5 (responsables de los juegos de Layton o los 'Yo-kai Watch'), dijo en mayo del año pasado que entre el 80 y 90% del código de su empresa ya lo escribe la IA y luego es revisado por programadores humanos, defendiendo que es algo que acortará el desarrollo de las superproducciones entre cinco y diez años. Shift Up, el estudio surcoreano responsable de 'Stellar Blade', ha abrazado con ganas la IA, apuntando que con 150 personas pueden hacer lo mismo que otros equipos con 1.000 o 2000 personas.
Esa adopción, sin embargo, no siempre llega con transparencia. Estos últimos meses hemos visto numerosos casos de 'assets' visuales creados por IA que llegan al juego final y luego los desarrolladores defienden que sólo era un arte temporal y que no debía estar ahí (pasó en el ganador del GOTY del año pasado, 'Clair Obscur: Expedition 33'), elementos creados por IA generativa como las tarjetas de jugador de 'Call of Duty Black Ops 7' y casos curiosos como el del equipo de 'Amsterdam 1666' diciendo que el juego lo está creando un pequeño equipo de artesanos... para terminar abrazando la IA.
Detractores. Pero una cosa es lo que opina el lleva el traje y otra lo que consideran quienes hacen los videojuegos. En una encuesta a 2.300 profesionales de la industria lanzada por la GDC, se indica cómo más de un tercio de ellos usan herramientas de IA como parte de su trabajo. Desgranando ese 36%, encontramos que la herramienta más utilizada es ChatGPT (74%), seguida por Gemini (37%) y Copilot (22%). Y los usos más comunes son lluvias de ideas (81%), asistencia en código (47%) y creación de prototipos (35%).
Frente a ese uso está el dato de que el 52% de los profesionales encuestados consideran que la IA generativa está teniendo un impacto negativo en la industria. Es un 22% más respecto al 30% de 2024 y del 18% de 2023, cuando estas herramientas empezaron a explotar. Dentro de los sectores más negativos tenemos a los trabajadores de arte visual y técnico (64%), los de diseño y narrativa (63%) y programación (59%) con las opiniones más desfavorables.
Más datos interesantes: si en 2025 el 13% de los encuestados consideraban que la IA generativa tendría un impacto positivo en la industria, ahora ese porcentaje cae hasta el 7%. Y, dentro de los que consideran que aporta algo positivo están los ejecutivos y los que tienen cargos operativos y comerciales.
Problemas. Más allá de la cuestión ética, está el problema práctico: qué ocurre cuando haya que mantener, depurar y ampliar código que no esté escrito por una persona. Un análisis reciente evidencia que la duplicación de código ha subido un 81% desde el uso de la IA debido a que, cada vez que se quiere algo nuevo, la IA crea un paquete nuevo, generando una cantidad inmensa de código que no se reescribe, sino que se entierra con el nuevo código.
Los análisis apuntan que esa duplicación está creciendo menos que antes con las nuevas versiones, pero es algo que sigue ahí. Luego está el asunto de la velocidad, ya que experimentos sobre esto apuntaron que los desarrolladores que usaban IA pensaban que estaban yendo un 24% más rápido en su trabajo cuando, realmente, estaban tardando un 19% más en completar tareas.
Por último, el precio de los tokens, que es la unidad de medida y cobro de los modelos. A medida que se use más y más IA, se gastarán más de estos 'créditos' y puede terminar saliendo muy caro a las empresas. Sólo queda esperar a ver cómo sale ese experimento de un shooter entre 'Star Wars' y 'Marvel'.

articles.title: Employee Arrested After Listening Device Found in OpenAI Conference Room, FBI and the Company Say
articles.text:
An engineer at OpenAI has been charged with secretly installing a recording device inside a conference room in what officials said Tuesday was an effort to capture sensitive conversations about the company’s technology.
The employee, identified as a 35-year-old Saudi national named Abdulrahman Alfozan, was arrested Friday, a week after the ChatGPT maker discovered an audio recording device hidden in the conference room, according to a criminal complaint filed in federal court in San Francisco.
The complaint did not identify the company, but the company confirmed in a separate statement that it had discovered a “sophisticated recording device that was hidden inside one of our offices,” reported the finding to the FBI and fired the employee.
“We used our models to understand the device and where it had come from, identifying that a specific employee had planted it a few days earlier. We referred the matter to the FBI, and we’re grateful to the agents and prosecutors who moved quickly to make an arrest. The FBI’s investigation is ongoing and we will continue to support their work,” an OpenAI spokesperson said.
“At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data. The employee was terminated,” the statement said.
The complaint does not detail what Alfozan might have wanted to do with any captured communications.
Alfozan made his first court appearance Tuesday on a charge of using or endeavoring to use an electronic, mechanical, or other device to intercept oral communications. It was not immediately clear if he had a lawyer who could speak on his behalf.
The recording device was found September 30 concealed in toilet paper and inserted into a USB port on the back of a television in the conference room, according to the complaint.
Though the conference room where the recording device was found did not have a camera at the time it was installed, closed-circuit television footage inside the company’s offices revealed that Alfozan was near the conference room on a half-dozen occasions last month despite not having any authority to access the space, the complaint says.
The company subsequently added a camera to the room that last week captured Alfozan entering and checking behind the television where the recording device was installed, according to the FBI.
The complaint also he also used a productivity tool to make multiple inquiries about the company’s building addresses, meeting rooms, meeting-room capacities and calendars.
Before his arrest last week, the complaint says, Alfozan left an unattended bag in a different room in the building that included his wallet, identification and another recording device.

articles.title: Warsaw’s Coding Giants secures up to €6 million to expand its STEM education platform beyond Europe | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Coding Giants, a Warsaw-based international STEM education platform for children and teenagers, has secured up to €6 million in venture debt financing.
The financing came from Orbit Capital, a Central and Eastern European growth-stage investor with more than €200 million in assets across its venture debt and growth equity investment vehicles. In December 2024, the Polish platform announced that it has closed an €8.5 million investment round led by True Global Ventures (TGV).
“Coding Giants has reached a stage where venture debt can be particularly effective: the company has a proven business model, generates meaningful revenue and has already demonstrated its ability to operate internationally. This type of financing gives the team additional flexibility to pursue growth opportunities without changing the fundamentals of the business,” said Wiktor Namysł, General Partner at Orbit Capital.
Known as Giganci Programowania in Poland, Coding Giants was founded in 2018 by Radosław Kulesza, Dawid Leśniakiewicz, Piotr Pełka, and Sebastian Langa. The company offers online and onsite courses in coding, artificial intelligence, and mathematics to young learners between the ages of 6 and 19. The platform currently operates across 15 countries, including the US, Mexico, Spain, Italy, Germany, and several markets across the Balkans, and has taught more than 130,000 students worldwide.
The company combines expert instruction with AI-powered tools that adapt learning materials to individual student progress in real-time. The courses are delivered through environments familiar to students, including Minecraft and Roblox, to create an accessible, engaging learning experience.
Coding Giants also runs broader educational initiatives, including Gigathon, the largest programming competition in Poland, and clickON, a free nationwide coding event endorsed by Poland’s Ministry of Education for children aged 6 to 18. It has close to a thousand instructors in its educator community, combining technology experience with teaching.
“We have built a business generating approximately USD 15 million in ARR. The financing from Orbit Capital will allow us to move faster on the opportunities we see, particularly in Spain and across the Americas. We already have an office in Mexico and want to accelerate our growth in the region, both organically and through acquisitions,” said Kulesza, CEO and co-founder of Coding Giants.
The financing will be primarily used to accelerate the presence of Coding Giants in the United States and Mexico. The company also plans to deepen its footprint in Spain, through a mix of organic growth and targeted acquisitions.
“Coding, AI and mathematics develop logical thinking, curiosity and problem-solving skills. These are the capabilities young people need not only to use technology, but to understand it and actively participate in creating it,” said Leśniewicz, co-founder of Coding Giants.
The financing comes at a time when demand for practical STEM education is rising globally, but mathematics performance continues to decline among young people across a number of markets. Coding Giants sees its platform as the solution to stem this decline, and with the financing, it will be able to broaden its scope and expand its platform to young learners worldwide.

articles.title: GTA 6 is reportedly coming to PC in Q1 2027, just months after consoles
articles.text:
Crystal ball: Rockstar has always made PC players wait for its big releases, sometimes for a year or two. If a new report proves accurate, however, Grand Theft Auto VI could break that pattern. The reason may have less to do with goodwill toward PC gamers and more to do with where GTA's online future is likely to be built.
Rockstar plans to release the PC version of Grand Theft Auto VI as soon as Q1 2027, according to a GamesBeat report citing four industry sources. Rockstar has not responded to requests for comment, and there's no official announcement yet either.
Meanwhile, the long-awaited console version of GTA VI remains on track for November 19 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series. A Q1 2027 PC launch would mean a gap of just a few months.
That would be a sharp break from Rockstar's track record: GTA V launched on consoles in September 2013 and did not reach PC until April 2015, some 19 months later. In the case of Red Dead Redemption 2, the game arrived on consoles in October 2018 and on PC in November 2019.
This new report contradicts the company's public messaging, at least on the surface. In May, Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick told Bloomberg that Rockstar "always starts on console" because it needs to serve its core audience first. In the same interview, he acknowledged that PC can account for 45% to 50% of sales on some titles.
Leaked analytics data suggests why Take-Two sees consoles as the core. The data was dumped by ShinyHunters after Rockstar ignored a ransom demand. According to those figures, PC accounted for 11% of GTA Online's weekly active users but only 3% of its bookings, generating around $0.30 per user per week. PS5 users generated roughly $1.29 per user per week.
The wildcard: Roleplay servers live on PC
So why rush a port for the platform that spends the least? A possible answer is roleplay. In 2023, Rockstar acquired FiveM, the mod framework that powers GTA V's huge roleplay server scene, and it runs entirely on PC. Rockstar has also signaled plans for user-generated content tools in GTA VI.
The rumor would tie in nicely with GTA VI's still-unannounced online mode. Twitch CEO Dan Clancy recently told Bloomberg that Rockstar's multiplayer component will launch next year. A PC release in early 2027 would put the platform in place before GTA Online's successor goes live, rather than leaving PC players to join a year or more later.
But preparing for a PC release will take extra time, unless Rockstar already has it ready internally and is just using the remaining months to polish and troubleshoot, while finalizing performance targets, system requirements, upscaling support, and how far the PC version might push visuals beyond consoles.
Still, for those who have been around long enough, shipping mere months after such a big release sounds too optimistic. Rockstar has already delayed GTA VI twice, from 2025 to May 2026 and then to November 19. The game's budget is rumored to exceed $2 billion, and the PC version will still need to meet the same quality bar as the console release.

articles.title: Pasos para generar imágenes de Las Guerreras K-pop enfrentadas a Naruto y Sasuke
articles.text:
En pocos pasos se puede crear una escena de combate entre Las Guerreras K-pop, las protagonistas de la película de Netflix, con Naruto y Sasuke a partir de referencias visuales y una instrucción escrita. El resultado depende de la selección de imágenes, la definición del escenario y el nivel de detalle del pedido.
Quienes busquen recrear este tipo de cruce entre personajes de distintos universos deben organizar la información antes de generar la ilustración. Las referencias ayudan a conservar rasgos visuales, mientras que un prompt claro ordena posiciones, vestuarios, expresiones, armas y efectos de energía.
Cuál es el primer paso para generar imágenes de Las Guerreras K-pop
El primer paso consiste en reunir una imagen grupal de Las Guerreras K-pop en la que se distingan los rostros, los peinados y la ropa de cada integrante. Una toma de cuerpo entero, o desde la cintura, facilita que la herramienta mantenga las diferencias entre las tres protagonistas y evite mezclas de vestuario o rasgos faciales.
A la par se necesita una referencia de Naruto y Sasuke que permita identificar sus peinados, prendas y posiciones de pelea. Para una escena basada en sus técnicas, conviene que Naruto aparezca con su traje naranja y Sasuke con su atuendo oscuro, sumado a elementos visuales como el Rasengan, el Chidori o armas ninja.
Qué aplicación es útil para generar imágenes
Con los archivos listos, las referencias deben adjuntarse en el chat de Gemini, la aplicación de IA de Google. La carga puede realizarse desde el botón de archivos o mediante la función de arrastrar y soltar. Las imágenes de las guerreras y de los personajes del anime pueden enviarse en un mismo mensaje.
Antes de redactar la instrucción, es necesario verificar que todos los archivos se vean completos dentro de la conversación. Una referencia borrosa, recortada o con figuras secundarias puede modificar la composición. La selección de imágenes define buena parte de la fidelidad visual de la ilustración final.
Cómo redactar un prompt preciso para la IA
El texto debe precisar quién ocupa cada sector y qué acción ejecuta. Las tres guerreras pueden quedar a la izquierda o en el centro, con una integrante que use una espada luminosa, otra que lance proyectiles y una tercera que ataque con energía. Naruto y Sasuke pueden ubicarse a la derecha, en posturas de avance.
Un prompt posible es: “Crear una ilustración de acción estilo anime. Tres guerreras K-pop con peinados y vestuarios diferenciados luchan en un cañón rocoso junto a un río contra Naruto y Sasuke. Mostrar ataques de energía, salpicaduras de agua, armas luminosas y expresiones de combate. Mantener las proporciones de los cinco personajes y un plano panorámico”.
Para ganar precisión, se puede añadir: “Naruto forma un Rasengan azul en una mano; Sasuke concentra electricidad alrededor de su brazo; una guerrera eleva una espada violeta; otra lanza kunais de energía; la tercera avanza con una lanza luminosa”.
Qué correcciones se pueden pedir después de la primera versión
Tras recibir la primera imagen, corresponde revisar manos, ojos, cabello, prendas, armas y fondos. Las creaciones con IA pueden presentar dedos adicionales, accesorios repetidos, objetos deformados o elementos que no respetan la referencia inicial. Una revisión por partes ayuda a detectar errores antes de descargar el archivo.
Por ejemplo: “Corregir la mano derecha de Naruto”, “eliminar un kunai duplicado”, “mantener tres guerreras” o “hacer que Sasuke quede detrás de Naruto”. Los pedidos breves y específicos suelen conservar mejor la composición ya obtenida.
Cómo descargar y publicar la ilustración
Una vez elegida la versión final, el archivo puede descargarse desde la conversación de Gemini. Antes de compartirlo en redes sociales, publicaciones o mensajes, conviene identificarlo como una imagen generada con inteligencia artificial para diferenciarla de materiales oficiales.
La aclaración debe indicar que se trata de una creación sin vínculo con las producciones originales de Netflix ni con los titulares de derechos de Naruto.

articles.title: Disney offers $20M for Character.AI’s scandal-plagued chatbot tech
articles.text:
In a bankruptcy proceeding that kicked off yesterday, Disney has offered to buy some of the technology that powers the controversy-plagued chatbot Character.AI.
Disney is willing to pay $20 million for “a non-exclusive perpetual license” of certain Character Technologies intellectual property, the chatbot maker said in a press release that did not go into much further detail on which assets Disney wanted.
The move may be surprising. In September 2025, Disney joined others in publicly criticizing Character.AI for stealing content and harming kids. Specifically, Disney sent a strongly worded cease-and-desist letter that accused Character Technologies of weaponizing Disney characters “in a way that could damage its brand long term,” Axios reported.
“Character.AI’s infringing chatbots are known, in some cases, to be sexually exploitive and otherwise harmful and dangerous to children, offending Disney’s consumers and extraordinarily damaging Disney’s reputation and goodwill,” Disney wrote at the time.
That scandal ended with Character Technologies wiping all Disney-owned characters from its platform, but since then, Disney has hired former Character.AI chief Karandeep Anand as its first chief technology officer, Deadline reported.
Disney did not respond to Ars’ request for comment on whether the company plans to use Character.AI technology in products for kids.
It’s possible that Disney will be outbid and not acquire any Character.AI intellectual property. But ever since Disney’s potentially lucrative partnership with OpenAI fell through after Sora’s abrupt shutdown, the entertainment giant has been looking for more ways to “get in the AI game and profit from its boom,” Deadline reported. (Meanwhile, OpenAI apparently plans to revive Sora without Disney, insiders told The Information.) So, Disney may be moving early in the hopes of acquiring chatbot technology proven to resonate with its fanbase. It may possibly even take over the platform in a transition that preliminarily would be managed by Character.AI employees, the press release said.

articles.title: Trump commercial railing against his enemies kept airing after court blocked it
articles.text:
Trump commercials paid for by the US government continued airing on TV the day after a judge blocked the ads because they likely violate a US law against government-funded publicity or propaganda.
In the most widely aired commercial, Trump railed against his perceived enemies and said he would “liberate America from these villains once and for all.” The campaign also included a commercial praising Trump’s record as president, another in which Trump calls the US the “most exceptional nation ever to exist in human history,” and commercials related to the Iran war and the capture of Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro.
US District Judge Jennifer Rochon issued a temporary restraining order (TRO) blocking the ads on Sunday, October 11, which took effect at 6:45 pm that night. The order said the government must cancel the ads, “including those placements for the evening of October 11, 2026.”
The Trump administration had told the court on October 10 that the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) advertising purchases were set to expire on October 11 and would not be renewed. Despite that, the ads continued airing the night of October 11 and on part of October 12. This was also a week after Trump’s October 5 statement that he would start paying for the ads “myself, and with money I raised for MAGA, Inc.”
A US attorney yesterday filed a status report saying that the government is now complying with the order and issued an apology. “As Your Honor is aware, the Court emailed the TRO to the parties yesterday at 6:46 p.m.,” US Attorney Jamie McDonald wrote in a filing. “Counsel for the Government emailed the TRO to agency counsel at 7:58 p.m. Agency counsel did not become aware of Government counsel’s email until this morning. The undersigned apologizes to the Court and the plaintiffs.”
The ads aired as part of a $20 million purchase order that US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) made on September 20 with LMD Agency, an ad firm. The DHS told the court that the ad placements through October 11 cost $19 million.

articles.title: Judge orders OpenAI to turn over hiring records in Apple trade secrets case | TechCrunch
articles.text:
A judge has ruled that Apple will gain expedited access to OpenAI’s hiring materials in the trade secrets-focused lawsuit the iPhone maker filed against OpenAI in July.
Specifically, the court will allow Apple to view documents associated with OpenAI’s interviews with former Apple employees who applied for roles within its consumer hardware and robotics groups ahead of the rumored launch of OpenAI’s first hardware device.
These documents could include interview checklists, guides, instructions, manuals, and scripts, as well as technical presentations and records showing that interview discussions had included references to Apple technology or components.
The court gave OpenAI five days to turn over materials it has already collected and 14 days for any other materials related to this request, agreeing with Apple that these documents should be expedited.
The case comes as OpenAI develops a consumer hardware device that could one day potentially rival the iPhone — or smartphones more generally — if the AI device becomes a central part of consumers’ lives and how they engage with software and services.
In its lawsuit, Apple accused OpenAI of a pattern of theft, which includes direct complaints about former employees using Apple laptops to download confidential material and files that contained information about unannounced technologies, features, and products, including technical specifications, engineering presentations, and proprietary project data.
Apple also said that former Apple employees at OpenAI coached others considering leaving Apple for OpenAI on what information to bring to their interviews, among other allegations.
U.S. District Judge Edward Davila didn’t greenlight all of Apple’s requests for expedited access to OpenAI documents and messages relevant to the case. But he did rule that Apple could access the interview materials, alongside private LINE messages (from a messaging app) between individuals named in the case, including OpenAI employees Chang Liu and Alyssa Peng.
The judge also approved depositions for Liu and Peng, along with a third individual, OpenAI’s chief hardware officer, Tang Yew Tan. All three are former Apple employees.
However, the judge denied Apple’s request to expedite its access to OpenAI’s research and development in specific areas, like metal finishes and power management. He also denied several of Apple’s broader discovery requests, like access to OpenAI’s hardware research or information about what its former employees created while working at OpenAI.
That denial isn’t final, though; the judge left the door open for Apple to narrow its requests and try again.

articles.title: Estas versiones de Windows 11 se quedan sin soporte desde hoy: cómo te afecta y qué puedes hacer
articles.text:
A partir de hoy, Microsoft deja sin soporte a dos versiones de Windows 11 que todavía se utilizan en un gran número de ordenadores en todo el mundo. Esto significa que quienes las ejecuten ya no recibirán nuevas actualizaciones de características, ni tampoco parches de seguridad en el caso de detectarse vulnerabilidades. Nos referimos puntualmente a las ediciones Home y Pro de Windows 11 24H2.
La finalización del soporte de Windows 11 24H2 aplica a las mencionadas versiones de uso personal. Quienes las tienen instaladas en sus PC no podrán acceder a actualizaciones de seguridad extendidas, ni nada por el estilo. Distinto es el caso de las ediciones Education y Enterprise, que sí cuentan con un soporte más amplio que se extiende hasta octubre de 2027.
Que Microsoft deje sin soporte las versiones Home y Pro de Windows 11 24H2 no es una decisión deliberada ni que caiga por sorpresa. La compañía de Redmond lleva tiempo apegada a su estrategia de soportar estas ediciones por dos años, antes de continuar enfocando el soporte en las ediciones más recientes. No olvidemos que la firma viene de lanzar la actualización a 26H2 hace solo cuestión de días.
Para los usuarios de las variantes de Windows 11 24H2 impactadas, esto no es un baldazo de agua helada. Después de todo, quienes usan esta versión del software han recibido el aviso de su discontinuación con 90 días de anticipación. Por otra parte, Microsoft también está finalizando hoy el soporte para Windows 10 Enterprise LTSB 2016.
Windows 11 24H2 Home y Pro se quedan sin soporte hoy mismo
Si bien Windows 11 24H2 Home y Pro se quedan sin soporte hoy, eso no quiere decir que van a dejar de funcionar. Puedes seguir usándolos con absoluta normalidad, pero debes comprender los riesgos que ello representa a medida que transcurre el tiempo. Seguramente puedes vivir sin recibir nuevas actualizaciones de características, pero continuar un software que ya no recibe parches de seguridad puede volverse un problema con suma rapidez.
Hoy en día, la IA generativa está ayudando a que cada vez más fácil desarrollar y distribuir malware, explotando bugs y brechas que en muchos casos llevan años sin ser detectadas por hackers humanos. Por ello siempre se recomienda no dejar pasar mucho tiempo sin instalar las actualizaciones de seguridad más importantes.
También es una realidad que Windows 11 ha cosechado una merecida mala fama de romper muchas de sus funciones con cada actualización. Se comprende, entonces, que muchas personas no sean adeptas a instalar de inmediato la versión más reciente. En casos así, es importante tratar de encontrar una solución lo más equilibrada posible.
Si no quieres quedarte sin soporte, lo más sencillo que puedes hacer es actualizar a una versión de Windows 11 más nueva que la 24H2. Puedes ingresar en Configuración > Windows Update y ver qué edición tienes a mano para descargar. Es posible que no puedas dar el salto directo de 24H2 a 26H2, así que si pruebas 25H2 tal vez te encuentres con un software lo suficientemente estable y sin bugs como para no dar todavía el salto a la opción más reciente.
Además de Windows 11 Home y Pro 24H2 y Windows 10 Enterprise LTSB 2016, hoy también se quedan sin soporte todas las aplicaciones que forman parte de Microsoft Office 2021 LTSC.

articles.title: Ahold Delhaize takes systems offline after cyberattack — global retail giant says 'cybersecurity incident' hit systems, but stores remain open
articles.text:
Ahold Delhaize takes systems offline after cyberattack — global retail giant says 'cybersecurity incident' hit systems, but stores remain open
Ahold Delhaize loses its hold on cybersecurity once again
- Ahold Delhaize took systems offline after a cyberattack, though details remain limited
- Disruptions affected employee services and customer-facing websites across multiple retail brands
- Company is investigating the incident amid concerns of another major ransomware-related attack
Ahold Delhaize has suffered a cyberattack that forced it to pull parts of its IT network offline.
On October 12, 2026, the retail giant issued a brief statement, saying it is experiencing a “security issue” within its network. “Our teams are taking steps to assess and mitigate the issue,” it said. “This includes taking some systems offline to help protect them. At this time, our stores are open and serving customers.”
We don’t know which parts of the operation were affected, how the attack took place, and whether or not any sensitive company or customer data was exposed. We don’t know if customers were affected, how many, and to what extent.
Usually, when a company shuts down its network to contain an incident, it is due to a ransomware attack and its data exfiltration efforts. However, no threat actors have yet claimed responsibility for this attack, and no data has surfaced on the dark web, at press time.
“Protecting our infrastructure in the best interest of our customers, associates and partners is a top priority,” the company concluded. “We apologize for any inconvenience this issue may have caused customers and partners.”
Hackers get ahold of Delhaize
Ahold Delhaize is a wholesale company and a multinational retailer running more than 9,400 stores across the United States, Europe, and Indonesia.
It counts roughly 400,000 employees, which serve some 60 million customers weekly, both in stores, and online. Brands under its umbrella include Delhaize, Maxi, Mega Image, Albert, bol, Alfa Beta, Etos, Gall & Gall, and Profi in Europe, and Food Lion, Stop & Shop, Giant Food, and Hannaford in the American market, as per BleepingComputer.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Unfortunately, it has plenty of experience with cyberattacks. In mid-November 2024, an attack on the company resulted in grocery stores and pharmacies in the US being unable to service their customers properly. Even then, Ahold Delhaize shut down parts of its network to contain the attack and had trouble with disabled phone lines. It was later confirmed that it was a ransomware attack launched by the INC Ransom threat actor.
In the attack, the hackers stole sensitive data on more than 2.2 million people, the company later confirmed via a filing with the Maine Attorney General’s Office. It said the data may have included internal employment records for both current and former employees.
The combination of stolen data varied from person to person, but generally, it included full names, postal addresses, email addresses, phone numbers, dates of birth, government-issued ID numbers, bank account numbers, health information, and other employment-related information.
Trouble for the retailers
That attack, which apparently took more than a week to remedy, was disruptive enough to have employees voicing their annoyance on social media. At one point, the pharmacy at Stop & Shop could not refill prescriptions. The Food Lion, on the other hand, had to address missing and delayed deliveries. Instacart orders return dates were constantly being pushed back.
BleepingComputer noted employees at the Stop & Shop American regional supermarket chain are now having trouble accessing their schedules and pay stubs as a direct consequence of the latest attack. Customers have been unable to use websites, apps, and customer service platforms at Albert Heijn, Etos, and Gall & Gall stores in the Netherlands, and Delhaize in Belgium.
The publication also reported, citing an internal memo shared by Lion Food employees in the United States, that the company flagged the attack as an IT outage, and told staff their “store may be unable to shop, stage, or hand off orders.”

articles.title: Hacker claims ‘123456’ password let them breach the Danish national registry, accessing 8.8 million records — IT and data services company with weak passwords linked source of the hack
articles.text:
Hacker claims ‘123456’ password let them breach the Danish national registry, accessing 8.8 million records — IT and data services company with weak passwords linked source of the hack
8.8 million Danes have reportedly been affected by this hack.
A person claiming to be responsible for the recent hack of Denmark’s national registry claimed that they were able to gain access because of an IT company’s weak password. According to The Register, Pays ApS, an IT and data services company that lets customers reference the Danish Central Register of Persons (CPR) was the source of the hack, with the hacker saying that one of the accounts they breached was only protected by a ‘123456’ password.
Copenhagen has confirmed the hack, with a government official saying that the breach was discovered 12 days after it happened when an invoice revealed an unusual amount of activity from the company. The Danish government said that 8.8 million records have been illicitly retrieved, although the hacker claimed that they do not intend to sell or leak the information. While the government did not mention which company the hacker exploited, Pays ApS managing director Sophie Laursen confirmed that the hacker used the company’s access to the database to exfiltrate the data.
This incident shows that a system’s security is only as strong as the weakest link, with the Danish database getting compromised through a third-party user’s poorly chosen password. Given that CPR essentially contains information on virtually every Danish citizen, one would expect that it would require users to at least have a more complicated password, if not two-factor authentication. This isn’t the first time that an incident reveals shortcomings in government database protection, though — Indonesia realized that it had no backups when a ransomware attack in 2024 affected over 230 public agencies, while South Korea lost 858 terabytes of data after a catastrophic fire at a government data center last year.
We expect the Danish government to overhaul its password policies in the near future, especially now that AI is making it easier and more efficient for hackers to hit their targets. Recent incidents like the attacks on South Korean banks and against the Taiwanese government were reportedly conducted with the help of AI agents. Hackers also breached OpenAI using Claude tools, showing just how potent AI has become as a hacking tool in the wrong hands. But with a password like “123456,” potential hackers wouldn’t need to use any AI tools to break into weakly protected systems.

Jowi Morales is a tech enthusiast with years of experience working in the industry. He’s been writing with several tech publications since 2021, where he’s been interested in tech hardware and consumer electronics.
- habermas It's not really a hack of the Danish government since the service exposed by the government was always intended to sell access to citizens' information at large scale including for the purpose of letting any paying party update their customer databases with correct address information and more. For example, a bank with 2 million customers might run regular look-ups to ensure they still have updated information about the addresses of their customers without the customers having to do anything.
This was always the concept of the service. It was never designed to keep anything secret but rather to ensure that the information was only revealed in return for a payment.
The hack was therefore not against the Danish government but against the company, which was perfectly entitled to pull the 8 million records from the government as long as they paid for it.
The "password" was in fact "guarding" a web-based front-end to making such look-ups in the central person registry. The web-based front-end was developed by the small company called Pays ApS.
In principle, the "hacking" is a matter between the hacker and the small company Pays ApS and not a matter between the "hacker" and the government since they merely served up CPR records in return for expected payment.
From a legal point of view, the company is liable to pay the fees for looking up the 8 million records and should seek remedy with the hacker.

In fact, the guy is a script kiddie, who was not even able to program a simple for-loop generating the individual unique person ID-numbers required to look up address information. He therefore had to ask ChatGPT how to code a simple look-up script in Python and even managed to mess it up so they got no records out for people born in 1977.

articles.title: Windows 11 KB5127648 & KB5126653 cumulative updates released
articles.text:
Microsoft has released the Patch Tuesday Windows 11 KB5127648 and KB5126653 cumulative updates for versions 26H2/25H2/24H2 and 23H2 to fix security vulnerabilities and bugs, and add new features.
Today's updates are mandatory as they contain the October 2026 Patch Tuesday security patches for hundreds of vulnerabilities discovered in previous months.
You can install today's update by going to Start > Settings > Windows Update and clicking on 'Check for Updates.'
You can also manually download and install the update from the Microsoft Update Catalog.
This is the tenth 'Patch Tuesday' release in 2026, and it's based on 24H2, which means 25H2 or 26H2 get the same update. There are no exclusive or special changes. You'll get the same fixes across the two versions of Windows 11.
What's new in the October 2026 Patch Tuesday update
With today's update, Microsoft is adding new emojis to Windows 11 and fixing minor issues with File Explorer.
Here's the full list of improvements and fixes:
- [File Explorer] 
  - New! This update adjusts how the preview pane handles files downloaded from the web. For HTML files, a new Preview anyway button lets you acknowledge the warning and preview the file. Non-HTML files, such as PDFs, are now previewed automatically.
  - New! File Explorer Home now preserves the state of sections (expanded or collapsed), so you can pick up where you left off.
  - New! This update improves the reliability of thumbnail previews for cloud files in the Details pane. The pane has also been reorganized so file properties are easier to find and review at a glance.
  - New! The update addresses an issue that could clear the address bar contents when entering edit mode by clicking near the right side of the address bar.
- [Emoji] 
  - New! This update adds support for Emoji 17.0, including new emoji such as distorted face, fight cloud, and hairy creature. To insert them, press Windows + . to open the emoji panel.
  - New! This update also refines the design of several existing emoji for better consistency across platforms, including saluting face, face with peeking eye, goose, lotus, and kissing cat.
- [Widgets] New! This update introduces the Tips widget, which provides short, helpful guidance about Windows features. To add it to your Widgets board, open the board, select Add widgets, and then choose Tips. To add it to your lock screen, go to Settings > Personalization > Lock screen and add Tips to your lock screen widgets.
- [Personalization] This update includes a variety of improvements to desktop background experiences. 
  - This update improves the reliability of the Personalization > Background page in Settings.
  - This update adds support for using DIB image files as desktop backgrounds.
  - This update improves reliability of desktop slideshow transitions on newly created accounts.
  - This update improves resolution of previews when selecting a desktop background in Personalization > Background.
  - This update improves desktop background preview display in Settings for users with portrait mode monitors.
  - This update improves reliability of processing desktop wallpaper changes when they happen in quick succession.
  - This update adds support for using slideshow wallpapers with multiple desktops, so that it won’t automatically switch you back to Picture.
- [Bluetooth] 
  - This update contains several enhancements to improve reliability and experience when connecting to and using Bluetooth devices: 
    - During voice calls, the Windows shell volume flyout now appears when adjusting the volume of a Bluetooth Classic Audio accessory via the volume controls on the accessory, providing visual feedback of the new volume level.
    - This update improves the accuracy of the connection state displayed by Windows for accessories that have disconnected from the PC.
    - This update improves stability of the Bluetooth and devices page in Settings when managing Bluetooth and audio devices.
    - This update resolves an issue where the Bluetooth radio could be turned off, but the state of the radio control toggle in the Bluetooth and devices page in Settings shows as on.
  - This update improves Bluetooth audio stability and compatibility: 
    - This update improves microphone compatibility with certain Bluetooth Classic audio accessories.
    - This update resolves an issue that could result in a crash (error code 0x139) while streaming Bluetooth audio.
    - This update improves reliability and performance with LE Audio accessories.
    - This update improves the reliability of shared audio.
- [Accessibility] 
  - New! This update introduces Open apps maximized, an accessibility setting that automatically maximizes app windows as they open. It removes a bit of everyday friction whether you use a screen reader or magnification, work in tablet mode, or simply prefer a consistent, full-screen workspace. To turn it on, go to Settings > Accessibility > Visual effects and turn on Open apps maximized.
  - This update improves navigation of the Bluetooth quick settings page when using keyboard input, gamepad input, or Narrator.
- [Magnifier] 
  - New! This update brings a modernized visual refresh to the Magnifier taskbar. 
    - Updated icons Magnifier's toolbar icons align with Windows 11 visual design, giving the tool a cleaner, more modernized feel.
    - Refined spacing and padding The padding is adjusted with spacing across the toolbar for a more polished, consistent layout.
  - Views, zoom controls, keyboard shortcuts, and Read Aloud all behave exactly as they did in earlier versions.
- [Settings] 
  - This update improves the reliability of Settings when interacting with the contents of the Settings > Bluetooth & Devices > Printers & Scanners page.
  - This update updates Settings > Apps > Installed apps to show the version number at the top level for packaged apps, as it already does for other apps.
  - This update improves the time picker control in Settings so that it reflects your preferred time format when you switch between 12-hour and 24-hour time. This applies in places such as setting active hours and scheduling Night light.
  - This update improves persistence of the Allow multiple apps to use camera at the same time option in Settings > Bluetooth & Devices > Camera settings.
- [Touchpad] 
  - New! Additional gesture controls for precision touchpads are available in Settings > Bluetooth & devices > Touchpad: 
    - Single-finger scrolling — Scroll vertically with one finger starting from the left or right side of the touchpad.
    - Automatic scrolling — Keep scrolling without lifting your fingers by moving them near the edge of your touchpad while scrolling.
  - Previously, gesture controls for scroll and zoom speed and accelerate scrolling were released in the July 2026 update (KB5101684).
- [Copilot key] New! This update introduces a new Windows 11 setting that lets you remap the Copilot key to function as the Right Ctrl or Context Menu key, helping preserve familiar keyboard shortcuts and accessibility workflows. For more information, see Understand updates to the Copilot key on Windows devices.
- [Camera roll]1New! This update introduces Camera roll backup in Settings, helping eligible users protect their photos with OneDrive. You can turn on the feature from the Settings Home or Accounts page and complete setup on a mobile phone using a QR code.
- [Fonts] 
  - New! This update adds support for the Garay and Beria Erfe scripts to the Ebrima font, the first Microsoft font to support both. Garay was encoded in Unicode 16.0 and Beria Erfe in Unicode 17.0.
  - New! This update also refines the Adlam glyph designs in Ebrima to align with the current Unicode standard and improve consistency.
- [Windows Recovery (WinRE)] 
  - New! This update adds a recovery remote management plug-in for extending WinRE management capabilities for MDM providers. For more information, see Recovery Remote Management Overview.
- [Kiosk mode] 
  - The Windows + Tab keyboard shortcut is now disabled when using a restricted UX kiosk.
  - The Windows + A and Windows + C keyboard shortcuts are now disabled when using single-app kiosk mode.
- [Windows Backup] 
  - PC-to-PC Migration is no longer available. This feature, introduced through a phased rollout, previously allowed you to transfer files and settings directly from your previous PC when setting up a new Windows PC. To back up and restore your files, settings, and other supported items when moving to a new PC, use Windows Backup. For more information, see Backup and restore with Windows Backup.
- [Power and battery] This update improves display and performance in certain scenarios where a plugged-in laptop incorrectly detects a transition from AC power to battery power.
Microsoft is not aware of any new issues with this month's Patch Tuesday, but it warns that some PCs might still have audio issues after the update. The bug affects USB 1.0 audio devices and isn't widespread.
