articles.title: SA's KhayaHR builds AI-first workforce platform for frontline economy - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
South African startup KhayaHR is building an AI-first workforce platform for the country’s frontline economy, and has already signed up more than 12,000 workers since launching in May.
Founded by Jacques Roux, KhayaHR gives workers a portable digital workforce passport. Employers can use it to find, assess, hire and then manage frontline staff in one place.
“Most recruitment technology assumes that candidates already have formal CVs, established digital histories and easily verifiable employment records,” Roux told Disrupt Africa.
“That assumption excludes many frontline workers. Their work experience may be informal, references fragmented, certificates stored as photographs or paper documents, and availability known only through personal networks or WhatsApp groups.”
The worker passport holds identity and right-to-work confirmation, skills, experience, references, employer recommendations, certificates, availability, and optional voice or video introductions. Workers cannot publish a profile until their identity and right to work in South Africa have been confirmed.
On the employer side, Khaya AI turns a natural-language hiring requirement into a structured search of the available workforce.
“An employer can describe the role, location and experience they need, and Khaya AI converts that into a structured search,” said Roux. “Employers can then assess real profile evidence, connect with suitable workers and manage employment through KhayaHR’s HR and payroll system.”
Khaya AI also works as an on-demand HR assistant for households and small businesses that do not have an internal HR department. It offers practical guidance on onboarding, contracts, leave, pay, UIF and managing workers correctly.
“This is an important part of the model – KhayaHR does not stop when a worker is found,” Roux said. “Once a worker is hired, many households and small businesses have no affordable HR support to help them manage contracts, leave, payroll, UIF and everyday employment questions correctly. We help smaller employers move from recruitment into responsible, structured employment.”
The platform also includes KhayaHR Academy, which offers short, mobile-friendly certificate courses. Certificates earned there are added automatically to the worker’s profile.
“That creates a direct link between learning, verified evidence and employability,” said Roux. “The longer-term objective is to create a complete workforce operating system connecting worker identity, skills development, recruitment, accessible HR support and ongoing employment management.”
KhayaHR is entirely self-funded and run by the husband-and-wife team. Roux leads product, technology and commercial strategy, while his wife manages most day-to-day operations and worker-facing activity.
“We have deliberately kept the team small while building and validating the platform,” he said.
Workers have taken to the platform quickly. KhayaHR now has a live, publicly discoverable workforce spanning all nine South African provinces and 50 occupations. It has also launched its first five Academy courses and an integrated HR and payroll platform.
“Worker uptake has been significantly faster than we initially expected,” said Roux. “The strongest demand has come from domestic work, housekeeping, cleaning, care, hospitality, retail, general labour and related frontline roles.”
KhayaHR competes with conventional job boards, specialist domestic-worker marketplaces, recruitment agencies, HR consultancies and standalone HR or payroll products. Roux said its point of difference is bringing everything together in one platform.
“Our distinction is combining the worker passport, identity and right-to-work requirements, AI-assisted discovery, on-demand HR guidance, the Academy and employment-management tools,” he said.
The startup earns revenue in several ways. Employers pay to unlock and connect with workers, and they subscribe to the HR and payroll platform on a per-employee basis. Workers can buy Academy courses, and larger employers can engage KhayaHR for targeted sourcing, readiness and placement programmes.
“We are generating early revenue, but the business remains in its initial commercialisation stage,” Roux said. “We are currently reinvesting in product development, verification, worker acquisition and employer adoption rather than optimising for short-term profitability.”
The rapid growth on the worker side has brought its own problems.
“The largest challenge has been balancing rapid worker adoption with employer demand,” said Roux. “Building a workforce supply base has proven faster than changing employer recruitment behaviour. The next commercial challenge is translating that worker adoption into consistent employer demand, successful placements and ongoing use of the HR platform at scale.”
Verification is also demanding work.
“Maintaining trust means reviewing identity, right-to-work and supporting evidence carefully rather than allowing every registration to become a public profile,” he said.
Designing for a mobile-first audience with different levels of literacy, data access and digital confidence has also shaped the product.
“This has required us to simplify onboarding, use WhatsApp extensively and continually rethink how workers complete profiles and learning content,” Roux said. “Making AI-supported HR guidance simple, useful and responsible is another important challenge. Small employers need practical answers in plain language, while the platform must still recognise when a matter requires professional or legal intervention.”
“As a self-funded two-person business, prioritisation is constant. We have had to build the technology, operate the platform, support workers and develop the commercial market simultaneously.”
For now, KhayaHR is focused on growing employer adoption and placements in South Africa. Once that is working, it plans to expand into selected Southern African markets.
“Once the model has repeatable employer demand and sustainable unit economics, we intend to expand through local partnerships,” said Roux. “We do not want to copy South African employment rules into other countries; identity, right-to-work and employment requirements would need to be adapted for each market.”

articles.title: Google Wallet : 4 nouveautés débarquent, dont le scan des tickets de caisse
articles.text:
Google continue d’améliorer l’écosystème Android avec une série d’améliorations repérées dans la dernière mise à jour de Google Play Services. L’application Google Wallet gagne ainsi quatre nouveautés, dont une très attendue.
Google Wallet va pouvoir scanner les tickets de caisse
La numérisation des tickets de caisse débarque enfin dans Google Wallet. Cela va vous permettre de stocker et de suivre directement vos tickets dans l’application sans avoir à saisir manuellement chaque information. Google n’a pas encore détaillé l’ensemble du fonctionnement ni précisé le calendrier exact du déploiement de cette mise à jour, mais c’est une nouveauté très attendue par de nombreux utilisateurs de l’application.
Un nouveau centre de messagerie fera également son apparition dans l’interface, même si l’on ne sait pas encore grand-chose à son sujet. Cette section devrait centraliser les notifications et les informations utiles transmises par l’application. Du côté des alertes de transaction, les noms des marchands s’affichent désormais de manière beaucoup plus lisible pour identifier immédiatement à qui vous avez fait un paiement.
Un paiement plus rapide sur Chrome pour Android et de nouvelles fonctions sur le Play Store
L’expérience de paiement en ligne est également améliorée pour les utilisateurs de Google Pay sur Chrome pour Android. Lors du partage des coordonnées comme le nom, l’adresse e-mail et le numéro de téléphone avec un site marchand, il devient possible de contourner l’interface classique de demande de paiement pour finaliser l’achat plus rapidement.
À lire : Google Wallet change complètement l’affichage de vos cartes de paiement, voici à quoi ça ressemble
Google profite aussi de la mise à jour des services Google Play pour améliorer le Google Play Store, qui intègre désormais des résumés générés par intelligence artificielle pour les avis d’utilisateurs et de nouvelles étiquettes pour filtrer les collections. Comme toutes les mises à jour, nous avons également droit à des correctifs de stabilité pour l’ensemble des appareils compatibles.

articles.title: Hostinger’s Auksė Žirgulė on winning customer experience in the AI era
articles.text:
Hostinger’s Auksė Žirgulė on winning customer experience in the AI era
Žirgulė highlighted on how AI tools are changing the way businesses are built, customer expectations are changing and how experimentation is now the key to success.
As AI lowers technical barriers in website building by making coding cheap and accessible, where does this leave businesses building for an online audience?
During a fireside chat on the inaugural day of TechSparks 2026 on October 13, Shradha Sharma, Founder and CEO of YourStory and The Bharat Project spoke with Auksė Žirgulė, VP of Product at Hostinger about the changing customer expectations as AI takes over the bulk of software building.
Žirgulė highlighted on that experimentation is now the key to building customer experience. "I’ve noticed that their [customer] questions have become more complex. Earlier, the focus was on building a product. Now, customers are asking questions such as: “The market is saturated, and there are already so many products. What should I do next? How do I attract customers? How do I drive traffic?”
"They’re asking more fundamental business questions rather than simply asking how to build something," she added.
As AI makes building now easier, Žirgulė noted that innovation still remains the key.
"You can build anything, but if you don’t know what problem you’re solving, what’s the point? Founders need to understand the problem they’re addressing and test their products as early as possible. The second factor is innovation. There are so many products in the market that you need to find ways to stand out."
Žirgulė drove the point home using Apple as an example. "Apple didn’t invent the mobile phone or the touchscreen. What it did was deliver an exceptional customer experience. We sometimes become so focused on building products and watching our competitors that we forget to look for new ways to solve problems. That’s where innovation comes in."
However, she noted that even with AI, founders form the core of the company.
"Founders are still the final decision-makers. I don’t know what will happen over the next two years; perhaps AI will eventually make many of these decisions. But, for now, a founder’s job is to understand customers and exercise product judgement. AI can do a lot, but the founder still has the final say," added Žirgulė.
Adding to this, she said that although there is a rush to build and test a product, without thinking how to take it to the market, founders need to think about the business model and the route to market, not just the product.
With AI tools making website in minutes, Sharma asked if the tools can churn out mediocre designs and how founders can navigate this issue
Commenting on this, Žirgulė said,"If you have a website that generates sales and supports your business, it may already be doing its job well. It doesn’t necessarily need to win a design award. The same applies to software. You need to test it, speak to customers and iterate. Ultimately, you need to evaluate whether it delivers the intended results."
With the increasing number of products now easily available in the market, Žirgulė said that this will eventually change customer expectations. "As more people gain the ability to build products, expectations will rise. Products that deliver better user experiences and higher quality will stand out."
As AI agents are now taking independent decisions in business workflows, Žirgulė advises caution. "We need to test how it works, put the right safeguards and capabilities in place, and observe its actions. Experimentation, testing and quality assurance are essential."
Founded in 2004 in Lithuania, Hostinger is a global web hosting and domain provider. It claims to serve 4.6 million businesses and creators across 150+ countries.

articles.title: Neues Modell zum Ende des Sonnensystems prognostiziert frühen Zerfall
articles.text:
Hundertmal schneller als gedacht: Warum unser Sonnensystem viel früher im Chaos versinkt
Bislang galt das äußere Sonnensystem in der Wissenschaft als ein äußerst stabiles Konstrukt, bei dem selbst nach dem Tod der Sonne in einigen Milliarden Jahren die äußeren Planeten für weitere 30 bis 100 Milliarden Jahre geordnet auf ihren Bahnen verbleiben sollten. Zwar wird unsere Sonne als Roter Riese vermutlich die inneren Planeten zerstören, doch erst externe galaktische Einflüsse galten als endgültige Bedrohung für Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus und Neptun.
Ein Team von Forscher:innen um den Astronomen Konstantin Batygin am California Institute of Technology (Caltech) im US-amerikanischen Pasadena kommt nach neuen Analysen jedoch zu einem vollkommen anderen Ergebnis. Wie aus einer im Fachmagazin The Astrophysical Journal Letters veröffentlichten Studie hervorgeht, destabilisieren sich die Planetenbahnen vermutlich hundertmal schneller, als es bisherige Simulationen prognostiziert haben.
Ungleichmäßiger Masseverlust verändert die Bahnen
Bisherige Computermodelle gingen davon aus, dass unsere Sonne ihre äußere Hülle in der Endphase gleichmäßig abstoßen wird, wodurch sich die Umlaufbahnen der äußeren Planeten zwar ausdehnen, aber stabil bleiben. Die wahre Ursache für die nun berechnete beschleunigte Destabilisierung liegt jedoch in eben jener Art und Weise, wie der sterbende Stern seine Masse verliert.
Beobachtungen an anderen Weißen Zwergen deuten auf ein abweichendes Verhalten hin, bei dem Sterne in dieser Endphase ihre Materie oftmals asymmetrisch in Schüben abstoßen, wie Scinexx einordnet. Jeder dieser Auswürfe erzeugt einen leichten Rückstoß, der den Stern physisch bewegt, wodurch sich dieser stochastische, solare Massenverlust deutlich auf die Gravitationsverhältnisse im gesamten Sternensystem auswirkt.
Stochastische Rückstöße sorgen für Chaos
Die Forscher:innen um Batygin simulierten die zukünftigen Entwicklungen und nahmen für ein plausibles Szenario an, dass die Sonne ihre Hülle in rund 4.600 einzelnen Auswürfen abstößt. Jeder einzelne Auswurf entspricht in der Simulation dabei einem Verlust von etwa einem Zehntausendstel der ursprünglichen Sonnenmasse.
Die dadurch entstehenden Rückstöße von typischerweise sieben Metern pro Sekunde summieren sich über die Zeit und verändern die Planetenbahnen minimal, aber kontinuierlich, wie AAS Nova berichtet. Um die langfristigen Konsequenzen dieser fortlaufenden Impulse zu evaluieren, führte das Team des Caltech insgesamt 672 Simulationen mit unterschiedlichen Auswurfgrößen durch.
Instabilität beginnt schon im Riesenstadium
Diese vielen kleinen Störungen führen laut den Berechnungen der Forscher:innen dazu, dass sich die Bahnen der äußeren Planeten massiv verschieben. Bei Modellen, die Auswürfe während der gesamten Riesenphase der Sonne berücksichtigten, kam es in 37 von 48 Durchläufen bereits zu Bahnkreuzungen, bevor der Weiße Zwerg überhaupt entstanden war.
Rund 40 Prozent dieser Simulationen zeigten schon zu diesem frühen Zeitpunkt massive Zerrüttungen, durch die das Sternensystem seine bisherige Ordnung verliert. So wurde Saturn in einigen Durchläufen komplett aus dem Sonnensystem geschleudert, während in anderen Berechnungen Uranus und Neptun schlichtweg ihre Positionen tauschten.
Auch bei moderaten Auswurfmassen zeigte sich ein dynamisches Bild, bei dem den Daten zufolge eine Wahrscheinlichkeit von etwa 20 Prozent besteht, dass Jupiter und Saturn sowie Uranus und Neptun in sogenannte Bahnresonanzen eintreten. In diesen Zuständen stehen die Umlaufzeiten der Planeten in einem bestimmten Verhältnis zueinander.
Den Berechnungen zufolge schützen solche Resonanzen die Planeten jedoch nicht vor dem endgültigen Zerfall, da rund drei Milliarden Jahre nach der Entstehung des Weißen Zwergs nahezu 90 Prozent der simulierten Modellverläufe instabile Eigenschaften aufwiesen. Das bisherige Zeitfenster für ein geordnetes Ende korrigiert sich auf Basis der wahrscheinlichsten Berechnung damit von bis zu 100 Milliarden auf lediglich rund eine Milliarde Jahre.
Unsicherheiten im physikalischen Modell
Diese Zahlen stellen allerdings keine absoluten Prognosen, sondern lediglich bedingte Wahrscheinlichkeiten auf der Basis eines physikalischen Modells dar, dessen Ausgang stark von der Masse der tatsächlichen solaren Schübe abhängt. In Simulationen mit sehr geringen Auswurfmassen blieben beispielsweise mehr als 98 Prozent der Systeme dauerhaft stabil.
Ob die Sonne jene Asymmetrien entwickelt, die in den drastischeren Modellen angenommen werden, lässt sich aus den aktuellen Daten noch nicht abschließend beweisen. Beobachtungen der zukünftigen Sonne sind naturgemäß unmöglich, weshalb die Parameter auf Messungen an anderen Sternen basieren und weitere Validierungen durch astronomische Beobachtungen erfordern.

articles.title: Environ 5 € par brossette : le lot de six Oral-B iO Ultimate Clean est à 30,39 €
articles.text:
Le lot de six brossettes Oral-B iO Ultimate Clean noires est à 30,39 €
Réservées aux brosses à dents électriques Oral-B iO, les brossettes Ultimate Clean possèdent une tête ronde et des brins inclinés pour atteindre les zones difficiles d’accès.
Amazon propose le lot de six brossettes Oral-B iO Ultimate Clean noires à 30,39 €, contre un prix conseillé de 49,90 €. L’écart atteint 19,51 €, soit environ 39 %. Par rapport au prix le plus bas des 30 derniers jours de 31,99 €, la baisse représente 1,60 €, soit 5 %. Le lot est vendu et expédié par Amazon.
Des brossettes réservées aux brosses à dents Oral-B iO
Les Ultimate Clean sont des têtes de rechange pour la gamme Oral-B iO. Elles ne sont pas destinées aux manches des gammes Vitality, Pro, Smart ou Genius, qui utilisent d’autres brossettes. Il faut donc vérifier la référence de sa brosse à dents avant de commander : la marque Oral-B seule ne suffit pas à garantir la compatibilité.
Chaque brossette possède une tête ronde avec des brins inclinés à 16 degrés, conçus pour atteindre les zones difficiles d’accès et accompagner le nettoyage autour des dents. Le lot comprend uniquement les six brossettes noires, sans manche électrique. Il permet de renouveler les têtes d’une brosse déjà possédée.
Six recharges à environ 5,07 € pièce
À 30,39 € le lot, chaque brossette revient à environ 5,07 €. Oral-B recommande un remplacement tous les trois mois, ou plus tôt si les brins sont usés. Pour une seule personne, six brossettes représentent donc une réserve théorique de 18 mois, à adapter à leur état réel.
Les brins se décolorent progressivement pour signaler le moment du remplacement. Le tarif de 30,39 € correspond à un achat ponctuel. Amazon affiche également une option à 28,87 € avec « Prévoyez et Économisez », qui implique des livraisons récurrentes : il faut sélectionner la formule correspondant à ses besoins au moment de la commande.

articles.title: Can the RAM crisis get any worse? Quite possibly, as Intel CEO reportedly predicts another 2 to 3 years of pain, and DDR4 price has shot up 24% over the last 3 months
articles.text:
RAM is getting pricier than ever, with DDR4 up 24% in the last quarter — and Intel's CEO has reportedly said we have another 2 to 3 years of this
Reasonable prices are becoming even more of a distant memory
- Intel's CEO has said that AI hardware will be in short supply for the next 2 to 3 years
- Of course, this refers to the ongoing memory crisis, and consumers will get shorter shrift than AI players
- A new report from Barclays also shows that contract pricing for RAM has risen 24% over the past quarter for DDR4 (and 20% for DDR5)
Need more fuel to stoke the idea that the RAM crisis is here to stay? Doubtless you don't, but sadly we've had a couple more indications that the memory shortage will last for a depressingly long time, with Intel's CEO the latest to weigh in.
Wccftech reports that Intel's Lip-Bu Tan was speaking in Singapore at the Asia Future Forward event, a conference organized by DBS Bank, where the CEO discussed his thoughts regarding trends with AI – including the amount of memory it's eating up.
As flagged by Theresa Perrin on X, Tan observed that "AI hardware will stay in short supply for the next 2 to 3 years" — primarily referring to memory — and that this was "driven by persistent constraints in the underlying tech supply chain."
While the CEO is talking directly about RAM (as well as GPUs, and to an extent CPUs) used in data centers for AI applications, the fact that the AI industry is going to be short on supply for perhaps the next three years means that consumer RAM is going to be even thinner on the ground. It's no secret that the greater profits to be had by catering to the AI industry mean that this memory is the priority for chip makers.
Wccftech also noticed another post on X, from 456X, highlighting a new report from Barclays that shows contract pricing (from chip makers) for DDR4 RAM has risen 24% over the last three months, and that DDR5 has gone up 20%.
Barclays further observed that one of the big memory chip makers, Micron, will see its supply levels of RAM remain constrained through 2028. In other words, we can expect that memory supply is going to keep on being a major problem for the next two years, with 'through' 2028 meaning that this year is included in the gloomy prediction.
Analysis: yet more doom nuggets — and then there's the rise of the robots
The reported rises in the contract price of RAM according to Barclays match what we've seen at retail over the past few months, with some notable jumps in the price of DDR5 memory (which in Germany has reached a ridiculous level of 544% up on the price it was before the RAM crisis began last July).
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
What Barclays, and Intel's CEO, are now telling us is that this kind of pain is likely to continue, and that RAM supply will continue to be frustratingly short until 2029. Unfortunately these kinds of forecasts are becoming more commonplace, with pretty much everyone's view appearing to align with the idea of the RAM crisis hanging around until the end of the decade.
At the very least, we can expect 2027 to be a repeat of this year — meaning more memory prices hikes, and other components besides, such as GPUs — with 2028 likely to follow in a similar vein. Indeed, Micron has said as much itself, while letting us know that robots (or 'physical AI') will be eating up a lot of RAM supply in the future.

articles.title: Nvidia doubles DLSS 5 performance, reduces 4K VRAM usage by 20% with latest model — October update cuts footprint by 24% to roughly 118 million parameters
articles.text:
Nvidia doubles DLSS 5 performance, reduces 4K VRAM usage by 20% with latest model — October update cuts footprint by 24% to roughly 118 million parameters
A big step.
Nvidia has today announced that its somewhat controversial DLSS 5 technology — AI-powered neural rendering for gaming — is now two times faster than the current model, marking a 10x performance leap since March. The model is also now smaller and uses up to 20% less VRAM.
Nvidia says it has achieved this through a combination of "systematic pipeline optimizations and neural model refinements." As mentioned, the latest performance jump over the current model is a 2x leap, which means that the transformation DLSS applies to games through lighting and beyond will now run at higher frame rates or more intense settings.
Nvidia says the DLSS 5 October update shrinks the overall DLSS 5 model's footprint by nearly a quarter to 118 million parameters, and reduces VRAM usage at 4K by 20%. As such, the company claims that at similar visual fidelity, the GPU overhead versus the September model has been halved. Elsewhere, Nvidia says the change can boost frame rates by up to 1.4x.
The new faster model will debut in NBA 2K27 on October 16; you can see a comparison in the video below:
Nvidia confirmed it will bring DLSS 5 to Hogwarts Legacy next month. The technology continues to be supported on RTX 50-series GPUs, as well as GeForce NOW and the new RTX Spark lineup.
Nvidia is also introducing a new faster Performance Mode for Frame Generation on RTX 50 Series, as well as RTX 40 series GPUs, and RTX Spark laptops. The company says that a new "Preset C" mode replaces the AI model previously used "to calculate optical flow for elements like UI or ray-traced effects" with a new algorithm that is faster and lighter, boosting DLSS Frame Generation, MFG, and Dynamic MFG. The company says this is worth 35% in terms of speed on the RTX 5060.

articles.title: Una demo gratis en Steam usa tanta IA que sus autores han tenido que pedir un crédito para pagar las facturas
articles.text:
¿Quién no se ha bajado alguna vez la demo de algún juego? Es una manera perfecta de saber cómo es la experiencia antes de pagarla, por eso las demos son una gran herramienta de marketing para los desarrolladores. Pero ¿qué ocurre cuando cada partida le cuesta dinero al estudio? Y no poco: la demo de 'Enseñar a conducir a mi hermana' está poniendo en jaque a sus desarrolladores.
Un simulador de conducción diferente. El juego parte de la premisa de la simulación, pero no encarnas al piloto, sino al pasajero. Quien conduce es tu hermana, de ahí el nombre. La gracia es que debes enseñarle a conducir a fuerza de explicárselo a viva voz.
En países como Estados Unidos, alguien sin carnet de conducir puede ponerse al volante si un copiloto experimentado hace de instructor, siempre que cuenten con permisos. Es justo el papel que recrea la demo de 'Enseñar a conducir a mi hermana' ('Teach my little sister how to drive'): empiezas diciéndole a tu hermana cómo arrancar el coche y terminas en contradirección sorteando coches de frente.
El pozo de los tokens. El juego utilizaba Google Gemini para interpretar lo que le dices a tu hermana y para las respuestas del propio juego, con ChatGPT como modelo secundario (el estudio actualmente prioriza a OpenAI). Los desarrolladores no esperaban un número muy alto de jugadores, pero estos sobrepasaron los 430 simultáneos en Steam. Con esa afluencia, la infraestructura que había montado Easy Fox, creadores del juego, empezó a arrojar errores por límites de uso.
'Enseñar a conducir a mi hermana' requiere una conexión constante con modelos de IA en la nube con el gasto en tokens que eso supone. Muchos tokens, según Easy Fox, que no esperaba que una simple demo les pudiera empujar a problemas financieros. Porque el juego definitivo no tiene planes de salir hasta enero de 2027.
Un crédito para sobrevivir al éxito. En una actualización de su página de Steam, el equipo reconocía el agujero:
"Actualmente, gastamos más de 1.000 dólares estadounidenses al día en los servicios de IA de la demo. Esto no se debe a que cada jugador tenga un costo especialmente elevado. El costo total ha crecido por la cantidad de personas que están jugando. Para seguir manteniendo la demo, también hemos recurrido a un préstamo bancario".
La paradoja es que estos problemas para el estudio están surgiendo con una demo que es completamente gratuita y que tampoco tiene un pico excesivo de usuarios simultáneos. Aun así, Easy Fox mantiene el compromiso con Steam y con todos los jugadores que ya se descargaron el avance del juego.
"Queremos continuar ofreciendo la demo y nos encantaría que más personas pudieran disfrutarla. Sin embargo, somos un equipo pequeño de cuatro personas, y la presión económica podría obligarnos a retirar la demo antes de lo previsto, todavía antes del lanzamiento completo. Por el momento, no hemos tomado esa decisión".
La factura de la versión final. La IA es imprescindible para jugar, por lo que retirarla no entra en los planes de Easy Fox. Cuando llegue la versión de pago en enero de 2027, el estudio tiene previsto repercutir el uso estimado de los modelos en el precio cerrado del título, sin cobrar tokens aparte a los usuarios. También planean incluir soporte para modelos locales en aquellos equipos que tengan suficiente hardware.
Un juego donde la IA es el soporte vital. Easy Fox ha desarrollado un título donde la jugabilidad se basa en cómo interactuamos mediante la voz. Es lo que mueve a 'Enseñar a conducir a mi hermana', sin los modelos interpretando las interacciones no hay juego. Y es un buen adelanto de lo que se está cocinando en el mundillo: la IA quiere desterrar a los NPC que repiten siempre la misma frase. Esperemos que la factura no terminemos pagándola los jugadores.

articles.title: Avengers Doomsday : il manquera bien un autre membre des avengers dans le film
articles.text:
Selon son interprète, Hawkeye, l’un des six Avengers d’origine, ne sera pas dans le film. « Non, non, non, non. Pas dans celui-là », a lâché l’acteur lorsqu’on l’a interrogé sur sa présence face au Docteur Doom de Robert Downey Jr. ce 12 octobre 2026. « Je ne suis pas dans Doomsday, donc les Avengers vont probablement perdre, juste pour que vous le sachiez… Ils ne m’ont pas appelé, donc c’est de leur faute s’ils perdent. » Un mauvais signe pour Avengers Doomsday ?
La statistique Hawkeye, un porte-bonheur trop voyant pour être ignoré ?
Sur les réseaux sociaux, les fans du Marvel Cinematic Universe ont vite ressorti une statistique : dans Avengers: Infinity War, Hawkeye était aux abonnés absents et l’équipe s’est fait écraser par Thanos, qui efface la moitié des êtres vivants de l’univers. Dans Avengers: Endgame, Clint Barton revient dans le rang et les super-héros l’emportent, comme dans Avengers (2012) et Avengers: L’Ère d’Ultron, où il était déjà de la partie. Hawkeye porte-t-il chance ?
Autant dire que si Kevin Feige a décidé de se passer de son archer fétiche face au Docteur Doom, les Avengers partent statistiquement avec un handicap majeur. Mais faut-il vraiment croire Renner ?
Doomsday : le casting paquebot qui n’a plus de place à bord
Même sans Hawkeye au compteur, la fiche de paie d’Avengers: Doomsday frôle déjà l’absurde. Entre le retour de Robert Downey Jr. sous le masque de Doom, Chris Hemsworth (Thor), Chris Evans (Steve Rogers), l’introduction des Quatre Fantastiques, les Thunderbolts, la garde de Wakanda et une bonne partie des X-Men de l’ère Fox (Patrick Stewart, Ian McKellen, James Marsden…), le film ressemble à un embouteillage géant.
Dans ce bazar multiversel où Kevin Feige tente désespérément de raviver la flamme des grands jours, l’absence (réelle ou feinte) de Clint Barton résonne comme un symbole. Que Renner mente comme un arracheur de dents sous la pression des clauses de confidentialité de Disney ou qu’il ait réellement été oublié par la production, sa déclaration met le doigt là où ça fait mal : sans la cohésion de son équipe d’origine, la nouvelle mouture des Avengers risque fort d’aller au casse-pipe face à Doom.
Avengers: Doomsday est attendu dans les salles sombres pour décembre. On saura alors si la prédiction de Renner était une prophétie ou juste de la comédie bien rodée.

articles.title: De nouvelles stars de la jeunesse arrivent sur les Freebox avec Kidjo
articles.text:
Les abonnés Freebox et Free Mobile peuvent désormais lancer Kidjo depuis leur téléviseur. La plateforme ludo-éducative, sans publicité, arrive avec Peppa Pig, La Pat' Patrouille et un mois d'essai offert.
Depuis ce mardi 13 octobre 2026, Kidjo, la plateforme jeunesse du groupe Cafeyn, bien connue des opérateurs, s'installe directement sur le téléviseur des abonnés Freebox et Free Mobile. Les 3-10 ans y retrouveront leurs séries préférées, des histoires audio et des jeux, dans un cadre garanti sans publicité. Pour les parents, la facture est douce, puisqu'une formule mensuelle sans engagement est proposée, et même un pass à la journée pour les week-ends pluvieux.
Kidjo ne se limite pas seulement à la Freebox
L'histoire de Kidjo remonte à une dizaine d'années, lorsque la plateforme fut lancée comme une application de streaming. Depuis, le service a pris du galon et s'est mué en plateforme ludo-éducative complète, organisée en trois univers, avec la TV pour les vidéos, les Stories pour les livres audio, et Games pour les jeux.
Des centaines d'heures de programmes y sont rangées. Hello Kitty, Peppa Pig, Les Schtroumpfs, Trotro ou Masha y côtoient des comptines, des premières pas avec les chiffres et les lettres, des sujets scientifiques, et même des tutos de magie et de dessin.
Le grand écran du salon n'est qu'une porte d'entrée parmi d'autres. Car Kidjo reste accessible dans tout l'écosystème Free TV, la plateforme télé de l'opérateur, réservée à la France métropolitaine. Il se glisse aussi sur téléphone, tablette TV connectée, Amazon Fire TV, Apple TV et même sur le web. Il s'invite également dans le casque Apple Vision Pro. Peppa Pig et sa bande ne sont donc jamais bien loin.
Sans pub ni engagement, l'abonnement Kidjo joue la sérénité
Kidjo s'ouvre d'abord sur 30 jours d'essai gratuit, ce qui est toujours appréciable. Il faut ensuite compter sur un tarif de 4,99 euros par mois, sans engagement comme nous le disions plus haut. Pour une journée chez les grands-parents ou un long trajet, un Pass 24 h est proposé, avec un prix relativement accessible, à 2,99 euros. L'offre vise ici les clients Freebox Ultra, Pop, Delta, Révolution et Mini 4K. Chez Free Mobile, seuls les Forfaits Free 5G/5G+ et Série Free sont concernés, sans le Forfait 2 euros.
L'autre promesse, c'est un environnement entièrement sécurisé, sans la moindre publicité. Les enfants peuvent piocher dans leurs programmes en toute confiance, et les parents souffler un moment. Le service Kidjo est donc porté par Cafeyn, la plateforme de presse en ligne qui aujourd'hui revendique plus de 2,5 millions d'utilisateurs.
Kidjo figure par ses acquisitions, aux côtés de miLibris ou Blendle. En tout as, cette arrivée renforce la place du groupe chez Free. Le fondateur et PDG de Kidjo, Martin Poix, espère toucher toujours plus de familles, et parie sur un partenariat durable avec l'opérateur de Xavier Niel.

articles.title: London's Obsero raises €1 million to help brands improve visibility in AI-powered search | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Obsero, a British AI Search platform and consultancy, has raised €1 million ($1.2 million) in Seed funding to develop their first specialist AI agents (trained on their GEO playbook), double its engineering team, and accelerate GTM.
The round was led by SFC Capital alongside several of Obsero’s own customers.
Mike Logue, co-founder and CEO of Obsero, says: “When customers put their own money into your business, it tells you something no pitch deck can. AI is changing how people discover brands faster than any shift I’ve seen in marketing, and most teams are still flying blind. We’ve spent a year learning what actually moves the needle. Now it’s time to put that into the hands of every marketing team that needs it.”
Obsero’s Seed round comes amid investment in European startups developing AI search visibility and marketing automation tools.
In 2026, EU-Startups reported that fellow British company Searchable raised €11.9 million to expand its AI-led search performance platform, while London-based geoSurge secured €10 million to develop technology addressing how brands are represented within generative AI systems.
Elsewhere, Lisbon-based DOJO AI raised €5.1 million to develop its AI marketing platform and expand in the US, while Manchester-based Revnu secured €2.6 million to grow its AI-driven sales and marketing automation business, which also incorporates generative engine optimisation.
Together with Obsero, these five funding rounds represent approximately €30.6 million in disclosed investment across AI search visibility and adjacent marketing technologies in 2026.
EU-Startups has also previously covered Obsero’s lead investor, SFC Capital, including its €11 million commitment from the British Business Bank in July 2026.
Andy Francos, co-founder and CPO of Obsero, adds: “I’ve spent my career in organic search, and I’ve never seen the ground move this quickly. Much of what worked in SEO still matters, but AI engines weigh sources, context and credibility in new ways. Brands that assume their old playbook will carry over are already losing ground. Over the past year we’ve built a clear, evidence-based view of what drives visibility in AI Search. Now we’re putting that expertise into agents, so every team can apply it, not just the ones that can afford a specialist.”
Founded in 2025, Obsero is an AI Search platform and consultancy that helps brands increase their visibility in AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Google’s AI Overviews.
Obsero was founded by Mike Logue and Andy Francos, who met at IG Group in 2019. Watching AI assistants start to answer the questions their customers used to type into Google, they saw that brands had no way of knowing whether they were being recommended, or what to do about it.
In its first year, Obsero has reportedly tracked and analysed over 10 million AI answers. Its clients include Zopa Bank and Pepperstone, and agency partners include IDHL and Silverbean.
Obsero pairs its proprietary AI Search platform with a senior consultancy team. Together they track how AI engines talk about brands, which sources they trust, and what marketers can do to increase visibility.
Ed Stevenson, Fund Principal at SFC Capital, says: “AI assistants are quickly becoming the new front door to the internet, and brands need to know whether they’re being recommended. Obsero combines proprietary technology with senior expertise, and its plan to productise those learnings into specialist agents gives it a clear path to scale. Mike and Andy are precisely the kind of founders we want to back.”

Pour 9,99 euros par mois, ce forfait ne fixe plus aucune limite de data en France métropolitaine, à condition d’être abonné Freebox. Selon l’Arcep, un abonné consomme en moyenne 19,3 Go par mois au deuxième trimestre 2026. Autant dire que l’illimité vise surtout les gros consommateurs. Streaming en haute qualité, jeux en ligne ou partage de connexion avec un ordinateur passent sans surveiller son compteur. Sans Freebox, le même forfait coûte 19,99 euros pour 350 Go, ce qui montre bien l’intérêt de l’offre groupée.
Free ajoute plusieurs services habituellement facturés en option. L’option eSIM Watch permet d’utiliser une montre connectée sans son smartphone, en France comme à l’étranger. Free mVPN chiffre la connexion en France, et l’application Free TV donne accès à plus de 300 chaînes. À l’étranger, 35 Go sont utilisables dans plus de 115 destinations, et les appels, SMS et MMS restent illimités depuis plus de 65 destinations.
Freebox Pop et Free Family, comment ça marche ?
La remise s’adresse aux abonnés Freebox Pop, hors Freebox Pop S. La box coûte 29,99 euros par mois la première année, puis 39,99 euros. Elle apporte la fibre jusqu’à 5 Gbit/s partagés en téléchargement (2,5 Gbit/s au maximum sur un seul port Ethernet et 0,5 Gbit/s en Wi-Fi, selon Free), le Wi-Fi 7 et le Player TV Free 4K. Avec un Forfait Free 5G+, l’ensemble revient donc à 39,98 euros par mois la première année, puis 49,98 euros. Pour en profiter, la ligne mobile doit être rattachée à l’abonnement Freebox depuis l’Espace Abonné, sur le même compte, avec le même RIB et la même adresse.
L’offre Free Family fonctionne pour toute la famille, dans la limite de quatre forfaits. Les lignes Free 5G+ supplémentaires profitent aussi de 10 euros de remise la première année, puis de 4 euros, soit 9,99 euros puis 15,99 euros par mois. La remise ne se cumule pas avec d’autres promotions, et elle disparaît en cas de résiliation de la box ou de détachement de la ligne.
Côté réseau, Free affiche la meilleure couverture de la population en 5G selon le baromètre nPerf publié en septembre 2026, avec 88,61 %. En revanche, Free arrive dernier sur la couverture géographique 5G (54,49 %) et troisième sur l’indice global de nPerf (71,55 %), derrière SFR et Bouygues Telecom.

articles.title: GTA 6 en PC: una nueva filtración revela que podría llegar antes de los esperado
articles.text:
La versión para PC de Grand Theft Auto VI podría lanzarse durante el primer trimestre de 2027, de acuerdo con un reporte de GamesBeat, que cita a cuatro fuentes familiarizadas con los planes de Rockstar Games. La desarrolladora no ha confirmado el calendario y tampoco ha respondido a la solicitud de comentarios del medio.
El juego tiene previsto debutar el 19 de noviembre de 2026 en PlayStation 5 y Xbox Series X|S, según la fecha comunicada por Take-Two Interactive, empresa matriz de Rockstar. Si el reporte sobre PC se cumple, quienes jueguen en ordenador tendrían que esperar entre dos y cuatro meses, según el momento del primer trimestre en que llegue el port.
La posibilidad contrasta con el lanzamiento de Grand Theft Auto V en PC. Ese juego apareció en PlayStation 3 y Xbox 360 en septiembre de 2013, mientras que la versión para ordenadores llegó en abril de 2015, aproximadamente un año y siete meses después. Un intervalo más corto para GTA 6 sería un cambio importante en la estrategia de lanzamiento de la serie, aunque por ahora la fecha se basa en fuentes anónimas y no en un anuncio oficial.
Una espera más corta cambiaría los planes de los jugadores
La falta de una fecha confirmada para PC ha dejado a los jugadores ante una decisión: esperar por esa versión o jugar desde el lanzamiento en una consola. El reporte podría influir en esa elección, ya que una demora de unos meses sería considerablemente menor que la que hubo con GTA V.
Algunos usuarios de ordenador podrían considerar comprar el juego para PS5 o Xbox Series X|S, o incluso adquirir una consola para jugar desde noviembre. Si la versión para PC efectivamente llegara entre enero y marzo de 2027, otros podrían preferir esperar y evitar una compra adicional.
Sin embargo, el plazo podría cambiar. Rockstar no ha publicado información sobre los requisitos técnicos, las funciones o la fecha de llegada del juego a ordenadores. Tampoco se sabe si el lanzamiento para PC sería simultáneo en tiendas digitales o si habría diferencias entre plataformas.
La historia de Rockstar con las versiones para PC
Rockstar suele lanzar sus grandes juegos primero en consolas y publicar la versión para PC más adelante. Además de la espera de GTA V, Red Dead Redemption 2 también llegó a ordenadores después de su estreno en consolas. Estas diferencias pueden responder a necesidades de desarrollo y optimización, aunque la compañía no ha explicado qué calendario aplicará para GTA 6.
El reporte de GamesBeat no detalla cómo habría cambiado la producción para permitir un lanzamiento tan cercano al de consolas. Tampoco aclara si la versión de PC estaría completa en noviembre o si su desarrollo continuaría en paralelo durante los meses siguientes. Esos aspectos siguen pendientes de información oficial.
El modo en línea añade expectativa
La conversación sobre PC coincide con las expectativas en torno al componente multijugador. Dan Clancy, director ejecutivo de Twitch, dijo que el modo en línea de GTA 6 se lanzaría “el próximo año”, según declaraciones recogidas previamente por medios. Rockstar todavía no ha anunciado cuándo llegará ese modo ni ha detallado si formará parte de una experiencia independiente.
El juego en línea es una parte importante del negocio de la franquicia. GTA Online mantiene una comunidad activa y ha impulsado actividades como el roleplay en servidores modificados, donde los participantes interpretan personajes y situaciones dentro del mundo del juego. La disponibilidad de GTA 6 en PC podría ser relevante para esas comunidades, aunque no se ha confirmado qué herramientas o modos incluirá.
Por ahora, el estreno del 19 de noviembre corresponde únicamente a las versiones de consola. El posible lanzamiento de PC entre enero y marzo de 2027 debe tratarse como un reporte sin confirmar. Hasta que Rockstar o Take-Two comuniquen sus planes, no hay una fecha oficial para los jugadores de ordenador.

articles.title: Startup Map Hub has found the founders. Will they pay?
articles.text:
Finding the right funder can take as much work as building a startup. Founders must sift through funding directories, check eligibility requirements, and answer similar questions across dozens of applications. Duncan Muriithi, a Nairobi-based software engineer and serial founder, wants to cut that work with his latest venture, Startup Map Hub.
Launched in October 2025, Startup Map Hub helps founders find funding opportunities, check their eligibility, and prepare applications. It has attracted 2,415 registered founders, with at least 35 paying for its services. According to Muriithi, the company has generated over $2,000 in revenue since it began accepting payments in February 2026.
Muriithi has spent most of the past decade building startups. In 2016, he joined the Meltwater Entrepreneurial School of Technology (MEST) in Ghana, where he co-founded Nestmetric, an artificial intelligence tool for predicting customer churn. The company raised $80,000 before he left in 2020. That December, he co-founded Africa Data School, an online school teaching data science and machine learning to young African professionals. He says revenue grew from about $10,000 to $110,000 in just over a year.
He was later accepted into 500 Global’s accelerator in Canada in 2023 and Antler East Africa in 2024. That year, he co-founded Prosper Hedge as chief technology officer and helped raise $150,000.
According to Muriithi, his fundraising experience exposed a gap in the process. Funding deadlines were scattered across websites, eligibility rules buried in documents, and investor directories offered little guidance on which funds might back a particular company. Applications also demanded hours of repetitive work.
“I thought that if founders could see every opportunity, they would apply and win,” Muriithi told TechCabal in an interview. “The directory brought the traffic, but the real bottlenecks are knowing whether you qualify and the hours each application takes.”
He launched Startup Map Africa as a free directory of startups, funding opportunities and technology events. Investors joined a month later. Weekly visitors grew from about 20 to a peak of 1,214 in May 2026, largely through Google Search.
Feedback from founders exposed the directory’s limits. Peter Nyaga, who runs the tourism startup Soko Guide, said that “each application took me more than four hours and asked for the same things in different words.”
“Soko Guide had sent hundreds of applications without ever getting past a first stage,” Nyaga added.
Michelle Ngugi, another founder, found the platform’s pitch deck generator lacking in depth and used another AI tool to refine the output.
Muriithi began building readiness checks and an application-drafting workspace in March 2026, followed by a pitch-deck editor the next month. In August, he renamed the company Startup Map Hub and opened it to founders outside Africa after noticing that US visitors were reluctant to click a website with “Africa” in its name.
“Google was showing us to as many Americans as Africans, but almost none clicked a domain with “Africa” in it,” Muriithi said.
The platform now focuses on helping founders complete applications rather than simply find opportunities. Muriithi has bootstrapped the business and remains its only employee, using AI coding tools to build the product. He says he has shipped nearly 900 code changes since October 2025. His constraint, he says, is time rather than cash.
How Startup Hub Map works
Startup Map Hub begins with a funding listing, often found through Google or ChatGPT. Founders can see the amount available, deadline, eligibility requirements, and application instructions without paying. After registering, they provide details about their startup, including its stage, country, and funding needs.
The platform then recommends five funding programmes and checks whether the startup meets their requirements, such as incorporation, revenue, product readiness, and location. Founders receive a strong, medium, or weak assessment, with reasons provided. Those unlikely to qualify are directed to other opportunities rather than being asked to pay.
Founders who pass can upload a pitch deck for a free review or build one using the platform’s editor. The paid basic plan, at $4.99 for a week, opens a workspace that drafts answers to a funder’s actual questions using information from the founder’s deck and profile. The founder can edit the responses, reuse saved answers, and submit the application through the funder’s own website.
The company also offers a done-with-you service. Growth costs $250, while Premium costs $999. These plans involve working with founders or organisations to identify suitable grants and prepare applications.
The approach is designed to limit generic AI writing. Startup Map Hub does not invent missing financial figures or submit applications on a founder’s behalf. A team member enters each funding opportunity, uses AI to structure the details, then checks them against the source before publication.
The platform has recorded 2,260 readiness checks, 182 pitch deck reviews and 494 applications started in its workspace, of which 143 have been completed. It also maintains a directory of 279 investors.
The figures show founders use the product, but they do not establish whether it improves their chances of raising money. Startup Map Hub has only recently begun systematically following up with applicants to record their results.
Why the company is on our radar
Startup Map Hub sits between funding directories and application portals. Platforms such as F6S and VC4A help founders find programmes and apply, while general AI tools draft responses. Muriithi says his company combines these functions with verified eligibility data and applications tailored to each fund.
The company has attracted users without buying traffic, but few have paid. It earned nothing in 2025 because it could not accept payments until February 2026. Three growth sales at $250 each have generated more revenue than 26 Basic purchases at $4.99 combined.
One customer is AIThesaurus, which describes itself as the first thesaurus to cover 10 African languages. Muriithi expects the done-with-you service to become the company’s largest revenue stream, both because it generates more revenue per sale and because it offers greater scope to demonstrate results.
There are early signs of value. In April 2026, Soko Guide, the tourism startup, advanced to the second stage of a Baobab funding application after working with Startup Map Hub. The platform also helped Hadaa.app, an AI landscaping app, secure $2,000 in Google Cloud credits and $5,000 in AWS credits, according to Muriithi. But the company has yet to establish how often its users secure funding. About one in five customers who buy a Basic week make another purchase, he said.
Almost every paying customer comes through Google or an AI assistant, Muriithi says, leaving the business exposed to changes in how those platforms direct traffic.
“If those platforms change how they send traffic, we feel it immediately,” he said.
True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. We’ve filtered the noise out of Moonshot 2026, optimising the conference strictly for high-calibre connections between startup founders, global financial operators, enterprise leaders and individuals rewiring Africa’s technical frameworks. articles.title: Apple refreshes Apple TV 4K with Siri AI upgrade, faster A19 chip, and smart remote
articles.text:
In a nutshell: Apple has introduced its fourth generation Apple TV 4K, complete with an A19 chip that the company claims delivers 50% faster CPU performance and up to twice the GPU performance compared to the previous model. The long-awaited set-top box also ships with three far-field microphones, Siri AI, and a smarter remote.
Apple said the A19 chip inside its new box includes a new, dedicated AV1 decoder that enables more efficient, high-quality streaming while simultaneously using less bandwidth. It also includes secure enclaves that protect and compartmentalize runtimes used to process Siri data from the trio of far-field microphones.
Siri on the Apple TV 4K is powered by Apple Intelligence, enabling a fully hands-free experience. Apple baked in echo cancellation to intelligently isolate voices from background noise. This means the system can pick up on "Hey Siri" commands in noisy environments, even if audio is playing in the background.
Apple's new smart remote, meanwhile, features a 100% recycled aluminum enclosure. New this year is Find My support with Precision Finding, and you can even ping it and have it play a sound to make it easier to locate between the couch cushions.
Apple says the 4th gen Apple TV 4K can be paired with four HomePod mini 2 or HomePod speakers to create an immersive home theater surround sound setup. It also doubles as a home hub, allowing users to manage their smart home from anywhere.
The refreshed streaming box has been a long time coming. The third-gen streamer launched nearly four years ago in November 2022.
The new Apple TV 4K is available to pre-order from today in the US and 29 other countries. Pricing is set at $299 up front, or you can break it down into six monthly payments of $49.83 if that's more convenient. Look for it to launch on November 13. It comes with the new Siri Remote, which can also be purchased separately for use with other Apple devices. It retails for $59 and also arrives on November 13.

articles.title: Ivanti Zero-Day Chain Gave Attackers Root Access to Fully Patched VPN
articles.text:
Ivanti on Tuesday warned customers that a zero-day vulnerability in its Connect Secure (ICS) VPN appliances has been exploited in the wild.
Tracked as CVE-2026-104935 and rated high severity, the issue is an authentication bypass that lets a remote, unauthenticated attacker execute arbitrary commands. Ivanti says it’s aware of exploitation affecting a limited number of customers.
Volexity discovered the in-the-wild exploitation while investigating an incident at one of its customers. A previously undocumented threat actor it tracks as UTA0576 had chained three zero-days to gain unauthenticated, root-level code execution on a fully patched ICS appliance.
According to Volexity, CVE-2026-104935 covers two of the flaws: an authentication bypass and a remote code execution bug. Ivanti has patched these vulnerabilities with the release of ICS versions 22.8R2.5, 25.1.1.2, 25.1.3.0, and 25.1.3.1.
The third vulnerability, a privilege escalation issue, remains unpatched, and the vendor plans to fix it over the coming weeks.
Volexity, which found evidence of exploitation starting on October 3, says UTA0576 focused primarily on credential theft, data exfiltration, network reconnaissance, and log tampering.
The attackers stole domain credentials stored on the appliance and exfiltrated limited Active Directory metadata. Using a custom tool, they searched Active Directory for LAPS passwords and BitLocker recovery keys.
They also ran password-spraying attacks, tested credentials with a custom Kerberos tool, and tried to extract credentials from captured network traffic. They also scanned the network, collected the appliance’s configuration data, and parsed authentication logs to identify valid usernames. Volexity found no backdoor or web shell on the device.
The operation was detected and disrupted before the attackers’ ultimate goals became clear. Volexity believes with high confidence that their actions pointed to preparation for lateral movement and a wider compromise of the network.
“Volexity assesses with low confidence that UTA0576 has criminal, rather than espionage, motivations based on the target of this activity,” the company says.
“As with many other threat actor operations Volexity has investigated in 2026, Volexity assesses with medium confidence that UTA0576 makes use of large language models (LLMs) for exploit development and post-exploitation activity,” it added.

articles.title: Meta lança o Muse Wonder, sua IA mais avançada até agora • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Meta lança o Muse Wonder, sua IA mais avançada até agora
Novos modelos focam em agentes capazes de lembrar informações, usar computadores e executar tarefas.
A Meta apresentou o Muse Wonder e o Muse Wonder Full, seus novos modelos de inteligência artificial voltados para agentes pessoais e profissionais. Segundo a companhia, os sistemas são os mais poderosos que já criou e reforçam a disputa com modelos de ponta das rivais OpenAI e Anthropic.
Os modelos foram treinados para executar tarefas que demandam várias etapas, como analisar contratos, desenvolver aplicativos e utilizar navegadores ou outros programas.
Uma das principais novidades é o recurso Active Memory, que permite ao modelo guardar informações importantes entre diferentes conversas e recuperá-las em novas tarefas. Já o Active Focus foi desenvolvido para manter o agente trabalhando mesmo diante de dificuldades.
Segundo a Meta, o modelo pode tentar métodos alternativos ao encontrar obstáculos, adaptar o plano conforme surgem novas informações e pedir ajuda ao usuário quando necessário. Antes de executar ações consideradas importantes, ele também pede confirmação.
A novidade combina essas funções com capacidade de operar computadores. Em demonstrações, a Meta mostra o Muse Wonder usando um navegador e outros aplicativos para criar e encomendar produtos a partir de fotos de um perfil no Instagram. O modelo também foi treinado para programação e pode dividir um projeto entre subagentes, realizar alterações em vários arquivos e continuar trabalhando mesmo quando encontra erros.
Esses recursos ampliam as funções do Muse, que já conseguia navegar em sites e preencher formulários sozinho, um nível de autonomia que já gerou conflitos. A Amazon bloqueou recentemente o serviço em sua loja após acusá-lo de não se identificar adequadamente.
O Muse Wonder já está disponível para desenvolvedores a US$ 4 por milhão de tokens de entrada e US$ 20 por milhão de tokens de saída (cerca de R$ 20 e R$ 100 em conversão direta, respectivamente). Já o Muse Wonder Full, versão mais avançada, fica restrito aos planos pagos do Muse Code e não possui cobrança individual por tokens.
A big tech afirma que Muse Wonder e Wonder Full atingem desempenho de ponta em avaliações envolvendo programação, memória e agentes profissionais. A companhia destaca tarefas longas de desenvolvimento de software e atividades envolvendo áreas como finanças, saúde e direito, mas os resultados precisam ser vistos com cautela, já que parte das comparações foi realizada ou selecionada pela própria Meta.
Em testes independentes da Artificial Analysis, o Muse Wonder marcou 52 pontos no Intelligence Index, um índice que reúne avaliações de raciocínio, programação e outras capacidades, resumindo o desempenho em uma pontuação. O Muse Wonder Full chegou a 56 pontos. Ambos superaram o Muse Spark 1.3, com 48, mas ficaram abaixo do Claude Opus 5.5, com 58.
A Meta afirma que o Muse Wonder chegará “em breve” ao aplicativo Muse, inicialmente para assinantes. O serviço continua limitado principalmente aos Estados Unidos e Canadá, sem previsão de lançamento no Brasil.
