articles.title: Skydance’s Discovery+ prices increase by up to 20 percent
articles.text:
Discovery+ subscription prices went up today.
Ad-free plans for new subscribers went from $10 per month to $12/month. Ad-based plans went from $6 to $7.
The new prices take effect for new subscribers immediately. Current subscribers to the streaming service, which primarily features unscripted content, like reality shows and documentaries, will receive 30 days’ notice before the new prices take effect, starting with bills issued as of November 12.
The higher prices come a week after Paramount Skydance bought Discovery+ parent company Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD), forming Skydance.
However, a Skydance spokesperson told Ars Technica that the pricing changes were in the works before Discovery+ knew about the merger’s closing date and were not planned in anticipation of a merger.
The spokesperson said that Discovery+’s prices are regularly evaluated to ensure that they are in line with the content and experience that the service offers, and the new prices reflect that.
Discovery+ has increased its prices three times since launching in 2012. Before today, the most recent price hike occurred in January 2025, when ad-based monthly subscriptions increased from $5 to $6, and ad-free plans went from $9 to $10.

articles.title: Exclusive: Cambridge Heavy Industries has been quietly building a desktop fusion device | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Fusion power usually conjures images of massive industrial facilities laced with large lasers or magnets, but a startup in Cambridge, Massachusetts, has been quietly building a device that can fit on a tabletop.
The optics of the device were on display behind Yun Kai, co-founder and CEO of Cambridge Heavy Industries, while he chatted with me on a video call. The company has been operating in stealth out of a small lab near MIT, and Kai gave TechCrunch an exclusive look at the technology it has been developing.
“We purposely built a small modular reactor. It’s tiny, it’s benchtop,” he told me. “Because it’s small, it makes everything easier.”
The small size has allowed Cambridge Heavy to experiment and iterate quickly. “The small module nature can enable 50 to 80 experiments, 50 to 80 shots per day,” he said. Data from those experiments will feed simulations that use AI to optimize the design.
That nimble approach has attracted investor attention. The startup recently raised a $6.2 million seed round led by Azolla Ventures with participation from Overlay, Neta Foundation, P3A, MassCEC, and the Rothrock family.
Cambridge Heavy’s fusion reactor uses lasers to compress a fuel target, similar to the groundbreaking experiment that proved controlled fusion reactions could produce more power than they consume. But unlike other inertial confinement designs, Cambridge Heavy’s minimizes the number of lasers required to spark fusion.
The system uses two main lasers to drive ignition. One laser is split into multiple beam lines that deliver light in concentric rings. Those rings of laser light are timed to hit the flat, round fuel target successively, starting from the outside and working in. The first ring starts a compression wave within the target that starts traveling inward. The subsequent laser rings are timed to boost the wave at just the right moment to further compress the fuel.
As the shock wave reaches the center of the target, a laser fires on the target, generating heat and producing a magnetic field. With the right amount of pressure and heat, fusion occurs.
Cambridge Heavy’s design generates high pressures with relatively low laser power, Kai said. The concept emerged from the lab of Keith Nelson, a chemist at MIT. There, researchers used the laser pulses to study materials under extreme conditions. As they ramped up pressures, they realized they were approaching fusion-ready conditions.
In about a decade, Cambridge Heavy plans to develop a power plant from the concept, though that’ll require scaling up the design. It will be larger than the current benchtop prototype, though not quite as large as other fusion power plants. Kai said it should be about the size of two basketball courts, and it will test whether the approach can generate enough energy to support a power plant.
Before that happens, though, Cambridge Heavy plans to use its smaller-scale devices to make tritium, a rare isotope of hydrogen that will be used by nearly all fusion power plants in the works today. Tritium sells for around $30,000 per gram today.
Each power plant won’t need a lot of tritium — on the order of grams per year — but the substance is so rare that only about 40 kilograms exist today. One recent study predicts that without new sources, the fusion power industry will be short by about 28 kilograms in 2054. At current prices, that’s about $840 million worth of tritium.
Fusion startups are in the process of designing fuel systems that will help the reactors be largely self-sufficient when it comes to tritium supplies, though they may need occasional top-ups. But that process could take up to 10 years, Kai said, giving Cambridge Heavy years of potential revenue as it pursues its power plant.

articles.title: Google ya permite crear apps para Android gratis y sin programar: así funciona la nueva herramienta con IA
articles.text:
Hasta hace unos meses, crear una aplicación para el móvil exigía conocimientos de programación y dominio de herramientas de desarrollo. La llegada de la IA y el "vibe coding" vinieron a cambiar todo y ahora cualquiera puede crear una app con unos cuantos prompts. Esto lo sabe Google y ha decidido lanzar una herramienta para crear aplicaciones para Android sin necesidad de escribir código.
De acuerdo con una publicación en el blog de la compañía, cualquier persona con una cuenta de Google gratuita puede crear una app. La herramienta convierte una simple instrucción en lenguaje natural (prompt) en una aplicación funcional que se ejecuta en tu móvil. Los usuarios solo requieren acceder a Google AI Studio para comenzar a construir la aplicación y probarla de forma local.
Las aplicaciones creadas con IA están separadas del catálogo público de la tienda, por lo que no habrá necesidad de marcarlas como privadas. Los usuarios pueden experimentar y construir las apps que quieran sin coste alguno, las cuales se pueden compartir con su círculo de amigos y familiares. En caso de que quieras ofrecerla al resto del mundo, necesitarás una cuenta de desarrollador profesional para publicarla en la Play Store.
Si optas por esto último, tu app tendrá que cumplir con los mismos lineamientos que se aplican al resto de aplicaciones de Android. Esto incluye las revisiones de Trust & Safety y el estándar de calidad con el que se mide el trabajo de otros desarrolladores.
Vale la pena mencionar que esta no es la primera vez que Google experimenta con este tipo de herramientas. AI Studio ya incluía un creador de apps con Gemini, pero estaba enfocado a cuentas profesionales y requería conectar el móvil a tu PC a través de la depuración USB. Ahora se puede instalar en el móvil con un clic y compartirla más adelante.
Android se prepara para recibir una oleada de apps creadas con IA
A primera vista, las apps creadas con IA parecen un paso lógico para Google. La compañía no solo tiene las herramientas y la plataforma, sino que busca recuperar el terreno perdido frente a OpenAI y Anthropic. La tecnológica está eliminando el requisito principal de una cuenta de desarrollador, permitiendo que cualquier persona con una cuenta gratuita pueda generar una aplicación desde cero sin conocimientos de programación.
Debido a que las aplicaciones se ejecutan de forma local, los usuarios pueden construir alternativas a apps que cumplen tareas sencillas. Por ejemplo, puedes generar una app que convierta divisas o una que te ayude con tus pendientes. Android ya ofrece miles o millones de estas aplicaciones, pero son lentas o imposibles de utilizar sin ver anuncios antes.
La herramienta para desarrollar apps de Android con Google AI Studio estará disponible a partir de hoy. Lamentablemente, el despliegue comienza en Estados Unidos con idioma inglés, aunque la compañía planea expandirlo a otros países en un futuro no muy lejano.

articles.title: 17 Years with China: What Really Makes a Partnership Work - EE Times
articles.text:
China has changed considerably over the past 15 years — and so have European companies’ expectations of Chinese manufacturers. Robert Tarantowicz of Honya Europe looks back on that shift, from his first attempts to work with Chinese suppliers in 2009 to building a Polish-Chinese company that now operates across Europe. Why shouldn’t price be the main selection criterion? How do you hold a productive conversation with a Chinese partner? And what is worth looking for during a factory visit? Here’s what he told us.
1. How did your cooperation with Chinese manufacturers begin, and what were the early stages like?
In 2009, I was looking for a new printed circuit board supplier for a rapidly growing company. We made several attempts to work with Chinese manufacturers, but none of them resulted in a successful supplier qualification. The main obstacles were communication misunderstandings, quality issues, and differences in business practices.
Several months later, I met Hong Xu from Honya International. Subsequent orders were handled efficiently. Problems did arise, as they do in any manufacturing environment, but this supplier stood out because of its willingness to jointly investigate root causes, share the costs of justified claims, and implement preventive actions. That created a foundation of trust, and Honya International became a key PCB supplier.
In 2013, we entered into a partnership and began working together in the European market. In 2020, we transformed that cooperation into a joint venture, HONYA EUROPE, registered in Poland. Today, our Polish-Chinese company holds a market share in the low double digits in Poland’s PCB supply market and serves customers across Europe.
2. How much has China changed as a business partner over the last fifteen years?
The business environment has changed dramatically. Manufacturers’ technological capabilities have increased, labor costs have risen, compliance requirements have become more demanding, and geopolitical risk has gained importance. China is no longer viewed simply as a low-cost manufacturing base. It is also a major market, a sophisticated industrial base, and an increasingly strong technological competitor.
In our specific relationship, however, less has changed than one might expect. We still base our cooperation on long-term trust, shared risk management, and personal contact. The relationship has evolved beyond business.
3. What are the main concerns European companies have when working with a Chinese supplier for the first time?
The most common questions we hear are: Will the goods actually be delivered? Is the advance payment safe? Will the product match the documentation? Is the person we’re dealing with the manufacturer or just an intermediary?
There are also concerns regarding document protection, certificate authenticity, complaint handling, delivery reliability, and customs clearance.
These concerns are entirely reasonable, but they can be managed through proper verification of both the company and factory, trial orders, clearly defined acceptance criteria, quality control measures, and payment terms appropriate to the level of risk and the history of cooperation.
4. What mistakes do companies most often make when starting to work with Chinese suppliers?
The most common mistake is reducing supplier selection to a price comparison. If a buyer pushes pricing below what is sustainable for the required technology and quality level, the manufacturer will inevitably look for savings in materials, processes, inspection, or delivery schedules. The consequences may only become visible during mass production.
Quotations should be compared on an equal basis: material specifications, performance class, tolerances, testing requirements, documentation, delivery terms, and responsibility for claims. Price is important, but it should always be assessed together with the total cost of risk.
5. Are there any significant cultural differences that can affect negotiations and day-to-day cooperation?
Yes, although entire societies should not be reduced to simple stereotypes. In many Chinese companies, context, hierarchy, personal relationships, and avoiding situations where someone “loses face” tend to play a greater role than they do in Europe. Agreement expressed during a meeting may sometimes mean “I understand” rather than “I accept the terms.”
For that reason, it is worth asking open-ended questions, requesting detailed explanations of how work will be carried out, and summarizing agreements in writing. Critical feedback is best discussed objectively and without publicly putting a partner in an uncomfortable position. Most importantly, focus on getting to know the particular company and the people within it, rather than relying on stereotypes.
6. How is trust built in business relationships with Chinese partners?
Trust develops gradually. It is built through small orders that are successfully completed, on-time payments made according to agreed terms, fair handling of complaints, predictable communication, and visits by both parties. What matters most is that actions consistently back up what has been promised.
Chinese partners usually appreciate a genuine interest in their language and culture. One of my favorite sayings is Qiānlǐ zhī xíng, shǐ yú zúxià, which literally means, “A journey of a thousand li begins beneath one’s feet” and is often rendered in English as “A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.” It perfectly reflects the nature of cooperation, where everything starts with a small but meaningful first step.
It is very important to simultaneously build a personal relationship, which is the foundation of joint action. In our company, this relationship is very strong, as evidenced, for example, by the fact that my daughters stay in touch with their “uncle from China,” and on two occasions I was asked to give Chinese children Western names. This shows that a lasting business partnership can grow into a relationship between people and families.
7. Can experience gained in Europe be transferred directly to the Chinese market, or is a different approach required?
It cannot be transferred without adjustment. European standards regarding documentation, quality, compliance, and accountability are highly valuable, but communication styles, negotiation methods, and relationship building need to be adapted to the local business environment.
It is also worth challenging our own assumptions about China. Some stereotypes were formed decades ago and no longer reflect today’s technological capabilities. The best approach is to combine European process discipline with curiosity and a willingness to learn from a partner.
8. How can a potential supplier be verified before cooperation begins?
The full legal company name, registration number, business scope, legal representative, and consistency between the bank account and the invoicing entity should all be verified. Useful sources include Chinese government databases such as the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System and Credit China, as well as reports from independent verification companies.
Documentation alone is not a substitute for an audit. It is advisable to verify whether the factory actually performs the processes it claims to perform, confirm certificate validity directly with the issuing bodies, inspect quality-control procedures, review samples, and start with a limited pilot order. Only after successful results would I recommend scaling up cooperation.
9. What role do personal visits to China and direct contact with manufacturers play?
They are extremely important. Meeting in person accelerates trust-building and makes it easier to discuss issues that may remain unclear through email correspondence. It also allows you to assess how a company responds to detailed questions and whether it truly understands the product’s application.
A factory visit helps evaluate actual production capacity, process organization, material storage, quality-control equipment, and batch traceability. Simply walking through the production floor is not enough. The most valuable insight comes from following a real order through the process, from material receipt to final inspection, and speaking directly with the people responsible for engineering and quality.
One must also accept that part of the visit will be dedicated to getting to know one another. For many Chinese partners, a relationship comes before a transaction, whereas European customers often prefer to move straight to specifications and pricing.
10. What aspects deserve special attention when placing your first orders?
You should assume that any information not clearly documented may be interpreted differently. The order package should specify the current documentation revision, material, stack-up, copper thickness, tolerances, surface finish, performance class, scope of testing, packaging requirements, and acceptance criteria.
Before moving into mass production, it is advisable to approve the DFM analysis and either a sample or a pilot batch. Procedures for handling non-conformities, delivery schedules, shipping terms, and payment conditions should also be agreed upon in advance. Having these points confirmed in writing is more important than hearing repeated assurances that “everything is clear.”
11. What does quality control look like in an international supply chain, and which mechanisms are worth implementing?
Quality control begins before production starts. First, requirements and acceptance criteria must be clearly defined, and then it should be confirmed that the selected factory has the appropriate processes, equipment, and expertise. In PCB manufacturing, this includes DFM approval, material and stack-up validation, and agreement on the required performance class.
The scope of inspection should be aligned with the project’s risk profile. It may include AOI, electrical testing, impedance measurements, microsection analysis, surface-finish inspection, batch traceability, and a final quality report. Incoming quality inspection is also necessary after delivery, and in the event of a non-conformity, a documented root-cause analysis and corrective actions should follow.
Payment terms can help reduce risk, but they can never replace a well-designed quality system. The safest approach is a process in which requirements, inspection results, and responsibility for claims are agreed upon before production begins.
12. Does the current economic and geopolitical situation affect trade relations between Europe and China?
Yes. Day-to-day business is affected by export restrictions, sanctions, tariffs, dual-use regulations, country-of-origin requirements, and growing pressure to increase supply chain resilience. Even when business partners take a pragmatic approach to cooperation, they cannot ignore these frameworks.
As a result, companies are more frequently qualifying alternative suppliers, maintaining safety stock for critical items, and conducting more detailed assessments of logistics routes and regulatory compliance. This does not mean the end of cooperation with China. It does mean that purchasing decisions must take regulatory risk and continuity of supply into account, not just price and production lead time.
13. How have European customers’ expectations of Chinese manufacturers changed over the years?
European customers are increasingly looking beyond low prices. Technological capability, consistency, short implementation times, complete documentation, traceability, compliance with industry requirements, and responsive complaint handling are now equally important.
The role of manufacturers themselves has also evolved. The best suppliers are no longer simply executing customer documentation. They actively participate in DFM analysis, propose material solutions, and help prepare designs for stable volume production. At the same time, manufacturing capabilities vary significantly from one factory to another, making supplier selection for a specific technology more important than ever.
14. In the PCB industry, quality is critical. How can companies effectively balance cost control with maintaining high production standards?
The most effective way to reduce costs is through design optimization and production organization, not by compromising on critical materials or inspections. The greatest benefits come from early DFM analysis, realistic tolerances, optimized panelization, standardized materials and stack-ups, consolidated orders, and reliable volume forecasts.
Requirements related to safety, reliability, and end-use applications should never be negotiable. A printed circuit board is the foundation of a device that may operate in fire protection systems, hazardous environments, or safety-critical infrastructure. Cost savings made at the wrong stage can multiply the cost of claims, downtime, or field failures many times over.
Our role is therefore to identify process efficiencies without compromising the agreed level of quality.
15. What logistical challenges most commonly arise in projects between Europe and China?
The most common challenges include fluctuating transit times, seasonal congestion before holidays, incomplete customs documentation, inappropriate Incoterms selection, damaged packaging, and insufficient buffers for delays. In electronics, additional considerations include moisture control, ESD protection, batch labeling, and maintaining traceability.
We mitigate these risks through advance planning, clearly assigned responsibility for customs clearance and insurance, trusted freight forwarders, document verification before shipment, and selecting transportation methods based on the value and urgency of the order. For critical projects, it is advisable to build in time buffers and consider alternative transportation routes or delivery methods.
16. Can you share an example that illustrates the unique nature of working with a Chinese partner?
One good example is a machine purchase project we carried out several years ago. For several days we discussed specifications, service support, certifications, costs, and transportation. At the same time, we talked about China, cars, baijiu, our families, and where the machine would be installed after delivery. From a European perspective, it might have seemed that we were drifting away from the main topic, but for our partner this was part of building the foundation for the transaction.
Initially, the supplier expected full prepayment. After extensive discussions and the development of mutual trust, we agreed on a payment structure of 20 percent before the order was launched, with the remaining balance payable after confirmation that the machine was ready for shipment through photographs, videos, and responses to technical questions.
This case demonstrates that personal relationships can influence commercial terms, but they should always go hand in hand with measurable acceptance milestones. Trust alone is not a substitute for verification.
17. How has the technological development of Chinese manufacturers affected the global electronics market?
Chinese manufacturers have evolved from contract producers into organizations playing an increasingly important role in process development, automation, and the advancement of their own technologies. Their production scale, extensive supplier networks, and rapid investment cycles have shortened product development timelines and increased pricing pressure across the global market.
In the PCB sector, technologies that were once available from only a handful of suppliers are now offered by a much broader range of factories. While this improves access to advanced solutions, it also increases the importance of supplier qualification. Similar technological claims do not necessarily translate into the same level of process stability, documentation quality, or complaint-handling capability.
18. What trends are you currently observing in electronics and PCB manufacturing in China?
The strongest growth can be seen in HDI, high-layer-count, high-speed, and high-frequency PCBs, as well as rigid-flex constructions. Demand is being driven by data centers and AI applications, telecommunications, automotive electronics, industrial automation, and devices requiring high interconnection density.
A second major trend is factory automation, including expanded optical inspection, process-data collection, and traceability systems. The third is specialization. Individual factories increasingly focus on specific technologies and production volumes, which means there is no single “best factory” for every project.
From a European customer’s perspective, this creates more opportunities but also requires more careful matching of manufacturers to the material requirements, design complexity, reliability expectations, and production volume of each project.
19. What advice would you give to companies considering cooperation with Chinese suppliers?
I would start with six steps: a detailed specification, verification of the supplier and factory, a pilot order, written acceptance criteria, quality control measures, and direct personal contact. Order volumes should be increased only after the supplier has demonstrated quality and delivery reliability in practice.
It is not worth choosing a partner solely on the basis of the lowest quotation. Companies should evaluate how the supplier responds to technical questions, documents its processes, and handles non-conformities. It is also wise to plan a second source for critical components from the very beginning.
20. In your opinion, what will cooperation between Europe and China in the electronics sector look like in the coming years?
I expect Europe and China to remain highly interconnected, but in a more selective form than in the past. China will remain a major manufacturing and technology hub, while European companies will invest more heavily in supply chain resilience, second-source strategies, and regulatory compliance.
In some sectors, production for local markets will become increasingly localized, and additional restrictions will emerge in certain critical technologies. Nevertheless, the need for engineering and commercial cooperation will not disappear. The companies that succeed will be those capable of combining strong supplier relationships in China with sensible diversification and effective risk management.
Meet Robert during the matchmaking sessions at electronica 2026.

articles.title: La version PC de GTA 6 pourrait sortir plus tôt qu’espéré
articles.text:
Si l’information se confirme, ce délai serait très court pour Rockstar Games, qui a jusqu’ici fait patienter les joueuses et les joueurs PC bien plus longtemps. D’après le site américain GamesBeat, ce 13 octobre 2026, Rockstar Games viserait une sortie de GTA VI sur PC entre janvier et mars 2027.
Le site affirme tenir cette information de quatre sources de l’industrie au courant des plans du studio. Rockstar n’a pas confirmé cette fenêtre de lancement et n’a pas répondu à la demande de commentaire de GamesBeat.
L’idée d’une version PC plus rapide que d’habitude circulait déjà depuis plusieurs semaines. Comme le détaillait Frandroid début septembre, le manque de consoles disponibles pourrait pousser Rockstar à revoir son calendrier pour ne pas perdre de ventes.
Ce délai serait nettement plus court que pour les précédents jeux du studio. GTA VI doit sortir le 19 novembre 2026 sur PS5 et Xbox Series X|S. Une arrivée sur PC avant la fin du mois de mars 2027 représenterait donc moins de cinq mois d’attente, contre environ dix-neuf mois pour GTA V, sorti sur consoles en septembre 2013 et sur PC en avril 2015.
Red Dead Redemption 2 a suivi le même chemin : sorti sur PS4 et Xbox One en octobre 2018, il n’est arrivé sur PC qu’en novembre 2019, un peu plus d’un an plus tard.
Un changement de stratégie chez Rockstar ?
Une sortie sur PC permettrait à Rockstar de toucher un public encore plus large, et plus rapidement que pour ses précédentes productions. Rockstar a d’autant plus intérêt à aller vite que GTA VI représente un investissement colossal. GamesBeat évoque un budget de production de plus de 2 milliards de dollars (environ 1,7 milliard d’euros), un chiffre que ni Rockstar ni sa maison mère Take-Two n’ont jamais confirmé.
GamesBeat avance également un autre argument : le jeu en ligne. En août 2023, Rockstar a racheté Cfx.re, l’équipe à l’origine de FiveM, un outil qui permet de créer des serveurs personnalisés sur PC, notamment pour jouer un personnage et interagir avec d’autres joueurs dans l’univers de GTA V. Le studio pourrait vouloir développer ce type d’expérience dans GTA VI, ainsi que les contenus créés par la communauté. Une sortie PC serait alors essentielle. D’autant que Dan Clancy, le PDG de Twitch, a déclaré à Bloomberg que le mode en ligne de GTA VI arriverait « l’année prochaine ».
Rockstar n’a pas encore annoncé officiellement de version PC de GTA VI, et donc encore moins de date de sortie. Seule la sortie du 19 novembre 2026 sur PS5 et Xbox Series X|S est confirmée.

articles.title: Neues Apple TV 4K vorgestellt: Was die Box kann – und wo deutsche Kunden das Nachsehen haben
articles.text:
Neues Apple TV 4K vorgestellt: Was die Box kann – und wo deutsche Kunden das Nachsehen haben
Bei fast schon jedem Apple-Event der vergangenen Jahre galt das Apple TV 4K als sicherer Kandidat für eine Neuvorstellung. Die bis jetzt aktuellste Variante der Streaming-Box stammte von 2022 und ist nicht fit für Apple Intelligence. Das ändert das Unternehmen jetzt mit der neuen Set-Top-Box, die ebenfalls schlicht Apple TV 4K heißt. Die sieht dem Vorgänger auf Pressebildern sehr ähnlich, bietet aber einen deutlich größeren Funktionsumfang.
Apple TV 4K mit eingebauten Mikrofonen
Zu einem taktet im Inneren nun der A19-Chip aus dem iPhone 17. Dadurch soll das Gerät nicht nur eine 50 Prozent schnellere CPU- und eine doppelt so schnelle GPU-Leistung liefern, wie das Vorgängermodell. Dank des enthaltenen Decoders soll Streaming außerdem auch „in hoher Qualität bei geringerem Bandbreitenbedarf“ möglich sein. Es ist aufgrund des neuen Prozessors auch kompatibel mit Apple Intelligence und Siri AI. Um problemlos mit der Sprachassistenz kommunizieren zu können, ist nicht einmal die Fernbedienung möglich. Apple integriert Fernfeldmikrofone ins Gehäuse, die Sprachbefehle erkennen. Neu ist die Idee allerdings nicht. Mit dem Fire TV Cube bietet Amazon seit Jahren ein Gadget mit derselben Lösung an.
Wie der Vorgänger kann auch die neue Version des Apple TV 4K als Smarthome-Zentrale eingerichtet werden. Kompatible Gadgets lassen sich via Siri steuern. Außerdem ist es möglich, sich etwa das Bild der smarten Türklingel direkt auf dem Fernseher anzeigen zu lassen.
Auch abseits davon lässt sich das Apple TV 4K ins Ökosystem im Wohnzimmer einbinden. So lässt sich die Box mit vier der ebenfalls neuen Homepod Mini 2 oder ebenso vielen Homepods der zweiten Generation verknüpfen. Die Lautsprecher fungieren dann als Surround-System. Mit der jeweils ersten Generation funktioniert das allerdings nicht. Mithilfe der Kamera vom iPhone können Nutzer:innen über die TV-Box zudem Facetime-Anrufe tätigen.
Das Kleingedruckte als Spielverderber
Deutsche Kund:innen müssen allerdings Einschnitte in Kauf nehmen. Zwar wirbt das Unternehmen auch hierzulande in seinem Shop mit den neuen Fähigkeiten von Siri AI. Anders als auf dem Mac wird die KI-Version der Sprachassistenz hierzulande aber nicht auf Englisch zur Verfügung stehen. In der englischen Pressemitteilung heißt es, dass Siri AI mit tvOS 27.2 nur in den USA, Australien, Kanada, Indien, Neuseeland, Singapur, Südafrika und Großbritannien funktionieren wird. Wie auf dem iPhone dürfte auf Deutsch hierzulande also die altbekannte Version zum Einsatz kommen.
Außerdem ist es zwar möglich, die neue Siri-Remote-Fernbedienung via „Wo ist?“-App zu ordnen, wenn sie sich nicht auffinden lässt. Die sogenannte „genaue Suche“ funktioniert aber nur mit iPhones ab dem iPhone 17 aufwärts. Das iPhone 17e ist davon ausgenommen.
Kund:innen können das neue Apple TV 4K ab sofort vorbestellen. Apple will es aber erst ab dem 13. November ausliefern. Die Box kostet hierzulande 349 Euro.
Hinweis: Wir haben den Part zu Siri AI nachgeschärft. In einer ursprünglichen Fassung hieß es, es sei unklar, ob die KI-Version in Deutschland auf Englisch zur Verfügung stehe.

articles.title: 'I look to China as gurus': Zoho's Sridhar Vembu
articles.text:
'I look to China as gurus': Zoho's Sridhar Vembu
Speaking at TechSparks 2026, Vembu said India has more to learn from China's technology ecosystem than America's, arguing that technology ownership, rather than engineering talent alone, is essential for lasting economic prosperity.
India should look to China for lessons on building technological capabilities rather than continue relying on a model centred on providing software services to global companies, Zoho Co-founder and Chief Scientist Sridhar Vembu said on Tuesday.
Speaking at YourStory's TechSparks 2026 in Bengaluru, Vembu argued that China had successfully built and retained ownership of critical technologies, allowing it to capture economic value and develop globally competitive businesses. "As much as we think of China as adversaries, I actually look to them as gurus," Vembu said.
"Chinese technology landscape has many more lessons to offer us than America does today," he added.
Vembu said Zoho's own journey had drawn inspiration from East Asian economies, including Japan, Taiwan, South Korea and China, which developed sophisticated technology industries despite constraints involving resources, population density and economic development. He recalled how Chinese engineers visiting Zoho's Chennai operations around 25 years ago were perceived by their Indian counterparts as coming from a poorer country.
"Nobody would say this today," he said, pointing to China's subsequent transformation into a major technology power.
Why ownership matters
At the heart of Vembu's argument was a distinction between developing technology for others and owning the intellectual property that generates long-term economic value. India, he said, performs a significant share of the engineering work for some of the world's largest technology companies but does not capture a proportionate share of the resulting profits.
Vembu claimed that approximately 40–50% of NVIDIA's chip design work, including substantial verification work, happens in India. He also pointed to the significant software development undertaken in the country for Microsoft, Oracle and Cisco. These estimates were not independently verified.
"If you are doing 50% of the work and 50% of the value accrued here in a hypothetical world," Vembu said, Karnataka's GDP could be at least two or three times its current size.
Vembu contrasted India's experience with that of China, which invested in domestic technology platforms even when they initially lagged their international competitors. He cited Baidu, which emerged as a Chinese alternative to Google, and WeChat, which became central to China's digital ecosystem.
These platforms, he argued, helped create the technological capabilities, user bases and data ecosystems that supported subsequent innovation, including the emergence of globally competitive companies such as TikTok and advances in AI. "That foundation layer was necessary for them to build the next stage," he said. For India, the lesson was to invest in the underlying technologies rather than focus exclusively on developing the latest AI models.
Preparing for a new software economy
The push for indigenous technology capabilities also comes as Vembu anticipates significant disruption to India's traditional software industry.
During his keynote, he estimated that AI already writes better code than 60–70% of software engineers and could outperform as many as 90% within three to six months. These were his projections, not independently established benchmarks. He compared software development to the handloom industry before mechanisation, warning that AI could dramatically reduce the number of engineers required to build software. However, Vembu said Zoho was not responding to the prospect of automation by laying off employees. Instead, the company was redeploying engineers to work on other technology capabilities.
"We know we can redeploy them to build all this stuff," he said.
As AI threatens to change the economics of software development, Vembu believes India must use its engineering capabilities to build more of the underlying technology itself. China's experience, he argued, demonstrates the long-term value of that approach, even if the path requires years of investment and the willingness to develop products that may initially lag established global alternatives.
"The new tech order is: you have to learn to solve our own problems," he said.

articles.title: Rätsel der Monsterwellen gelöst: Wie KI die Gefahr auf See berechenbar macht
articles.text:
Formel statt Seemannsgarn: KI analysiert die Entstehung von Monsterwellen
Am 17. November 2020 registrierte eine Sensorboje des kanadischen Unternehmens MarineLabs eine Wassersäule, die Ozeanograf:innen weltweit beschäftigte. Das im Pazifik vor der Küste von Ucluelet verankerte Messgerät zeichnete eine Einzelwelle von 17,6 Metern Höhe auf. Das Ereignis sticht deshalb heraus, weil der restliche Seegang zu diesem Zeitpunkt bei lediglich rund sechs Metern lag.
Damit ein solches Ereignis in der Wissenschaft als Monsterwelle (im Fachjargon Rogue Wave genannt) eingestuft wird, ist nicht die absolute Höhe entscheidend, sondern das Verhältnis zur sogenannten signifikanten Wellenhöhe. Dieser Referenzwert beschreibt die Durchschnittshöhe des höchsten Drittels aller Wellen in einem Messzeitraum. Übertrifft eine einzelne Welle diesen Durchschnitt um mehr als das Doppelte gilt sie als Monsterwelle.
Mit dem fast Dreifachen der signifikanten Wellenhöhe ist das Ereignis von Ucluelet proportional die extremste jemals gemessene Welle. Zum Vergleich: Die berühmte Draupner-Welle, die am 1. Januar 1995 an einer norwegischen Ölplattform in der Nordsee den ersten Beweis für die Existenz des Phänomens lieferte, war zwar 25,6 Meter hoch, trat aber in einem schweren Seegang von ohnehin schon zwölf Metern auf.
Warum etablierte Erklärungsmodelle auf dem Ozean versagen
Nach dem Draupner-Ereignis suchten Forschungsteams weltweit nach den Ursachen. In der Ozeanografie etablierte sich die Theorie der sogenannten Modulationsinstabilität als wahrscheinliche Hauptursache. Diese auch als Benjamin-Feir-Instabilität bekannte Theorie besagt, dass einzelne Wellen in der Lage sind, benachbarten Wellen ihre Energie zu entziehen, wodurch sie sich zunehmend aufschaukeln.
In eindimensionalen Wellenkanälen unter Laborbedingungen ließ sich dieser Mechanismus gut nachweisen. Eine detaillierte Untersuchung der Ucluelet-Welle durch den Forscher Johannes Gemmrich ergab jedoch für die Realität auf offener See ein anderes Bild. Wie in einer im Wissenschaftsmagazin Scientific Reports veröffentlichten Studie der kanadischen University of Victoria zu lesen ist, spielte diese Instabilität bei der Entstehung kaum eine Rolle.
Der Grund dafür liegt im realen Ozean: Wellen laufen dort nicht nur stur in eine Richtung, sondern kreuzen sich aus verschiedensten Winkeln. Dadurch verpufft der Effekt des gegenseitigen Energie-Entziehens in der Praxis fast vollständig. Vielmehr identifizierte das Forschungsteam ein physikalisches Prinzip als Hauptauslöser, das als lineare Superposition bekannt ist. Treffen Wellensysteme mit unterschiedlichen Frequenzen und Richtungen im exakt gleichen Moment zusammen, können sich die einzelnen Wellenberge kurzzeitig zu einer enormen Spitze addieren.
Die Analyse von Milliarden Sensordaten durch künstliche Intelligenz
Um diese These empirisch zu belegen und ein belastbares Vorhersagemodell zu entwickeln, nutzte ein Team um den Forscher Dion Häfner vom dänischen Niels-Bohr-Institut der Universität Kopenhagen Methoden der Künstlichen Intelligenz. Das Team griff auf die Aufzeichnungen von 158 Messbojen zurück, die entlang der Küsten der USA und in Überseegebieten rund um die Uhr den Seegang dokumentieren.
Das Trainingsmaterial für das neuronale Netz umfasste historische Daten von rund einer Milliarde Einzelwellen. Würde eine einzelne Boje diese Menge an Daten sammeln, müsste sie 700 Jahre lang ununterbrochen messen.
Laut einer in der Fachzeitschrift PNAS publizierten Arbeit fanden die Wissenschaftler:innen in diesem Datensatz mehr als 100.000 Monsterwellen. Diese Auswertung widerlegt die in älteren Prognosemodellen getroffene Annahme, dass derartige Extremereignisse weltweit extrem selten seien. Statistisch gesehen formt sich im globalen Ozean jeden Tag eine derartige Welle, wenngleich nicht immer in Form einer extremen Wasserwand.
Symbolische Regression liefert eine transparente Gleichung
Der technologisch interessanteste Aspekt der Arbeit aus Kopenhagen ist die spezifische Methode des maschinellen Lernens. Das Team setzte ein Verfahren namens symbolische Regression ein. Gewöhnliche neuronale Netze arbeiten oft als sogenannte Black Box. Sie liefern hochpräzise Vorhersagen, lassen aber nicht erkennen, wie sie zu diesem Ergebnis gelangen. Für die Wissenschaft ist das unzureichend, da der physikalische Zusammenhang unsichtbar bleibt.
Die symbolische Regression hingegen destilliert aus den Milliarden von Datenpunkten eine transparente, von Menschen lesbare mathematische Gleichung. Der Algorithmus lieferte den Forscher:innen eine physikalische Formel, die exakt beschreibt, unter welchen Bedingungen die lineare Überlagerung kritisch wird. Markus Jochum, Professor am Niels-Bohr-Institut, vergleicht diesen Vorgang mit der Geschichte der Astronomie: Tycho Brahe sammelte über Jahrzehnte astronomische Beobachtungen, aus denen Johannes Kepler durch Versuch und Irrtum die Keplerschen Gesetze ableitete. Die KI tat mit den Wellendaten nun exakt das, was Kepler mit Planeten tat.
Der entscheidende Parameter für die Schifffahrt
Das resultierende Modell bestätigt, dass das nautische Risiko vor allem dann ansteigt, wenn sich Wassertiefe, Wellensteilheit und die sogenannte Kamm-Tal-Korrelation auf eine bestimmte Weise kombinieren. Letztere erwies sich als der aussagekräftigste Indikator. Diese Korrelation beschreibt in der Ozeanografie, wie stark Wellenberge und darauffolgende Wellentäler statistisch zusammenhängen. In Seegangsbedingungen, in denen auf einen hohen Berg mit großer Verlässlichkeit ein tiefes Tal folgt (eine hohe Korrelation), ist das Risiko für die Bildung einer Monsterwelle durch Überlagerung signifikant erhöht.
Da sich dieser Parameter aus üblichen Wellenprognosen berechnen lässt, steht Wetterdiensten nun eine konkrete Berechnungsgrundlage zur Verfügung, die das in der Realität unwirksame Modell der Modulationsinstabilität ersetzen kann. Die Formel sowie das zugrundeliegende Forschungsmaterial sind öffentlich zugänglich.
Damit ergibt sich für Reedereien die Möglichkeit, das Risiko für Monsterwellen entlang geplanter Routen der weltweit rund 50.000 Frachtschiffe im Vorfeld dynamisch zu berechnen. Routen können angepasst werden, bevor die nautischen und meteorologischen Bedingungen das gefürchtete Zusammentreffen der Wellensysteme erzeugen.
Allerdings ordnet das dänische Forschungsteam die Ergebnisse kritisch ein. Dem Modell fehlen derzeit noch Daten zu lokalen Winden, extremen Ozeanströmungen oder unregelmäßigen Meeresböden, die das Wellenverhalten vor Ort massiv verändern können. Zudem berechnet das System statistische Wahrscheinlichkeiten für Meeresgebiete und liefert keine punktgenaue Vorhersage einer einzelnen Welle zu einer bestimmten Uhrzeit. Die Technologie bietet folglich eine erheblich verbesserte Entscheidungsgrundlage auf Basis harter Physik, kann das naturbedingte Restrisiko auf den Ozeanen aber nicht vollständig eliminieren.

articles.title: Endeavor Catalyst closes $320m Fund V - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Endeavor Catalyst, the venture capital arm of global entrepreneur network Endeavor, has closed its oversubscribed Fund V at US$320 million, taking its total assets under management past US$850 million.
Endeavor Catalyst invests exclusively in companies led by Endeavor Entrepreneurs, co-investing alongside leading venture capital and growth equity firms. Across its five funds, it has already backed 437 companies in 44 markets, deploying more than US$500 million across 469 investments.
Africa makes up seven per cent of both the portfolio and Catalyst capital, with 29 companies backed across five African markets, including the likes of Flutterwave, Moniepoint, MAX and Moove. Six of these are valued at US$1 billion or more. A decade ago, the fund had made no African investments.
Fund V has already backed 30 companies and deployed more than US$55 million, with a further US$25 million to US$30 million expected to be invested before the end of 2026.
“For the founders we have yet to welcome into the Endeavor community, it sends an important signal: world-class capital is looking for ambition, wherever that ambition is being built,” said Ireayo Oladunjoye, managing director and CEO of Endeavor Nigeria.

articles.title: Meta presenta Muse Wonder y Muse Wonder Full, sus modelos de IA más punteros para ponerse en la frontera de la tecnología
articles.text:
Meta ha lanzado este lunes Muse Wonder y Muse Wonder Full, los primeros modelos de sus “Superintelligence Labs” que, según la compañía, se colocan a la vanguardia junto con los mejores modelos de OpenAI y Anthropic. Llegan en un momento en que Meta intenta demostrar que toda la oleada de despidos y la profunda reestructuración de su división de IA, puesta en marcha el año pasado, está dando sus frutos.
Muy atrás. Meta se quedó atrás en la carrera de la IA después del fiasco de Llama 4 el año pasado. Desde entonces, sus rivales han avanzado con sistemas mucho más capaces. Mark Zuckerberg respondió creando Meta Superintelligence Labs y contratando a Alexandr Wang, el exdirector ejecutivo de Scale AI, y uno de los nombres propios más destacados de la IA, para liderarlo.
Muse Wonder es la primera prueba real de si esa apuesta ha funcionado. De momento, si hablamos en términos económicos, los inversores han reaccionado positivamente. Y es que según Bloomberg, las acciones de Meta subieron hasta un 4,7 % tras la noticia.
Qué hay de nuevo. Hay dos modelos. Muse Wonder será pronto el cerebro de Muse, la app de agentes de IA personales de Meta, para los suscriptores de los niveles mensuales de 20 y 100 dólares. Por otro lado está Muse Wonder Full, que se trata de la versión más potente y estará limitada a los suscriptores de Muse Code, la herramienta de programación de IA de Meta. De momento ésta no se ofrecerá a través de la API.
Wonder en sí llegará a los desarrolladores a través de la API de modelos de Meta, con un precio de 4 dólares por millón de tokens de entrada y 20 dólares por millón de tokens de salida, lo que según TechCrunch lo sitúa aproximadamente al nivel de GPT-6 Sol o Claude Opus 5.5.
Las cifras. A falta de poner a prueba el modelo en profundidad, Meta afirma que la versión más grande del modelo supera a Claude Fable 5.1 de Anthropic y se sitúa justo por debajo de Claude Opus 5.5 en el Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, uno de los rankings de referencia para valorar modelos de IA. La compañía también afirma que supera al GPT-6 Astra de OpenAI y a ambos modelos de Anthropic en algunas pruebas especializadas, incluyendo trabajo con documentos legales y desarrollo de software.
UN VISTAZO A...
De momento, todas estas cifras proceden de las propias pruebas de Meta, así que debemos esperar a las pruebas independientes para hacernos una idea realmente de la potencia de estos nuevos modelos.
La propuesta. Wang declaraba a Bloomberg que el resto de la industria se ha "centrado realmente en los agentes de programación", mientras que Meta quiere hacer que el caso de uso del agente personal "destaque de verdad". Y para ello hacen referencia a dos técnicas: Active Memory y Active Focus.
Según cuenta la compañía, mientras que la primera mencionada permite al modelo retener lo que le importa a un usuario durante "días, semanas, meses", para que la gente no tenga que repetirse, la segunda está diseñada para mantener al modelo enfocado en un objetivo establecido durante tareas largas y complejas, evitando errores acumulativos que puedan encarecer la factura cuando se trabaja con agentes.
¿Y qué pasa con la seguridad? El lanzamiento se produce en medio de una preocupación generalizada por los agentes de IA descontrolados, un tema del que llevamos meses viendo ejemplos poco alentadores. Meta afirma que ha entrenado a Muse Wonder para rechazar solicitudes peligrosas, como ayuda con armas biológicas o nucleares, un “mal uso cibernético” y otros asuntos, y ha publicado un marco para escalar las capacidades “de manera responsable”.
Sin embargo, cabe señalar que Meta no ha dicho si los agentes que se ejecutan en el modelo se comportaron de forma errática en las pruebas, ni cómo abordaron este riesgo específicamente. La compañía tampoco ha revelado cómo se construyeron o entrenaron los modelos, más allá de afirmar, que el entrenamiento tuvo lugar en su centro de datos Prometheus en Ohio.
Qué sigue. Wang declaraba a Bloomberg que su equipo ya está trabajando en "modelos más grandes y a mayor escala" mientras desarrolla versiones más baratas y especializadas de Wonder que podrían dar servicio a miles de millones de usuarios. Meta también ha afirmado que planea lanzar modelos más grandes de pesos abiertos, según comparten desde Wired, tras el pequeño Muse Glimmer.

articles.title: Jusqu’à 4 500 € de remise immédiate : on a déniché les meilleures promos du Mondial de l’Auto pour acheter votre voiture électrique au meilleur prix — Frandroid
articles.text:
Dans les allées du parc des expositions à Paris, c’est déjà l’effervescence. Le Mondial de l’auto vient à peine d’ouvrir ses portes au grand public, ce mardi 13 octobre, qu’il y a déjà foule. Les visiteurs profitent de décors somptueux, d’animations, de concept-cars assez fous et de modèles de voitures fraîchement commercialisés.
Mais en coulisse, la pression est maximale. Une armada de vendeurs s’affairent pour faire du business. Car oui, l’événement est avant tout un salon de vente. S’il y a le stand à rentabiliser, il faut dire aussi qu’il est question de suivre la cadence des commandes concernant les voitures électriques, plutôt bonne en ce moment. Pas question de ralentir ou d’attendre que les consommateurs se décident, encore frileux sur la conduite en électrique ou par rapport au prix.
C’est la fête de l’automobile
Le Mondial de l’auto se transforme en un véritable showroom géant. À la différence qu’il y a semble-t-il davantage de bonnes affaires qu’à l’accoutumée. C’est la fête de l’automobile alors ces rabais, ces promotions, ces remises, ces ristournes, appelez-les comme vous le voulez, mais elles sont un peu plus agressives -parce que cumulables avec ce qui existe déjà en concession ou éphémères le temps du salon.
Nous avons posé la question pour vous aux marques. Alors voici un petit florilège d’offres commerciales. Celles qu’on a bien voulu nous confirmer.
Parce que certaines marques sont quand même restées discrètes sur le sujet, comme Renault qui mentionne seulement 2 mois de loyers offerts en location (LOA/LLD). Sauf que deux clients attrapés à la sortie des bureaux de ventes nous ont bien parlé de 1 000 euros de remise « nette » sur des Scénic E-Tech, Twingo et R5…
BYD transparent sur ses prix
Ce qu’il faut retenir, c’est que si jamais vous êtes lancés dans un processus d’achat, c’est peut-être le moment de concrétiser car certains se montrent agressifs. C’est le cas de BYD par exemple.
Non seulement, le constructeur chinois a mis le paquet pour ériger un stand remarquable, mais il a joué la totale transparence sur les promos, visibles sur les petites pancartes placées à côté des modèles. Ce qui peut tout de suite attirer le chaland.
On y voit par exemple que l’Atto 3 Evo bénéficie d’entrée d’un bonus BYD de 3 500 euros en plus de la prime CEE de 365 euros. Le modèle vaut ainsi 35 125 euros sur le salon au lieu de 42 490 euros.
Le prix de la Dolphin Surf descend à 20 325 euros grâce à un bonus de 3 800 euros cumulé à la prime. Sur la Sealion 7, le bonus BYD atteint 4 500 euros, ce qui permet de l’obtenir à 42 125 euros (prime CEE déduite aussi).
Kia va tenter de vous faire craquer pour l’achat de son EV3. Entre autres promos sur ses hybrides, la marque active un booster de 500 euros supplémentaires pendant le salon (valable en concession aussi), et ce en plus d’une remise client d’un montant de 4 000 euros. Vous pouvez donc acheter le SUV environ 30 000 euros (prime CEE de 660 euros déduite aussi) au lieu de 35 490 euros en prix catalogue.
Si vous êtes fin négociateur ou même très motivé, il est possible d’aller chercher d’autres rabais sur la reprise de votre ancien véhicule ou sur une des options qui vous tiennent à cœur…
Rappelez-vous que les vendeurs et les constructeurs ont une sacrée marge de manœuvre, donc il est facile de gratter quelques économies en plus sans culpabiliser.
Des loyers beaucoup plus attractifs
À Paris, Xpeng tente aussi de frapper fort. Le constructeur chinois propose son SUV électrique G9 à taux zéro, quand le taux de financement sur 48 mois est à 5 % en temps normal. Il prend donc en charge la différence et cela donne un loyer à 649 euros par mois.
En quelque sorte « l’argent est gratuit et il faut en profiter », me dit-on sur le stand. Sur le tout nouveau L03, le loyer se cale à 299 euros par mois grâce à la subvention au lieu de 500 euros.
À la concurrence, on négocie aussi sur les loyers en offrant la finition supérieure au prix de la finition de base. Geely propose par exemple une E2 Pro+ à 289 euros par mois au lieu de 319 euros ou une E5 Pro+ à 379 euros au lieu de 439 euros.
Pour ses 1 000 premiers clients, Gac va cumuler les offres sur ses Aion (UT et V) avec 300 euros de recharge et 4 ans d’entretien offerts, ainsi que des loyers rabaissés à 299 et 399 euros.
Volvo a le même discours : s’il offre 6 ans d’entretien sur le EX40, il promet « un accompagnement sur les offres de financement plutôt avantageuses ». Idem, nous pensons que c’est le minimum de la négo et que vous pouvez obtenir bien plus dans l’euphorie du salon.
Chez Stellantis aussi on fait des ristournes
Alors que Peugeot n’a pas répondu à nos sollicitations, Citroën confirme qu’il y a bien des « conditions commerciales pour les clients sur le salon » sans pour autant vouloir nous les communiquer.
Dans le groupe Stellantis, il y a aussi la petite ristourne qui va bien du côté d’Alfa Romeo. Si les acheteurs se laissent tenter par le Junior et le Tonale en version haute et teinte rouge, ils pourront ainsi obtenir des « montants de loyers spécifiques » et/ou selon les négociations 1 000 euros de « remise nette ».
    Pour aller plus loin
Lancia ressuscite la mythique Gamma : le SUV électrique aux 740 km d’autonomie
            
Lancia se montre aussi généreux pendant ce Mondial de l’auto, surtout que le constructeur est en plein lancement de ses modèles Gamma. Il maintient donc un loyer à 495 euros sans apport pendant tout le mois. Après, ça risque d’augmenter nous dit un commercial. Ce dernier lâche aussi qu’il y a éventuellement des offres améliorées supplémentaires à déclencher.
Chez Fiat et Leapmotor, deux autres marques du groupe Stellantis, le prix est variable selon le client et le vendeur, si l’on comprend bien. Les tarifs sont affichés mais on nous assure que les équipes commerciales ont « des moyens supplémentaires pour proposer un prix en dessous de ce qui est affiché afin de remporter le deal ».
Et les jeux concours, alors !
Alors que Skoda assure faire des « offres pendant la période du Mondial et offrir des vouchers de recharge de 300 euros pour l’Epiq et de 600 euros pour Peaq », Volkswagen fait un geste commercial sur les ID. Polo, ID.Cross et ID.Tiguan concernant le taux bancaire.
Il est bonifié dans le cadre d’un financement locatif sur 37 mois : l’écart par rapport aux loyers traditionnels monte à une vingtaine d’euros par mois. Cette bonification est également valable dans l’ensemble des concessions pour ne pas léser les clients en province qui ne pourraient pas se rendre au salon, nous dit-on.
Ah, le dernier petit bonus peut peut-être vous faire plaisir : les cadeaux ! Que vous veniez pour acheter ou visiter, les constructeurs sont là pour faire la fête avec vous. Sur tous les stands, je dis bien tous, il y a des jeux concours, et souvent gagnants. Hyundai vous fait gagner des places pour des matchs de la Ligue des champions.

articles.title: Shareholder revolt leaves Africa Bitcoin Corporation with two directors
articles.text:
Africa Bitcoin Corporation (ABC), South Africa’s listed Bitcoin treasury firm and financial services group, faces a new battle over who joins its board after four directors, including its chairperson and interim chief executive, resigned following a shareholder push to remove them.
With just two directors remaining, the company must rebuild its board while a separate demand to appoint two new non-executive directors remains unresolved.
The dispute centres on two shareholder demands. Investors holding approximately 76% of ABC’s shares called for the appointment of two new non-executive directors, a move the board opposed on governance grounds. A subsequent demand, backed by shareholders holding approximately 71.8% of the company’s shares, sought the removal of four existing directors.
All four have since resigned, making the removal resolutions unnecessary, but the original demand for two new appointments remains in force.
ABC now faces a governance test at a critical point in its transformation from a small-business financier into a Bitcoin treasury company. Shareholders have forced out most of its board, but the fight over who should replace them remains unsettled, raising questions about how the company will balance investor control, regulatory scrutiny, and independent oversight as it pursues its new strategy.
The four directors who resigned are Norma Sephuma, board chairperson; Stafford Masie, the company’s interim chief executive officer (CEO); and independent non-executive directors Snowy Masakale and GG Alcock. The company disclosed the departures in a Stock Exchange News Service (SENS) announcement on Monday, following the supplementary shareholder demand.
The departing directors said they had not taken the decision lightly, but that differences with WGW Capital Proprietary Limited, an ABC shareholder, had become irreconcilable.
“Recently, however, material differences emerged between the Board and WGW,” ABC said in the announcement.
The remaining directors are Robin Coode, an independent non-executive director, and Jonathan Phillips, the company’s financial director. They are working with the company’s advisers to restore the board and committee structures in line with statutory, regulatory, and JSE listing requirements.
Shareholder push for new directors
The dispute began with the demand for two additional directors, which the board addressed in an October 8 announcement. ABC acknowledged that shareholders had validly demanded a meeting under section 61(3) of the Companies Act, but said it did not support the proposed appointments at that time.
“The Board’s concern relates primarily to governance and regulatory integrity given the exceptional circumstances currently facing the Group,” ABC said.
The company stressed that its objection was not a general assessment of the candidates’ professional experience or capabilities. It committed to taking the necessary steps to convene the meeting and put the proposed resolutions to shareholders in accordance with applicable legal and regulatory requirements.
However, the announcement did not identify the proposed candidates, specify a meeting date, or provide further details about the board’s objections.
The original appointment demand remains unresolved. The two remaining directors must oversee the company while addressing the shareholder request and restoring the board’s composition.
Before its Bitcoin treasury pivot, the company listed as Altvest Capital on the Cape Town Stock Exchange (CTSE) in May 2022, initially valued at R50 million ($3 million). It later introduced three additional share classes—Class A for Umgani Lodge, Class B for Bambanani, and Class C for Altvest Credit Opportunities Fund (ACOF)—to raise funding for investments, but trading in its securities remained thin.
Figures published in its 2024 prospectus show just 42,420 ordinary shares changing hands between July 2023 and July 2024, generating about R131,031.05 ($7,948) in reported turnover.
Altvest moved its equity listing to the Johannesburg Stock Exchange’s (JSE) AltX Market in October 2024, citing limitations in the Cape Town exchange’s ability to attract retail investors and support sizeable capital raises. In May 2026, it transferred its shares to the JSE Main Board.
In 2025, ABC expanded beyond small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) lending to adopt Bitcoin as a long-term treasury asset, making its first disclosed purchase in February. Shareholders approved its rebrand from Altvest to Africa Bitcoin Corporation on September 10, 2025, with the new name and ticker taking effect on the JSE two weeks later.
Since then, the company has retained its SME financing business, while aggressively pushing its Bitcoin investment strategy for institutional investors seeking access to the cryptocurrency.
Deepening leadership crisis
The boardroom dispute comes amid a series of leadership changes following enforcement action by the Financial Sector Conduct Authority (FSCA), South Africa’s financial services regulator, against three individuals associated with ABC, which previously operated as Altvest Capital.
The regulator found that former CEO Warren Wheatley, his wife Tatum Keshwar-Wheatley and former chief investment officer Akshay Karan manipulated Altvest shares in September 2022 to artificially inflate the share price and create a misleading impression of market demand and trading activity.
The three were fined a combined R9 million ($546,000) and debarred from the financial services industry for 20 years. The FSCA’s enforcement action was against the individuals, not ABC itself.
Wheatley has disputed the regulator’s findings, describing the transactions as three trades involving just 50 shares worth R301 ($18.26) that were intended to test the CTSE’s trading platform.
In a podcast interview with financial publication Moneyweb on October 9, Wheatley said those trades aimed to document pricing errors on the trading platform ahead of Altvest’s first public offering, disputing the regulator’s finding that they were part of a scheme to manipulate the share price for profit.
FSCA did not respond to a request for comment on its findings, the evidence supporting the market manipulation allegations, and the status of any appeals against its enforcement action.
In an email to TechCabal on September 8, Wheatley declined to comment, saying “none of the affected parties would be providing commentary” until their appeals are submitted.
In a September 1 SENS announcement, ABC said the affected individuals had informed the company that they disputed the findings and intended to seek reconsideration and suspension of the decisions before the Financial Services Tribunal, an independent body reviewing financial regulator decisions.
The Tribunal told TechCabal in September that it had not received applications for reconsideration or suspension involving the named parties at that time. Lwandiso Mgijima of the Financial Services Tribunal confirmed that no applications had been filed at the time.
“We confirm that the Tribunal has not received any applications for reconsideration or suspension involving the parties [Wheatley, Keshwar-Wheatley, and Karan] mentioned in your e-mail. The Tribunal is, accordingly, not in possession of any documents relating to the matter,” Mgijima said.
In a subsequent response to TechCabal, the Financial Services Tribunal confirmed that it received applications for reconsideration and suspension on September 25, 2026, after previously stating that no applications had been received. The matter, registered under case number A43/2026, lists Warren Gregory Wheatley, WGW Capital (Pty) Ltd, Tatum Lucy Wheatley, Tatum Keshwar Investments (Pty) Ltd, and Akshay Suresh Karan as applicants. The Tribunal said it had not yet ruled on the suspension application or set a hearing date.
“We confirm that applications for reconsideration and suspension involving the parties mentioned in your e-mail were received and processed by the Tribunal on 25 September 2026,” the Tribunal said. “We confirm that the Tribunal has not issued a ruling in respect of the suspension application. The process is ongoing.”
Wheatley, ABC’s co-founder and former CEO, resigned from the company with effect from September 21, 2026, after being placed on precautionary leave. Karan, who had also been placed on precautionary leave, resigned as chief investment officer with effect from October 1.
Masie took over as interim CEO after Wheatley was placed on precautionary leave. He has now also quit as interim CEO and director of Bitcoin Strategy, ABC’s Bitcoin investment subsidiary, with an intended final day of service of February 28, 2027.
ABC said Masie had agreed to continue fulfilling his executive responsibilities, supporting the management team, maintaining operational continuity and facilitating an orderly transition to permanent executive leadership.
Despite the board departures, ABC says its executive management team remains in place and will continue managing day-to-day operations within its existing lawful delegated authorities.
The company said its remaining directors, in consultation with its advisers, were addressing the steps needed to restore the appropriate board and committee composition.
Editor’s note: This article has been updated to include confirmation from the Financial Services Tribunal that it received applications for reconsideration and suspension. The case remains pending.

articles.title: Epic Games apostaría por crear videojuegos con IA: un shooter de Disney sería su primer gran proyecto
articles.text:
Epic Games apostaría por crear videojuegos con inteligencia artificial, con un shooter de Disney como posible primer proyecto de gran escala bajo este modelo. La compañía, conocida por Fortnite, Unreal Engine y su tienda digital, buscaría situar la IA generativa en el centro de su proceso de desarrollo, aunque conservaría la supervisión de equipos humanos.
La información cobra relevancia porque plantea un cambio en la producción de juegos comerciales de alto presupuesto. Epic ya ha incorporado herramientas de inteligencia artificial en Unreal Engine y en personajes de Fortnite, pero el supuesto título de Disney llevaría esa estrategia a un producto basado en franquicias como Marvel y Star Wars.
Epic Games prepararía un cambio en la producción de videojuegos
Según la información atribuida a fuentes internas, Epic Games avanzaría hacia un flujo de trabajo centrado en inteligencia artificial. El objetivo sería utilizar sistemas generativos para acelerar tareas de programación, creación artística y diseño de recursos dentro de los videojuegos.
El cambio no significaría que los desarrolladores desaparezcan del proceso. Los equipos humanos mantendrían la responsabilidad de revisar el contenido generado, corregir errores y decidir qué elementos cumplen con los estándares técnicos y creativos necesarios para llegar a una versión final.
La compañía ya había mostrado interés por estas herramientas. Unreal Engine, su motor gráfico, incorpora cada vez más funciones relacionadas con IA generativa, mientras que Fortnite ha experimentado con personajes capaces de responder a los jugadores mediante sistemas de inteligencia artificial.
La nueva estrategia buscaría reducir el código escrito manualmente y aumentar el uso de recursos generados con IA, una transformación que puede afectar a la organización tradicional de los equipos de desarrollo.
Un shooter de Disney reuniría personajes de Marvel y Star Wars
El primer gran proyecto bajo esta fórmula sería un videojuego de disparos de Disney que todavía no cuenta con anuncio oficial. El título combinaría personajes de Marvel y Star Wars, dos de las propiedades más conocidas del grupo de entretenimiento.
La información disponible señala que la herramienta Claude participaría en la generación de personajes y otros componentes del juego. No hay detalles confirmados sobre su argumento, sus plataformas, sus modos de juego o el sistema de progresión que tendría.
El lanzamiento parecía previsto inicialmente para marzo del próximo año, aunque el proyecto habría sufrido un retraso. La ausencia de una presentación pública impide conocer si Epic mantendrá ese calendario o si modificará por completo sus planes antes de revelar el videojuego.
La participación de franquicias de Disney elevaría el alcance del proyecto, ya que Marvel y Star Wars cuentan con comunidades globales y una larga presencia en videojuegos, películas, series y productos de consumo.
La transición genera dudas entre los desarrolladores
La apuesta por la IA no tendría consenso completo dentro de Epic Games. Algunos desarrolladores habrían cuestionado el cambio frente al modelo tradicional, donde artistas, programadores, guionistas y diseñadores elaboran cada elemento de manera directa.
El debate se repite en buena parte de la industria. Las herramientas generativas pueden agilizar prototipos, automatizar tareas repetitivas y facilitar pruebas técnicas. Sin embargo, también abren interrogantes sobre la calidad de los resultados, los derechos de autor, la originalidad y el impacto en puestos de trabajo especializados.
Epic Games Store regala Out of Sight hasta el 15 de octubre
Mientras prepara este posible salto hacia la IA, Epic Games Store permite descargar gratis Out of Sight, un juego de terror desarrollado por The Gang Studio. La promoción estará activa hasta el jueves 15 de octubre y permite conservar el título de forma permanente en la biblioteca digital.
El juego suele costar USD 6 y cuenta con cerca de un 90% de valoraciones favorables en Steam. La historia sigue a Sophie, una niña ciega cautiva en una mansión, que debe escapar de sus perseguidores con ayuda de un osito de peluche.
La mecánica permite observar el entorno a través de los ojos del muñeco. Esa perspectiva ayuda a localizar rutas, detectar obstáculos y resolver acertijos, mientras la protagonista intenta avanzar sin enfrentamientos directos.
Cómo reclamar Out of Sight en Epic Games Store
- Ingresar a store.epicgames.com
- Crear una cuenta o iniciar sesión
- Abrir la sección “Tienda”
- Buscar Out of Sight entre los juegos gratuitos
- Verificar que el precio sea 0
- Pulsar “Obtener” y confirmar la operación
- Revisar que el título aparezca en la biblioteca
Una vez reclamado, Out of Sight quedará asociado a la cuenta y podrá instalarse más adelante, incluso después de que termine la promoción.

Adobe Patches 176 Vulnerabilities Across 11 Products
articles.text:
Adobe has published 11 new security advisories to inform customers about roughly 176 vulnerabilities found and patched in its products.
Adobe Experience Manager (AEM) received patches for 36 vulnerabilities, including several critical flaws allowing arbitrary code execution. The list also includes privilege escalation and security bypass issues.
Adobe ColdFusion updates address 32 vulnerabilities, including critical bugs that can be exploited for code execution and privilege escalation.
A significant number of flaws have been patched by Adobe in the Content Credentials SDK. The product received fixes for 30 vulnerabilities, many described as high-severity issues that can lead to a security feature bypass. Some security holes can be exploited to cause a DoS condition.
Adobe patched 18 vulnerabilities in Photoshop, nearly all allowing arbitrary code execution.
In Substance 3D Stager, Adobe fixed 16 vulnerabilities, including many high-severity arbitrary code execution flaws.
Eleven vulnerabilities have been resolved in Adobe Commerce, including several critical issues that can be exploited without authentication to execute code or escalate privileges.
Several vulnerabilities that allow arbitrary code execution have been fixed in each of the following products: FrameMaker, Dimension, Substance 3D Sampler, Substance 3D Designer, and Bridge.
Adobe says it’s not aware of any in-the-wild exploitation. Most advisories have a priority rating of 3, which indicates Adobe does not expect to see these vulnerabilities exploited in attacks. Commerce and AEM the only products with a priority rating of 2 (threat actors have historically targeted Commerce).
Adobe has been using frontier AI models to hunt for flaws in its own code, which helps explain the higher volume of fixes. However, the company has still credited external researchers for many of the newly patched vulnerabilities.
While AI has helped Adobe find more vulnerabilities in its software, engineers still review, validate, and approve all AI-assisted code changes before deployment.
The rise in discoveries led Adobe to stop publishing security bulletins monthly. The company has moved to a twice-monthly schedule, on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month.
* Updated with information on Adobe Experience Manager patches. Headline and lede have been updated to include AEM vulnerability count
