articles.title: The traditional PC layout might not be the best: unusual GPU placement cuts temperatures by 17°C
articles.text:
In a nutshell: PC builders have long tried to find the most optimal cooling setups for their components, moving around fans, cables, etc. to find the best configurations. A YouTube channel decided to try something a little different: moving the components themselves. This included shifting the GPU next to a case's side-intake, which resulted in a 17-degree drop in temperatures.
The experiment was carried out by TrashBench, which used an Asus ROG Strix RTX 3080 inside a dual-chamber case. The cooling came from three side-intake fans, a rear exhaust, and a top-mounted 360mm CPU AIO.
The idea was to change component placement without moving the case fans. PCIe riser cables were used so the graphics card could be moved away from its usual slot on the motherboard.
Testing involved looping 3DMark Time Spy alongside 7-Zip running on 12 CPU threads. All fans stayed at fixed RPMs, with each configuration tested for ten minutes and temperatures averaged over the final five.
The GPU's first position was on the case floor, which required the removal of the bottom mesh because it touched the card's fans. GPU temperatures barely changed, but the CPU and motherboard VRM dropped around 4°C and 7°C, respectively. Conventional vertical mounting slightly worsened GPU temperatures while modestly improving everything else.
However, placing the card directly against the side intake made all the difference. GPU core temperatures fell 16.7°C, the hotspot dropped 19.3°C, and VRAM cooled by 14°C. Motherboard VRMs also dropped around 8°C, while the CPU warmed just 1.1°C.
Moving the card behind those intake fans, into the rear chamber, improved on stock temperatures but couldn't match the previous arrangement.
Next came the CPU. Relocating its radiator would have introduced another variable, so TrashBench placed the GPU back in its usual position and reversed the radiator fans from exhaust to intake. CPU temperatures dropped about 6°C, but the graphics card suffered from the radiator's warm exhaust.
Combining the intake radiator with the GPU beside the side intake improved both components over stock. It led to a 3.3°C reduction in CPU temperature and a 14°C cooler GPU hotspot, sacrificing some GPU cooling for a better overall balance.
TrashBench acknowledges that the experiment wasn't rigorously scientific, and different cases, fans, and fan positions will likely change the results. But as the channel points out, it illustrates how the normal PC layout might not be the best one.
TrashBench carries out lots of experiments like these. Last year, it strapped dual CPU tower coolers to an RTX 2060, cutting temperatures by 31°C.

articles.title: ZCS Command Injection via SNMP Handlers Enables Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution
articles.text:
A critical remote command execution vulnerability affecting the Zimbra Collaboration Suite mail platform has come under active, widespread exploitation, allowing adversaries to harvest complete mailbox archives and persistent authentication credentials without prior system access.
The defect, tracked as CVE-2026-73570, carries a CVSS score of 8.9 and stems from improper input sanitisation inside the platform's SNMP notification subsystem. When paired with public-facing mail transfer agents, the pipeline permits unauthenticated remote attackers to inject arbitrary operating system commands that execute under the context of the underlying Zimbra operating system user account.
Maintainer Synacor initially addressed the vulnerability quietly in Zimbra Collaboration Suite version 10.1.20 on July 20, 2026, but delayed public disclosure until August 13, 2026. During this multi-week disclosure lag, adversaries reverse-engineered the binary changes and launched scanning campaigns against public instances. Telemetry captured by Microsoft and Polish national cybersecurity agency CERT Polska confirmed that threat groups actively probed enterprise mail infrastructure throughout late July and August, deploying backdoors before most operations teams recognised the severity of the patch.
At the protocol level, the flaw sits within the path where Postfix and upstream mail services hand off operational status alerts to the internal Simple Network Management Protocol daemon. Zimbra installs an optional telemetry service package, designated as zimbra-snmp, which runs the swatchdog log monitoring utility to scan log lines and dispatch snmptrap alerts. When inbound SMTP transactions parse user-controlled header parameters, specifically crafted envelope fields are logged directly into local syslog targets without shell argument sanitisation.
The swatchdog daemon watches these logs using regular expression pattern rules. Once matched, it interpolates the captured text variables into an unquoted string passed directly to a system shell execution call. Because characters such as semicolons, backticks, and pipes remain intact through the log parsing process, the external caller can append commands directly into the operating system trap execution string.
Image Source: Microsoft Blog Post
Observed exploitation begins with lightweight recon sweeps, where threat actors dispatch SMTP packets carrying shell logic designed to invoke out-of-band network calls via curl or nslookup. These callbacks confirm command execution before heavier payloads arrive. Once verification succeeds, attackers inject base64-encoded strings that write JSP web shells directly into web-accessible server directories, such as the Jetty application server root (/opt/zimbra/jetty/webapps/zimbra/).
With arbitrary file write and execution established within the Jetty container, operators execute zmprov command-line utilities natively available to the zimbra Unix user. This yields administrative LDAP tokens, authentication keys, and database credentials, unlocking access to export full user mailboxes into encrypted staging archives before exfiltration to external cloud buckets.
POST /zimbra/public/jsp_shell.jsp HTTP/1.1
Host: mail.target-enterprise.com
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
cmd=zmprov+getAllAccounts+-v+domain.com
zmmailbox -z -m user@domain.com getRestURL "//?fmt=tgz" > /tmp/backup.tgz
Remediating CVE-2026-73570 requires updating nodes to Zimbra version 10.1.20 or newer, which replaces shell-concatenated string execution within the monitoring subsystem with direct parameter arrays passed safely to system execve routines. For organizations unable to perform an immediate binary migration across multi-node clusters, maintainers recommend disabling the SNMP service package entirely to eliminate the vulnerable swatchdog loop.
su - zimbra
zmcontrol stop snmp
zmprov ms `zmhostname` -zimbraServiceEnabled snmp
Disabling SNMP halts outbound telemetry and automated performance trapping, which degrades central monitoring pipelines and cluster observability dashboards. However, operational intelligence from the Shadowserver Foundation indicates that approximately 274 compromised production instances were observed following disclosure, while roughly 10,000 public-facing Zimbra deployments remain exposed to scanning scripts. Systems teams running exposed mail gateways must treat unpatched servers as compromised, review Jetty deployment directories for unauthorized JSP files, rotate all LDAP and zimbra service account credentials, and restrict administrative endpoints to internal jump hosts.

articles.title: Apple tiene nuevo hogar inteligente con HomeView, Apple TV 4K y HomePod mini 2: precio, disponibilidad y características
articles.text:
Apple renueva su apuesta por el hogar inteligente con el lanzamiento de HomeView, una pantalla con Siri AI, un Apple TV 4K actualizado y el HomePod mini 2. La compañía presentó los tres dispositivos durante Welcome Home, una jornada dirigida a reforzar su ecosistema doméstico conectado y ampliar el papel de la inteligencia artificial.
Apple busca reunir en sus equipos el control de luces, cámaras, cerraduras y termostatos, además de acceso a entretenimiento y comunicaciones. La estrategia incorpora una pantalla doméstica propia y actualiza dos productos que ya funcionaban como centros de control dentro de la aplicación Casa. El despliegue, no obstante, dependerá de los mercados y del idioma.
HomeView incorpora una pantalla de siete pulgadas para gestionar la casa
El nuevo HomeView combina una pantalla Liquid Retina de siete pulgadas, un altavoz y una central para el hogar conectado. Apple lo ofrecerá en una versión de sobremesa con base de altavoz regulable y en otra preparada para fijarse a la pared. El modelo de mesa llegará en plata, blanco estrella, rosa y gris espacial.
Su sistema reconoce hasta seis rostros y adapta la información de cada perfil, con acceso separado a mensajes, calendarios, recordatorios y aplicaciones. También permite videollamadas mediante FaceTime y cambia el contenido según la distancia del usuario.
El equipo integra el chip A18, Apple Intelligence y Siri AI para comprender peticiones más complejas y utilizar el contexto de dispositivos compatibles. Si se vincula a un iPhone o iPad, puede consultar información personal de Calendario, Mensajes o Apple Music para responder a solicitudes concretas.
En la vivienda, permite gestionar accesorios compatibles con Matter, mostrar hasta nueve cámaras y detectar personas, mascotas, paquetes o vehículos con un plan compatible de iCloud+.
Apple TV 4K incorpora chip A19, WiFi 7 y funciones de Siri AI
El nuevo Apple TV 4K conserva el diseño de la generación anterior, pero cambia los componentes internos. Su procesador A19 aumenta el rendimiento de la CPU hasta un 50% y duplica la potencia gráfica respecto al modelo previo, según la información presentada. El dispositivo incorpora también un decodificador AV1 para mejorar la reproducción de contenidos en streaming.
La conectividad suma WiFi 7, Bluetooth 6.0 y HDMI 2.1, mientras mantiene Dolby Vision y Dolby Atmos. Tres micrófonos de largo alcance permiten activar Siri sin utilizar el mando.
El equipo podrá controlar accesorios domésticos desde el televisor y mostrar imágenes de cámaras o videoporteros. Además, permitirá conectar hasta cuatro altavoces HomePod para crear un sistema de sonido envolvente. La configuración será compatible con los HomePod mini 2 y los HomePod de segunda generación, con ajustes automáticos de sincronización y niveles de audio según su posición en la habitación.
HomePod mini 2 mantiene su diseño e incorpora el chip S10
El HomePod mini 2 llega seis años después del modelo original, presentado en octubre de 2020. Mantiene su forma esférica recubierta de tela y su superficie táctil, pero incorpora un procesador S10, WiFi 7, Bluetooth, Thread y banda ultraancha. Estará disponible en rosa, verde, azul, blanco y negro.
El altavoz conserva un transductor de rango completo, dos radiadores pasivos y cuatro micrófonos para interactuar a distancia con Siri. También permite formar parejas estéreo, reproducir música en varias habitaciones mediante AirPlay y utilizar un Mac como fuente de audio.
Las funciones de Siri AI llegarán posteriormente mediante una actualización de software. La plataforma reconocerá hasta seis voces y, al conectarse con un iPhone o iPad compatible, podrá utilizar datos de aplicaciones personales para responder con mayor contexto. El equipo también podrá controlar luces, persianas, cerraduras y termostatos, además de detectar alarmas de humo o monóxido de carbono. Costará 299 dólares y llegará en noviembre próximo.
Precio, disponibilidad y límites de Siri AI
El HomeView tendrá un precio de 299 dólares, con reservas desde el 13 de octubre y llegada al mercado el 13 de noviembre. Apple prevé venderlo inicialmente en Estados Unidos, Reino Unido, Canadá y Australia.
El dispositivo no estará disponible por ahora en la Unión Europea, incluida España. Apple atribuye esa decisión a que Siri AI todavía no está habilitada en iOS en ese territorio y señaló que mantiene conversaciones con las autoridades europeas para encontrar una solución.
El nuevo Apple TV 4K costará 349 euros, también podrá reservarse desde el 13 de octubre y llegará el 13 de noviembre. El HomePod mini 2 tendrá un precio de 169 euros, con reservas desde la jornada de presentación y disponibilidad desde el 30 de octubre en los mercados anunciados.
Las funciones avanzadas de Siri AI estarán disponibles inicialmente en inglés y en determinados países. Por ese motivo, España no contará desde el lanzamiento con las nuevas capacidades de inteligencia artificial ni en HomeView, ni en Apple TV 4K, ni en HomePod mini 2.

articles.title: Google Partially Reverses Chrome Bug Bounty Cuts
articles.text:
Google announced Tuesday that it’s raising bug bounty rewards for some Chrome vulnerabilities, focusing on memory safety issues.
AI has been changing the pace and profile of vulnerability discovery, and the tech giant has been adjusting its bug bounty programs in recent months.
Google significantly lowered standard payout amounts for some Chrome vulnerabilities in April to shift focus to actionable reports, with researchers noting that some rewards became 10 times smaller. At the time it announced a base reward of $500 for memory safety issues, with multipliers for reachability and the level of exploitability.
The company is now quadrupling base rates for memory safety flaws, to $2,000. Despite the increase, the new rates remain well below those offered before the April overhaul.
Vulnerabilities in Chrome’s browser, GPU and network processes can now earn researchers up to $20,000. In the case of the renderer process, bug bounty hunters can receive up to $8,000 for use-after-free and memory write bugs.
V8 sandbox vulnerabilities are moving to a flat rate of $5,000, while V8 logic bugs will be rewarded with $4,000.
As for issues not related to memory safety, medium-severity flaws will be rewarded with $2,000 if the vulnerability report includes or directly leads to an identified fix. Sandbox escapes not involving memory safety bugs can get bug bounties of up to $20,000.
Google is also reintroducing a $2,000 fuzzer bonus for developing novel fuzzers.
The company noted that “any submissions that are currently in our evaluation queue submitted after April 30th, 2026 will be evaluated and rewarded under the new payout rules.”
Google recently announced it’s temporarily closing its Open Source Software Vulnerability Reward Program (OSS VRP) to product vulnerability submissions, prompted by a growing number of AI-generated reports.

articles.title: Funcionária é demitida após recusar “sentinela” que tira foto a cada 3 minutos • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Funcionária é demitida após recusar “sentinela” que tira foto a cada 3 minutos
Monitoramento com IA previa até 160 fotos por dia durante o trabalho no home office. Caso deu origem a processo judicial nos EUA.
Uma funcionária afirma ter sido demitida após se recusar a aceitar um sistema de monitoramento que tiraria cerca de 160 fotos de seu rosto por dia. O caso virou uma ação judicial em Nova Jersey, nos Estados Unidos. Segundo o processo, Glennis Von Sander-Timinski trabalhava de casa na Sutherland Healthcare Solutions desde 2018.
Em agosto, a companhia informou que adotaria uma ferramenta chamada Sentinel AI, que usaria a webcam do notebook para registrar uma imagem a cada três minutos durante um expediente de oito horas. Segundo o processo, o sistema também utilizaria reconhecimento facial para confirmar se a funcionária estava perto do computador.
De início, ela solicitou uma adaptação por preocupação com a privacidade e com os efeitos do sistema sobre a sua saúde. Seu médico enviou uma recomendação para que as capturas fossem menos frequentes, afirmando que o monitoramento estava aumentando o estresse e agravando sintomas de ansiedade.
A ação alega que a empresa não aceitou reduzir a frequência. A funcionária teria recebido como alternativas aceitar o monitoramento, voltar ao trabalho presencial ou deixar a empresa. A ação estima que o deslocamento consumiria aproximadamente seis horas por dia. Ela acabou demitida em 8 de setembro.
Os advogados alegam que a companhia não ofereceu uma adaptação razoável prevista pela legislação de Nova Jersey. O processo ainda está em andamento, portanto as acusações não representam uma decisão legal sobre a conduta da empresa. Caberá à Justiça determinar se houve violação da legislação estadual.
Alguns estados americanos começaram a impor limites a esse tipo de prática. No Maine, uma lei que entrou em vigor em 2026 proíbe o monitoramento dentro de casa, em bens pessoais ou no veículo particular do funcionário, exceto quando necessário para o trabalho. Empresas também precisam avisar os empregados antes de iniciar a vigilância.
Empresas já podem acompanhar localização, produtividade, comunicações e atividades realizadas em dispositivos corporativos. Algumas ferramentas também conseguem acessar câmeras de notebooks e celulares fornecidos pelos empregadores.
Recursos semelhantes aparecem até em softwares muito usados no ambiente corporativo. O Microsoft Teams, por exemplo, pode identificar quando um funcionário está no escritório ao detectar a conexão com a rede Wi-Fi da empresa. A Microsoft também precisou alterar o Microsoft 365 após críticas de que a plataforma permitia acompanhar atividades como envio de e-mails e participação em chats corporativos.
O caso lembra outro episódio em que uma empresa americana foi condenada na Holanda depois de demitir um funcionário que se recusou a manter a webcam ligada durante o expediente remoto.

articles.title: Google wants to host your personal vibe-coded apps in the Play Store
articles.text:
Google has already added a few AI features to the Play Store, but a lot more are coming. The previously released Ask Play feature is expanding to offer more AI-powered discovery options in Google’s app store, and Google is also using AI to build a recommendation engine called Game Finder. For people who have embraced AI to build their own apps, the Play Store will soon offer a way to privately host and share those creations.
Google rolled out Ask Play in 2025 as a small chatbot interface on Play Store listings. It lets you ask questions about an app or game, either by typing it in manually or choosing from a list of suggested queries. Starting today, Ask Play is expanding into a more general way to search for apps and games. You ask the robot questions, and it generates recommendations that can include detailed comparison charts. Gemini will roll out a similar capability soon.
Google’s other AI discovery announcement focuses on games. The new Game Finder feature leans on all the usage data Google’s app platform has hoovered up over the years, featuring insights into the way 1.2 billion people play games on Android. It builds a profile called Gamer DNA and matches you with players who have similar DNA.
You can tune your DNA profile by rating the games you’ve played, which supposedly leads to more accurate recommendations. There will be game playlists to peruse, along with various contextual lists like relaxing, trending titles, and more specific lists based on mechanics you’ve seen in previous games. Game Finder also lets you add or remove tags to further adjust the games Google’s AI suggests. Google says you’ll eventually be able to prompt Game Finder with fairly specific game preferences, but it’s unclear how much customization will be available at launch. Game Finder and Gamer DNA are rolling out in the US today, with other markets following “soon.”

articles.title: Niobia takes the guesswork out of some of tech's most expensive mistakes | TechCrunch
articles.text:
San Francisco-based startup Niobia is betting big on a critical but often overlooked part of battery and chip making: helping engineers understand how and why things go wrong. Its AI software flags production defects and lets engineers ask a chatbot what caused them, aiming to deliver answers in minutes rather than days.
How it works (broadly): The company’s customers place AI agents on their production lines to look for defects, then loop in human engineers to work out what might cause a product to fail. The agents run on self-contained GPUs mounted directly on manufacturing equipment, much like a sensor. They can spot pinhole-sized flaws such as scratches. Niobia’s AI also gathers all the data in one place so engineers can ask a chatbot what went wrong and dig deeper into the cause.
Speed is so critical because chips and batteries are some of the world’s most important products, while also increasingly in short supply. As manufacturers continue to develop and improve their technologies, things inevitably go awry during research and development. Engineers then spend days or longer figuring out a fix before they can restart production. Each flaw or mistake can prove costly — sometimes running into the millions of dollars — and set back manufacturing timelines.
Niobia co-founders Gaurav Jha and Harveen Kaur both have PhDs in chemistry and have worked at chipmakers and battery manufacturers, giving them firsthand experience with the challenges within the industry. In a call ahead of TechCrunch Disrupt 2026, where the company is a Battlefield finalist, Jha explained that while what Niobia does is specialized, it serves a multibillion-dollar market that includes some of the biggest battery and semiconductor makers today.
“It’s extremely niche; maybe people will never know about it,” said Jha, speaking of the battery and chip manufacturing market that his company aims to serve. “But it’s like behind the scenes, this is powering everything… we just don’t see it in the regular world.”
“Every product around you, like glasses or shoes, slippers, wallets, and headphones — these processes touch every single part of it,” added Jha.
Niobia’s agents run on open source models that the company trains further with battery and chip research and other data. That training is what lets them identify pinhole-sized defects. Jha said that Niobia chose open source models largely because its customers don’t want their highly sensitive company information going into a public AI cloud where it might be used to train the model.
“None of our customers want their proprietary data to go to the cloud, even if we tell them it’s safe,” said Jha. The startup also outlines how it approaches cybersecurity, given the high-stakes race among adversarial nations to innovate in the battery and chip space. Niobia, for instance, lets its customers hold their own encryption keys so that the startup cannot decrypt the customers’ data.
Jha said that the company’s priority for now is to focus on three specialties, such as film coating, electroplating (which is coating a surface with metal using an electric current), and fluidized bed reaction (a chemical process where solid particles are suspended in a gas or liquid).
He said that the company also wants its technology to become more autonomous, with the eventual aim of building out a fully self-driving factory for its customers.
If you’re curious to learn more, Niobia will present onstage at TechCrunch Disrupt this afternoon in San Francisco. Join us to catch the company and the 19 startups against which it’s competing as part of our storied Startup Battlefield competition, happening today, Tuesday, through Thursday, October 15.

articles.title: Bad Bunny’s huge world tour show runs off one small rack of servers
articles.text:
Bad Bunny’s record-breaking soldout tour was one of the hottest tickets in the UK this summer, drawing over 104,000 fans across the weekend of June 27th, 2026.
The show was highly anticipated following his Album of the Year Grammy Award for Debí Tirar Más Fotos and history-making Super Bowl Halftime Show.
But the excitement around the show wasn’t just because of the scale of the artist, it was also due to the incredibly ambitious scale of the production.
The best stadium tours have a way of making their use of technology seamless and in some cases, invisible.
You see a 100ft screen tracking the band’s movement from across the field without missing a beat, or members of the audience picked out and flashed on the giant LED walls around the venue.
None of it looks labored or complex, at least not to the general public in attendance. To them it’s all part of the magic of the show, which is exactly the point.
Media servers
Carlos “Charly” Camina is the tour’s media server engineer, and the size of the kit he oversees is much smaller than the grand scale of the show might suggest. The entire production runs on four Disguise GX 3+ servers, with a fifth GX 3 unit held in reserve as an understudy for the show’s director.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
That’s down from five servers during the tour’s earlier Puerto Rico leg, despite the fact that the World Tour carries significantly more content layers and considerably bigger screens at 10,752 x 2,816px, requiring a 4K input.
The GX3+ upgrade alone roughly doubled the processing headroom for the same effects load, which is what made it possible to deliver more with a smaller footprint. The lighting runs on grandMA kit, the unchallenged global industry-standard for live event lighting control, with a grandMA light desk as the main control surface and a grandMA3 compact unit as backup.
The whole setup sits on a dedicated network split into eight isolated VLANs, a structural choice to provide containment, so that a fault in one part of the system can’t spread and collapse the whole thing. The engineering challenge on a show of this scale isn’t cramming in more and more hardware, it’s finding the smallest reliable solution that can do the job every single night, in any venue, anywhere on the planet.
Adaptability is key on any tour
The most unique piece of engineering on the Bad Bunny Tour wasn’t actually planned or commissioned ahead of the show. During rehearsals, the creative team at Sturdy suggested photographing the crowd during the opening act and then displaying those images on LED screens around the venue later on in the show. Charly’s instinct was to push back. Loading fresh, unvetted content into the live system with zero headroom for troubleshooting is the kind of risk that wise engineers know to avoid.
His solution was to keep the additional photography content out of the Disguise system altogether. Instead, he built a standalone application using HTTP Sockpuppet and OSC (Open Sound Control) to communicate with the main Disguise system, running off a laptop. A photographer hands over images for Charly to upload. When the relevant cue fires inside Disguise, it sends a request to the laptop for specific images, which are mapped to specific locations on a four-way live layout.
Charly said that the hardest part wasn’t the concept, it was the live timing: ensuring that front-of-house and the on-stage servers sync closely enough so that there’s no discernable lag, and making sure the system never repeats the same face twice in one night.
How this curveball was handled is a good example of a pattern that shows up across the whole build: rather than adding risk to a proven core system, Charly builds smaller satellite systems to support it and keeps them loosely connected. It’s a slick approach that preserves the magic and spontaneity of a seamless live experience, without risking the core build or compromising the show’s production value.
Animated CGI Frog - Why not?
The tour’s most curious element involved a Puerto Rican-inspired 3D animated frog called “Concho” rendered live using Unreal Engine and a face-tracked performer, which enabled Concho to interact directly with Bad Bunny mid-show as part of a FaceTime call. The segment needed a camera that could move freely, handheld, so the team decided to use an iPhone.
However, the phone could not have any visible external antennas. This meant the feed from the iPhone had to be captured over NDI (Network Device Interface) on a dedicated Wi-Fi network, rather than a standard wireless link that could have been easily interrupted by the tens of thousands of audience and staff devices around the arena. Charly’s team has to scan the RF spectrum every night to find clear channels before the Concho segment goes live.
The benefit of reliability
The ultimate stress test of the system came during the show’s finale where the production deployed a 40-tile feed, displayed in a grid across the main 5K screen and two IMAG screens. Together with Screens Producer Vishal Sharma and his team at All of it Now, who created all the show’s Notch content, Charly decided to route four separate 4K video inputs through a Notch block to build the grid live.
Nothing was pre-rendered or keyframed and the color-grading also took place in real-time. That final segment pushed the servers to their limit, with all four of the GX 3+ units red lining on their performance markers. Despite the load, the system held and delivered a truly spectacular end to the show.
Charly has worked with Disguise servers for over a decade. In that time he’s worked on shows of all types, from festivals like Coachella to state-of-the-art mixed-use venues like the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. With that much experience using these systems, what’s clear to him is that the value in this system isn’t in a specific creative feature. The value is knowing that if a server has an issue mid-show, he can switch to a backup with just one click and have full confidence that the backup will take over seamlessly.
For an engineer, touring a production this huge, reliability and predictability is the actual product. The breathtaking visuals that we get to enjoy as part of the audience will rightly get their applause, but the job is protecting the integrity of the show from its own scale and demands, every night, in every city, until the tour comes to an end.
Jon Devo is a seasoned professional with 20 years of experience in photography and videography. After studying Journalism and Psychology at City University London in 2009, he transitioned into presenting and journalism. Jon is the founder of Devoted Creatives, a photo and video studio based in West London. He hosts two podcasts: Spotify’s Shot & Chaser and The Devoted Creatives Podcast. In addition to his podcasting work, Jon writes a monthly column, "Scanning Ahead," for Digital Camera Magazine and contributes for TechRadar.

articles.title: Epic Games reportedly delays Disney shooter title so it can pivot to AI coding — staff allegedly told 'no more handwritten code' with art 'generated with full AI workflows'
articles.text:
Epic Games reportedly delays Disney shooter title so it can pivot to AI coding — staff allegedly told 'no more handwritten code' with art 'generated with full AI workflows'
Will this speed up development times long-term?
Epic Games has reportedly delayed a shooter based on Disney’s Marvel and Star Wars franchises, with its developers told to use more AI. According to Bloomberg, the yet-to-be-named game was supposed to be released in March of 2027, but its launch date has been pushed back to an unspecified date. Aside from that, the company also told the people working on the project to switch to an “AI first” production model. One of the game directors was quoted telling staff that there will be “no more handwritten code” and that the game’s art would now be “generated with full AI workflows.”
Around the same time this news came out, Epic boss Tim Sweeney posted an update on X that seemingly confirms the change. “We have a huge pivot underway here at Epic, moving developers around to retool for maximum AI acceleration,” the Epic founder said on the platform. “The aim isn’t to do the same stuff with fewer people, but to enable everyone here to build MORE and BETTER stuff, and to bring the benefits to all teams using Unreal.” Sweeney has previously criticized Steam for putting AI tags on games, calling it “irresponsible of Valve.” He says that AI is just a tool and that it’s useful for handling boring, menial, and repetitive tasks like finding errors in code or rigging 3D models. “We’re embracing AI-accelerated development, led by Epic developers who are the visionaries and creative drivers for everything we do,” Epic Games communications director Jake Jones told the publication.
The announcement still reportedly left some of the developers working on the project in a state of astonishment. They were hoping that the directive wasn’t serious or that Epic Games would change its mind about the decision, while others jokingly asked if they should ask Claude to fix its own errors. The delayed title was supposed to be the first in a series of games involving Disney intellectual property, which had invested $1.5 billion in the game developer and publisher in 2024. However, Bloomberg reports that progress on the game has suffered because it lacked the number of people required to keep the schedule on track. It seems that the company is trying to make up for lost time by pushing its people to use AI in the hopes that they’ll be able to work much more quickly.
AI is indeed quite a useful tool, with some developers using it to build surprisingly complicated vibe-coded games, like this GTA clone set in Taipei or this decompiled version of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2. One group even used Gemini for their free game demo, leading to a cost of $1,000 a day in AI usage bills. Despite that, many creators and developers have been against the use of AI in the industry, with one major gaming convention in the UK outright banning games that were built mostly using AI.

articles.title: Justiça obriga OpenAI a entregar documentos de contratação em processo da Apple
articles.text:
A Justiça dos Estados Unidos determinou que a OpenAI entregue documentos relacionados à contratação de ex-funcionários da Apple, em processo no qual a fabricante do iPhone acusa a empresa de inteligência artificial (IA) de se beneficiar de informações comerciais confidenciais.
A decisão, proferida nesta terça-feira (13), permite que a Apple tenha acesso antecipado a registros de entrevistas, mensagens privadas e outras evidências que podem ajudar a esclarecer as acusações.
O juiz federal Edward Davila, responsável pelo caso no Distrito Norte da Califórnia, concedeu parte dos pedidos apresentados pela Apple para acelerar a fase de produção de provas. A OpenAI terá cinco dias para entregar os materiais que já reuniu e 14 dias para apresentar os demais documentos abrangidos pela determinação.
A disputa está relacionada à contratação de antigos funcionários da Apple pela OpenAI, especialmente para equipes envolvidas no desenvolvimento de produtos de hardware e robótica. A empresa de Tim Cook suspeita que informações confidenciais sobre tecnologias e produtos ainda não lançados tenham sido obtidas e utilizadas indevidamente durante esse processo.
Quais documentos a OpenAI terá de entregar?
- A determinação judicial abrange diferentes categorias de materiais que podem ajudar a reconstruir como informações da Apple teriam circulado durante o recrutamento de funcionários;
- Entre os documentos solicitados estão listas de verificação, guias, instruções, manuais e roteiros utilizados nas entrevistas de candidatos provenientes da Apple para a equipe de produtos de hardware de consumo da OpenAI;
- A empresa também deverá apresentar apresentações técnicas e outros registros que documentem o conteúdo dessas entrevistas, incluindo eventuais referências a tecnologias, componentes e projetos da fabricante do iPhone;
- Outro ponto importante envolve as evidências digitais. A decisão prevê a entrega de imagens forenses de dispositivos já coletadas no contexto das acusações, além de conversas privadas trocadas pelo aplicativo de mensagens LINE entre Chang Liu e Alyssa Peng desde janeiro de 2026;
- O juiz também autorizou depoimentos antecipados de três ex-funcionários da Apple: Chang Liu, Alyssa Peng e Tang Yew Tan, atual diretor de hardware da OpenAI. Os depoimentos deverão ajudar a esclarecer as circunstâncias das contratações e o possível uso de informações confidenciais;
- A Apple argumenta que o acesso antecipado é necessário para compreender a extensão do suposto desvio de segredos comerciais e fundamentar seu pedido de medidas judiciais contra os envolvidos.
Apple acusa ex-funcionários de levar informações confidenciais
A Apple entrou com a ação em julho de 2026, alegando que antigos funcionários teriam obtido ou utilizado indevidamente informações relacionadas a produtos e tecnologias ainda não anunciados.
Entre as acusações estão o download de documentos técnicos confidenciais em computadores fornecidos pela Apple, a retenção de equipamentos corporativos após o desligamento e o compartilhamento de informações com outros profissionais interessados em trabalhar na OpenAI.
A fabricante também afirma que candidatos teriam sido orientados sobre quais conhecimentos estudar para entrevistas e que o processo de recrutamento teria sido usado para obter detalhes sobre projetos sigilosos, componentes e métodos de desenvolvimento.
Um dos nomes centrais da disputa é Tang Yew Tan, que trabalhou na Apple por 24 anos e ocupou o cargo de vice-presidente de design de produtos para o iPhone e o Apple Watch antes de ingressar na OpenAI. Chang Liu, outro ex-funcionário citado no processo, teria trabalhado durante oito anos na Apple como engenheiro sênior de sistemas elétricos.
A Apple sustenta que as informações envolvidas na disputa incluem especificações técnicas, apresentações de engenharia, dados de projetos proprietários e detalhes sobre tecnologias ainda não lançadas.
Essas alegações fazem parte do processo judicial e ainda não representam uma conclusão definitiva de que houve roubo de segredos comerciais.
Leia mais:
- OpenAI nega retaliação após demitir três pesquisadores de segurança
- OpenAI e Anthropic querem controlar relatórios de segurança da IA
- OpenAI encontra gravador escondido em escritório e funcionário é preso
Disputa envolve futuro dispositivo de hardware da OpenAI
O processo ocorre enquanto a OpenAI trabalha no desenvolvimento de produtos físicos voltados ao consumidor. A empresa adquiriu a startup io, ligada ao ex-chefe de design da Apple Jony Ive, em negócio anunciado em 2025 por US$ 6,5 bilhões (cerca de R$ 35 bilhões).
A iniciativa ampliou as ambições da OpenAI no mercado de hardware, em momento no qual a companhia busca levar suas tecnologias de inteligência artificial (IA) para além dos computadores e smartphones tradicionais.
A Apple considera que informações confidenciais sobre seus projetos podem ter sido incorporadas aos esforços de desenvolvimento da OpenAI. A disputa, portanto, não se limita à saída de profissionais de uma empresa para outra: envolve a possibilidade de utilização de conhecimentos protegidos por segredo comercial em produtos concorrentes.
A OpenAI, por sua vez, contestou as acusações e classificou o processo como infundado. A empresa também argumenta que a ação seria uma tentativa da Apple de compensar dificuldades na disputa por talentos do setor tecnológico.
Até agora, não há decisão definitiva sobre a existência de apropriação indevida de informações nem sobre o eventual impacto dessas informações nos produtos desenvolvidos pela OpenAI.
Juiz rejeita parte dos pedidos da Apple
Embora tenha autorizado o acesso antecipado a documentos de contratação, mensagens e evidências digitais, Davila não atendeu a todas as solicitações da Apple.
O juiz rejeitou o pedido para acelerar a entrega de documentos relacionados às pesquisas e ao desenvolvimento da OpenAI em áreas como acabamentos metálicos, gerenciamento de energia e funcionamento de baterias para dispositivos de consumo.
Esses materiais poderão ser solicitados durante a fase regular de produção de provas, mas não terão o mesmo tratamento prioritário concedido aos registros de entrevistas e às demais evidências previstas na decisão.
O magistrado também deixou em aberto alguns pedidos mais amplos relacionados ao que a Apple chama de informações originadas na própria empresa. Segundo a decisão, a definição apresentada era vaga demais e poderia impor uma tarefa excessivamente onerosa à OpenAI. A Apple poderá tentar reformular o pedido para torná-lo mais específico.
A decisão sobre a produção antecipada de provas ocorre às vésperas de audiência marcada para discutir o pedido da OpenAI para encerrar o processo e a solicitação da Apple por uma liminar que impeça o uso dos segredos comerciais supostamente envolvidos.
A disputa judicial ainda está em andamento. Os documentos e depoimentos autorizados poderão ampliar o conjunto de evidências disponível às partes, mas não determinam, por si só, o resultado final do caso.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Confirmado el regreso de 'The X-Files' con una nueva serie del director de 'Black Panther' y 'Sinners'
articles.text:
The X-Files, la icónica serie de FOX, prepara su regreso con una nueva versión de la mano de Ryan Coogler. Hulu ha dado el visto bueno a una nueva producción creada por el director de Black Panther y Sinners, que funcionará como una suerte de reboot del título original.
La nueva serie de The X-Files no tendrá a David Duchovny y Gillian Anderson como protagonistas, pero tampoco pondrá a nuevos actores en la piel de los icónicos Fox Mulder y Dana Scully. Esto significa que el proyecto presentará a dos nuevos personajes originales interpretados por Himesh Patel y Danielle Deadwyler.
De acuerdo con la sinopsis oficial de la nueva serie de The X-Files, Patel y Deadwyler darán vida a dos agentes del FBI muy diferentes, pero con una química muy especial, que son asignados a una división que lleva mucho tiempo cerrada y que se encarga de casos relacionados con fenómenos no explicados.
A primera vista, es lógico pensar que la serie de Ryan Coogler intentará replicar la dinámica original de Mulder y Scully. Sin embargo, no está claro si la nueva serie de The X-Files será un reboot total o si tomará algunos elementos del título original y lo reimaginará para un público más actual. Tampoco se sabe si Duchovny y Anderson pueden llegar a tener alguna participación invitada o si se busca hacer borrón y cuenta nueva a nivel argumental.
The X-Files tendrá nueva serie en Hulu
Además de Patel y Deadwyler, se espera que la nueva serie de The X-Files incluya a otras varias figuras de renombre en su reparto. Tales los casos de Steve Buscemi, Ben Foster y Amy Madigan, por solo citar algunos. Ryan Coogler no solo oficia de productor ejecutivo del proyecto, sino que también ha estado a cargo de escribir el guion y de dirigir el episodio piloto. El cargo de showrunner está en manos de Jennifer Yale.
Coogler se ha reconocido fanático de The X-Files, por lo que este proyecto guarda un lugar especial en su portfolio. "Lo que creó Chris Carter es algo especial, y quisimos honrar todo aquello que hizo que la serie original conectara con tanta gente, al tiempo que encontrábamos nuestra propia manera de adentrarnos en ese mundo. Danielle e Himesh, junto con el resto del reparto, han aportado perspectivas e interpretaciones sumamente originales a estos personajes, y ver cómo todo ello ha cobrado forma ha sido una de las partes más gratificantes de la experiencia", remarcó el cineasta.
Todavía no se sabe cuándo se lanzará la nueva serie de The X-Files. Lo que sí es un hecho es que se trata de una producción de Hulu, de modo que a nivel internacional su distribución estará disponible a través de Disney+.

articles.title: The Download: open model trade-offs and geothermal power’s promise
articles.text:
The Download: open model trade-offs and geothermal power’s promise
Plus: A cyberattack overheated fridges at hundreds of French supermarkets.
This is today's edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what's going on in the world of technology.
Open models have real benefits. Do they outweigh the risks?
Anthropic recently released a report arguing that a powerful new model released by the Chinese company Z.ai, poses a major cyberattack risk. Its core concern was that it is freely available for anyone to download and modify.
The warning was the latest flashpoint in a debate over whether frontier AI models should be open or kept behind the doors of frontier labs. Safety advocates warn that open models can be misused by bad actors, while supporters argue they could prevent a handful of companies from controlling this powerful technology.
Here’s why the debate over open AI is more complicated than it seems.
—Grace Huckins
This story is part of MIT Technology Review Explains, our series untangling the complex, messy world of technology to help you understand what’s coming next. Read more from the series here.
10 Climate Tech Companies to Watch: Fervo Energy and its plan to streamline geothermal power
Fervo Energy is one of MIT Technology Review’s10 Climate Tech Companies to Watch 2026, available exclusively to subscribers.
Fervo Energy wants to expand geothermal power beyond the handful of places where it has traditionally been practical. The company uses horizontal drilling and hydraulic fracturing to open pathways through underground rock, potentially making geothermal development possible in far more places.
Now, Fervo is betting that AI’s power boom will help scale up enhanced geothermal energy. With a $2.2 billion public offering and an expanded agreement with Google, it plans to build larger plants and drive down costs. But can its approach work beyond Utah and Nevada? Read the full story to find out.
—Eshan Raul
Subscribers can now access the full 10 Climate Tech Companies to Watch, spanning everything from sustainable cement to shipping containers packed with old EV batteries.
The must-reads
I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology.
1 A cyberattack overheated fridges at hundreds of French supermarkets
Temperatures rose to 120°F, spoiling food and sparking fires. (BBC)
+ The attack has sparked alarm about cyber threats to food security. (FT $)
+ It joins a recent wave of cyberattacks and cybercrimes. (CNBC)
+ AI is exacerbating the threats. (MIT Technology Review)
2 Meta has launched a bunch of new AI models
It hopes the models, built for complex, multi-step tasks, will rival OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s.(BI)
+ They scored well on tests of reasoning, writing, and coding. (NYT $)
+ Mark Zuckerberg says they bring Meta to the “frontier” of AI. (FT $)
+ And will soon power the Muse agent. (Verge)
3 Anthropic warns that AI models may soon self-replicate across devices
Without even requiring access to data centers. (Reuters $)
+ It says models could spread through smart TVs and appliances. (CNBC)
+ We’re putting too much faith in AI saying no. (MIT Technology Review)
4 Police have a new AI tool that finds homes from interior photos
It can match single pictures to Airbnb and Zillow listings. (404 Media)
+ Police-tech giant Flock is tightening its rules. (MIT Technology Review)
5 The world’s first utility-scale enhanced geothermal plant is online
Fervo Energy’s Utah facility will supply carbon-free electricity. (IEEE)
+ AI is uncovering hidden geothermal resources. (MIT Technology Review)
6 Did drone strikes on Yandex data centres blitz Russian bots?
Zelenskyy claims the attacks quietened Kremlin-funded social media accounts. (Euronews) 
+ But troll farm experts aren’t convinced. (Verge)
7 NASA’s Perseverance rover has set a Mars driving record
It’s covered 28 miles since landing in 2021. (Reuters $)
+ The rover passed Opportunity after detouring to study ancient rocks. (NYT $)
8 Elon Musk has become the 2026 midterms’ biggest known donor
He gave $158 million to a Republican Senate super PAC. (AP News)
9 Anduril and Palantir founders have backed execution livestreams
Palmer Luckey and Joe Lonsdale support Pete Hegseth’s plan. (Mother Jones)
10 A spacecraft has traced how a mysterious solar switchback formed
The Solar Orbiter’s discovery could improve space weather forecasts. (Gizmodo)
Quote of the day
“Many AI researchers have started smoking as a way of signaling to other researchers how much they believe in AI.”
—Palantir CTO Shyam Sankar tells CBS News that Silicon Valley’s “social delusion” has convinced researchers to smoke because they expect AI to cure cancer.
One more thing
A brain implant changed her life. Then it was removed against her will.
Sticking an electrode inside a person’s brain can do more than treat a disease. Take the case of Rita Leggett, an Australian woman whose experimental brain implant changed her sense of agency and self. She told researchers that she “became one” with her device.
She was devastated when, two years later, she was told she had to remove the implant because the company that made it had gone bust.
Her case highlights the need for a new category of legal protection: neuro rights. Explore how they could be protected.

articles.title: Apple’s HomeView ad is confusing to everyone except parents
articles.text:
Apple’s ad introducing its new HomeView smart display is a little unusual. It’s fast-paced and unruly, depicting a family of five as they rush through the morning routine. There’s yelling and mess, misplaced keys and discarded eggshells. Apple’s typical vibe is clean, simple, orderly; this commercial is chaos.
Apple’s HomeView ad is confusing to everyone except parents
The chaos is surprisingly real for an Apple commercial.
But the spot has parents — those with teen children in particular — feeling seen.
I’ll admit that it stressed me out the first time I watched it, too. Mornings getting my five-year-old out the door are a special breed of chaos, and usually culminate in us playing whatever ad-libbed game will get him to put his shoes on. But it’s not quite as intense as this one, which features dad making French toast, mom losing and finding keys in her pocket, a proxy battle over the thermostat, a teenage boy helping himself to whipped cream from a can, and an unexpected video call. There’s also a microdrama about the daughter’s ride to school with a boyfriend nobody knew about that ends with everyone gathered around the HomeView watching the security camera feed of the two of them departing the porch. It’s a lot for just over three minutes of screentime.
If I know anything, though, I know to trust my colleague Jen Tuohy, senior reviewer and parent to two teens, on matters of the home. Her take? “The most unrealistic part of the video is that no one is holding an iPhone.”
Other parents of teens shared similar reactions on Threads. When tech analyst Benedict Evans posted about the ad feeling stressful and confusing, CNET editor at large Bridget Carey chimed in to defend it, saying “It was exactly what my morning is like and it was the most real ad I’ve ever seen from Apple.” Others agreed, saying it “accurately captured” real life and that it “hit home,” no pun intended, at least I think.
Even if Apple didn’t need to do much to heighten the stakes of a family getting out the door, there is of course plenty of sleight of hand at work when it comes to making the HomeView appear so essential. The family has seemingly drilled a hole directly into the middle of their kitchen island to accommodate the charging cable, for one. And what sibling is going to check a text message from a secret boyfriend on the communal kitchen screen with their brother sitting at arm’s length? I don’t believe any teenager trusts Apple’s privacy features that far.
The confusion about the commercial is understandable. This is a far cry from the quiet luxury lifestyle everyone seems to enjoy in Apple’s Vision Pro ads. There’s also Evans’ observation that the HomeView doesn’t really solve any of the problems that come up throughout the course of the video. In the case of a spontaneous FaceTime call from the grandparents, the screen in the middle of the kitchen seems to make things worse.
But maybe morning chaos isn’t the problem that’s being solved. If the alternative is five people all interacting with their own phones, then the HomeView presents a different picture where everyone gets the essential information they need from one shared screen and stays more present.
A screen that makes you be more present is a lovely idea, but the real test will come when it’s in real households. Is the HomeView going to be enough to convince families to put their personal devices down? Will everyone just ignore it and keep scrolling on their own iPhones? These are questions worth answering before you start drilling holes in your kitchen island! In any case, an ungovernable morning routine is probably a feature of a busy household, not a bug. Just ask a parent.

articles.title: Le dernier tir de SpaceX a fait flotter une immense méduse lumineuse dans le ciel, voici les photos les plus incroyables
articles.text:
Le 13 octobre 2026, une « méduse spatiale » a envahi les réseaux sociaux après un décollage depuis Cap Canaveral de la Falcon 9 de SpaceX (mission CRS‑35).
Des photographes ont même immortalisé la « méduse » et le passage lumineux de l'ISS sur une même image.
La Nasa explique que ce type de nuage provient des gaz d'échappement — principalement vapeur d'eau et dioxyde de carbone — éclairés par le Soleil levant à haute altitude, créant cette illusion céleste.
Le 13 octobre 2026, une « méduse spatiale » a envahi les réseaux sociaux après un décollage depuis Cap Canaveral de la Falcon 9 de SpaceX (mission CRS‑35).
Des photographes ont même immortalisé la « méduse » et le passage lumineux de l'ISS sur une même image.
La Nasa explique que ce type de nuage provient des gaz d'échappement — principalement vapeur d'eau et dioxyde de carbone — éclairés par le Soleil levant à haute altitude, créant cette illusion céleste.
De superbes images d’une « méduse spatiale » aperçue aux États-Unis sont diffusées ce 13 octobre 2026. Ce phénomène lumineux est dû au décollage d’une fusée Falcon 9 de SpaceX, le matin même en Floride.
En parcourant les réseaux sociaux ce mardi 13 octobre 2026, vous avez peut-être croisé une étrange « méduse spatiale », observée dans le ciel des États-Unis. Des images spectaculaires de ce phénomène sont diffusées par des photographes et passionnés d’astronomie.
Les photos montrent une forme lumineuse, teintée de bleu et de doré, se détachant sur le ciel sombre. À l’origine de cette créature céleste éphémère, un événement bien tangible : un lancement de fusée.
« Méduse spatiale » et ISS réunies : le jackpot pour ces photographes
Ce mardi 13 octobre, SpaceX lançait en effet une fusée Falcon 9 dans l’espace. Son décollage a eu lieu à la mi-journée (pour nous, en France métropolitaine). Il s’agissait de la mission CRS-35, dédiée au ravitaillement de la Station spatiale internationale (ISS) à l’aide d’une capsule Dragon. Le lanceur est parti de la Floride, depuis la base de Cap Canaveral.
Certains photographes ont réussi à saisir sur la même image la « méduse » et l’ISS en train de traverser le ciel – on reconnaît le passage de la station spatiale à une ligne droite très lumineuse, qui ne peut pas être confondue avec une étoile filante.
La formation de la « méduse spatiale » a même été photographiée par SpaceX, juste après ce décollage.
Ce n’est pas la première fois qu’un lancement de SpaceX donne lieu à une « méduse spatiale ». En mars 2026, le décollage d’une autre Falcon 9, qui lançait des satellites Starlink dans l’espace, avait provoqué la formation de ce phénomène.
Comment se forme cet étrange nuage lors du décollage d’une fusée SpaceX ?
La fusée a décollé à 6h33 heure locale, peu avant le lever du Soleil sur la Floride. Une situation propice à la formation d’une « méduse spatiale ». Comme l’explique la Nasa, lorsque le panache qui s’échappe de la fusée lors du décollage se trouve assez haut dans le ciel, il peut être éclairé par la lumière du Soleil levant. Le photographe, lui, est encore dans l’obscurité.
Peu avant le décollage de la Falcon 9 ce 13 octobre, la possibilité que le phénomène survienne avait été anticipée par des photographes et passionnés d’astronomie, qui prévoyaient que la fusée entrerait dans la lumière du Soleil 3 minutes et 20 secondes après le décollage.
« Cette combinaison d’ombre et de lumière, observable à l’aube ou au crépuscule, donne à ces gaz d’échappement, composés principalement de vapeur d’eau et de dioxyde de carbone, l’apparence d’un nuage lumineux », selon la Nasa. Une forme qui donne l’impression de descendre, « car la fusée suit la courbure de la Terre dans son trajet vers l’espace ».

articles.title: SA’s Kuunda completes $5m secondary share sale led by E4E Africa - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
South African digital lending infrastructure startup Kuunda has completed a US$5 million secondary share sale led by E4E Africa, returning capital to early investors while bringing the investment firm on board as a larger long-term shareholder.
Established in 2018, Kuunda is a B2B digital lending-as-a-service company that provides tailored liquidity solutions built through meaningful collaborative partnerships. By partnering with mobile money operators, POS network providers, e-commerce players and banks, Kuunda embeds credit products into existing digital platforms, using data-driven credit scoring to provide productive financing to mobile money agents, merchants, and consumers in emerging markets.
Disrupt Africa reported in October last year that the startup had raised a US$7.5 million pre-Series A round of funding, with E4E Africa among the participants alongside the likes of Portugal Gateway Fund, Seedstars Africa Ventures, 4Di Capital, Accion Ventures, and Nedbank.
Growth has continued since. Kuunda’s infrastructure has now disbursed more than 870 million loans, delivering over US$4.4 billion in credit to 14.6 million agents, merchants and consumers. The company is currently live in five markets, with launches planned in a further seven.
The new transaction sees E4E Africa expand its stake in the business, with existing investors Accion Ventures, Portugal Gateway Fund and Seedstars Africa Ventures also increasing their positions. Kuunda says the deal gives early backers a meaningful return, and shows African fintech companies can generate liquidity for shareholders well before an IPO or acquisition.
“This is an important milestone for Kuunda and our investors,” said Andrew Milne, Kuunda’s CEO. “Delivering a successful secondary at this stage reflects the strength of the business we’ve built – profitable, scalable lending infrastructure serving millions of people across Africa. We’re grateful to our early backers and excited to grow with a strong, aligned shareholder base.”
Bas Hochstenbach, managing partner at E4E Africa, said Kuunda was using technology, distribution and banking partnerships to deliver essential financial services where traditional institutions could not reach.
“Kuunda is an exceptional company, building a very healthy and fast-growing business while offering much needed products at fair prices to African small businesses and consumers,” he said.

articles.title: 10 Milliarden Jahre altes Radiosignal erreicht die Erde – Teleskope finden den Ursprung
articles.text:
10 Milliarden Jahre unterwegs: James-Webb-Teleskop findet den Ursprung eines uralten Radiosignals
Ein internationales Forschungsteam hat das bislang am weitesten entfernte Radiosignal der Astronomiegeschichte aufgezeichnet. Der als Fast Radio Burst bekannte Ausbruch reiste mehr als zehn Milliarden Jahre durch das Weltall, bevor er die Erde erreichte und von den Instrumenten der Wissenschaftler:innen verarbeitet werden konnte.
Wie in einer im Wissenschaftsmagazin Science veröffentlichten Studie zu lesen ist, entstand das Signal mit der Bezeichnung FRB 20240304B, als das Universum erst etwa drei Milliarden Jahre alt war. Die initiale Aufzeichnung gelang zunächst mit dem Radioteleskop MeerKAT in der südafrikanischen Provinz Nordkap, das für derartige Himmelsdurchmusterungen konstruiert wurde.
James-Webb-Teleskop lokalisiert den Ursprung
Um den Ursprungsort zu bestimmen, nutzten die Astronom:innen im Nachgang das James-Webb-Weltraumteleskop der US-Raumfahrtbehörde Nasa. Dessen Infrarotinstrumente zeigten bei der Analyse, dass der Ausbruch aus einer sehr kleinen Galaxie stammt, die aktuell in hoher Geschwindigkeit neue Sterne bildet.
Diese Galaxie weist im direkten Vergleich zu unserer Milchstraße nur einen geringen Anteil an schweren Elementen auf. Der Astronom Themiya Nanayakkara von der Universität Sydney im australischen Bundesstaat New South Wales erklärte gegenüber The Guardian, dass zum Zeitpunkt der Signalentstehung weder die Erde noch die Sonne existierten.
Magnetare als wahrscheinliche Quelle der Ausbrüche
Fast Radio Bursts sind kurze Radiowellen-Ausbrüche, die in wenigen Millisekunden so viel Energie freisetzen wie unsere Sonne in mehreren Monaten oder Jahren. Seit ihrer ersten Entdeckung im Jahr 2007, als der US-Astrophysiker Duncan Lorimer einen solchen Ausbruch in alten Archivdaten der Magellanschen Wolken fand, wird in der Astronomie über die physikalische Ursache diskutiert.
Die Signale lassen sich identifizieren, weil sie auf ihrem Weg durch den intergalaktischen Raum verschiedene Frequenzen unterschiedlich schnell transportieren. Niedrigere Radiofrequenzen werden durch ionisiertes Plasma im Weltraum stärker gebremst als hohe Frequenzen, wodurch das Signal verzerrt auf der Erde eintrifft und sich die zurückgelegte Distanz berechnen lässt.
Eine in der Forschungsgemeinschaft gängige Theorie besagt, dass sogenannte Magnetare für diese Radioausbrüche verantwortlich sind. Dabei handelt es sich um dichte Neutronensterne mit einem starken Magnetfeld, die in der Regel als Überrest einer Supernova-Explosion entstehen.
Kosmische Materie mit Radiosignalen berechnen
Für die wissenschaftliche Analyse sind diese Signale auch unabhängig von ihrer Entstehung wertvoll, da Fast Radio Bursts durch die mikroskopischen Partikel beeinflusst werden, die sie auf ihrem Weg durch das All durchqueren. Der Astrophysiker Matthew Bailes von der Swinburne Universität im australischen Bundesstaat Victoria beschreibt die Signale daher als mechanische Methode, um die Atome im Universum auf großen Distanzen zu zählen.
Laut der Astrophysikerin Sara Webb, die ebenfalls an der Swinburne Universität tätig ist, funktionieren die Ausbrüche wie eine Sichtlinien-Zählung für die Materie, die sie auf dem Weg zur Erde passieren müssen. Seit der ersten Entdeckung im Jahr 2007 wurden mehr als 10.000 Fast Radio Bursts registriert, wobei sich einige kontinuierlich wiederholen und andere lediglich als einmaliges Ereignis auftreten.
Ob der nun lokalisierte Ausbruch FRB 20240304B in der näheren Zukunft weitere Signale in Richtung unseres Sonnensystems senden wird, müssen nachfolgende astronomische Beobachtungen zeigen. Bis dahin werten die Astronom:innen die bisherigen und gespeicherten Datenströme systematisch aus, um Rückschlüsse auf die Verteilung der Materie im frühen Universum zu ziehen.

articles.title: Un clavier pour travailler sur plusieurs appareils : le Logitech MX Keys S à moins de 80€ chez Amazon
articles.text:
Le clavier Logitech MX Keys S associe une frappe discrète à un rétroéclairage automatique, ainsi qu’à la capacité à se connecter à trois appareils en même temps. Amazon le propose à 79,99 € au lieu de 129,99 €.
Pour les télétravailleurs ou les freelances, un clavier Bluetooth multiappareil peut s’avérer idéal. C’est ce que propose le clavier Logitech MX Keys S à 79,99 € chez Amazon : il est fin, rétroéclairé et, dans cette version en promotion, il est accompagné d’un repose-poignets. Ce clavier AZERTY avec pavé numérique intégré peut également être connecté à trois appareils en simultané.
Le clavier sans fil Logitech MX Keys S AZERTY est disponible à 79,99 € au lieu de 129,99 € chez Amazon.
Pourquoi choisir le Logitech MX Keys S ?
- Pour son confort de frappe : les touches plates et concaves offrent une saisie discrète et très confortable.
- Pour sa connexion à trois appareils : les touches Easy-Switch permettent de passer d’un ordinateur professionnel à un smartphone ou à une tablette.
- Pour son rétroéclairage : les touches s’illuminent à l’approche des mains et leur luminosité s’adapte à l’éclairage ambiant.
Un clavier complet pour le bureau et le télétravail
Dans notre test du Logitech MX Keys S, noté 9/10, nous avons apprécié sa frappe fluide et la qualité de sa fabrication. Le pavé numérique est très utile pour utiliser un tableau ou faire de la comptabilité. Pour la connexion sans fil, deux choix s’offrent à vous : le Bluetooth ou le récepteur USB Logi Bolt fourni. Sur Windows et macOS, le logiciel Logi Options+ permet de personnaliser certains raccourcis et d’automatiser des tâches répétitives via les Smart Actions. Enfin, l’autonomie du clavier monte jusqu’à dix jours avec rétroéclairage ou cinq mois lorsqu’il est désactivé. La batterie se recharge simplement en USB-C.
Un format pas aussi compact qu’on pourrait le penser
Le Logitech MX Keys S est un clavier sans fil très pratique pour l’associer à plusieurs appareils en même temps. Mais il faut tout de même souligner que ses 43 cm de long et son poids de 810 grammes le rendent moins facile à transporter que l’on pourrait le croire de prime abord. C’est un point à prendre en considération pour les travailleurs nomades.
✅ Les points forts
- Frappe fluide et discrète.
- Bascule entre trois appareils.
- Rétroéclairage automatique et récepteur Logi Bolt inclus.
❌ Les limites
- Format encombrant pour les petits bureaux.
- Logiciel obligatoire pour configurer certaines fonctionnalités.
Vendu et expédié par Amazon, le clavier sans fil Logitech MX Keys S est en stock à 79,99 € accompagné de son repose-poignets.
Pour les télétravailleurs, les rédacteurs et les utilisateurs qui jonglent entre plusieurs machines, le clavier Logitech MX Keys S se présente comme un choix adapté.
Néanmoins, les amateurs de touches mécaniques ou de formats compacts feraient mieux de passer leur chemin afin d’opter pour un clavier plus adapté à leurs exigences.

articles.title: Pramatra Space building chip-based quantum security for space & ground networks
articles.text:
Pramatra Space is building chip-based quantum security for space and ground networks
Bengaluru startup Pramatra Space plans to demonstrate its technology in space in 2027, ahead of its first mission in 2028, while exploring applications in telecom, drones, and data centres.
Bengaluru-based Pramatra Space is building on the quantum-security technology it has been developing since 2023. The startup has completed a third tape-out of its quantum key distribution (QKD) chip, filed its final patent, and is seeing growing interest in using the technology for terrestrial applications.
Founder and CEO Richa Hukumchand says that the 11-member startup plans to raise a funding round soon. She also says Pramatra's QKD chip has progressed from two tape-outs at the time of the previous update to three.
"Our QKD chip has progressed from two tape-outs to three now, and our latest chips are being tested. We expect the results within the next 15–20 days," she says.
The company has also made progress on its intellectual property. Pramatra, which previously held a provisional patent, has now filed the final patent. The specification is complete and examination is under way.
Taking quantum security beyond satellites
Pramatra's core technology combines QKD with post-quantum cryptography (PQC). While QKD uses quantum physics to distribute encryption keys, PQC uses mathematical algorithms designed to withstand attacks from quantum computers.
Hukumchand says feedback from the defence sector prompted the company to take a hybrid approach.
"For holistic security, including authentication, we got feedback from defence that they want hybrid PQC and QKD," she says. "For encryption, you can use QKD, but for authentication we need an additional layer of PQC."
The spacetech startup is also developing a software layer to orchestrate the different security hardware it deploys. Its data-centre product remains in development, while the company is also seeing demand for terrestrial free-space applications.
Hukumchand says the compact nature of its chip-based technology has led to discussions around applications such as secure communication between telecom towers, and between drones and ground stations.
"Pilot discussions are going on to see if it can be used for terrestrial operations," she says.
Pramatra is also working with Japanese ground-station company Infostellar Inc to explore additional optical ground stations and define requirements for last-mile security. Hukumchand says the startup has made progress on its "hybrid agile methodology" and on integrating PQC into its broader quantum-security offering.
Building a space-to-ground security stack
Pramatra's original roadmap centred on satellite-based QKD, with its technology designed to sit inside space payloads and connect secure communications infrastructure on the ground.
The startup is currently working with about three satellite companies and plans its first in-space demonstration of the product in 2027. It is targeting its first mission with the product in 2028.
Hukumchand says Pramatra sees its ability to work across both satellite and terrestrial infrastructure as an advantage. Its competition in space remains global, with Hukumchand naming qtlabs and IonQ among its competitors.
Pramatra was also selected for Bharat Innovates, a government-backed programme involving 120 deeptech companies. IISc has validated the company's results and its hypothesis around using chip-based technology for space-based QKD.
Pramatra Space is part of YourStory's Tech30 cohort—a showcase of India's most promising startups of 2026, unveiled at TechSparks Bengaluru.
Edited by Teja Lele

articles.title: The agent did the work. The audit log couldn’t say who asked.
articles.text:
The agent did the work. The audit log couldn’t say who asked.
More than 20 percent of the MCP-related access policies that Shawn Petty’s team reviewed across customer and prospect environments were broken or missing, according to a recent account published in The New Stack. In most cases, the MCP server ran on someone’s personal token rather than a service account.
At 12 p.m. Eastern/9 a.m. Pacific on Tuesday, October 27, Petty, Chief Customer Officer at CloudBolt, and Mike Bombard, Director of Global Pre-Sales Engineering at CloudBolt, will join The New Stack host Viktor Farcic for a live demo of how to trace an agent’s actions back to the person responsible for them.
You have successfully registered for the webinar.
The problem, though, usually shows up after an incident: That personal token puts an engineer’s name into the audit trail for everything the agent did. Meanwhile, a shared service account puts the account’s name there instead. In both cases, the audit trail isn’t able to identify who precisely asked the agent to do the work or who approved the access it used.
Access that goes through a request, approval, and grant in the identity provider is provisioned, and the identity provider records it. Access that an agent picks up along the way is emergent: A role inherited from the service that launched it, or a developer’s own token lent out to finish a task. The identity provider holds no record of those grants, so when an agent touches something it shouldn’t, you can’t trace it back.
In this live conversation, the CloudBolt team will explain how agents end up with access nobody approved, then show how to trace that access back to a person with CloudBolt: linking agent activity to your existing identity provider, setting limits on what an agent can touch, and reading the audit trail that results.
Live attendees can ask these experts questions in real time. Register today to join us!
You’ll learn:
- How to tie agent activity back to your existing identity provider instead of building a parallel system
- Which infrastructure actions an agent should be allowed to take without a human signing off
- What a usable audit trail for agent behavior contains, and how to keep one without slowing teams down
- A live trace of one agent’s credentials and actions, from the task it ran to the person responsible

articles.title: Avec ou sans Huawei ? Les SUV électriques chinois d’Aito arrivent enfin en Europe, mais plusieurs mystères demeurent — Frandroid
articles.text:
Autant certaines marques chinoises arrivent en Europe sans trop crier gare, autant d’autres préfèrent prendre leur temps. C’est par exemple le cas d’Aito, qu’on a d’abord vu à Paris en 2024, avant de les recroiser à Munich en 2025, les deux fois avec des promesses pour le moins floues.
Disons donc que la conférence de presse de la marque chinoise au Mondial de l’Auto de 2026 était donc attendue, et notre attente a enfin été récompensée : Aito arrivera bien en Europe à l’automne 2027. L’occasion de se pencher sur cette marque chinoise et ses SUV, aux racines bien plus tech qu’il n’y paraît.
Une marque cofondée avec Huawei…
Derrière Aito ne se cache pas une, mais deux marques. Côté auto, il y a Seres, une marque chinoise fondée en 1986 ; c’est elle qui s’occupe de l’ingénierie, de la plateforme technique, du développement, de la production et de la distribution.
À ceci, il faut ajouter Huawei, qui fournit l’OS des écrans (HarmonyOS), ainsi que les aides à la conduite (système Qiankun). Un partenariat qui peut surprendre en Europe, mais dont Aito est loin d’être le seul exemple.
Il faut ici rappeler que Huawei s’est créé un empire discret dans l’industrie automobile chinoise. À l’inverse de Xiaomi, qui s’est lancé dans l’automobile avec sa propre marque, Huawei a préféré développer toute une galaxie de coentreprises, regroupées sous le terme ombrelle HIMA (Harmony Intelligent Mobility Alliance).
Outre Aito, cofondée avec Seres, on peut également retrouver Luxeed (avec Chery), Stelato (avec BAIC), Maextro (avec JAC) et SAIC (avec… SAIC).
…privée de son atout phare en Europe
Seul problème : cet écosystème et cette intégration avec Huawei ne sont valables qu’en Chine – les marchés extérieurs sont privés des équipements du géant de la tech, notamment pour des raisons de réglementation. Il est d’ailleurs intéressant que Huawei n’apparaisse jamais dans les communications européennes d’Aito.
À la place, Seres redéveloppe un infodivertissement complet, que nous n’aurons pas pu découvrir : les voitures présentées sur le stand étaient équipées d’HarmonyOS ; pour les aides à la conduite, Aito a annoncé s’entourer de partenaires locaux (comme Bosch) pour offrir un système aux goûts des Européens.
Encore beaucoup de mystères
Si la conférence de presse a été l’occasion d’apprendre qu’Aito arriverait en Europe dans un an, à l’automne 2027, nous avons été loin d’avoir eu toutes les informations.
Si les dirigeants ont insisté sur le travail en cours pour se conformer à toutes les régulations, sans oublier les essais pour les calibrations et les réglages des voitures et de leurs systèmes pour se conformer aux goûts européens, aucune information n’a été communiquée sur les pays retenus, sans oublier les stratégies de développement, les réseaux de distribution… ou même les voitures qui feront le voyage.
Toujours est-il que l’intégralité de la gamme chinoise était présente, à savoir les Aito 6, 7, 8 et 9. Tous des SUV électriques ou à prolongateur d’autonomie, qui visent clairement le premium avec une présentation clinquante et des équipements ultra high-tech.
Le « plus européen », car le moins grand, c’est sans nul doute l’Aito 6 – entendons-nous bien, il s’agit tout de même d’un SUV de 4,96 m de long, soit l’équivalent d’un BMW iX5 ou d’un Volvo EX90. Il existe en prolongateur d’autonomie (345 kW / 470 ch) ou en 100 % électrique (340 kW/462 ch), sans mention d’autonomie ou de vitesse de recharge.
Au-delà, on bascule dans une autre dimension. L’Aito 7 mesure 5,08 m de long et peut accueillir six passagers (deux par rangée) dans un luxe qui commence à faire parler de lui ; l’Aito 8, c’est 5,19 m de long, avec des phares « Nebula » (comprendre : avec des motifs étoilés) et un écran pour les passagers arrière de 9,2 pouces.
Enfin, l’Aito 9 ne se refuse rien avec ses 5,28 m de long, ses projecteurs avant et arrière aux motifs personnalisables, ses kilos de chrome et ses peintures biton très Maybach dans l’âme.
    Pour aller plus loin
On a roulé en Chine avec l’Aito M8 : le SUV de Huawei qui cartonne va-t-il séduire l’Europe ?
            
En configuration 5 places, le luxe à l’arrière est effarant, d’autant plus qu’un vidéoprojecteur prend place dans le plafonnier pour projeter ses vidéos sur une toile descendant du toit. La suspension active est branchée à la batterie 800 volts, de quoi réussir le « test du champagne » où les flûtes posées en équilibre sur le plateau ne s’effondrent pas lors de passages de dos d’âne.
Bref, des SUV très haut de gamme, qui s’attaquent donc à un marché aussi compliqué qu’exigu, vendu depuis des années aux marques allemandes et suédoises. Il reste encore un an à Aito pour peaufiner son plan d’attaque afin d’espérer percer dans ce segment si concurrentiel. On leur souhaite bonne chance.
