articles.title: Small AI Models Could Soon Self-Replicate on IoT Devices, Anthropic Warns
articles.text:
Small AI models may be only months away from being able to self-replicate across commercial IoT devices, without needing a data center, according to research from Anthropic’s Frontier Red Team.
The study looks at AI worms that run their own model directly on the devices they compromise. Such malware would be hard to shut down because it has no central point to switch off, though it would likely spread slowly.
The researchers bought 15 off-brand Android-based TV boxes for about $55 each. A 26-billion-parameter open-weight model split across them ran at 0.39 tokens per second.
Rather than exploitation, which prior studies have already examined, the team focused on whether models could get AI inference running on unfamiliar hardware. A 9-billion-parameter model did so on eight of the nine hardware types tested.
The researchers then tested the full replication cycle on a closed network of eight emulated Android devices, with the hacking step deliberately kept trivial. Of the open-weight models tested, only GLM-5.2 completed it, reaching all eight devices in four of five runs.
Anthropic considers the results an upper bound for real-world success, but notes that past IoT botnets such as Mirai spread simply by trying default manufacturer credentials.
Models with 30 billion parameters or fewer can already complete many of the individual steps but make mistakes when chaining them together. If they keep improving at their historical rate, Anthropic expects them to reach GLM-5.2’s level by the end of 2026.
“Small weight-based replicators may be possible soon after,” the company says.
Anthropic also looked at a botnet as large as Kimwolf, which infected more than two million devices. If every 15 TV boxes ran one copy of the 26-billion-parameter model, such a botnet would host roughly 133,000 copies. Their combined compute would be worth at most about 40 Nvidia H100 GPUs, and each replication would take more than a day.
[ Read: AI Turns Familiar Cyberattacks Into a Race Against Time ]
Unlike traditional botnets built for specific devices, an AI worm could work out unfamiliar hardware on its own, Anthropic says. Defenders, however, still have some advantages.
Large model transfers and sustained traffic between devices that don’t normally communicate would stand out in ISP monitoring. In addition, moving manufacturers to more secure defaults, such as eliminating default passwords, would also shrink the target pool.
There is no full rogue replicator yet, Anthropic says, but models are getting better at each step in the chain and at passing what they learn on to their copies.

articles.title: Europe cannot be sovereign without control of its own AI | EU-Startups
articles.text:
AI is steadily being integrated further into the systems and workflows that run many European businesses. What was once a tool for analysing information and assisting employees with basic administrative tasks, is now an integral part of how many of these businesses operate.
The problem with Europe’s growing dependence on AI, is that much of the technology they are dependent upon comes from elsewhere.
The companies producing the most sophisticated AI models and supporting infrastructure are concentrated heavily in the US and China, giving them huge influence over the technology that is becoming so important to the global economy. That influence is becoming more significant as these nations continue to develop competing AI ecosystems, with their rivalry increasingly tied to their wider geopolitical interests.
Recent reports suggest that the US is preparing to tell dozens of countries to choose between rival US and China-led AI ecosystems, and China last week called for countries to respect their “digital sovereignty”. AI sovereignty is no longer an abstract debate. We are watching AI divide along geopolitical lines in real time, and Europe is now at risk of becoming a customer of whichever superpower controls the intelligence it relies upon.
Europe needs choice, not complete self-sufficiency
The vulnerability this presents was arguably already demonstrated in June, when the US ordered Anthropic to restrict foreign nationals’ access to its most advanced AI models, prompting European concern about how reliant businesses and governments could become on American frontier AI.
For Europe, the question is how much autonomy will it have to make its own decisions as this divide widens?
Europe should be able to use the best models available, wherever they might be developed, but it cannot build its economy on imported AI that might get cut off.
This is not to say that Europe needs to be completely self-sufficient in AI, but it needs enough choice to switch suppliers and maintain viable alternatives.
That choice becomes more important as AI continues to become embedded into the everyday running of businesses.
In July, The European Commission launched a call for up to seven AI Gigafactories, backed by up to €10 billion in EU and national funding and intended to unlock at least €20 billion in private investment.
However, the question of sovereignty goes beyond the models themselves, it also extends to the knowledge businesses create through AI.
Businesses risk renting back their own knowledge
Every time an employee uses AI, they are writing down how their work gets done, often for the first time. The companies that hold onto that knowledge can use it to fuel their AI transformation. But many risk handing it to their vendors, teaching them how to commoditise their businesses, and will end up renting back their own know-how.
The consequences of this extend beyond technology. AI will shape which companies become most productive and which industries adapt quickest. If European companies are importing these capabilities from foreign entities, the value created will likely flow outside of Europe, also.
This creates a different type of dependency. A business might be able to switch model or supplier, but separating from a system that has spent years learning its processes and organisational knowledge is much more difficult. The longer a business spends building its operations around external AI providers, the harder it will be to separate themselves from it.
For startups and scale-ups, this is particularly important. Their advantage often lies in their specialist knowledge, their understanding of a problem and the distinctive way they carry out their work. If that knowledge becomes trapped within an external platform, they risk giving away part of what makes the business valuable.
This does not mean that European businesses need to stop using foreign AI. This is unrealistic, and also poses the threat of Europe falling further behind.
Europe’s opportunity is applied AI
Europe’s opportunity instead lies in building on top of these models and turning them into systems that are designed around the needs of its own businesses. This is where European businesses can build intellectual property and competitive advantage around AI, even if the technology is developed elsewhere.
The opportunity is also in building the infrastructure that lets businesses use different models, without rebuilding their systems each time the market changes. This flexibility can help businesses avoid vendor dependency and maintain greater control over how they use AI.
This applied layer is where AI is connected to a company’s systems and put to work. It is also where businesses can govern what agents are allowed to do, monitor their actions, test their performance and investigate when something goes wrong. Europe may not lead every part of the race to build the largest model, but it can lead in making AI safe, accountable and useful for the companies deploying it.
Europe has a large industrial base, strong expertise across sectors, and businesses that understand their own processes better than any general-purpose model ever could.
Sovereignty means control and continuity: control over what AI agents can do, ownership of the workflows and knowledge they create, and the freedom to choose or change the underlying technology.
Europe has the talent, industry and trust to become a genuine power in AI, but that does not mean it has to be a distant third participant.
It must be the counterbalance to this race: deploy its talent and expertise into the applied layer, and build systems that are safe, sovereign and equitable by design, for the benefit of everyone, not just those in Europe.
We need AI that works for us, not the other way around. Building a sovereign applied AI layer that can be deployed in good faith, creating productivity and lasting values for businesses across the globe, is Europe’s decisive opportunity in this race.

articles.title: Bitcoin: cuál es su precio este día
articles.text:
El bitcoin fue la primera criptomoneda que salió al mercado. Ideada por Satoshi Nakamoto en 2008, esta divisa digital promovía un ideal libertario y buscaba poner en jaque a las instituciones monetarias y financieras tradicionales luego de la crisis financiera mundial que se vivió ese año.
La victoria electoral de Donald Trump significó un movimiento positivo para las principales criptomonedas del mercado. A finales de 2024, bitcoin registró un nuevo máximo histórico que logró superar los 107.000 dólares por unidad, después de que el presidente estadounidense reiteró su idea de crear una reserva estratégica de la criptodivisa en Estados Unidos.
Las divisas digitales serán un foco de atención durante este año, las iniciativas del presidente de Estados Unidos y el desarrollo de nuevos modelos de inteligencia artificial fungirán un papel importante en la cotización de estos activos. Después del lanzamiento del nuevo modelo de IA chino DeepSeek, BTC y otras criptos cayeron en la mayoría de los mercados de valores.
Cotización de la criptomoneda Bitcoin
El precio de la criptomoneda bitcoin para este día a las 14:00 horas (UTC) es de 83287.78 dólares. Esto quiere decir que la moneda digital tuvo un cambio de 0.75% en el último día, así como un movimiento de 0.0% en la última hora.
Por su nivel de capitalización, esta moneda digital ocupa la posición #1 entre las más populares.
Bitcoin alcanzó su máximo histórico
En marzo del año pasado el bitcoin ha logrado un nuevo máximo histórico, superando los valores anteriores y reafirmándose como la criptomoneda más importante en el mercado, acercándose a los 73 mil dólares. Este récord se obtuvo en medio de un flujo sin precedentes de inversiones hacia las criptomonedas, un acontecimiento notable para el sector financiero digital.
El aumento en el valor de bitcoin ocurre en un contexto donde hay un entrante masivo de capital hacia las criptomonedas, lo que indica un creciente interés y confianza de los inversores en estos activos. La subida del precio beneficia no solo a bitcoin sino que también tiene un impacto positivo en el mercado de las criptomonedas en general, favoreciendo una mayor estabilidad y visibilidad, de acuerdo a un análisis de Bloomberg.
Expertos financiaron este aumento a diferentes factores, como la adopción institucional de las criptomonedas, la búsqueda de alternativas de inversión debido a la incertidumbre económica mundial y la innovación continua en la tecnología blockchain que respalda a bitcoin y otras divisas digitales. Esta combinación de factores ha creado un entorno propicio para el crecimiento continuo en el valor de Bitcoin.
Cómo adquirir criptomonedas
Para comprarlas e intercambiarlas se utilizan portales especializados. Su valor varía en función de la oferta, de la demanda y del compromiso de los usuarios, por lo que puede cambiar más rápido que el dinero tradicional, pero mientras más gente esté interesada y quiera comprar determinada divisa, mayor será su valor.
No obstante, quien invierte en este tipo de monedas digitales debe tener muy claro que esta forma trae consigo un elevado riesgo al capital, pues, así como puede haber un incremento, también puede tener inesperadamente un desplome y acabar con los ahorros de sus usuarios.
Para almacenarlas, los usuarios deben contar con un monedero digital o wallet, que en realidad es un software a través del cual es posible guardar, enviar y hacer transacciones de las criptomonedas. En realidad, este tipo de monederos sólo guarda las claves que marcan la propiedad y el derecho de una persona sobre cierta criptomoneda, por lo que estos códigos son los que en realidad se deben proteger.

articles.title: Store-bought hardware crypto wallets had secret chips installed that enabled stealing crypto recovery phrases — $93 million and counting stolen thanks to implanted eSIM and LTE modules in Ledger wallets
articles.text:
Store-bought hardware crypto wallets had secret chips installed that enabled stealing crypto recovery phrases — $93 million and counting stolen thanks to implanted eSIM and LTE modules in Ledger wallets
Hardware sold directly by Ledger appears safe, but some reseller supply chains may be compromised.
Cryptocurrency enthusiasts are often advised to acquire a hardware wallet like one of the Ledger models, theoretically adding the ultimate layer of security. And yet not even that approach is 100% safe, as a currently unfolding investigation revealed that Ledger resellers in Southeast Asia and Europe are carrying hacked wallets laden with eSIM and LTE modules for exfiltration of recovery phrases. At least $93 million (and going) has already reportedly been siphoned off users' balances. Hardware sold directly by Ledger is so far unaffected.
The first booby-trapped wallet originated from reseller Cryptobilis, which has currently ceased all sales of hardware wallets of all brands. The offending unit came from a store in Malaysia, though Cryptobilis also sells in Indonesia and the Philippines. Researcher Mark Karpelès has been looking into hacked wallets for a while now, and one of them came via Amazon Japan, bought from a Chinese seller and shipped from Malaysia. Cryptobilis also sells other brands of wallets such as Trezor, Coolwallet, and Tangem, though so far there is no news of contamination beyond Ledger.
Ledger recommends that users who bought wallets from Cryptobilis in the past 90 days do not perform their initial setup, as that's where the private key exfiltration reportedly occurs. To those who have already done so, Ledger recommends moving their assets to a new wallet with a new seed. The data theft is performed by hiding a flexible PCB under the display assembly to capture the pixels showing the private key entered during the first setup. The information then heads off to the aforementioned eSIM+LTE combination for exfiltration.
Meanwhile, new reports have come in from Europe, as techie Johannes, seemingly located in Germany, found at least two hacked wallets at MediaMarkt, a well-known tech and appliances retailer. He bought one unit and found that it had the same exact hardware modifications as its Asian counterparts, suggesting that the Asian and European events may be related. Johannes then bought a second one at a different MediaMarkt location, and sure enough, it was also modded.
Notably, most hacked wallets found so far are confirmed to be brand-new units instead of returns. Malfeasants will often buy new hardware and return it to the store with modifications, so that the next unsuspecting customer gets bit.
Johannes had a MediaMarkt employee at one of the stores look up the wallets' stock information, and at least the one unit came from Aqipa GmbH, a Europe-wide distributor — meaning the blast radius may be much wider than MediaMarkt or Germany. Since this is a recent development, Ledger hasn't published any guidance, though we imagine it'll be similar to the aforementioned steps.
In his blog post, Mark Karpelès notes that earlier iterations of hacked wallets with eSIM cards had hand-made implants, but that, concerningly, the hardware bolt-ons inside the latest finds appear to be manufactured to order. If true, this might mean that there's a production line somewhere intercepting Ledger wallets and manufacturing hacked wallets in bulk.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Ledger publishes instructions detailing how users can verify the physical integrity of their wallets, including pictures of every component, for every model of wallet the company offers, so they can closely inspect for add-ons. Likewise, prospective users should only download software from the official Ledger website URL — a task made harder by numerous scam sites with booby-trapped software, pretending to be the official ones.

articles.title: GTA 6 pode chegar ao PC já no início de 2027, aponta site
articles.text:
Os jogadores de PC podem não precisar esperar tanto para jogar GTA 6. Segundo uma reportagem do site GamesBeat, publicada nesta terça-feira (13), a Rockstar Games planeja lançar uma versão do jogo para computadores no primeiro trimestre de 2027, entre janeiro e março.
A informação foi atribuída a quatro fontes da indústria familiarizadas com os planos do estúdio, que pediram anonimato. Até o momento, a Rockstar não anunciou oficialmente a data de lançamento do jogo para PC nem confirmou a previsão.
A versão para PlayStation 5 e Xbox Series X/S continua programada para 19 de novembro de 2026, conforme o site oficial da desenvolvedora. Se o rumor estiver correto, a edição para computadores chegará poucos meses depois da estreia nos consoles.
GTA 6 pode ter espera menor no PC que o antecessor
- A possível janela de lançamento representaria uma mudança importante em relação ao histórico recente da franquia;
- GTA 5 estreou no PlayStation 3 e no Xbox 360 em setembro de 2013, mas só chegou ao PC em abril de 2015. O intervalo foi de aproximadamente um ano e sete meses;
- Outro grande lançamento da Rockstar, Red Dead Redemption 2, também demorou mais de um ano para chegar aos computadores após sua estreia nos consoles;
- Caso a previsão para GTA 6 se confirme, a espera será consideravelmente menor. Ainda assim, como não há confirmação oficial, não é possível garantir que o cronograma será cumprido.
Lançamento pode afetar calendário de outros jogos
A chegada de GTA 6 é considerada um dos grandes acontecimentos da indústria de games. O interesse em torno do título pode influenciar o calendário de lançamentos de outras empresas, que precisam disputar a atenção dos jogadores com a produção da Rockstar.
Entre os jogos previstos para o primeiro trimestre de 2027 estão Stranger Than Heaven, Metroid Prime 4: Beyond — cuja denominação aparece de forma diferente em algumas listas —, Until Dawn 2, Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis, God of War: Sons of Sparta e Fable.
A proximidade de grandes lançamentos pode levar empresas a reconsiderar suas datas para evitar competir diretamente com um dos títulos mais aguardados do setor. No entanto, não há confirmação de que algum desses jogos será adiado por causa de GTA 6.
Leia mais:
- GTA 6 transforma Miami em Vice City com outdoor de quase US$ 1 milhão
- Governo australiano orienta trabalhadores sobre como pedir folga para jogar GTA 6
- GTA 6 confirma retorno da Flash FM e revela seis estações de rádio; veja músicas
E o modo online de GTA 6?
Outra questão em aberto é quando a Rockstar pretende lançar o modo online de GTA 6. A empresa ainda não detalhou publicamente seus planos para essa modalidade.
O CEO da Twitch, Dan Clancy, afirmou que o modo online do jogo deve chegar em 2027, segundo a Bloomberg. A informação, porém, não substitui um anúncio oficial da Rockstar sobre a data ou os recursos do modo multiplayer.
O componente online é especialmente relevante para os jogadores de PC, já que GTA 5 abriga uma comunidade expressiva de servidores e modificações de interpretação de personagens, conhecidos como roleplay.
A Rockstar adquiriu a equipe por trás do FiveM, plataforma de servidores de roleplay, e posteriormente adicionou uma opção de roleplay ao inicializador de GTA 5 para PC. Ainda não está claro se a empresa pretende adotar uma estratégia semelhante para o novo jogo.
Por enquanto, os jogadores de computador terão de aguardar uma confirmação oficial sobre a versão de GTA 6 para sua plataforma. A previsão de lançamento entre janeiro e março de 2027 continua baseada em informações atribuídas a fontes anônimas.

articles.title: Facebook is giving users more control over their algorithm | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Facebook is the latest social media platform to give users greater control over the algorithm that determines what appears in their feeds.
Meta announced the launch of its new AI-powered feature, “Your Algorithm,” on Tuesday, a feature it first launched on Instagram. The new tool allows Facebook users to influence the content they see in Feed and Reels by describing their preferences in their own words using natural language. Rather than relying entirely on automated recommendations, users can now communicate directly with the platform about the topics and content they want to see more or less frequently.
According to Meta, the feature is designed to make content recommendations more relevant. Users can adjust their preferences and interact with the algorithms responsible for ranking and recommending posts, with changes reflected in their recommendations in real time.
The company has also updated Facebook’s three-dot menu, making it easier for users to manage their content preferences directly from individual posts. By opening the menu, users can access “Your Algorithm” or select the “Interested” and “Not interested” options to indicate whether particular content aligns with their preferences.
Meta says the platform may ask follow-up questions to better understand what users liked or disliked, allowing them to provide more detailed feedback. Users can explain what they want to see more or less of, helping Facebook refine its recommendations based on their responses.
The introduction of “Your Algorithm” reflects Meta’s broader effort to give people more influence over their social media experiences as AI increasingly shapes content discovery. The move signals a shift away from the traditional recommendation systems that have shaped social media experiences for years, bringing the platform closer to streaming services that allow users to personalize recommendations based on their interests and preferences.
The launch also builds on Meta’s existing personalization efforts across its other platforms. Instagram introduced Your Algorithm in June, extending customization options across Feed and Explore after first launching the feature for Reels in December 2025.
Threads also introduced its own related feature, called “Dear Algo,” which allows users to influence the content recommended to them.

articles.title: 'GTA 6' llegaría a PC mucho antes de lo que todos pensábamos
articles.text:
La espera por GTA 6 en PC podría ser mucho más breve de lo que todos imaginábamos. Según reporta GamesBeat, Rockstar Games planea lanzar la versión para ordenadores apenas meses después de su debut en PS5 y Xbox Series X|S. Si esto se confirma será un auténtico bombazo, considerando que hasta aquí el estudio ha dado pistas prácticamente nulas de que la llegada del nuevo Grand Theft Auto podría darse en un plazo tan acotado.
De acuerdo con el citado medio, GTA 6 se lanzará en PC durante el primer trimestre de 2027. La información fue supuestamente ratificada por cuatro fuentes relacionadas con los planes de Rockstar y Take-Two Interactive. De ser cierto, el debut del título en ordenadores se dará, a más tardar, en marzo del próximo año.
Claro que la información debe tomarse con pinzas y no hay que dar nada por hecho. Por lo pronto, los responsables de GTA 6 no han realizado anuncios oficiales sobre una versión para PC. De hecho, cada vez que se les ha consultado sobre el tema han brindado respuestas evasivas. Y si bien todos esperaban que el juego llegara eventualmente a Windows, nadie en sus cabales pensaba que podría llegar a darse tan rápido.
Después de todo, suponiendo que la información es certera, GTA 6 estaría llegando a PC apenas 4 meses después de su debut en consolas, considerando marzo de 2027 como fecha más tardía. Esto pondría patas arriba cualquier especulación previa respecto de la expansión del juego más allá de su disponibilidad inicial en PlayStation y Xbox.
GTA 6 podría llegar a PC a más tardar en marzo de 2027
Desde que GTA 6 lanzó su primer tráiler a finales de 2023, Rockstar Games ha evitado ofrecer cualquier tipo de mención a una posible versión de PC. Las únicas referencias a su potencial llegada a la plataforma han sido de Strauss Zelnick, el CEO de Take-Two Interactive, la casa matriz del estudio. Desde 2024 hasta la actualidad, el ejecutivo ofreció referencias sobre el tema (algunas más crípticas que otras), dando a entender que una edición para ordenadores llegaría tarde o temprano, pero que no sería prioridad.
Recién en mayo de este año, Zelnick brindó una respuesta más directa sobre por qué todavía no se había anunciado GTA 6 en PC. El empresario argumentó, simplemente, que la mayoría de los jugadores de Grand Theft Auto estaban en consolas, y que por ese motivo preferían enfocarse primero en servir a su base de usuarios más amplia.
"Rockstar siempre empieza en consola porque creo que [...] se te juzga por cómo atiendes a tu público principal. Es decir, realmente atender a tu consumidor principal. Si tu consumidor principal no está ahí, si no se le atiende primero y de la mejor manera, no llegas a tus otros consumidores", explicó por entonces.
Pero esa parecía ser solo una parte de la historia. John Ricchio, histórico productor de Rockstar con pasado en GTA 5, Red Dead Redemption y Max Payne, explicó que también existía una justificación técnica. Según su experiencia, optimizar GTA 6 basándose en las limitaciones técnicas de la PS5 y las Xbox Series X|S haría mucho más fácil el proceso de portear el juego a PC.
"Siempre es mejor empezar por las limitaciones y luego ampliar, porque reducir es mucho más difícil que ampliar. Es mucho más difícil lograr un buen rendimiento en un juego que simplemente pensar: 'Oh, tenemos espacio extra, genial, podemos desoptimizar algunas cosas o hacerlas más llamativas'", comentó.
Considerando los antecedentes, el consenso general era que GTA 6 posiblemente se demorara unos dos años en llegar a PC. Pero si lo que reporta GamesBeat es certero, la historia esta vez podría ser muy diferente. Esto despierta un gran interrogante: ¿Por qué Rockstar cambiaría de estrategia ahora?
El citado reporte plantea dos opciones:
- Por un lado, la necesidad de capturar a cuantos jugadores sea posible para recuperar sus bestiales costes de desarrollo. GTA 6 habría costado unos 2.000 millones de dólares, y llegar temprano a los jugadores más casuales en PC podría agilizar la amortización.
- Por el otro, implementar una estrategia basada en mods, la creación de contenidos por parte de los usuarios y el role-playing. En tal sentido, se menciona que la compra de CFX.re por parte de Rockstar en 2023 podría jugar un papel clave en esta historia.
También se especula con que lanzar la versión para PC de GTA 6 apenas meses después de su llegada a consolas podría estar relacionada con ampliar la base de GTA Online desde el primer día. Según el CEO de Twitch, Rockstar planea lanzar el componente multijugador online del nuevo Grand Theft Auto en 2027. Por ende, ya hay teorías de que el arribo temprano del juego a los ordenadores podría estar relacionado con esto. Por lo pronto, no hay que dar nada por hecho, pero seguiremos atentos a cualquier novedad.

articles.title: Fed up with Apple Intelligence? I tried the Mac app that banishes it for good — and it claims it can free up 12GB of storage space too
articles.text:
I tried the new Mac app that helps you ditch Apple Intelligence — and it saved me 12GB of storage too
Apple Intelligence, begone
- A new app called RemoveMacAI can delete Apple Intelligence files
- Doing so can reclaim up to 12GB of storage space
- But it comes with some scary warnings that shouldn’t be ignored
Apple promises that its new Siri AI and Apple Intelligence tools can help improve your daily experience through the magic of AI. Many people aren’t convinced, though, and a new Mac app has been doing the rounds that promises to delete Apple’s AI for good — so I decided to take it for a spin to see what all the fuss was about.
Dubbed RemoveMacAI, the app originally gained popularity in late September. At that time, though, it was just a simple Terminal command, which — given the obvious security risks of entering unknown code into a utility as powerful as the Terminal — turned some people off.
Now, the same developer is back with a Mac app that is essentially a wrapper for the command. This makes it a lot easier to understand what you’re deleting and what you’re enabling when you use the app, with a built-in tutorial and clear toggles spread across several different tabs and categories.
Apple makes it pretty difficult to eliminate every aspect of Apple Intelligence from your machine, which is why something like RemoveMacAI has gained a foothold. Its developer says Apple’s System Integrity Protection layer — which stops unauthorized code from running on your Mac — is never disabled, and that the app doesn’t make any network requests and doesn’t collect telemetric data.
That said, I loaded RemoveMacAI onto my Mac and was immediately met with a concerning warning: macOS did not trust the app and wouldn’t let me run it. The developer said this is due to the app being unsigned, and you’ve got to manually let it through Apple’s gates. I’ve occasionally encountered apps that do this, and it’s never a pleasant experience.
Foolishly or not, I pushed on. You can either choose the app’s recommended settings, which delete Apple Intelligence and turn off some privacy-invading settings, go “maximum privacy” and also disable Game Center and some Safari settings, or choose what to do yourself.
I opted to just delete Apple Intelligence and nothing else. RemoveMacAI breaks your options down into sections — you can switch off Siri AI, ChatGPT’s extension, Writing Tools, Image Playground, and much more, all with modular toggles.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Once that’s done, there’s another jarring moment: RemoveMacAI wants you to install a custom profile that it uses to enact your changes. Fortunately, you can read through every change it includes, so there’s visibility over what’s being done.
I accepted that and let RemoveMacAI get to work deleting Apple Intelligence. In the end, it freed up 11.7GB, which is nothing to sniff at and is in line with the developer’s claims. If you’re running low, it could be a good way to claw back precious disk space.
Although RemoveMacAI comes with some scary settings, it attempts to ease your fears by letting you read through everything that’s going to be changed, including the macOS profile. You can undo your decisions too, and doing so will revert your settings changes and redownload the Apple Intelligence models when they’re needed next.
Ultimately, I found RemoveMacAI to be a handy utility, especially if you want one resource for not only deleting Apple Intelligence, but also for restricting some of macOS’s more privacy-invading practices. The lack of notarization and the subsequent alarming warnings will likely put some people off, though, and they stop me from wholeheartedly recommending the app as a result.

articles.title: Shopify opens its catalog up to more AI agents
articles.text:
More AI agents will soon be able to browse and purchase from Shopify listings, marking an expansion of the company’s agentic commerce ambitions.
Shopify opens its catalog up to more AI agents
Shopify previously announced a partnership with Meta’s Muse for AI-powered shopping and checkout.
Shopify announced Tuesday it will let shoppers configure their AI agents to purchase products on their behalf, giving more agents access to over a billion listings in Shopify’s catalog. (The catalog consists of both items on and off Shopify storefronts.) In September, Shopify announced it was partnering with Meta to allow its Muse agent to browse and purchase items on a human’s behalf; now, shoppers can use any agent without a partnership integration.
To set up the feature, customers connect an agent with their account on Shop, a Shopify-owned platform that consolidates orders, tracks packages, and recommends products. Like the Muse partnership, customers use the one-click Shop Pay feature to check out within the conversation with the agent. Orders placed through the agent are funneled back to the Shop app. Shopify is marketing the feature as a “personal shopper” that humans can give rules to, like setting budget guardrails or only displaying products with fast shipping. Buyers must approve each purchase.
E-commerce has become one of the battlegrounds in the era of AI — it’s no coincidence that many demos of agentic tools end with a transaction, whether it’s buying clothing, booking a flight, or ordering takeout on a human’s behalf. The tech industry, including big commerce players like Google and Amazon, are investing in AI-driven shopping tools where the end goal is an “agent” purchasing things for a human user. It’s also the basis of an ongoing fight between Amazon and AI companies like Perplexity — and more recently, Meta’s Muse — over whether agents should be able to shop on a customer’s behalf.

articles.title: AI could outperform 90% of coders in six months: Zoho's Sridhar Vembu
articles.text:
AI could outperform 90% of coders in six months: Zoho's Sridhar Vembu
At TechSparks 2026, Zoho’s Sridhar Vembu spoke about why software automation is not nessarily a crisis, urging the nation to focus on technological ownership, hardware foundations, and self-reliance over foreign IP dependency.
Rapid advances in AI software creation are driving an existential shift in the industry. With this, traditional coding is entering its “handloom” era, according to Sridhar Vembu, Co-founder and Chief Scientist of enterprise software firm Zoho.
Comparing software to a “handloom business,” Vembu said “powerful machine looms” are emerging, referring to automated systems generating complex computer scripts at high speed. Automated systems can already write functional code faster and more efficiently than many human developers, he added.
“AI already can write better code than at least 60-70% of software engineers out there. And in maybe three to six months, when things accelerate, AI can do better software than maybe 90% of software engineers,” Vembu said, speaking at the 17th edition of YourStory’s flagship tech-startup event, TechSparks.
Venture capitalists like Chamath Palihapitiya have suggested that intellectual property, the underlying proprietary ownership of written software code, is effectively dead, he added.
Despite the impending disruption to tech professionals, a huge part of India's population will remain largely unaffected, said Vembu, presenting a counter-intuitive macro perspective. He pointed out that roughly 97% of the broader population does not write software and operates as consumers of technology.
Outside major tech hubs such as Bengaluru, districts like Tenkasi in Tamil Nadu or Patna in Bihar will experience minimal direct economic upheaval if coding jobs disappear, said Vembu.
Furthermore, as software creation costs fall, automated efficiency could exert deflationary pressure across the broader economy. Lower production expenses mean non-technology workers, including teachers, nurses, and barbers, effectively gain increased real purchasing power as consumer goods become more affordable.
The technology ownership gap
The true obstacle to national prosperity is not the loss of outsourcing jobs, but a fundamental lack of technology ownership, according to Vembu.
Although Indian engineers write a vast portion of software for Microsoft and Cisco, and design up 40-50% of Nvidia's chip design work, the primary financial returns flow to foreign intellectual property holders, the entrepreneur pointed out.
To highlight this disparity, Vembu compared a Swiss school teacher, who can earn an iPhone in 3-4 days of work, with an Indian teacher who needs to put in months of work for the same item, despite neither being directly involved in technology.
“Ultimately, who has ownership of the technology determines what is the income level of the non-tech people in that economy. Not the income of tech people alone,” Vembu emphasised.
Reflecting on the 1990s, he argued that India was misled by Western commentary, such as Thomas Friedman’s writing celebrating IT services outsourcing, which rewarded labour over true technology ownership.
To achieve lasting economic independence, India must adopt the strategy of East Asian nations such as Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, and China. Instead of rushing into top-level AI applications, China established durable national sovereignty by developing foundational domestic layers first, including search engines like Baidu and messaging ecosystems like WeChat.
Vembu cautioned against prioritising AI over essential industrial hardware and infrastructure, warning that a nation relying entirely on foreign hardware and foreign operating systems risks extreme geopolitical vulnerability.
“One reason I came to AI last is, we obsess about AI. We should not be obsessing about AI first. We should be obsessing about the more foundational layers,” he said.
True national resilience requires mastering core technologies such as lasers, x-rays, robotics, operating systems, and agricultural technology, according to him.
This philosophy guides Zoho's operational strategy amid rising infrastructure demands. The surge in AI adoption has caused server and graphics processing unit costs to explode, with server prices climbing from $8,000 to $45,000. Instead of executing corporate layoffs, Vembu said Zoho is redeploying its engineering talent towards deeptech hardware, including building server infrastructure in-house.
Highlighting this approach, Vembu noted, “As much as our jobs are challenged by the present generation of AI. You know why we don’t lay off anybody? We know we can redeploy them to build all this stuff.”
The emerging tech order, according to the entrepreneur, demands a shift from exporting software services to securing genuine national technological ownership.
Edited by Swetha Kannan

articles.title: The MFA Gaps Attackers are Still Exploiting
articles.text:
On August 4, 2026, an Akira ransomware affiliate began spraying passwords against a SonicWall SSL VPN. Around seven minutes later, one attempt succeeded. The credentials were valid, and the VPN account had no multi-factor authentication (MFA) protecting it. Roughly two hours later, the attacker used RDP to access the domain controller and began enumerating Active Directory.
The ransomware deployment ultimately failed, but by then the attacker had already stolen credentials and file-share data.
It highlights an issue that is still common in 2026, where an organization might require MFA for Microsoft 365 and other SaaS applications while leaving certain access paths protected only by passwords. It’s this gap that attackers are regularly exploiting.
Stolen Credentials Remain a Valuable Tool for Attackers
Once an attacker has a valid account, they can begin interacting with the environment through the same authentication mechanisms used by legitimate employees and administrators. AI is adding another dimension to this problem by helping attackers operate at greater speed and scale.
The underlying identity tactics are largely unchanged: attackers still compromise identities, reuse credentials, escalate privileges and misuse legitimate access. The threat is that AI makes familiar techniques cheaper and easier to run at scale.
Mandiant’s ransomware investigations illustrate why that matters once credentials are obtained. Compromised legitimate credentials accounted for initial access in 21% of the 2025 incidents where the entry point could be established, typically through RDP or VPN.
RDP also appeared frequently later in the attack chain, with attackers using compromised or newly created accounts over RDP for lateral movement in around 85% of the ransomware incidents it investigated.
Identifying Stolen Credentials in Your Organization
Strong authentication helps limit what an attacker can do with a stolen password, but it is still worth finding exposed or risky credentials before they are used. Password reuse, weak choices and credentials that have appeared in previous breaches all increase the chance that an attacker will find a password that still works somewhere in the environment.
That makes regular password auditing a useful part of Active Directory security. Specops Password Auditor is a free, read-only password auditing tool that scans Active Directory for password-related vulnerabilities and presents the findings in an interactive report covering user and password policy information.
This gives IT teams another opportunity to reduce credential risk at source: identify password weaknesses, address them where possible, and make sure that a compromised password is not enough on its own to gain access.
Secure your Active Directory passwords with Specops Password Policy
Verizon’s Data Breach Investigation Report found stolen credentials are involved in 44.7% of breaches. 
Effortlessly secure Active Directory with compliant password policies, blocking 4+ billion compromised passwords, boosting security, and slashing support hassles!
Why Cloud MFA Doesn’t Necessarily Protect the Entire Windows Estate
Microsoft 365, identity providers and SaaS applications are obvious places to add additional authentication factors because they are internet-facing and frequently targeted. The problem is that cloud MFA does not automatically extend to every system that relies on the same user identity.
A user may need MFA to access a SaaS application through the corporate identity provider, but the same account could still be accepted elsewhere with just a password.
That creates a fragmented authentication environment where some routes are better protected than others, which leaves a gap for attackers to exploit.
VPNs are another potential gap. As the August Akira ransomware attack demonstrated, a threat actor that obtains or brute forces a valid username and password may be able to turn those credentials directly into remote network access if MFA isn’t enforced.
For IT and security teams, the useful question is therefore not simply whether MFA is deployed, but where a password is still enough on its own. Windows logon, RDP, VPN access and older AD-backed services are all worth including in that review.
Closing the Authentication Gaps
Closing these gaps means applying stronger authentication to the places where credentials are still being trusted, rather than treating MFA as something that only sits in front of cloud applications.
That is where solutions like Specops Secure Access fit by extending MFA to Windows logon, RDP and VPN authentication. This adds strong protection to some of the access paths attackers regularly target with stolen Active Directory credentials.
It also supports SSO for SaaS applications through OIDC and SAML, helping organizations apply a more consistent authentication approach across on-premises and cloud services.
Authentication is also a useful source of security telemetry. Specops Secure Access integrates with SIEM, SOC and analytics platforms, allowing authentication events and suspicious activity to feed into the wider monitoring process.
Protecting the user is only part of the picture, though. A second question is whether the device making the request should be trusted.
Mitigate the Risk of Stolen Passwords
In 2026, stolen passwords are still powerful tools for attackers if they are accepted by VPNs, RDP sessions or Windows systems without additional checks. That is why MFA coverage matters as much as adopting MFA in the first place. Protecting cloud applications is important, but it does not remove the risk created by authentication paths elsewhere in the environment that still rely on a password alone.
No single control will stop every intrusion, and MFA is no exception. But organizations can make credential theft much less useful by asking a simple question: where can a password still be used on its own?
Adding another protective layer to those areas with Specops Secure Access ensures that one stolen credential does not become the easiest route into the rest of the network.

articles.title: 10 points de permis perdus en 20 minutes : j’ai testé la voiture autonome à Paris
articles.text:
La conduite 100% autonome est la promesse faite notamment par Tesla à ses clients depuis de nombreuses années. À l’occasion du Mondial de l’automobile qui se déroule à Paris du 12 au 18 octobre, la marque américaine — tout comme la chinoise Xpeng — permettent d’ailleurs aux plus curieux de tester le dispositif qu’elles aimeraient bien voir chacune homologué en France. Mais ces deux constructeurs ne sont pas les seuls sur les rangs. Il y a quelques jours, c’est Denza, l’enseigne haut de gamme du groupe BYD, qui nous a convié à parcourir les rues de Paris « sans les mains ». Du gâteau ? Pas vraiment…
La capitale française n’est pas spécialement connue pour être un cadeau fait aux automobilistes de chair et d’os. Ronds points aux règles très parisiennes, zones de travaux, rues étroites, signalisation verticale pas toujours visible ou entretenue, marquage au sol aléatoire : nombreux sont les conducteurs qui voient monter le stress au passage du panneau Paris. Qu’en sera-t-il pour le robot de conduite de Denza ?
Le CNOA — pour City Navigation On Autopilot — de Denza existe depuis déjà environ deux ans en Chine. Baptisé God’s Eye (l’œil de Dieu, rien que ça !), le système fonctionne en mode « map free », c’est-à-dire qu’il ne repose pas sur des cartes de haute définition mais utilise plutôt une batterie de capteurs (27 en tout), dont un lidar haute précision à très longue portée, des caméras ultra-haute définition, des radars à ondes millimétriques et d’autres capteurs à ultrasons connectés au cerveau unique de la machine via l’architecture Xuanji maison pour décider de ses manœuvres telles que le passage aux carrefours (conduite en ligne droite, virage à gauche, virage à droite, demi-tour, etc.), dans les giratoires, le franchissement des feux tricolores, les dépassements, l’évitement intelligent des obstacles, les changements de voie, le maintien de voie, la conduite en régulateur de vitesse, le passage d’une voie à l’autre et la priorité aux piétons et aux véhicules non motorisés.
L’ensemble est en outre connecté en 5G, par satellite et aux éventuels véhicules également connectés qui circuleraient dans la zone. Mais en premier lieu et pour faire simple, la voiture voit et perçoit son environnement puis adopte ce que son cerveau pense être la bonne stratégie à chaque étape de son évolution urbaine. Pour l’aider dans ces décisions, des milliers de kilomètres de tests sont nécessaires, durant lesquels les opérateurs apprennent à la machine les bonnes décisions au regard des règles de conduite locales.
On ne conduit pas à Paris comme à Shanghai, où tous les feux de circulation sont connectés, par exemple. Dans la capitale française, il n’est pas rare d’en trouver cachés derrière un utilitaire, une branche d’arbre, ou qui sont tout simplement défectueux. Alors qu’il s’agit déjà souvent d’un défi pour un humain, à la machine de se débrouiller avec. Enfin, la cartographie Google Maps intégrée à la voiture sert quant à elle à définir le parcours à suivre pour arriver à destination.
Une voiture immense dans les rues bondées de Paris
C’est par paire que les cobayes — nous autres journalistes, donc — sont invités à monter à bord d’une Denza Z9 GT, grande berline électrique de plus de 1150 chevaux. Ce n’est évidemment pas cette caractéristique qui fera la différence à 30 km/h maximum, vitesse autorisée à Paris et que l’auto est évidemment tenue de respecter. En revanche, son encombrement — 5,18 mètres de long, 2 de large — constitue un handicap sérieux pour se faufiler dans la circulation de ce milieu d’après-midi de fin de semaine.
Le reste de l’équipage est constitué d’un superviseur formé spécialement pour la tâche et dont le rôle est de reprendre les commandes si cela s’avère nécessaire, ainsi que — nous concernant — d’une ingénieure venue de Chine pour assurer le suivi de l’opération, prendre en note tout ce qui ne va pas et, éventuellement, remettre en route le logiciel s’il venait à défaillir.
D’ailleurs, Denza nous prévient dès le départ : pas question de proposer cette technologie au client avant au moins l’année prochaine, nous sommes réellement en phase de test et de développement. Et des bugs, certaines des autos en ont rencontré, parfois avant même de prendre leur premier départ.
Un circuit de 20 mn et quelques grosses frayeurs
Pour nous, la sortie de la place de stationnement située au pied de la concession BYD des Champs-Élysées se déroule sans difficulté, mais toujours sous l’œil inquiet du staff pléthorique chargé de sécuriser les abords, au cas où. Quelques minutes plus tôt, certaines autos ont eu plus de mal. Il faut dire que le tempérament du conducteur parisien est rarement caractérisé par la patience, et nombreux sont ceux qui veulent prendre les devants en se glissant sous le nez de la Denza, stoppant net sa procédure de départ.
Nous voici partis pour un tour d’un peu plus de 5 kilomètres dans Paris : Étoile, Trocadéro, Passy, Tour Eiffel, Iéna et retour vers la rue Pierre Charron. Premier feu, à l’angle des Champs-Élysées, nous mettons cap à droite vers la place de l’Étoile, ce fameux giratoire à 12 sorties que plus de 100 000 voitures empruntent chaque jour et qui met souvent au défi même le plus chevronné des Parisiens.
L’engagement se passe bien, la voiture prend sa place dans le flot remontant. D’abord sur la file de gauche, puis elle se décale vers la droite, plus roulante. Loin d’être fluide, la circulation ne semble pas poser de problème particulier à la Z9 GT. À l’Étoile, le parcours prévoit trois-quarts de tour, avec une sortie Avenue Kléber. L’engagement est plutôt bon, la berline chinoise se positionne sur une des files du milieu, file toute virtuelle puisque ce giratoire ne dispose d’aucun marquage au sol. Particularité : c’est l’un des seuls, sinon le seul giratoire en France à imposer la priorité à l’entrée. À allure modérée, l’auto franchit la moitié du rond-point mais, au lieu d’anticiper sa manœuvre pour s’engager tranquillement vers les voies extérieures et prendre sa sortie, attend d’être rendue à la perpendiculaire de celle-ci pour virer à 90 degrés droite.
Coup de chance, aucun automobiliste énervé n’a cherché à forcer sa priorité. À ce stade, le code de la route suggère plutôt de refaire le tour. Engagé avenue Kléber, une nouvelle épreuve attend l’œil de Dieu environ 200 mètres plus loin. Un poids lourd en livraison, hayon ouvert et feux de détresse allumés, occupe la chaussée. Nous sommes loin de l’intersection suivante et la voie opposée est dégagée.
L’auto peut doubler… mais préfère laisser mourir son freinage littéralement au cul du camion, s’interdisant toute manœuvre pour s’échapper, tous les capteurs frontaux étant aveuglés par l’obstacle. Seule solution pour l’opérateur : reprendre la main et relancer le système une fois le camion contourné. Un peu plus loin, imperturbable, elle ignore un passage protégé sur lequel un piéton est pourtant déjà engagé sur une bonne moitié de la voie opposée. Une infraction sanctionnée d’un retrait de 6 points sur le permis de conduire, sans parler de l’amende pécuniaire qui l’accompagne.
L’œil de Dieu ne voit pas le rouge
Au Trocadéro, le parcours prévoit de remonter quelques dizaines de mètres puis de bifurquer à gauche sur la rue Benjamin Franklin. Mais alors qu’elle se prépositionne plutôt correctement, la Denza préfère finalement continuer tout droit. Une situation que l’ingénieure de bord semble ne pas vouloir lui laisser gérer. Tandis que Google Maps recalcule l’itinéraire, elle demande au chauffeur de reprendre la main et de prendre la rue prévue au départ. Demi-tour, donc.
Le giratoire de la place du Costa-Rica est négocié sans problème, direction les bords de Seine, avenues du Président-Kennedy, puis de New York. Face à la Tour Eiffel, au Pont d’Iéna, la Z9 s’engage avenue des Nations-Unies et prolonge avenue d’Iéna sans difficulté. Elle attend même le bon moment et la place nécessaire pour dépasser quelques cyclistes à la peine dans la côte sans les frôler. Place d’Iéna, tout semble aller pour le mieux. La voiture salue la statue équestre de Washington et vise la sortie pour continuer sur l’avenue d’Iéna.
Nous sommes à environ 50 mètres du feu de circulation lorsque celui-ci passe à l’orange. Calé à un peu moins de 30 km/h, la Denza n’hésite pas une seconde : elle garde l’allure et, en bonne Parisienne, franchit le feu alors qu’il est au rouge vif depuis une bonne seconde. Voilà quatre points supplémentaires supprimés sur son permis, tout virtuel qu’il soit !
Le virage à droite de la rue Georges Bizet passé, la Denza continue son chemin. On ignore comment elle s’assure que personne ne va prendre la priorité de la rue de Chaillot, mais tout se passe sans encombre. À 30 km/h, elle aurait probablement eu le temps de s’arrêter en cas de trafic transversal, difficile à détecter dans les rues parisiennes sans s’avancer un peu au-delà du début de l’intersection.
Une centaine de mètres plus bas : feu rouge. Comme si elle avait voulu se faire pardonner son loupé de la place d’Iéna, la Z9 s’arrête cette fois… une bonne trentaine de mètres avant le feu ! Pas vraiment d’infraction, mais une bizarrerie de plus sur ce parcours semé d’embûches.
Nous voici avenue Pierre Iᵉʳ de Serbie avec notre point d’arrivée presque en vue. La voiture en double file n’est cette fois pas ignorée : clignotant, la Z9 l’efface, non sans avoir pris en compte l’auto qui sortait de son stationnement sur la voie opposée pile à ce moment-là.
Mais être presque arrivé ne signifie pas la fin des curiosités. Un peu plus loin, aux abords de la rue Pierre Charron, une petite file de quatre véhicules se forme au niveau d’un feu de circulation. Deux voitures, suivies par deux side-cars promène-touristes. La Denza s’en approche et… engage une manœuvre de dépassement ! In extremis, l’opérateur reprend la main, se remet dans la file et adresse un petit signe d’excuses à l’automobiliste qui se présentait en face au même moment.
Allez, encore quelques mètres avant le point de stationnement. Le chauffeur engage le mode de parking automatique puis, au niveau de la concession BYD, indique la place qu’il souhaite occuper d’un clic sur l’écran. Manque de chance, il commande un stationnement à contre-sens. La voiture, qui ne semble pas savoir qu’il est interdit de stationner à contre-sens, entame tranquillement son demi-tour, que le chauffeur avortera avant d’appuyer sur le bon bouton. Nous voici garés, ouf !
Bilan : encore du travail
Quiconque prend le volant à Paris mesure le monde qui peut séparer la conduite parisienne de celle de n’importe quelle autre ville de province. Si BYD propose déjà cette conduite autonome de niveau 2+ dans les rues des villes chinoises, elle sait qu’il lui reste encore beaucoup de travail avant de délivrer cette fonction à ces clients européens, voire français.
À vrai dire, la marche vers une conduite déléguée fiable à Paris nous paraît encore si loin pour Denza qu’il faut saluer la sorte de courage, voire de témérité, dont elle a fait preuve en proposant à quelques dizaines de journalistes plutôt exigeants d’effectuer in vivo les premiers tests français de sa technologie.
Il ne serait pas très juste de vouloir comparer le CNAO au FSD de Tesla, que la marque américaine pousse aussi fort qu’elle le peut pour obtenir son homologation. Si les démos européennes de Tesla semblent se passer plutôt bien malgré quelques couacs notables (dépassement de vitesse maximum autorisée en ville, par exemple), il faut se rappeler que la marque a engrangé des milliards de données depuis plusieurs années, issues de la conduite de ses clients, pour alimenter l’IA de son autopilot. Denza, qui de plus ne roule pas aux USA, part donc avec quelques longueurs de retard, retard que des milliers d’ingénieurs tentent aujourd’hui de combler.
Tests de conduite autonome en ville : que permet la loi française ?
En France, les constructeurs automobiles peuvent expérimenter des systèmes de conduite autonome sur la voie publique, y compris en pleine ville. Mais cette liberté est encadrée. L’ordonnance du 3 août 2016 et le décret du 28 mars 2018 imposent une autorisation préalable du ministère chargé des Transports pour les essais impliquant une délégation effective de conduite. Cette autorisation précise notamment les fonctionnalités testées, les conditions de sécurité, la durée des essais et les voies sur lesquelles ils peuvent être réalisés.
Un constructeur autorisé à expérimenter son système dans certaines rues parisiennes ; ici BYD-Denza ne peut donc pas décider librement de poursuivre ses essais en mode autonome dans une autre ville. Les véhicules concernés doivent par ailleurs disposer d’un certificat spécifique et être sous la supervision d’un opérateur formé à cette tâche et seul habilité à se trouver derrière le volant lorsque la voiture évolue en mode autonome.

articles.title: Cómo China está transformando una zona rural donde se cultivan papas en el centro de su competencia tecnológica con EE.UU.
articles.text:
En los campos de patatas de Ulanqab, los agricultores cosechan junto a unos vecinos que no dejan de crecer: enormes bloques rectangulares donde se alojará buena parte del cómputo de la inteligencia artificial china.
Cientos de obreros con casco amarillo mueven maquinaria entre andamios y chispas de soldadura, y las grúas levantan tejados a toda prisa.
Cientos de grúas y 500.000 millones de yuanes
La prisa tiene una razón de Estado. El plan 'IA Plus' del Consejo de Estado fija para 2030 una penetración de terminales y agentes de IA superior al 90 %, y eso necesita cómputo.
Ulanqab, según las cifras de un análisis reciente, ha atraído 84 proyectos de centros de datos (81 de IA; otros recuentos suben a 89) y más de 500.000 millones de yuanes (unos 66.000 millones de euros), y el consumo eléctrico de sus servicios de datos subió un 85,2 % interanual en el primer semestre de 2026, hasta los 4.000 millones de kWh.
Los nombres propios ya están sobre la mesa. Envision puso en marcha el 6 de agosto su campus Galaxy: 120.000 metros cuadrados, hasta un millón de aceleradores de IA y, según la compañía, margen para superar los 2 GW con electricidad renovable conectada de forma directa. DeepSeek prepara cerca de 1 GW, con operación parcial a finales de 2027 o principios de 2028 y sin confirmación oficial. ByteDance quiere añadir entre cinco y seis gigavatios en dos años, apunta una fuente cercana a las conversaciones con proveedores locales.
¿Por qué una estepa y no en pleno Shanghái?
Por el frío (4,3 grados de media a 1.500 metros), el viento y una electricidad verde de 0,30-0,35 yuanes por kWh. Un centro de datos de 1 GW funcionando a carga constante consume unos 8.760 millones de kWh al año: a 0,35 yuanes, serían unos 3.066 millones de yuanes de factura (cuenta propia). Y Pekín queda a unos 4 milisegundos de latencia.
Nada de esto es improvisado. Ulanqab es uno de los nodos del plan ‘Datos del Este, Computación del Oeste’, lanzado en 2022 por la NDRC con ocho ‘hubs’ y diez clústeres, para llevar el cómputo pesado adonde sobra energía.
Wang Chaoyang, de Alibaba Cloud, lo explica con un reparto: el entrenamiento de modelos se va al oeste, por la energía barata, y la inferencia (lo que usamos los usuarios) se queda cerca del este.
Hay peros. China quiere que la mayoría de sus centros de datos funcionen con energía verde en 2030, pero parte de su red todavía tira de carbón, y el agua sigue siendo un problema en la Mongolia Interior árida.
Pekín juega la carrera desde tres puntos de vista
La carrera tiene meta política. A finales de septiembre, Trump y Xi se vieron en Washington, con la IA entre los temas. Poco antes, el consejero delegado de Anthropic, Dario Amodei, había defendido en un ensayo frenar el ritmo de los modelos más potentes y mantener las restricciones a la venta de chips avanzados a China; Trump respondió que no piensa frenar, porque quien gane en IA, gana. El portavoz de Exteriores chino, Guo Jiakun, lo tachó de alarmismo.
La carta del talento. Jack Zhang, de la Universidad de Ciencia y Tecnología de China (pasó por Yale y Cambridge), asegura que cada vez van menos estudiantes a EE.UU. y que más regresan. El país forma, se suele estimar, unos cinco millones de graduados en ciencia y tecnología al año frente a medio millón de EE.UU., aunque las estimaciones varían bastante.
La tercera vía son los chips propios. DeepSeek prepararía un pedido de chips Ascend de Huawei, con su modelo V4 optimizado para el Ascend 950, aunque ni el volumen ni el modelo están confirmados.
A la hora de comparar tamaños, el seguimiento de Epoch AI sitúa hoy a Colossus 2 (el de xAI) con 946 MW y a New Carlisle (Anthropic y Amazon) con 910 MW, y a Fairwater Wisconsin con 2.263 MW previstos para 2028, y en su lista no aparece ningún centro chino. Los 2 GW de Envision son capacidad de diseño, no consumo actual.
Mucho gigavatio y poco enchufado
Ahora, las cuentas. Los 4.000 millones de kWh del primer semestre equivalen a unos 0,92 GW de consumo medio (181 días, 4.344 horas, cuenta propia). Lo que ha trascendido de solo tres proyectos (Envision, DeepSeek y ByteDance) suma entre 8 y 9 GW: casi diez veces lo que Ulanqab gasta hoy, aunque solo lo de Envision es oficial.
Además, el oeste llega con sobrecapacidad. En 2025, apenas el 36,8 % de la capacidad de cómputo inteligente se utilizó, según la Academia China de Tecnologías de la Información y la Comunicación. Un análisis de mayo habla de centros de datos occidentales con tasas del 20-30 % frente al objetivo de más del 60%.
Y a pie de campo, la vara de medir es otra. Se han reubicado pueblos enteros, aunque nadie precisa cuántos ni con qué compensación, y pocos se atreven a hablar. Un vecino que pide anonimato asegura que pocos lugareños han encontrado trabajo en los centros y pregunta: “¿Qué beneficios nos han aportado?”. Otro hombre, que recoge patatas junto a las obras y solo da su apellido, ve el futuro con optimismo: sus hijos ya trabajan en las instalaciones.
Los centros de datos están al lado; el cambio, de momento, no.

articles.title: La RED Box 5G passe à 25,99 € : faut-il encore craquer ?
articles.text:
RED Box 5G : le prix augmente, mais l’offre reste sans engagement
La RED Box 5G coûte désormais 25,99 € par mois, soit 1 € de plus qu’auparavant, mais conserve son accès Internet illimité, son Wi-Fi 6 et son offre sans engagement.
La RED Box 5G passe à 25,99 € par mois
Le prix de la RED Box 5G augmente légèrement : il faut désormais compter 25,99 € par mois, contre 24,99 € auparavant. Pour le reste, la formule ne change pas avec une connexion 5G sans engagement et une installation sans technicien.
Le débit annoncé atteint jusqu’à 1,1 Gb/s en téléchargement et 150 Mb/s en envoi, avec du Wi-Fi 6. De quoi couvrir sans difficulté les usages courants d’un foyer : streaming, télétravail, jeux en ligne, visioconférences ou connexion de plusieurs appareils.
L’offre de base comprend :
●	25,99 € par mois, sans engagement ;
●	Internet illimité via la 5G ;
●	jusqu’à 1,1 Gb/s en téléchargement ;
●	jusqu’à 150 Mb/s en envoi ;
●	Wi-Fi 6 ;
●	installation autonome, sans intervention d’un technicien ;
●	appels illimités vers les fixes et mobiles en France et les DOM en option, pour 5 € supplémentaires par mois.
Le choix de la 5G peut être particulièrement intéressant pour les logements qui ne disposent pas d’une connexion fixe satisfaisante. Cependant, il reste nécessaire de vérifier l’éligibilité à l’adresse concernée avant de souscrire, puisque les performances dépendent notamment de la couverture disponible.
Une installation simple et une offre toujours sans engagement
Personnellement, ce qui me plaît surtout avec cette Box 5G, c’est la simplicité de mise en service. Le fait de pouvoir l’installer soi-même, sans attendre l’intervention d’un technicien, me semble particulièrement pratique lorsqu’une connexion Internet doit être activée rapidement.
Une fois la box reçue, son installation reste simple : il suffit de la placer dans un endroit où la réception 5G est suffisamment bonne. Un fonctionnement pratique pour disposer rapidement d’une connexion, notamment après un déménagement ou en attendant l’installation d’une ligne fixe.
Par ailleurs, RED maintient son positionnement sans engagement. Il n’est donc pas nécessaire de prévoir une durée minimale de souscription, ce qui laisse davantage de liberté qu’une offre liée à un engagement long.
RED prévoit aussi une offre de remboursement pouvant atteindre 100 € sur les frais de résiliation de l’ancien opérateur. Il faut néanmoins respecter les conditions prévues par l’opérateur pour en bénéficier.
La hausse de 1 € mérite évidemment d’être prise en compte. Elle reste limitée, mais elle modifie légèrement le rapport prix/prestations de cette box par rapport à son ancien tarif.
Au final, la RED Box 5G reste une solution intéressante pour profiter d’Internet rapidement sans engagement, notamment lorsque la fibre n’est pas disponible ou ne répond pas aux besoins du logement. À 25,99 € par mois, elle conserve surtout deux arguments simples : une installation autonome et un accès 5G sans durée minimale.

articles.title: La pochette officielle Switch 2 des 40 ans de Zelda revient en précommande chez Cultura
articles.text:
En février 1986, Link partait pour la première fois à l’aventure au Japon, sur le Famicom Disk System. Quarante ans plus tard, Nintendo marque l’anniversaire de The Legend of Zelda avec une pochette de transport officielle pour la Switch 2. Après une rupture de stock, elle revient en précommande.
Cultura la propose de nouveau en précommande à 39,99 €. La sortie est prévue le 29 octobre 2026.
C’est quoi, cette pochette Switch 2 des 40 ans de Zelda ?
Il s’agit d’une pochette de transport officielle Nintendo pour la Nintendo Switch 2, créée pour célébrer les 40 ans de The Legend of Zelda. Nintendo l’a annoncée lors du Direct consacré aux 40 ans de la saga, le 8 septembre 2026. Elle sort le même jour que la Switch 2 édition Zelda, et une semaine avant le remake The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, attendu le 5 novembre 2026 sur Switch 2. Son design associe le noir et l’or, avec la Triforce en vedette. Ce symbole emblématique de la série représente les trois forces au cœur de l’univers Zelda et devrait immédiatement parler aux fans de la licence.
Au-delà de son apparence, cette pochette sert à transporter la console tout en la protégeant des rayures et des petits chocs du quotidien. Elle est également livrée avec une protection d’écran spécialement conçue pour la Nintendo Switch 2.
La pochette Zelda vaut-elle le coup ?
La pochette standard de Nintendo, livrée elle aussi avec une protection d’écran, coûte 24,99 € sur le My Nintendo Store. À 39,99 € chez Cultura, l’écart atteint 15 €. Avec cette édition spéciale, vous payez aussi le design, avec le symbole des 40 ans de The Legend of Zelda, plutôt qu’un modèle classique. Elle s’adresse donc avant tout aux joueuses et aux joueurs attachés à la saga.
Si vous voulez acheter cette édition anniversaire, surveillez les stocks de Cultura. Rien ne garantit que la pochette sera encore disponible ces prochains jours : elle a déjà été en rupture une première fois. La Switch 2 édition Zelda, annoncée le même jour, s’est retrouvée en rupture chez la plupart des revendeurs dans les jours qui ont suivi le Direct. Si vous tenez à mettre la main sur cet accessoire, mieux vaut donc ne pas trop tarder et surveiller régulièrement la fiche produit.
