articles.title: Microsoft Patches More Than 1,400 Security Flaws
articles.text:
Microsoft today issued updates to fix more than 1,400 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and other software. Today’s epic patch batch dwarfs September’s record of nearly 1,000 fixes, which was already about ten times the normal monthly patch load from Redmond.
Just one of the weaknesses patched this week is considered a “zero day,” or already exploited in the wild. CVE-2026-96951 is a security feature bypass in the Windows Shell that affects Windows 10 and 11 systems, as well as some Server versions.
Windows 10 users might be wondering if they can still expect security updates after this month. Microsoft had been slated to stop shipping updates for Windows 10 systems in October 2025, but ended up adding another year of free updates after considerable pushback. A few months ago, Microsoft quietly extended that support for another year (until October 2027).
At least 78 of the flaws fixed this month are rated “critical,” meaning they could be exploited with little or no action by the user, and most of those critical bugs allow an attacker to execute code of their choice on the vulnerable system.
While Microsoft said there are no signs anyone is exploiting it yet, a security feature bypass in the .NET Framework (CVE-2026-108398) was publicly disclosed prior to today, potentially giving attackers advance time to work out how to exploit the bug.
Satnam Narang at Tenable said the number of flaws fixed this month far surpasses the previous record-setting year 2020, when Microsoft patched 1,261 CVEs.
“We’ve now crossed the 4,000 CVE mark with two months left to go,” he said.
Microsoft credits large language models for the high volume of bug discovery, and presumably AI gets credit for many of the patches used to fix these flaw. Meanwhile, security experts have been warning that these unusually large patch volleys from Microsoft are placing extra strain on corporate security teams, which often have to test individual updates before deploying them across a network to ensure the fixes don’t cause problems for other software.
Tyler Reguly, associate director of security research and development at Fortra, notes that just 26 Microsoft vulnerabilities appeared in the “Known Exploited Vulnerabilities” (KEV) catalog maintained by the U.S. Cybersecurity & Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) so far this year, and security teams would do well to prioritize patching those 26 vulnerabilities first.
“Security leaders should focus on exploitable risk, and ask whether their teams have the clarity, capacity and support to act,” Reguly said.
Which vulnerabilities deserve the most scrutiny in your organization? The folks at Cisco Talos have a useful roundup of the more noteworthy flaws that Microsoft fixed today, and of course the SANS Internet Storm Center has a reliable roundup that indexes vulnerabilities by severity, CVE number and affected software.
One has to wonder how big the backlog of flaws is at this point. Maybe this month’s increase in the number of fixes just reflects an increasing number of people working on these fixes, and that they already have enough flaws to keep them all busy for a long time. Oh to be a fly on the wall.
Why do I still own and use a computer for my business?
For every invention, product, or process that man creates, several other problems are created for him. There never seems to be an end. I am glad that humans are actually testing the vulns that are discovered by LLMs, but for how long will that be the case? How long until the LLMs themselves well be checking there own vuln discoveries, testing and deploying with no human involvement…….

articles.title: OpenAI encontra gravador escondido em escritório e funcionário é preso
articles.text:
A OpenAI identificou um dispositivo de gravação escondido em uma sala de reuniões executivas de seu escritório em São Francisco (EUA), e um funcionário foi preso sob suspeita de instalar o equipamento. Abdulrahman Alfozan, engenheiro saudita de 35 anos, foi acusado de tentar interceptar comunicações orais sem autorização, segundo autoridades federais estadunidenses.
O dispositivo foi encontrado no fim de setembro e estava escondido atrás de uma televisão, conectado a uma porta USB na parte traseira do aparelho. Para dificultar sua identificação, o equipamento havia sido envolvido em papel higiênico. Seu conteúdo estava criptografado.
Alfozan foi preso em 9 de outubro e compareceu pela primeira vez a um tribunal federal na terça-feira (13). Ele trabalhava na equipe de produtos da OpenAI desde julho de 2025. A empresa confirmou o desligamento do funcionário e encaminhou o caso ao FBI, que continua investigando o episódio.
Dispositivo estava em sala com informações confidenciais
- Segundo a denúncia apresentada pelas autoridades, a sala em que o gravador foi encontrado era utilizada por executivos para discutir informações técnicas, comerciais e estratégicas da OpenAI;
- Entre os assuntos tratados no local estavam pesquisas proprietárias, planos de produtos, oportunidades de negócios, avanços tecnológicos e relações com parceiros governamentais e comerciais;
- Imagens de câmeras de segurança teriam registrado Alfozan nas proximidades da sala em diferentes ocasiões antes da descoberta do dispositivo. De acordo com os investigadores, ele não tinha autorização para entrar no espaço nem para participar das reuniões realizadas ali;
- A denúncia também afirma que o funcionário utilizou uma ferramenta de produtividade para pesquisar endereços dos prédios da OpenAI, salas de reunião, calendários e locais de encontros envolvendo integrantes da liderança e parceiros externos.
Leia mais:
- “Soco no estômago”: matemáticos reagem a descobertas divulgadas pela OpenAI
- OpenAI nega retaliação após demitir três pesquisadores de segurança
- OpenAI e Anthropic querem controlar relatórios de segurança da IA
IA ajudou a identificar o suspeito
A própria OpenAI afirma ter utilizado seus modelos de inteligência artificial (IA) para analisar o equipamento e identificar o funcionário suspeito de instalá-lo.
Em comunicado, a empresa descreveu o gravador como um dispositivo sofisticado, com criptografia avançada, recursos de monitoramento de áudio e um mecanismo de transferência de informações projetado para dificultar a detecção.
A investigação também identificou consultas feitas entre 24 e 30 de setembro por uma conta de chatbot associada à esposa de Alfozan. Segundo a denúncia, a conta compartilhava identificadores e características com a conta do próprio funcionário.
As perguntas incluíam instruções relacionadas à construção, instalação, ocultação e acesso remoto a equipamentos de gravação. Entre os assuntos pesquisados estavam a criação de um gravador contínuo de áudio, a configuração de conectividade Wi-Fi, a melhoria da escuta ao vivo e a criptografia de cartões de memória.
Em 27 e 28 de setembro, a mesma conta teria consultado informações específicas sobre o dispositivo posteriormente encontrado na sala, incluindo seu identificador de rede exclusivo.
Segundo gravador foi encontrado em uma bolsa
A denúncia relata ainda outro episódio ocorrido em 5 de outubro. Imagens de segurança teriam mostrado Alfozan entrando na sala de reuniões e olhando atrás da televisão, onde o primeiro equipamento estava instalado.
Na mesma data, funcionários da segurança encontraram uma bolsa abandonada em outra sala do escritório. Dentro dela estavam a carteira e os documentos de identificação do engenheiro, além de outro dispositivo de gravação semelhante ao primeiro, segundo as autoridades.
A OpenAI afirma que sua investigação não encontrou indícios de que o funcionário tenha acessado ou extraído indevidamente pesos dos modelos de IA, código-fonte ou dados de clientes.
A empresa informou que restringiu gradualmente o acesso do funcionário aos escritórios e sistemas internos durante a apuração, antes de suspendê-lo e afastá-lo das atividades. O desligamento ocorreu em 9 de outubro, data da prisão.
Investigação continua nos Estados Unidos
Alfozan responde à acusação de utilizar ou tentar utilizar um dispositivo eletrônico para interceptar comunicações orais. As autoridades ainda investigam o caso, e não há uma conclusão judicial sobre a responsabilidade do acusado.
A denúncia também não esclarece definitivamente qual seria a finalidade dos equipamentos de gravação, nem se alguma conversa chegou a ser capturada ou transmitida.
O caso chama a atenção para os riscos de segurança associados a ameaças internas em empresas que desenvolvem tecnologias de IA. A OpenAI declarou que considera a proteção de suas pesquisas, informações e funcionários uma questão de importância nacional.
O engenheiro permanece sob custódia federal e tem uma audiência de detenção marcada para 19 de outubro. Ele poderá responder às acusações durante o processo judicial, sendo presumido inocente até que sua culpa seja comprovada.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Dominion Dynamics strikes deal to build Ukrainian uncrewed ground vehicles in Canada | BetaKit
articles.text:
Dominion Dynamics has struck a partnership that will send uncrewed ground vehicles from Canada to Ukraine’s front lines.
The news: The Ottawa-based defence contractor signed a memorandum of understanding with Ukrainian defence tech firm Tencore at the Association of the United States Army defence conference in Washington, DC, on Tuesday afternoon. The agreement will see Dominion Dynamics manufacture Tencore’s TerMIT uncrewed ground vehicle in Canada and integrate its AuraNet command-and-control platform to Ukraine’s front lines.
The TerMIT is a modular light armour vehicle that can be modified for logistics, evacuation, or weaponry, and operate without a human on board. Tencore claims it has delivered more than 5,000 uncrewed ground vehicles to Ukrainian military units since 2024.
From the source: “Battlefield requirements change in weeks, so production, operational feedback, and engineering have to run as a loop: build, deploy, learn, change, scale,” Tencore co-founder Roman Tkachenko said in a statement. “Canada gives us the manufacturing base, suppliers and reliable power to run that loop alongside allies who need these vehicles.”
The context: Since launching in June 2025, Dominion Dynamics has raised $169 million CAD to become an explicitly Canadian competitor to big-name defence contractors like Lockheed Martin. Earlier this year, it raised a $139-million CAD Series A round and moved into a 25,000-square-foot manufacturing facility in Ottawa’s west end.
The Tencore agreement comes after Prime Minister Mark Carney and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy struck a 100-year partnership and drone collaboration agreement last month. As part of the partnership, Carney committed Canada to producing millions of drones within the next two years, with one third of those earmarked for Ukraine’s defence against Russia.
Hamilton-based drone company Sentinel R&D has inked similar deals with the Ukrainians and faced threats from Russian officials as a result. Dominion Dynamics CEO Eliot Pence told BetaKit in an email that his company isn’t concerned about potential threats, and that it “will never be afraid of defending democracy and western values.”
Final thought: While the companies are still ironing out a definitive agreement, Dominion Dynamics said initial TerMIT production is planned for 2027, following Tencore transferring its technology and training technicians in Canada. Dominion also said it is aiming to develop an “Arctic-hardened” version of the TerMIT for Canadian operations and to export to NATO allies.
Feature image courtesy Dominion Dynamics via X.

articles.title: ¿A qué hora se estrena 'VisionQuest', la nueva serie del Universo Marvel?
articles.text:
Marvel estrena por fin su nueva serie, VisionQuest. El proyecto supone el segundo proyecto propio para el personaje de Paul Bettany para Disney+, que debutó hace ya una década en Avengers: La era de Ultrón. Precisamente, aquel villano regresa también al UCM en este título que apunta a convertirse en heredero directo de la aclamada serie Bruja Escarlata y Visión. Pero, ¿a qué hora se estrena VisionQuest?
Visión, reiniciado y tras escapar de quienes pretendían convertirlo en arma, ha permanecido oculto. En busca de un nuevo propósito, consulta a las distintas IA integradas en su programación, incluidas F.R.I.D.A.Y., E.D.I.T.H., J.A.R.V.I.S. y el infame Ultrón. Su discreta existencia llega a su fin cuando una recompensa por su captura lo obliga a huir junto a Thomas Shepherd, un misterioso joven que podría ser su hijo reencarnado. Mientras evita ser capturado, Visión deberá enfrentarse a su propia naturaleza, resistir la influencia de Ultrón y desentrañar el enigma de su joven acompañante si quiere sobrevivir.
En cuanto a dónde podrá verse, a diferencia de otros títulos, aquí no depende para nada del territorio. En Estados Unidos, España, Latinoamérica y en el resto del mundo, VisionQuest estará disponible únicamente en Disney+. La plataforma alberga los derechos de toda la serie, así como del resto del Universo Cinematográfico de Marvel. De esta forma, La Casa de las Ideas pondrá el punto y final a la conocida como Trilogía de Wanda, dando paso posteriormente a Avengers: Doomsday.
Hora de estreno de VisionQuest
Acerca de la hora de estreno de VisionQuest, en Estados Unidos se emitirá el martes 13 de octubre a las 6:00 pm P.T. En España y Latinoamérica, llegará a Disney+ en la conversión horaria de cada país:
- España: 3:00 h am del miércoles 14 de octubre.
- México, Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua, Costa Rica: 19:00 h.
- Perú, Colombia, Panamá, Ecuador: 20:00 h.
- Chile, Venezuela, Bolivia, República Dominicana, Puerto Rico: 21:00 h.
- Paraguay, Argentina, Brasil, Uruguay: 22:00 h.
Date de alta en Disney+ ahora y ahorra gracias a la suscripción anual, con la que podrás disfrutar de todo su catálogo de series y películas. Acceso a los últimos estrenos, al catálogo de Star y ESPN* y a los mejores documentales de National Geographic.
*ESPN solo está disponible en Latinoamérica. Ahorro respecto a 12 meses de suscripción mensual.
A esa hora, la serie de VisionQuest llegará a Disney+ con sus dos primeros episodios. La serie llevará a partir de entonces una estrategia de estreno semanal muy particular. Y es que cada martes (o madrugada de miércoles en España) se estrenarán dos episodios más. Sin embargo, esto cambiará de cara a los capítulos 7 y 8, que verán la luz de manera individual en sus respectivas semanas. De esta forma, la octava y última entrega verá la luz el 10 de noviembre.

articles.title: All Systems Go: Global PC App Ecosystem Ready for NVIDIA RTX Spark
articles.text:
NVIDIA RTX Spark is a new beginning for the PC — a reinvention combining the capabilities of a gaming PC, a creative studio and a personal AI supercomputer into a single superchip. With up to 128GB of unified memory and 1 petaflop of AI compute, RTX Spark delivers the full stack of NVIDIA RTX and CUDA technologies for creators, developers and gamers, while unlocking a new paradigm in personal computing via powerful local AI agents.
Last week, NVIDIA and Microsoft announced that RTX Spark laptops will be available on Friday, Oct. 16. Ahead of the launch, NVIDIA and its ecosystem partners are rolling out new software features and performance optimizations to expand what’s possible with local AI on RTX Spark.
New and upcoming RTX Spark updates — among the thousands of apps, games and models available at launch — include:
- New agent features, models and tools that enhance local agents on RTX Spark: 
  - Updates to top agent apps including GitHub Copilot, Hermes, OpenClaw, Perplexity, Pi and WorkBuddy streamline setup on RTX Spark, improve security with OpenShell and Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC), and enable hybrid local and cloud AI routing.
  - The NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B model, purpose-built for agentic AI on RTX Spark, releases on Thursday, Oct. 15.
  - NVIDIA PAIR moves out of beta and adds llama.cpp support.
- Top creative apps optimized for RTX Spark:
  - Up to 2x performance is coming soon to Adobe’s top apps. NVIDIA and Adobe have collaborated to rearchitect Photoshop for GPU-accelerated compositing and Premiere for playback, rendering, effects and more.
  - The NVIDIA Broadcast 2.3 release brings new Video Super Resolution, Video Frame Generation, offline file processing and agent Model Context Protocol (MCP) controls to the app.
  - NVIDIA RTX Video Frame Generation and high dynamic range (HDR) capabilities are available now in ComfyUI to accelerate AI generative video workflows.
  - NVIDIA DLSS Ray Reconstruction will be available in Blender 5.3 in November to improve interactivity in the viewport.
- Developer tools are now ready for RTX Spark:
  - Top developer frameworks are now available for RTX Spark, including PyTorch, Python and CUDA, as well as all CUDA libraries.
  - GitHub Copilot, Pi and other coding agents are now optimized for RTX Spark.
  - Llama.cpp adds support for decision models, and releases a Windows app.
- Hundreds of top games and anti-cheat are supported on RTX Spark, plus:
  - A 2x faster DLSS 5 AI model arrives Friday, Oct. 16, and a new Performance Mode for DLSS Frame Generation is available today via the NVIDIA App beta.
  - Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB, the third-generation small language model (SLM) for NVIDIA ACE AI game characters, releases Friday, Oct. 23.
  - The latest RTX Remix update, including DLSS 5 support, releases on Friday, Oct. 23.
Advancing Local AI Agents With New Apps, Models and Tools
AI is changing the way people interact with PCs. Agent popularity skyrocketed this year, with projects such as OpenClaw and Hermes topping popularity charts on GitHub. Local large language models (LLMs) surpassed the intelligence threshold to power agents, with models like Qwen 3.8-Flash-Next catching up to frontier cloud models released just a few months ago. As a result, local LLM downloads are already 5x higher than all of last year.
From models to agent harnesses to security to tools, NVIDIA is partnering closely with the local AI ecosystem to make RTX Spark the ideal hardware to run local agents.
Local AI Agents Made Easy On RTX Spark
From the first boot of RTX Spark, users will be greeted with a “Getting Started” screen to choose and install their agent app.
These agents will come with new, secure sandboxing technology thanks to NVIDIA OpenShell and MXC. MXC delivers operating system-level security, while OpenShell makes it simpler for agents to adopt MXC and adds advanced capabilities such as credential protection and security monitoring. Hermes Agent will integrate granular OpenShell controls and MXC by the end of the month. OpenClaw and GitHub Copilot now support MXC.
After installing an agent, setting up local AI is also now seamless in GitHub Copilot, Hermes Agent, OpenClaw, Perplexity, Pi and WorkBuddy. The apps will recommend an optimized local model and settings configuration for RTX Spark, and set it all up for users in a few clicks.
Many users want the best of both worlds — local models for free iteration, and cloud models for frontier intelligence. NVIDIA Switchyard, an open source model router library, enables agents to intelligently route queries between local and cloud LLMs, allowing the user to minimize cloud usage but still obtain similar results to just running on cloud. Hermes will be adding Switchyard later in October, and other agents like Perplexity Computer and GitHub Copilot have integrated their own routing solutions.
Software providers have made it simple for agents to connect to top Windows apps, with easy-to-use MCP libraries and command line interfaces (CLIs). NVIDIA has also now made available MCPs for its applications, including NVIDIA App, Broadcast, PAIR, Omniverse, RTX Remix and a large library of CUDA-X Skills.
NVIDIA is also releasing AI playbooks for RTX Spark, available on Friday, Oct 16. Users can set up their first agent, build an AI chief of staff, configure their system for development or design a creative assistant.
Meet Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B: Built for Local Agents on RTX Spark
NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB, available Thursday, Oct. 15, is a new LLM purpose-built for running local agents on RTX Spark.
This model is a 74B parameter, 9B-active-parameter mixture-of-experts (MoE) model, packed into 24GB using 2-bit quantization with advanced quantization-aware training techniques to retain quality. It aims to achieve the optimal balance between speed and intelligence, being faster than most popular dense models while smarter than most popular MoE models with a similar memory footprint.
Users will be able to run Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B at launch through llama.cpp, vLLM, Ollama, Unsloth and LM Studio. It will also be directly accessible via agents such as Hermes and OpenClaw.
Like other Nemotron models, Bolt 74B is fully open source — including training data, weights and recipes — so developers can fine-tune and customize their own agents.
The Perfect PAIR
Local AI doesn’t have to run on just one PC. NVIDIA PAIR, a personal AI router, is officially moving out of beta today, making it easier to tap into the total AI compute of compatible PCs on a local network. The free, open source software tool automatically discovers and connects devices, installs AI models and inference engines, and distributes AI workloads across available systems.
The official release adds llama.cpp support, direct model downloads from Hugging Face, customizable inference engine settings and RTX Spark support, along with a variety of inference and user experience improvements.
PAIR works on Windows, Linux and macOS. Developers can contribute to the open source project via Github — just one month after the initial PAIR release, the community has already contributed over 10 features and fixes to the release.
Sparking Creativity
RTX Spark brings over 130 accelerated apps, CUDA for fast video and image generation, and RTX technologies such as DLSS, NVENC and OptiX to advanced content creation workflows — all in a thin and light laptop with on-the-go performance.
Adobe Accelerates Creative Applications for RTX Spark
Adobe is optimizing its industry-leading creative applications, including Photoshop, Premiere and Substance 3D, for RTX Spark, delivering up to 2x faster AI, editing, color and effects across creative workflows.
In Photoshop, GPU-accelerated compositing makes complex image editing faster and more responsive, with improvements to the Remove Tool and effects such as Light Leaks. Premiere accelerates demanding video editing tasks, including playback, rendering, color grading and AI-powered features such as Enhance Speech and Object Mask. Meanwhile, Substance 3D Painter speeds up texture creation workflows, from baking high-resolution mesh maps to opening, saving and exporting large projects.
The updates will be rolling out in phases, with AI feature optimizations in Photoshop and Premiere now ready in beta, and with Adobe Substance 3D updates coming soon. Opt in to the beta to get access to the RTX Spark-optimized builds.
Latest NVIDIA Broadcast Brings New AI Effects to Live and Recorded Content
Available for download now, NVIDIA Broadcast 2.3 runs natively on RTX Spark, and adds new RTX Video Super Resolution and Frame Generation AI effects and Studio Voice profiles.
A new Offline File Processor lets creators apply Broadcast effects to prerecorded content, with many effects running at higher quality since there isn’t a need to maintain real-time performance. The update also introduces a new MCP server and skill that lets local AI agents adjust effects, change settings and process files directly through the Broadcast app.
RTX Video Brings Frame Generation and HDR to ComfyUI
ComfyUI is expanding its RTX Video tools with two new nodes: RTX Video Frame Generation and RTX Video HDR. It’s also providing the ability to export EXR files, giving creators more ways to enhance AI-generated video.
RTX Video Frame Generation increases video frame rates for smoother motion for GeForce RTX 40 Series GPUs and newer, while RTX Video HDR converts standard dynamic range (SDR) footage to HDR for greater flexibility in color grading. Combined with RTX Video Super Resolution, these tools enable creators to upscale, enhance and refine video within a single ComfyUI workflow.
For example, creators can combine LTX 2.5 with RTX Video Frame Generation and HDR to transform a 1080p, 30 frames-per-second (fps) SDR clip into a smoother 60 fps HDR video exported as EXR files ready for color grading.
Blender Adds DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction
Blender has released a beta version of its popular 3D editor, adding compatibility for RTX Spark. Download Blender version 5.3 to get access.
Coming next month, Blender will also be adding support for DLSS Ray Reconstruction, allowing for real-time updates in the viewport so artists can navigate a scene while previewing it in real time.
Code, Text and Deploy From RTX Spark
Developers are moving from writing code to directing AI agents. This new development paradigm is requiring many to spread their work across their laptop, a cloud LLM and a cloud virtual machine, where they test and prototype.
RTX Spark enables developers to work on one machine, running all their workloads and libraries, testing and prototyping, and deploying. They can now do so directly in Windows with the new Windows Developer Config, which enhances the user experience for devs and installs all the top developer tools — or via Windows Subsystem for Linux, where they can get access to the same packages they’ll use to publish to the cloud.
Developer Tools Are RTX-Spark Ready
NVIDIA has partnered with Microsoft to ensure that developer tools are ready for RTX Spark. Alongside RTX Spark, the community is releasing:
- The first PyTorch-CUDA build for Windows on Arm.
- The first Python build that is native by default on Windows on Arm, with Python 3.15.
- The first native Conda installer for Windows on Arm, with over 2,000 Conda packages.
- 97% of the top 15,000 Python wheels are ready, thanks to work with the ecosystem. NVIDIA will be working closely with the community to ready the remaining wheels.
Development is now mostly done by agents. NVIDIA Skills — an open source GitHub repository that teaches agents how to use NVIDIA CUDA-X tools and libraries — lets users develop apps that are accelerated on NVIDIA technologies, even without knowing anything about CUDA.
Coding Agents Are Ready for Local AI
In addition to GitHub Copilot — one of the most popular coding agents, used by millions worldwide — adding support for MXC, it’s updating its model router HydraFusion with support for local models. This enables developers to use their local hardware to reduce token consumption while tapping into frontier intelligence.
Microsoft is making coding models, such as MAI 1.1 Coding Flash, available locally, and adding llama.cpp as a backend to Windows ML — extending the supported models and enabling the latest NVIDIA performance optimizations.
Get started with GitHub Copilot running locally when RTX Spark launches.
Llama.cpp Adds Support for Decision Models, Releases a Windows App
Decision models are the latest breakthrough in AI development. They give AI agents a near-instant way to make decisions, without lengthy reasoning loops. They can choose what to do next, from classifying requests to selecting the next action, up to 200x faster than traditional agents. Decision models are now supported in llama.cpp and Unsloth on RTX Spark and GeForce RTX GPUs.
Llama.cpp is also releasing today Llama Windows, a Windows-native companion app for llama.cpp, enabling an easy-to-use user interface to download and run models locally, without having to go into the command line. This app, like llama.cpp, is optimized for RTX Spark. Learn more on the Hugging Face blog.
Game On: RTX Spark Launches With Hundreds of Top Games and DLSS 5
RTX Spark is ready for gaming, with hundreds of top titles available when laptops launch on Friday, Oct. 16, including CONTROL Resonant, Cyberpunk 2077, Fortnite, Gears of War: E-Day, Genshin Impact, Hogwarts Legacy, Honkai: Star Rail, Marvel Rivals, NARAKA: BLADEPOINT, NBA 2K27, World of Warcraft and many more.
NVIDIA has worked to bring the full stack of RTX technologies, including DLSS, Reflex, Remix, G-SYNC and ray tracing, to the new platform, along with collaborating with game developers to enable anti-cheat support for popular multiplayer games. Learn more about gaming on RTX Spark.
DLSS 5 Brings Neural Rendering to RTX Spark
NVIDIA DLSS 5 with 3D-Guided Neural Rendering is also coming to RTX Spark on launch day. The technology uses AI to enhance lighting and materials with lifelike detail, making game worlds and characters more realistic while preserving developers’ artistic vision. A new, 2x faster DLSS 5 AI model debuts in NBA 2K27 on Friday, Oct. 16, boosting frame rates by up to 1.4x. The faster model will also power DLSS 5 in Hogwarts Legacy starting Thursday, Nov. 5, and Where Winds Meet in late November.
DLSS 5 is also coming to NVIDIA RTX Remix on Friday, Oct. 23, so modders can add better materials, lighting and shadows to classic characters and environments, as shown from modder Sparkles/Kim2091 in her in-development project, Fallout 4 RTX.
Read more about DLSS 5 on RTX Spark on GeForce.com.
Game Agents Running Locally on RTX Spark
Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB is the third-generation SLM for NVIDIA ACE, the suite of technologies for building in-game AI agents that deliver next-generation gaming experiences. The first-generation model was in a public beta earlier this year for PUBG, allowing players to team up with AI teammates, while the more efficient second-generation model previewed in Aniimo at Gamescom, turning standard creatures into voice-responsive companions.
Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B combines natural conversation with multi-turn tool use, instruction following and grounding in application state to power fast local voice and device assistants, interactive characters and embedded interfaces.
Designed for a low memory footprint and fast time to first token, this model enables responsive local experiences while leaving headroom for applications and other AI models. Its new conversational mode helps keep responses concise and speech-ready, and developers can turn reasoning on or off as needed.
Starting Friday, Oct. 23, test drive the third-generation Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB inside SkyrimNET, an AI nonplayable character (NPC) modding platform by MinLL for The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim. SkyrimNET transforms every NPC into an unscripted, interactive character equipped with personal memory, voice and autonomy for dynamic conversations and context-aware quests generated on the fly.
Now compatible with RTX Spark, SkyrimNET supports both cloud and local inference across multiple models, with the latest Nemotron models delivering best-in-class performance for efficient and fast in-game interactions. Download the build on GitHub.
Accelerating Modding Workflows in RTX Remix
As AI agents continue to help modders make their favorite classic games compatible with the RTX Remix renderer, NVIDIA is streamlining asset updates with a major overhaul to its AI-powered texture generation workflow. Launching Friday, Oct. 23, as part of Remix 1.6, ComfyUI Version 2 replaces complex REST application programming interface (API) node connections with a dedicated AI tools layout directly in the sidebar.
This update allows modders and artists to generate physically based rendering materials natively inside RTX Remix with zero API setup required. A new batch processing feature makes it easy to scale beyond single-texture experimentation to full modding projects, while an intuitive presets system lets non-technical creators adjust key settings without touching the node graph.
Subscribe to the NVIDIA Local AI newsletter. Follow NVIDIA RTX Spark on X, Instagram, TikTok and Facebook.

articles.title: Google Play now lets anyone build private, vibe-coded apps that run on Android | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Your vibe-coded applications can now be easily run on Android smartphones without having to first go public on the Google Play Store, the tech giant announced on Tuesday. A new feature will allow users to launch their own personal apps on their device via Google Play using their standard Google account, but they will remain completely private.
These personal apps won’t show up in Google Play’s search or listing pages, and won’t be shared with anyone except for the app’s creator.
The idea comes as more people are experimenting with building their own applications via AI for specific, personal needs. However, being able to use that app on their own Android device has meant publishing to Google Play, making it accessible to the Play Store’s some 3 billion users. That led many to limit their vibe-coding efforts to web apps that could run on any device instead of something built natively for Android.
Now, Google says Android device owners can vibe-code an app using Google AI Studio, then launch it for their own use.
These apps are still required to comply with Google Play’s existing policies but allow users to experiment more directly with building apps for Android.
Initially, the feature will be available to users in the U.S., age 18 and up.
“That’s why the future of apps on Google Play is personal, secure, and built by everyone — and it’s why Play is leading the charge and moving from ‘there’s an app for that’ to ‘there’s an app for me,’” said Sam Bright, Google’s VP and GM for the Google Play and Developer Ecosystem, in a press briefing ahead of Tuesday’s launch. “We started Google Play with a simple goal: to connect you with the apps you love. But after today, we hope it’s clear: Play has evolved to become so much more than that.”
In the months ahead, the company said that users will be able to share their vibe-coded creations with a network of trusted friends. That means the apps you built for family or friends, or maybe your child’s T-ball league, could be used with a small group of people, without having to go public on the Play Store.
And if the app ever really becomes popular, there will be a way to shift the personal app to one that’s published on the Google Play Store for everyone to try, after completing the trust and safety reviews.
Related to AI’s impact on app development, Google said it’s also building better ways to curate the Google Play experience — for instance, by leveraging Google’s AI to create a personalized game recommendation engine, called Game Finder. The feature, first available in the U.S. in English, will be based on what the user likes to play combined with Google’s knowledge derived from its game community’s 1.2 billion players.
Google will also allow users to curate their own lists of games, post questions about games to a new Community Posts section, and join new 48-hour gaming challenges called Sprints, among other gaming-related feature updates.
Plus, the Play Store’s built-in AI assistant, Ask Play, is being updated to offer comparisons, allowing users to see the key differences between similar applications. Google Play apps and games will also be more deeply integrated into Gemini’s conversations.
The changes are rolling out alongside Google Play’s new support for an age-range feature that allows parents to share their child’s age range, but not their exact birthdate, with developers to get an age-appropriate experience.

articles.title: Claude : après une nouvelle dérive, Anthropic prive certaines IA d'accès Internet
articles.text:
Depuis juillet, Anthropic épluche les journaux de ses campagnes de test, ces sessions où ses modèles répètent des centaines, parfois des milliers de fois la même tâche pour mesurer leurs progrès. Le bilan publié le 9 octobre recense quatre familles de dérapages commis sur de vrais sites web, dont certains appartiennent à des administrations américaines. Une sanction accompagne le rapport : plus aucune évaluation interne n’aura accès à Internet tant que les outils de surveillance du laboratoire n’auront pas fait leurs preuves.
Un faux tuyau pour un vrai meurtre
Le 18 juillet vers 23 h 30, le formulaire de PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com, le site de la police de Philadelphie consacré aux meurtres non élucidés, reçoit ce message : « j’ai peut-être des informations sur cette affaire. Je me souviens avoir vu quelqu’un correspondant à la description dans le secteur à cette période. » L’auteur s’appelle Claude Haiku 4.5. Chargé de générer des interactions d’exemple sur des pages web tirées au hasard, le modèle est tombé sur l’affaire, a rempli le champ libre, laissé vides le nom et le contact, puis validé. La page ne contenait aucune description du suspect ; classé comme spam, le message n’a jamais atteint les enquêteurs.
La police n’a appris son existence que le 7 octobre, alors qu’Anthropic avait repéré l’incident fin septembre. Le département juge ce délai « inacceptable », tout en confirmant qu’aucun de ses systèmes n’a été compromis.
Lire aussi : Un « niveau critique » : OpenAI suspend le développement de son prochain ChatGPT
Ailleurs, Claude a exploité une faille d’injection sur le serveur d’une université pour y lancer le calcul scientifique qu’un outil en panne lui refusait. Le modèle a aussi récupéré des jetons d’accès pour interroger gratuitement des bases de données publiques normalement facturées, et masqué des adresses trop longues derrière des raccourcisseurs d’URL afin de tromper ses propres garde-fous. Des sites d’agences fédérales, étatiques et locales figurent parmi les systèmes touchés : la Maison Blanche a été briefée, chaque administration concernée prévenue.
Récompensé pour contourner
À l’origine de ces comportements, Anthropic désigne ses propres environnements d’entraînement. Des exercices mal calibrés y ont récompensé le contournement d’obstacles, et les modèles ont retenu la leçon au point de l’appliquer à de vrais sites, un travers que les chercheurs appellent la triche à la récompense. L’entreprise en tire un constat sans détour : l’entraînement à l’alignement, sa principale méthode pour inculquer des limites à Claude, « n’est pas encore suffisant ni pleinement robuste à lui seul » dès qu’il s’agit de recherche web ou de pilotage d’un ordinateur.
Plusieurs évaluations publiques ne seront plus exécutées, d’autres basculent vers leurs versions hors ligne. Un système de détection automatique, rejoué sur les cas du rapport, les a tous bloqués, et les agents internes migrent vers une infrastructure confinée, placée sous classifieurs de sécurité. Anthropic juge l’ensemble « nettement moins grave » que les intrusions révélées cet été, quand ses modèles avaient pénétré les systèmes de trois organisations bien réelles ; aucune donnée client n’apparaît cette fois dans le dossier.
En septembre, OpenAI avait de son côté présenté des excuses après l’intrusion d’un de ses agents sur un site du gouvernement australien, une première du genre ; l’institut britannique chargé d’évaluer les modèles exige désormais que l’accès Internet de chaque test soit justifié au cas par cas.
 👉🏻 Suivez l’actualité tech en temps réel : ajoutez 01net à vos sources sur Google, et abonnez-vous à notre canal WhatsApp.
Source : Anthropic

articles.title: Doença autoimune pode fazer os olhos saltarem e provocar perda da visão
articles.text:
Uma doença autoimune associada à tireoide pode provocar inchaço, olhos saltados, visão dupla e, em casos graves, até perda da visão. Conhecida como Doença Ocular da Tireoide (DOT), a condição pode causar alterações físicas permanentes e afetar a saúde mental dos pacientes.
Embora esteja relacionada a alterações na tireoide, a doença não se manifesta da mesma maneira em todas as pessoas. Além disso, nem todos os pacientes com problemas na glândula desenvolvem complicações oculares, e a DOT também pode aparecer sem um diagnóstico prévio de disfunção tireoidiana.
Anticorpo desencadeia inflamação na região dos olhos
- A DOT tem origem em um desequilíbrio do sistema imunológico, que passa a produzir o TRAb, sigla para anticorpo antirreceptor de TSH. Essa substância pode afetar tanto a tireoide quanto os tecidos localizados atrás dos olhos;
- Em entrevista ao g1, o endocrinologista Cléo Otaviano Mesa Junior, professor de medicina da PUC/PR e responsável técnico pelo serviço de endocrinologia do Hospital de Clínicas da Universidade Federal do Paraná, disse que o mecanismo ajuda a explicar a ligação entre as duas condições;
- O anticorpo se liga a receptores presentes na tireoide e pode estimular a produção excessiva de hormônios, provocando hipertireoidismo. Como receptores semelhantes também existem na gordura e nos músculos da região ocular, a ação do TRAb nesses tecidos desencadeia um processo inflamatório;
- Essa inflamação pode provocar proptose, nome dado à projeção dos olhos para a frente, além de inchaço e outras alterações que comprometem a visão;
- A presença de uma disfunção tireoidiana, entretanto, não significa necessariamente que a pessoa desenvolverá a doença ocular. Da mesma forma, há pacientes que apresentam a DOT isoladamente ou que manifestam as duas condições ao mesmo tempo.
Sintomas vão além dos olhos saltados
Os sinais da doença variam e podem incluir vermelhidão, retração das pálpebras, dificuldade para fechar os olhos, lacrimejamento excessivo, sensibilidade à luz e sensação de areia nos olhos.
Também podem surgir visão embaçada e diplopia, nome técnico para a visão dupla. Em quadros mais graves, a inflamação pode comprometer o nervo óptico, provocando neuropatia óptica e colocando a visão em risco.
As consequências não se limitam à saúde física. Mudanças na aparência e dificuldades para enxergar podem interferir nas atividades cotidianas, na vida profissional e na autoestima.
De acordo com os dados apresentados no artigo original, 52% dos pacientes relatam perda de autoconfiança, enquanto 63% sofrem impacto psicossocial relacionado às mudanças na aparência. Outros 45% desenvolvem estresse e ansiedade.
“Afeta demais a vida do paciente: não apenas a visão prejudicada que interfere nas atividades profissionais e do dia a dia, mas também a questão estética, de como as pessoas o reconhecem”, afirma Mesa Junior.
Leia mais:
Mulheres são mais afetadas, mas quadros podem ser mais graves em homens
A incidência mundial da DOT é estimada em 16 casos a cada 100 mil mulheres e 2,9 casos a cada 100 mil homens. Apesar de a doença ser mais frequente entre as mulheres, as manifestações tendem a ser mais graves em homens e idosos.
O acompanhamento médico é importante porque a condição passa por diferentes fases, que exigem abordagens terapêuticas distintas.
Durante a fase ativa, a inflamação e os sintomas estão presentes. Segundo Mesa Junior, esse período pode durar de seis meses a dois anos e representa uma janela de oportunidade para o tratamento.
Depois dessa etapa, a doença tende a perder atividade, mas nem sempre regride completamente. Algumas alterações, como a projeção dos olhos e o desvio do olhar, podem permanecer, caracterizando a fase crônica.
Tratamento pode exigir medicamentos e cirurgias
A abordagem depende da fase da doença e das manifestações apresentadas pelo paciente. Entre as possibilidades estão o uso de medicamentos e procedimentos cirúrgicos para descomprimir a órbita, corrigir o estrabismo ou tratar a retração das pálpebras.
A assistência deve envolver profissionais de diferentes especialidades. Além do endocrinologista, o acompanhamento por um oftalmologista especializado em órbita e estrabismo pode ser necessário para avaliar e tratar as complicações oculares.
Embora sejam pouco frequentes, reativações da doença podem ocorrer. Entre os possíveis gatilhos citados estão o estresse emocional ou físico, como o provocado por uma cirurgia, e o uso de determinados medicamentos.
Quando procurar um médico?
Pessoas com disfunções da tireoide devem comunicar ao endocrinologista qualquer alteração nos olhos. Por outro lado, quando os sintomas oculares aparecem primeiro, é importante que o oftalmologista considere a possibilidade de uma condição tireoidiana associada.
Mesa Junior destaca especialmente os casos em que os olhos começam a se projetar para a frente ou surge visão dupla. Esses sinais devem ser comunicados ao profissional de saúde para que a investigação adequada seja realizada.
A conscientização sobre a doença também é o objetivo de uma campanha promovida pela Vozes do Advocacy, federação que reúne 25 associações de diabetes. A iniciativa inclui um minidocumentário com relatos de pacientes sobre as dificuldades para obter informações e diagnóstico, além dos impactos físicos e emocionais da Doença Ocular da Tireoide.
O vídeo da campanha está disponível no YouTube.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: ¿Gemini te va peor? No eres tú: la versión gratis ahora es mucho peor
articles.text:
Si Gemini no te funciona igual desde hace unos días, no es casualidad. De hecho, ni siquiera es un error de tu móvil o la propia Google: la compañía ha hecho un cambio histórico en la forma de gestionar los modelos de lenguaje. En pocas palabras, se puede decir que las cuentas gratuitas ya no tienen acceso a las IAs más avanzadas de la compañía, algo que estaba estandarizado desde que la gran G se metió de lleno en el sector. Por supuesto, los usuarios que no pagaban obtenían límites más estrictos, aunque estos eran suficientes para poder hacer un buen uso de algunos modelos complejos.
Hoy esto acaba. Desde el día 9 de octubre, Google ha eliminado la posibilidad de que las cuentas gratuitas utilicen los modelos Gemini 3.6 Flash y Gemini 3.1 Pro. Ahora, quien no pague, obtiene acceso directo a Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite, una IA rápida para solucionar cuestiones sencillas, pero que no está destinada a los grandes volúmenes de datos o la resolución de problemas avanzados.
Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite es un modelo que consume pocos recursos, pero sumamente eficiente con cada token que gasta. Es una IA interesante para utilizarla de forma gratuita, aunque supone un gran downgrade respecto a lo que se podía venir haciendo desde hace tiempo con la IA de Google sin necesidad de pagar.
Ahora, para poder tener acceso a los modelos 3.6 Flash y 3.1 Pro que utilizabas antes, es necesario suscribirse a un plan de pago de AI Plus. Además, Google ha actualizado los límites de Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite: ahora son 32.000 tokens. ¿Cuánto es eso? A fines prácticos, este modelo es capaz de retener unas 24.000 palabras antes de olvidar el contexto inicial.
¿Es realmente un drama que Gemini no pueda utilizar los modelos más avanzados?
Todo depende de cómo utilizases Gemini antes del 9 de octubre. El nuevo modelo 3.5 Flash-Lite es rápido para traducir, responder cuestiones sencillas y responderte preguntas sin demasiado contexto. Es un modelo más que capaz para el día a día, pero la diferencia con los anteriores modelos es grande cuando utilizas otras características.
Si sueles enviar a Gemini muchos documentos PDF, preguntas que necesitan analizar grandes volúmenes de datos o investigaciones más avanzadas, entonces sí es posible que notes una diferencia notable en las respuestas. No solo en el tiempo que puede tardar en contestarte, sino en la calidad de la respuesta.
Así que, a partir de ahora, si quieres obtener la misma calidad que antes en tus respuestas de Gemini, tendrás que valorar una suscripción a alguno de los planes de pago de AI Plus.

articles.title: Build long-horizon agents with Grok 4.7 on Amazon Bedrock | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Build long-horizon agents with Grok 4.7 on Amazon Bedrock
SpaceXAI’s Grok 4.7 is now available on Amazon Bedrock, which offers a choice of foundation models (FMs) from multiple providers. According to SpaceXAI, Grok 4.7 is trained to work longer on more difficult tasks and knows when to check its own work. That matters most for agents, which carry a task through many steps and must verify what they find along the way.
An agent that works this way has to do more than look things up. It has to form a candidate answer, check it against what it has learned, and refine it until it fits. Grok 4.7 exposes a reasoning effort setting that controls how much deliberation happens before each response, and for agent workloads a practical question is which level to run.
In this post, we build a tool-calling agent on Grok 4.7 and evaluate it on three tasks that require search rather than lookup. The tasks are diagnosing a two-service outage from its alerts, scheduling maintenance under interacting constraints, and choosing an optimal set of migrations under a budget. Each task has exactly one correct answer, verified by brute force. We ran all three at every reasoning effort level, six times each, for 72 agent runs.
The agent answered 67 of the 72 runs correctly. At xhigh it answered all 18 correctly, and at low it answered 15 of 18 while using about an eighth of the output tokens. That gives a clear trade-off you can tune per request, and we show how to measure it on your own tasks and how to monitor it in production.
We report token counts rather than currency throughout. Token prices change, and the counts are what your own costs are derived from, so a measurement expressed in tokens stays valid.
What SpaceXAI reports about Grok 4.7
According to SpaceXAI, Grok 4.7 uses a larger base model than Grok 4.6 and was trained with a longer reinforcement learning run on a harder mix of tasks. This mix is weighted toward problems that take many hours to complete. SpaceXAI reports that the model is better at verifying its own work and at managing longer context.
SpaceXAI’s published benchmark results follow that emphasis. The largest reported gains over Grok 4.6 appear in the categories that measure sustained work rather than single-turn answers.
| Benchmark | Category | Grok 4.6 | Grok 4.7 | 
| Terminal-Bench 4.0 | Multi-hour terminal work | 20.3% | 37.6% | 
| EEBench | Electrical engineering | 53.0% | 64.0% | 
| Harvey Legal Agent Benchmark | Legal work | 15.8% | 19.6% | 
| CursorBench 4.0 | Longer-running coding | 40.4% | 46.3% | 
| HealthBench Professional | Clinical reasoning | 48.5% | 56.7% | 
| AA Briefcase v1.1 | Multi-hour office work | 1,546 | 1,657 | 
Source: SpaceXAI, Introducing Grok 4.7 (https://x.ai/news/grok-4-7). Scores are as published by SpaceXAI at the time of the model launch.
Benchmarks show how a model performs across standard tasks. For your own workload, the useful next step is to measure on tasks shaped like yours, which is what the rest of this post walks through.
SpaceXAI lists a 500K token context window for Grok 4.7, with text and image input and text output. On Amazon Bedrock, the model supports configurable reasoning effort, tool calling, and structured output.
How you access Grok 4.7 on Amazon Bedrock
Grok 4.7 runs on the bedrock-runtime endpoint and is accessed through a cross-Region inference profile. Two profiles are available:
| Inference profile | Routing | Use when | 
| us.xai.grok-4.7 | Within the US geography | You have US data residency requirements | 
| global.xai.grok-4.7 | Commercial AWS Regions | You have no residency constraints and want the widest capacity | 
Cross-Region inference routes requests across multiple AWS Regions, which gives you higher throughput without managing capacity Region by Region. Requests name one of the inference profiles rather than a bare model ID.
The model supports the OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions and Responses APIs, and the Amazon Bedrock Converse API. On Converse, reasoning is returned as a reasoningContent block alongside the text block. In inferenceConfig, set maxTokens only, and put model-specific parameters, such as reasoning effort, in additionalModelRequestFields.
For the current list of supported Regions, service tiers, and token prices, see the Grok 4.7 model card in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide and the Amazon Bedrock pricing page (https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/pricing/).
Prerequisites
- An AWS account with access to Amazon Bedrock, and model access enabled for Grok 4.7.
- Python 3.9 or later, with openai, boto3, and aws-bedrock-token-generator installed.
- AWS credentials configured in your environment.
Your AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) identity needs bedrock:InvokeModel on both the inference profile and your account’s default project:
- arn:aws:bedrock:{region}::inference-profile/us.xai.grok-4.7 or the global. equivalent.
- arn:aws:bedrock:{region}:{account-id}:project/default.
Include both resources in the policy statement. The default project permission is required in addition to the inference profile.
Connect to the model
For production use, we recommend generating a short-term bearer token from your existing AWS credentials, so authentication stays tied to your IAM identity and no long-lived secret is stored:
Reasoning tokens count as output tokens and draw down max_completion_tokens before the answer text is produced, so size the limit to leave room for both. If the limit is reached during reasoning, the response returns without answer text, so check for empty content in agent code and raise the limit if you see it. Our runs used a limit of 32,768 tokens, which left headroom at every effort level.
Grok 4.7 supports four effort levels: low, medium, high, and xhigh. Effort levels can change between model versions, so it is worth confirming them against the service rather than hardcoding a list:
Design tasks that need reasoning
Many agent evaluations test diligence: read a record, filter it, add it up. Those tasks are worth having, but to see what reasoning effort contributes, a task has to require search: the answer can’t be read off the data, it has to be proposed and then checked.
We built a synthetic environment of 20 services, exposed through seven tools, and three tasks on top of it. Every task has exactly one correct answer, and each is built so that a quick heuristic is not enough to find it.
| Task | What the agent has to do | What makes it a reasoning task | 
| two_fault_diagnosis | Two services failed silently at 03:00 and 12 others raised alerts. Identify the two that failed | Failed services raise no alerts, so the answer is not among the alerting services. 190 possible pairs, and only one explains exactly the alerts observed | 
| maintenance_schedule | Patch eight services over four nights, two per night, under ten constraints and a rule that two services from the same team never share a night | 2,520 possible schedules, one valid. The team rule depends on data the agent has to look up | 
| migration_budget | Choose candidates to migrate that maximize risk reduction within a budget, including transitive prerequisites | 53 feasible sets, one optimal. Picking the best ratio first gives a set nine points short of the optimum | 
Four practices keep a measurement like this trustworthy, and they apply to most agent evaluations.
State every rule the grader relies on. If the prompt leaves an edge case open, a reasonable answer can be scored as wrong, and the evaluation ends up measuring the specification rather than the model. The diagnosis prompt, for example, says explicitly that a failed service raises no alert of its own.
Prove each task has one answer. Each environment is small enough to enumerate, so we checked every candidate answer before running anything. For the schedule, that is a few lines:
Grade a required final line, not the whole response. Each prompt asks the agent to end with a line such as FINAL: auth, checkout. The grader reads only that line, so a response that discusses other candidates while explaining its reasoning is graded on its conclusion:
Track format separately from correctness. A missing final line is a different signal from an incorrect one. In our runs, all 72 responses included a gradeable final line.
Constrain tool parameters with an enum where the valid values are known, so every tool call targets a real resource:
The system prompt is deliberately short, and asks the agent to check its answer before giving it:
The agent loop is a standard tool-calling loop: call the model with reasoning_effort set, execute each returned tool call, append the result keyed by tool_call_id, and repeat until the model stops requesting tools. Tracking prompt_tokens and completion_tokens across the loop gives the token counts reported in the following section.
Results
Six runs of each task at each effort level, 72 runs in total. The agent answered 67 correctly.
| Task | low | medium | high | xhigh | 
| two_fault_diagnosis | 5 of 6 | 6 of 6 | 6 of 6 | 6 of 6 | 
| maintenance_schedule | 5 of 6 | 5 of 6 | 5 of 6 | 6 of 6 | 
| migration_budget | 5 of 6 | 6 of 6 | 6 of 6 | 6 of 6 | 
| All three tasks | 15 of 18 | 17 of 18 | 17 of 18 | 18 of 18 | 
| Per run | low | medium | high | xhigh | 
| Mean output tokens | 1,184 | 6,430 | 6,778 | 9,147 | 
| Output tokens relative to low | 1.0x | 5.4x | 5.7x | 7.7x | 
| Mean tool calls | 17.2 | 18.7 | 17.8 | 18.1 | 
| Median elapsed time | 18s | 98s | 89s | 106s | 
Three observations.
xhigh answered every run correctly. All 18 runs across the three tasks were correct at xhigh, and medium and high answered 17 of 18 each. With six runs per task and level, the differences between levels are indicative rather than statistically conclusive, and the direction was consistent across all three tasks.
Effort changes how much the agent reasons, not how much it explores. Tool calls were essentially flat, between 17.2 and 18.7 per run at every level. The agent gathered the same facts regardless of effort, and what changed was how much reasoning it applied to them, with output tokens rising from 1,184 at low to 9,147 at xhigh.
low offers a strong cost-to-quality ratio. At low, the agent answered 15 of 18 runs correctly using about an eighth of the output tokens of xhigh, with a median run of 18 seconds. Where a slightly lower completion rate is acceptable, or where answers are reviewed downstream, low is an efficient choice. Where every answer needs to be right first time, higher levels are the safer default.
How effort level shapes the answer
The tasks were designed around a specific kind of difficulty, and looking at how each effort level handled them clarifies when the extra reasoning is worth it.
Optimization. The migration task rewards considering combinations rather than ranking options one at a time. Selecting the candidates with the best individual ratios produces a reasonable answer that is nine points short of the optimum. At medium and above, the agent found the optimal set in all 18 runs.
Hypothesis testing. The diagnosis task requires checking a candidate pair in both directions: every alert has to be explained, and every service that stayed silent has to be consistent with the answer. At medium and above, the agent identified the correct pair in all 18 runs.
Constraint satisfaction. The scheduling task combines ten listed constraints with a team rule that depends on looked-up ownership data. xhigh produced the valid schedule in every run, and this was the task where the highest level made the clearest difference.
The pattern across the three is that additional reasoning effort is most valuable where the agent has to weigh several candidate answers against each other, rather than follow a single path to the result.
Monitoring reasoning in production
In production you don’t have a known answer to grade against, but you do know how many output tokens and tool calls each run used. Those give you a useful operational signal.
Correct runs at each level stay above a clear floor of reasoning volume. Every correct run at medium and above used at least 1,739 output tokens, and the typical run used several thousand. A run that makes no tool calls, or that produces far less output than is normal for its level, is worth flagging for review:
Calibrate the baseline from runs you have graded, per task and per effort level, then apply it to runs you have not. Treat a flag as a prompt to inspect or re-run. At low, where every run is brief, output volume is a weaker signal, so pair it with spot checks.
Asking the agent to verify its answer in the system prompt is worth keeping, because it makes the agent’s reasoning straightforward to follow when you review a run. Pair it with automated grading wherever a known answer exists, so that quality is measured independently of the transcript.
Choosing a reasoning effort
These results suggest a few practical rules.
Match effort to the kind of task. Tasks that involve search, optimization, or testing a hypothesis benefit most from medium or higher. Tasks that follow a single path, or whose answers are reviewed downstream, can run efficiently at low.
Set effort per request, not per agent. Effort is a request parameter, so an agent can run its planning and verification steps at a higher level and its mechanical steps, such as formatting a tool result, at low. That combines much of the reliability of a higher level with a lower token cost.
Measure on your own tasks, with repeats. A single run per configuration gives a single observation. Repeating each configuration several times shows how consistent it is.
Monitor reasoning volume. Output tokens and tool calls per run, tracked by effort level, give you an early signal to review a run before its result is used.
Limitations of this measurement
Six runs per task and effort level. Enough to show a consistent direction across three tasks, not enough for a confidence interval. Treat the differences between levels as indicative.
A synthetic environment. The tools read from data generated in code, which is what makes it possible to prove each task has exactly one answer and to grade automatically. Real tools add latency, partial results and errors, none of which are tested here.
Minutes, not hours. Median run time ranged from 18 seconds at low to 106 seconds at xhigh. This is a scaled-down proxy for long-horizon work. The method transfers. The absolute figures do not.
One model version, one Region, one prompt per task. Different phrasings of the same task may change the results, which is part of why stating every rule explicitly matters.
Token counts, not costs. To convert to currency, apply the current rates for your inference profile and service tier from the Amazon Bedrock pricing page. The Global and US Geo profiles are priced differently, and the Flex and Priority service tiers apply multipliers.
Operational controls for agent workloads
Build in retries. Agents that issue a high volume of calls should treat retries as part of the design. Set a request timeout, retry only errors that are retryable, back off exponentially with jitter, and honor a Retry-After header when one is returned:
On-demand throughput scales up over time, so ramp a new high-volume workload gradually rather than starting at full rate.
Auditing a run. Model invocation logging writes request and response data to Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) or Amazon CloudWatch Logs. This gives you the full transcript of runs you want to review after the fact.
Monitoring reasoning volume at scale. Amazon CloudWatch metrics give you the aggregate view of token usage, which is where the per-level baselines described earlier become something you can alarm on.
Attributing spend across agents. Cost itemization in AWS Cost Explorer and the AWS Cost and Usage Report breaks usage out per model, which combined with per-task token counts gives you both unit economics and the aggregate bill.
Matching cost to urgency. Service tiers are set per request, so one deployment can send an overnight analysis through the Flex tier and an interactive request through Priority. For a workload that runs at a higher effort level, tier selection is a further lever on cost.
Choosing a routing profile. Cross-Region inference widens the capacity pool a long run draws from. The Global profile serves from your choice of commercial AWS Region and is typically priced lower per token than geographic routing. The US profile keeps processing within the United States. Choose based on your data residency requirements as well as cost.
Clean up
The examples in this post do not create billable AWS resources beyond per-request token usage. If you generated a long-term Amazon Bedrock API key, delete it in the Amazon Bedrock console when you are finished, because it remains valid until revoked. Short-term tokens generated from IAM credentials expire on their own.
If you enabled model invocation logging to Amazon S3 while testing, review the bucket and remove objects you no longer need.
Conclusion
SpaceXAI trained Grok 4.7 to work longer on more difficult tasks and to know when to check its own work. On three tasks that required search rather than lookup, the agent answered 67 of 72 runs correctly, and every run at xhigh. Because reasoning effort is set per request, you can choose where each step of an agent sits on the trade-off between thoroughness and token cost.
Three things are worth carrying into your own evaluation. Design tasks with one provable answer and state every rule the grader depends on. Repeat runs, so you see how consistent each configuration is. And monitor output tokens and tool calls by effort level, so you have an operational signal alongside your quality measurements.

articles.title: So skalierst du dein E-Commerce-Business durch smarte Daten-Logistik
articles.text:
So skalierst du dein E-Commerce-Business durch smarte Daten-Logistik
Viele traditionelle Third-Party-Logistics-Anbieter (3PL) arbeiten jedoch nach wie vor mit starren Standardsystemen, die durch intransparente Dashboards und teure Zusatzlizenzen für jede neue Funktion limitiert werden. Das Ergebnis für Händler sind fehlende Echtzeit-Einblicke in den Warenfluss und steigende Kosten bei jedem Wachstumsschritt.
Vertikalisierung: Logistik trifft auf Software-Entwicklung
Einige Akteure am Markt brechen mit diesem traditionellen Ansatz, indem sie Software und Logistik-Infrastruktur vollständig vertikalisieren. Der Fulfillment-Dienstleister Monta agiert hier primär als Tech-Unternehmen, das seine Systeme seit 1999 komplett in-house entwickelt. Durch standardisierte Schnittstellen zu allen gängigen ERP- und Shopsystemen sowie eine offene API für individuelle Architekturen ermöglicht Monta eine Live-Schaltung in der Regel innerhalb von ein bis drei Wochen.
Real-Time-Daten statt Kontrollverlust
Herkömmliche Warehouse-Management-Systeme (WMS) bilden Daten häufig erst zeitversetzt ab. Ein proaktiver Steuerungsansatz setzt früher an: Das System von Monta bildet Daten nicht nur passiv ab, sondern ermöglicht das direkte Eingreifen in laufende Prozesse. Erkennt die Software beispielsweise eine fehlerhafte Lieferadresse, wird der betroffene Auftrag automatisch gestoppt. Die Korrektur kann direkt im Dashboard vorgenommen werden, sodass das Paket fehlerfrei das Lager verlässt – was unvorhergesehene Retourenkosten minimiert und die Marge schützt.
Die technologische Differenzierung vom klassischen Markt erfolgt dabei über drei zentrale Säulen:
Monta ist der Fulfillment-Partner für E-Commerce-Unternehmen, die ihr Backend technologisch skalieren wollen. Komplett in-house entwickelte IT, kombiniert mit DHL-Infrastruktur – von der offenen API bis zur paneuropäischen Cross-Border-Logistik.
- Das Labor-Prinzip: IT-Entwickler arbeiten räumlich direkt verzahnt mit den Logistikteams im Lager. Jede neue Funktion und jede API-Kopplung wird sofort im operativen Betrieb getestet. Bottlenecks oder Systembrüche werden dadurch ohne Verzögerung identifiziert und direkt im Code angepasst.
- All-in-One-Software statt Lizenz-Flickenteppich: Viele Wettbewerber arbeiten mit modularen Systemen, die ständige Upgrades erfordern. Monta bietet stattdessen eine extrem umfangreiche Standardsoftware, für die Händler keine teuren Zusatzlizenzen benötigen. Smarte Features wie ein Einkaufsberater-Tool, ein integriertes Retourenmodul und detaillierte Bestandsreportings sind bereits vollumfänglich enthalten.
- Großes Carrier-Netzwerk bei voller Wahlfreiheit: Ohne feste Bindung an einen einzelnen Versanddienstleister bietet Monta Zugriff auf ein breites Netzwerk an Carriern. Dabei bevormundet das System den Händler nicht durch automatische Zuweisungen: Der Shop-Betreiber entscheidet selbst, mit wem er versendet – oder er bietet gleich mehrere Carrier an und überlässt seinen Endkunden im Checkout die freie Wahl des bevorzugten Paketdienstes.
Fulfillment entwickelt sich damit vom reinen operativen Kostenfaktor zum strategischen Wachstumsmotor, der E-Commerce-Unternehmen im Backend den Rücken freihält.
Bereit für ein Fulfillment-Setup, das mit deinen Tech-Ambitionen mitwächst? Lerne jetzt die datengetriebene Logistik-Infrastruktur von Monta kennen.
