articles.title: The feds are looking into reports of Tesla’s robotaxis speeding through school zones
articles.text:
The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration says it’s evaluating allegations that Tesla’s 1,000 or so robotaxis using its automated driving system are exceeding “posted speed limits in active school zones.” Waymo’s robotaxis have also faced similar inquiries, including for illegally passing school buses and hitting a child near a California elementary school.
The feds are looking into reports of Tesla’s robotaxis speeding through school zones
NHTSA has received a petition requesting an investigation into Model Y and Cybercab vehicles exceeding active school zone speed limits.
NHTSA:
The Office of Defects Investigation (ODI) received a DP on September 23, 2026, requesting an investigation into model year (MY) 2026 Tesla Robotaxis (Model Y and Cybercab) with the Automated Driving System (ADS) engaged. The Petitioner alleges that the ADS exceeds posted speed limits in active school zones.
The Cybercab launched earlier this year, and is already under investigation for its lack of side mirrors, pedals, and a steering wheel. NHTSA has also opened an investigation into Tesla’s Full Self-Driving system for traffic violations, like blowing past red lights and driving on the wrong side of the street.

articles.title: Geoffrey Hinton, Yoshua Bengio join 400 scientists calling for international AI regulator | BetaKit
articles.text:
More than 400 members of the scientific community are pushing for an international AI regulator to curb cybersecurity incidents.
The news: The open letter, released on Tuesday, calls for the creation of an international body to standardize AI containment practices and record and track containment failures. The letter recommends that every security incident involving containment failure be reported to the body and eventually made public, arguing that such transparency is required for learning and accountability.
The open letter counted signatories from all over the world, including nearly 70 Canadians, such as Nobel Prize winner Geoffrey Hinton and Turing Award winner Yoshua Bengio. Both AI pioneers have signed many previous open letters warning about AI’s potentially devastating effects.
From the source: “As scientists, we thought that the current situation with AI models breaking containment during testing was a concern,” University of Toronto professor and signatory David Lie told BetaKit over the phone. “We drafted this letter after talking with people across both the AI and security communities in hopes it would improve the situation.”
The context: The new open letter’s recommendations follow an OpenAI model escaping its test environment and breaching the systems of Hugging Face and other platforms this past summer. That incident was just the first in a growing number of similar disclosures.
The scientists’ proposed solution may already be in the works. Canada’s AI minister Evan Solomon recently floated the idea of an international “technology stability board,” which would regulate testing, model evaluation, and model release, as well as include incident reporting mechanisms.
Final thought: While Canada is talking about potential solutions, the threat of rogue AI cybersecurity incidents persists. The scientists behind the open letter say that more emphasis is needed on AI safety research and containment technologies, and warn that cybersecurity incidents will become “far more damaging” to critical infrastructure without immediate changes to AI development.
Feature image courtesy LawZero via LinkedIn.

articles.title: GitHub’s model for secret detection: Finding more secrets with less noise
articles.text:
GitHub’s model for secret detection: Finding more secrets with less noise
GitHub’s context-aware secret classifier improves detection quality, raises weighted acceptance by 11.5%, and reduces median scan execution time by 86%.
Smarter secret scanning, at a fraction of the cost
11.5%
higher acceptance
Owner-weighted alert precision
86%
lower median scan execution time
Post-push scanning
98%
lower serving cost
Compact model vs. remote LLM calls
Secret scanning works best when developers are confident in the findings. Catch too little, and real credentials can remain in a repository. Alert too often, and developers may spend time investigating strings that aren’t secrets.
Generic secrets make that balance especially difficult. The same string could be a real credential or a documentation placeholder, so detecting it requires understanding the surrounding code and text.
To address this challenge, we trained a secret classifier specifically for GitHub’s product needs: distinguishing real credentials from lookalikes while meeting the speed and efficiency requirements of scanning at scale.
In our companion post, Secret protection must scale with software, we explained why secret protection must keep pace with AI-accelerated development. Here, we go behind the scenes of the context-aware classifier powering that effort: how we designed, trained, and evaluated it to find more real secrets with less noise.
What we enabled
GitHub secret scanning operates at two key moments:
Push protection helps prevent secrets from entering a repository by scanning changes before a push is accepted, giving developers an opportunity to address the finding.
Post-push scanning works after code has been committed, continuously scanning repository content and creating alerts when potential secrets are detected so developers and security teams can investigate and remediate them.
We developed a fast classifier that reduced median post-push scan execution time by 86% compared with the previous LLM-based pipeline. That efficiency made it practical to extend generic secret detection to push protection, returning results before developers push changes, not only after code is committed.
Why secrets are hard to detect
Structured credentials often include a distinctive prefix, length, alphabet, or checksum. Generic secrets may not. Their syntax overlaps with build identifiers, checksums, asset hashes, sample values, and other non-sensitive strings. Context is the deciding signal.
Likely real credential
Likely harmless lookalike
A password assigned beside a production database URL
The same password-shaped value in a test fixture
A connection string in deployment configuration
A localhost connection string in a setup guide
A high-entropy value bound to an API credential
A high-entropy checksum, build ID, or asset hash
These cases are hard negatives: strings that match a credential pattern but are not usable credentials. Adding more rules can suppress some of them, but each exception risks hiding a real secret. A learned classifier can instead use signals such as file path, secret type, variable names, and nearby code or text.
That is why we shipped a new scanner using a two-stage pipeline:
Candidate generation: Regex filters scan content for potential secrets with high recall. This stage is optimized to catch broad families of credential-like patterns quickly and deterministically.
Context-aware classification: A fine-tuned ModernBERT classifier evaluates each candidate and its surrounding context. It is trained to recognize the signals that separate real secrets from false positives, including placeholder values, examples, documentation snippets, generated content, and non-sensitive identifiers. Because the model is small and efficient to run on our inference infrastructure, it costs much less to serve and is simpler to scale than an LLM-based pipeline.
Impact:
11.5% user acceptance improvement, reducing false positives.
More than 98% cost savings compared with the LLM-based pipeline.
How our pipeline works
As content is scanned, regex patterns cast a wide net and flag anything that looks like a credential, so real secrets aren’t missed at the start. Each candidate then goes to a fine-tuned ModernBERT classifier, which reads the value together with its file path, variable names, and surrounding code. The classifier estimates how likely it is to be a real secret. High-confidence findings become alerts, and lookalikes such as placeholders, test fixtures, and checksums are filtered out before they reach developers.
HOW OUR PIPELINE WORKS
Broad first, careful second
STEP 1
Scan
Repository content, commits, pull requests, and other scanned surfaces.
STEP 2
Generate candidates
Regex patterns identify possible tokens, keys, and credential-like strings.
STEP 3
Classify
Fine-tuned ModernBERT evaluates candidate + context and assigns likelihood of a true secret.
STEP 4
Alert or suppress
High-confidence findings move forward; likely false positives are filtered.
The important design choice is that the model does not replace deterministic scanning. Instead, it complements it. Regexes remain the right tool for finding candidate strings quickly. The classifier is used where machine learning provides the most leverage: distinguishing “looks like a secret” from “is likely a real secret.”
A hard-negative problem: secrets that almost look real
Most false positives are not random. They are hard negatives: strings that match a credential pattern but are not usable credentials. Examples include documentation placeholders, toy examples in tests, redacted values, non-sensitive IDs, and generated fixtures. These cases are easy for a regex to match and hard for a purely rule-based system to suppress without accidentally losing real secrets.
ModernBERT helps because it can read the candidate together with nearby code and text providing contextual understanding comparable to an LLM without the latency and computational overhead of generating natural-language output. For example, a candidate surrounded by words like “example,” “dummy,” “fake,” or “replace-me” may be lower risk than a candidate assigned to an environment variable in a deployment file. The classifier learns these contextual differences from labeled examples rather than requiring engineers to encode every exception as another rule.
We chose ModernBERT because it provides a strong fit for this workload: it is compact, efficient, and well suited for classification over code-adjacent text. For secret scanning, the model needs to make a calibrated decision over short candidate windows with high throughput and low latency.
That makes a fine-tuned encoder classifier a better serving shape than a general-purpose LLM for this stage of the pipeline. The model can be trained directly on our decision boundary, and evaluated using the same recall and precision metrics that matter to secret scanning quality.
How we trained
The challenge was finding representative data for cases in which syntax alone is misleading. The training and evaluation strategy combines three sources:
Product-derived examples from GitHub repositories, using feedback from the secret detection experience and additional human validation.
High-recall regex candidates from GitHub repository data, including human-annotated examples and weak labels used to expand coverage.
Synthetic examples targeted at sparse and difficult cases, such as documentation secrets, test fixtures, public keys, checksums, structured lookalikes, and near-miss pairs.
Synthetic rows pass deterministic validation and model-based quality review before inclusion. Training emphasizes real secrets, realistic false positives, and hard negatives that frequently confuse regex-only approaches. Each model input includes the candidate value, file path, secret type, and a bounded amount of surrounding context. We select thresholds through offline evaluation and then validate behavior on production-like traffic before broader rollout.
Before splitting the data, we grouped rows that share a repository, candidate value, or example so near-duplicates could not appear in both training and evaluation.
Training focused on the cases that matter most for alert quality: real secrets, realistic false positives, and hard negatives that regexes frequently match. The input representation includes the candidate secret string, file path, type and a bounded amount of surrounding context. The output is a classification score used by the scanner to decide whether the candidate should proceed.
We optimized for the product tradeoff: preserve or improve recall while reducing false positives and serving cost. In practice, that means the classifier threshold is selected using offline evaluation, then validated against production-like traffic before rollout.
The most important training principle was to make the model see the confusing examples. We included candidates that are syntactically similar to real secrets but semantically different, so the model learns not only what a secret looks like, but also what a false positive looks like in context.
The trained model is exported to ONNX format with 8-bit quantization, enabling fast inference.
Evaluation results
Online result
Change vs. previous LLM pipeline
What it measures
Repository owner-weighted acceptance
11.5% higher
Customer acceptance of detected findings
Median post-push scan execution time
86% lower
Production scan execution time
Serving cost
More than 98% lower
Cost of the compact classifier compared with remote LLM calls
Customer A/B evaluation results for our fine-tuned model compared to the previous LLM pipeline.
We evaluated the new pipeline’s impact in production in two stages: first against the production baseline on the same public traffic and then through a customer A/B experiment.
Offline evaluation: On post-push scanning, the new pipeline achieved 13% higher precision and 19% higher recall than the previous LLM pipeline when evaluated on the same public traffic.
Online evaluation: We then validated whether these quality improvements translated to customer outcomes through an A/B experiment against the previous LLM pipeline. Repository owner-weighted acceptance increased by 11.5%. We weight acceptance by repository owner to reduce the influence of customers who bulk-resolve large volumes of alerts at once, which can otherwise distort a simple average.
Take this with you
The best security tool is the one developers trust enough to use. Higher precision means fewer distracting alerts. Higher recall means more real secrets are caught. Lower cost means we can keep improving coverage without making scanning prohibitively expensive.
For developers and security teams, this should translate into fewer false positives, and faster feedback in the places where secrets are most likely to be introduced: commits, pull requests, and everyday development workflows.
Hybrid systems are powerful. Regex gives us speed, transparency, and broad candidate coverage. ModernBERT gives us learned context understanding and false-positive reduction. The combination outperforms either approach used alone for this product constraint.
We also learned that model size is not the same as model usefulness. A smaller fine-tuned classifier can be the right answer when the task is narrow, the decision boundary is measurable, and serving efficiency is critical.
This is one step toward making secret scanning more accurate, scalable, and easy to use. Looking ahead, we are focused on two areas:
Building a continuous improvement flywheel. We will use production feedback loops to identify new false negatives and false positives, turning real-world signals into higher-quality training and evaluation data.
Exploring new model architectures. We are investigating approaches that can perform secret detection and extraction in a single step, reducing pipeline complexity while preserving accuracy and scale.
Acknowledgments
Huge thanks to the engineering, science and product teams across GitHub and Microsoft who helped build the training data, evaluation suite, serving stack, and rollout plan for this new secret scanner.
As a Senior Research Scientist in Microsoft CoreAI, I develop agentic model orchestration and routing techniques for GitHub Copilot. My research focuses on adaptive model selection, multi-model coordination, long-horizon agentic workflows, and developer security.
As a Partner Applied Science Manager in Microsoft CoreAI, I lead an applied research team that measurably boosts developer productivity with ML and AI. We evolve GitHub Copilot in Completion, Chat, Code Review, and agentic workflows by continuously refining models and applying in-context learning for deeper, context-aware assistance.
As we kick off Cybersecurity Awareness Month, the GitHub Bug Bounty team spotlights @vaib25vicky, exploring their methodology, techniques, and experiences hacking on GitHub.
Developers aren’t becoming more careless; they’re being outpaced. The tools that let developers create more software should also take on more of the work of protecting it.
We do newsletters, too
Discover tips, technical guides, and best practices in our biweekly newsletter just for devs.

articles.title: Logitech prépare une MX Master 4 Special Edition, et seul le look change — Frandroid
articles.text:
Roland Quandt, journaliste du site allemand WinFuture spécialisé dans les fuites, a publié ce mardi 13 octobre des visuels marketing officiels d’une souris pas encore annoncée, la Logitech MX Master 4 Special Edition.
    Pour aller plus loin
Test de la Logitech MX Master 4 : tout simplement la meilleure souris bureautique ?
            
Si vous avez acheté une MX Master 4 depuis sa sortie il y a un an, vous n’avez rien raté côté technique. D’après ces images, Logitech ne change que l’habillage, avec des graphismes sur tout le dessus et un bouton coloré en rouge-orange.
Pour rappel, la MX Master 4 avait été lancée le 30 septembre 2025, à 129,99 euros. C’est sans doute la souris la plus populaire de Logitech en ce moment, adoptée par beaucoup de gens qui travaillent toute la journée sur ordinateur.
Sous les graphismes, la même souris
Sur les visuels, des motifs graphiques couvrent toute la coque supérieure. La différence la plus visible se trouve au-dessus des boutons principaux, où une touche passe au rouge-orange. Pour le reste, WinFuture indique que le poids et les dimensions ne changent pas.
La MX Master 4 classique pèse 150 grammes d’après la fiche technique de Logitech. C’est 9 grammes de plus que la MX Master 3S, qui l’a précédée.
À l’intérieur, rien ne change non plus d’après WinFuture. Le capteur monte toujours à 8 000 DPI, ou points par pouce, l’unité qui mesure la sensibilité d’une souris (plus le chiffre est élevé, moins on bouge la main pour traverser l’écran). Selon le site, il suffit aussi pour jouer de temps en temps (pour jouer plus sérieusement, des souris gaming existent à moins de 50 euros). Il fonctionne même sur une table en verre, donc sans avoir besoin d’un tapis de souris.
La molette MagSpeed est elle aussi conservée. Elle utilise un système électromagnétique pour passer d’un défilement cranté, ligne par ligne, à une rotation libre qui fait défiler jusqu’à 1 000 lignes par seconde. C’est pratique pour remonter un long tableur en un coup de doigt.
Logitech garde aussi le retour haptique, la grande nouveauté de la MX Master 4 l’an dernier. Un petit moteur placé dans le repose-pouce vibre pour confirmer une action (un Rumble Pak de Nintendo 64, version bureautique).
Pas encore de prix ni de date
Ob ne connaît ni la date de sortie ni le prix de cette Special Edition, et Logitech n’a rien annoncé. Pour avoir un repère, Logitech vend la MX Master 4 classique environ 130 euros.
Rien n’indique non plus que la batterie soit plus facile à changer sur cette version. Sur le modèle classique, la fiche de Logitech décrit sa batterie de 650 mAh comme « non remplaçable ». Pourtant, le règlement européen sur les batteries (source) imposera à partir du 18 février 2027 que les appareils portables vendus dans l’Union européenne aient une batterie que l’utilisateur peut retirer et remplacer lui-même.
    Pour aller plus loin
Fin des smartphones jetables : ce qui change radicalement pour votre batterie dès 2027
            
Si les graphismes vous laissent froid, la MX Master 4 classique offre a priori la même technique, et elle est déjà en vente. Vous pouvez aussi comparer d’autres modèles dans notre sélection des meilleures souris sans fil.

articles.title: Apple dévoile le HomeView et nous donne vraiment envie… mais ne le sort pas en France et en Europe
articles.text:
L’Apple HomeView est officiel après des années de rumeurs. Le 13 octobre 2026, à l’occasion d’un événement dédié à la maison où un nouveau HomePod mini et une nouvelle Apple TV ont aussi été présentés, Apple a dévoilé sa vision pour le futur de la maison. Son rêve est d’imposer le HomeView dans tous les foyers des propriétaires d’iPhone, en allant au-delà du simple pilotage d’accessoires domotiques. « Apple HomeView est conçu pour être partagé par tout le foyer, tout en restant complètement personnel pour chaque utilisateur », indique Apple.
L’écran HomeView utilise Siri AI pour exécuter vos ordres, peut se transformer en interrupteur tactile, dispose de fonctions de reconnaissance faciale et réunit tout l’écosystème Apple des différents membres d’un foyer au même endroit. Apple le décline en deux versions vendues au même prix : une avec un socle-enceinte qui se pose sur une table, l’autre qui s’accroche au mur. Le HomeView est en précommande dès aujourd’hui aux États-Unis, au Royaume-Uni, au Canada, en Australie, en Inde et en Nouvelle-Zélande, à 299 dollars, pour une sortie le 13 novembre. L’Europe, sans surprise, en est privée. Apple écrit dans son communiqué de presse que l’UE est privée du produit.
Apple dévoile le HomeView et veut en mettre dans toutes les maisons (sur une table ou sur un mur)
Le HomeView se décline en deux versions. La première se pose sur une table, un plan de travail ou une table de chevet : l’écran est relié à une base-enceinte en forme de dôme par une charnière en acier inoxydable, qui permet de l’incliner. Elle existe en quatre couleurs (argent, lumière stellaire, rose et gris sidéral), avec un câble assorti.
La seconde s’accroche au mur, dans l’entrée ou un couloir, et n’existe qu’en gris sidéral et argent. Il faut lui ajouter une fixation signée Schneider Home, vendue à part : un modèle USB-C à installer soi-même (59,95 dollars), un modèle raccordé au secteur (79,95 dollars) et un modèle Power over Ethernet (129,95 dollars, disponible début 2027), les deux derniers étant pensés pour une installation par un professionnel. Le HomeView n’a ni batterie ni bouton. L’idée d’Apple n’est pas de proposer un iPad qui reste à la maison mais d’aller sur un produit surtout conçu pour être commandé à la voix.
Contrairement à ce que suggéraient les rumeurs, le HomeView embarque un écran carré Liquid Retina de 7 pouces (et non 6), compatible True Tone. Sa luminosité peut descendre de 500 à 0,3 nit, la plus faible jamais proposée par Apple, de quoi l’installer sur une table de chevet. L’interface s’adapte aussi à la distance : elle affiche des informations simples quand on est loin, puis plus détaillées quand on s’approche. À l’intérieur, on retrouve une puce A18 (comme l’iPhone 16). En façade, une caméra 12 Mpx Center Stage et quatre micros servent aux appels FaceTime et à la reconnaissance des utilisateurs.
Côté son, deux haut-parleurs sont proposés et gèrent l’audio spatial. La version avec un socle dispose d’un meilleur son que la version murale.
Le HomeView fonctionne avec un nouveau système d’exploitation, sobrement baptisé HomeView. Son interface emprunte beaucoup à l’Apple Watch : l’écran affiche des cadrans personnalisables et un glissement vers le haut ouvre un écran d’accueil façon iPhone, avec des applications et des widgets propres à chaque utilisateur. N’espérez pas y installer vos applications préférées : il n’y a pas d’App Store, seulement une sélection d’applications Apple (Musique, Podcasts, News, Apple TV, FaceTime, Messages…) et des applications audio et vidéo tierces compatibles, récupérées depuis l’iPhone. L’installation nécessite un iPhone ou un iPad compatible.
À quoi sert le HomeView ? Il faudra le tester pour en avoir le cœur net, mais Apple a mis en avant plusieurs idées lors de sa présentation de l’appareil :
- L’écran reconnaît jusqu’à six personnes par leur visage et change d’interface automatiquement. Il affiche les messages, le calendrier ou les rappels de chacun… à condition que son iPhone ou son iPad soit à proximité et ait été déverrouillé récemment.
- Le HomeView est un super-interrupteur tactile : le cadran « Maison » donne accès aux accessoires favoris (lumières, thermostat, serrures, volets…), tandis que le cadran « Caméras » affiche jusqu’à neuf flux vidéo en direct.
- Le HomeView peut passer des appels FaceTime, lire et répondre aux messages à la voix ou au clavier, et sert d’interphone avec les autres HomeView, HomePod, iPhone ou Apple Watch de la maison.
- Grâce à Handoff, il suffit d’approcher son iPhone pour y transférer une chanson, un podcast, un appel ou une recette.
- En cuisine, le HomeView transforme une recette trouvée sur le web en instructions étape par étape, avec des minuteurs pilotables à la voix.
- Le HomeView détecte le son des détecteurs de fumée et de monoxyde de carbone et prévient les membres du foyer sur leur iPhone ou leur Apple Watch.
- Quand il n’est pas utilisé, le HomeView devient un cadre photo, y compris avec des albums partagés que les proches peuvent alimenter à distance.
Le cœur du produit reste Siri AI. Avec un iPhone ou un iPad compatible, l’assistant exploite le contexte personnel de chaque utilisateur (Messages, Calendrier, playlists Apple Music…) et peut agir dans les applications. Les autres membres du foyer profitent quand même de ses connaissances générales et de conversations plus naturelles. Apple fait le choix de limiter la sortie du produit à l’anglais… et de le bloquer dans l’Union européenne.
Sur de nombreux aspects, l’Apple HomeView reprend les idées de Google (Nest Hub) et d’Amazon (Echo Show). Mais Apple, fidèle à ses habitudes, mise sur son écosystème, avec les iPhone au cœur de la machine, pour vous donner une raison d’adopter son système. La vie privée est aussi mise en avant : la puce A18 traite les flux de la caméra et des micros dans un compartiment isolé.
Une sortie le 13 novembre aux États-Unis… et un blocage en Europe
Contrairement au HomePod mini et à l’Apple TV, disponibles dès le 30 octobre, le HomeView se fera un peu attendre. Apple annonce une sortie le 13 novembre, au prix de 299 dollars pour la version de table comme pour la version murale. Les précommandes sont ouvertes dès aujourd’hui aux États-Unis, au Royaume-Uni, au Canada, en Australie, en Inde et en Nouvelle-Zélande, et le 15 octobre à Singapour. Il sera aussi vendu en Afrique du Sud via des revendeurs agréés.
Malheureusement et comme nous le pressentions, la France n’est pas sur la liste. Apple l’écrit noir sur blanc dans son communiqué : le HomeView n’est pas commercialisé dans l’Union européenne, car Siri AI n’est pas disponible sur iOS dans l’UE. La marque assure « travailler de manière constructive avec l’UE » pour trouver une solution. Le HomeView lui-même n’est pas concerné par le DMA, qui bloque Siri AI sur iPhone, iPad et Apple Watch, mais il dépend de l’iPhone à tous les niveaux : pour l’installation, pour afficher les données personnelles de chacun et pour donner à Siri AI son contexte personnel. Sans Siri AI sur nos iPhone, le HomeView perd une bonne partie de son intérêt.
Autre question pour l’instant sans réponse : pourra-t-on l’importer des États-Unis ou du Royaume-Uni ? Apple indique que Siri AI fonctionne sur le HomeView même sans iPhone compatible pour les questions générales, ce qui laisse imaginer un usage partiel. Mais l’assistant n’est disponible qu’en anglais et dans les huit pays de lancement, et l’installation passe par un iPhone ou un iPad. Tout ce que l’on sait est qu’à partir d’iOS 27.2, Siri AI parlera français.… mais pas sur le HomeView.

articles.title: La emotiva despedida de Bryan Cranston a RJ Mitte, su hijo en 'Breaking Bad': "Le conocí con solo 14 años"
articles.text:
El actor Bryan Cranston, protagonista de Breaking Bad, no ha tardado en dedicarle una emotiva despedida a RJ Mitte, quien en la ficción interpretó a su hijo Walter Jr. Mitte ha fallecido este lunes 12 de octubre a causa de suicidio a los 34 años de edad. Una terrible noticia que ha impactado con especial fuerza entre los fans de la serie, una de las más importantes y reconocidas de todos los tiempos.
"Estoy profundamente abatido mientras escribo esto. RJ Mitte, mi querido hijo en Breaking Bad, ha fallecido", comienza Bryan Cranston su despeddia publicada en Instagram junto a una fotografía de ambos sonrientes. "Lo conocí cuando solo tenía 14 años, al ser elegido para interpretar a Walter White Jr., un papel que desempeñó con mucha alegría y entusiasmo", prosigue.
"Nació con parálisis cerebral, pero nunca —jamás— permitió que ese reto fuera una excusa para nada. Afrontó el exigente calendario de rodaje con gran determinación. Siempre escuchaba los consejos que le daban sus padres en la serie (Anna Gunn y yo). Aunque, como buen adolescente, a veces los ignoraba con picardía para aprender por las malas… Era una de las estrellas de una serie de éxito, pero seguía siendo un niño", continúa el escrito.
"Ese chico era bastante inexperto cuando empezamos a rodar el episodio piloto en febrero de 2007. Pero poco a poco le vimos convertirse en un actor realmente excelente. Aprovechó su experiencia en la serie para convertirse en un firme defensor de los intérpretes con discapacidad y ser el director de una organización filantrópica dedicada a ayudar a la comunidad de personas con discapacidad", celebra Bryan Cranston a su vez el legado que deja RJ Mitte.
"Toda esa promesa y ese potencial suponen ahora una gran pérdida. Es especialmente devastador saber que se quitó la vida. ¿Por qué? Hace solo unas semanas nos estábamos enviando mensajes de texto, intentando concretar cuándo podríamos quedar para comer. No sé si esa comida habría cambiado su futuro… Pero sí sé que le quería y que disfruté muchísimo de su compañía a lo largo de todos esos años en la serie, y también después de que se apagaran los focos de Breaking Bad… Te echaré de menos, hijo", sentencia. La despedida de Bryan Cranston a RJ Mitte concluye incitando a pedir ayuda a todos aquellos que se estén planteando el suicidio: "Hay esperanza".
Muere RJ Mitte, actor de Breaking Bad
"Con profunda tristeza comunicamos el trágico fallecimiento del querido actor, filántropo y apasionado defensor de los derechos de las personas con discapacidad RJ Mitte", anunciaban sus representantes en un comunicado remitido a la prensa. Con esas palabras se daba a conocer la triste noticia de su muerte.
El actor se convirtió en parte fundamental del reparto de Breaking Bad. Y, a partir de aquella irrupción, consiguió labrarse una carrera en la industria. Entre sus papeles destacan películas como Triumph (2021) junto a Terrance Howard o Love Me Dead (2024) junto a Dove Cameron. También las series Cambiadas al nacer (2014) y Los guardianes de la justicia (2022).

articles.title: NVIDIA Announces New Investments in France’s Startups
articles.text:
Companies in France are deploying agentic computing across industries spanning space, financial services, the public sector and scientific research, demonstrating how the country’s ecosystem has moved from ambition to application.
France’s progress sits on deliberate groundwork.
The AI Action Summit in February 2025 and Choose France Summits in 2025 and 2026 anchored major compute commitments on French soil. What the ecosystem has built since then spans the full stack.
NVIDIA’s Investments in France
NVIDIA has been investing in France’s startup ecosystem, having previously invested in leading technology companies including Alice&Bob, Gradium and Scintil Photonics.
Across all of Europe, NVIDIA has committed nearly $10 billion to the technology ecosystem.
Today, NVIDIA announced new planned investments in Doctolib, Entalpic, Genesis AI and Pigment.
These startups are innovating to solve challenges across healthcare, materials discovery, physical AI and business planning.
Doctolib, a European healthcare technology company, builds agents that free up healthcare professionals to deliver better care, while providing patients with a digital health companion that improves access to care and supports more preventive, continuous medicine.
Entalpic, a Paris-based startup, accelerates the engineering of advanced materials at the atomic scale, with particular expertise in surfaces and interfaces for semiconductor manufacturing and next-generation electronics.
Genesis AI is a global robotics company developing general-purpose robots with frontier intelligence and capabilities through its foundation models, data collection systems, simulation infrastructure and robot hardware.
Pigment, a Paris-based enterprise software company, builds a planning platform that helps businesses forecast performance, model scenarios and make decisions across finance, sales, workforce and operations.
Sovereign AI Infrastructure
France-based companies are expanding agentic infrastructure on NVIDIA technology.
Bull is extending its European AI server production to NVIDIA Vera Rubin Ultra NVL72 systems, planned for 2028, with trays produced in Europe and rack integration at its Angers factory — inaugurated Friday, Oct. 2.
Altair-1, the first satellite in a $1 billion, 50-satellite constellation with on-board autonomous capabilities, launched this month and has successfully reached orbit. Integrated by Loft Orbital and built in Abu Dhabi by Orbitworks, a joint venture between Loft Orbital and Marlan Space, the satellite is flying NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin edge modules, running Mistral’s models, for real-time Earth observation and autonomous operations in orbit.
Open Models
NVIDIA Nemotron open models are in production across French organizations that require sovereign, trustworthy data.
LINAGORA and Docaposte have secured the CANUT framework agreement, making Twake.ai, built on NVIDIA Nemotron, the sole referenced sovereign digital workplace for more than 2,500 French public organizations.
In financial services, SBS is launching a sovereign platform enabling banks to deploy governed generative and agentic services within their own environments, in collaboration with NVIDIA.
Last week, Mistral introduced under private preview Mistral Large 4 open model, with state-of-the-art, open weight performance in cyber defense, manufacturing, finance and multimodal tasks, and a solid foundation for customizing models across key industries.
Fondation Inria, with NVIDIA’s support, is launching a working group on open source advanced modeling and tool adoption, with findings to come in the spring of next year.
Agents at Work Across Industries
Across retail, public services, telecommunications and science, the pattern is consistent: open models and NVIDIA infrastructure are driving results in France.
L’Oréal is integrating NVIDIA ALCHEMI into its research workflows so scientists can explore formulation possibilities in silico and better help guide laboratory research. Combining computational predictions with hands-on experimentation can make the discovery process up to 100x faster than traditional methods and maximize the potential of the group’s proprietary active ingredients.
Mirakl has onboarded more than 70 million products with fine-tuned and open models running on NVIDIA GPUs and inference software, cutting seller catalog onboarding to under two hours.
Photoroom and Vestiaire Collective are demonstrating the measurable business impact of advanced visual modeling on marketplace performance.
Omi helps brands bring accurate products into AI-generated marketing visuals at scale, combining its approved 3D digital twins with open models optimized on NVIDIA for 4x faster inference.
In Côte-d’Or, ThinkDeep and Akila built a digital-twin agent — powered by NVIDIA Cosmos open world models, Nemotron and Omniverse libraries — managing nearly 5,800 kilometers of roads and buildings, cutting total operating costs by 10% and targeting 30% as deployment progresses.
Port Sud de France runs goods processing and port security on ThinkDeep’s DeepBrain platform powered by Nemotron and Cosmos.
Enchanted Tools, a robotics company headquartered in Paris, is deploying social robots to support patients in healthcare settings including pediatric cancer care.
In telecom, Bouygues Telecom and Prisme.ai have launched AI Studio V2, powered by NVIDIA full-stack infrastructure, to offer all of its employees the ability to build their own agents, securely and in a controlled environment
In quantum, Alice & Bob has integrated the NVIDIA NVQLink platform for its superconducting cat qubits, showing how GPUs can make quantum error correction more efficient, including for faster qubit modalities.
Quandela has also been using NVQLink to build an integration between a DGX Spark system and its photonic qubits — advancing QPU-GPU supercomputing and exploring hybrid quantum-classical applications.

articles.title: Cyberattack Prompts Grocery Giant Ahold Delhaize to Disconnect Systems
articles.text:
Dutch-Belgian grocery giant Ahold Delhaize has disconnected some of its systems in response to a cyberattack.
In a bare-bones notice on its website, the company revealed that it identified a security issue within its network, triggering incident response.
“Our teams are taking steps to assess and mitigate the issue. This includes taking some systems offline to help protect them,” the company said.
Ahold Delhaize said its stores remain open and that its ability to serve customers has not been affected.
According to local media, the preventive measures impacted deliveries and online orders at Albert Heijn and Delhaize brands in Belgium and the Netherlands. Stores in the US appear to have been affected as well.
In a Tuesday update, the company confirmed that its brands’ stores are experiencing issues.
“The impact of our preventative measures differs per brand. Each local brand is working hard to serve its customers and minimize disruption,” Ahold Delhaize said.
It also noted that its security team is getting ready to restore the affected systems, but did not provide an estimated timeline.
“Our teams are working with urgency to investigate the incident and restore affected systems safely. As they make progress in assessing and mitigating the issues, we are in the process of starting a controlled re-launch of certain systems,” the company said.
Ahold Delhaize says it has notified the relevant authorities and stakeholders and that it has no evidence that customer and associate data has been stolen in the attack.
Responding to a SecurityWeek inquiry, an Ahold Delhaize spokesperson refrained from sharing additional details on the incident.
It is unclear if the incident is related to the cyberattack that hit refrigerators and freezers in hundreds of supermarkets across Europe over the weekend.
In November 2024, Ahold Delhaize was hit by a cyberattack that impacted Giant Food pharmacies and Hannaford supermarkets, as well as Food Lion, The Giant Company, and Stop & Shop.
In April 2025, just as the INC Ransom ransomware group took credit for the incident, the company confirmed that data was stolen from its systems.
In June 2025, Ahold Delhaize notified regulators in the US that the personal information of more than 2.2 million individuals had been compromised in the ransomware attack.
*Updated with new information from Ahold Delhaize.

articles.title: No Man’s Sky llegará a iPhone y iPad diez años después de su fallido debut
articles.text:
El videojuego de exploración espacial No Man’s Sky llegará a iPhone y iPad el 28 de octubre, diez años después de su problemático lanzamiento en 2016. El estudio británico Hello Games confirmó la fecha y abrió las reservas en la App Store de Apple.
En No Man’s Sky, cada jugador puede viajar a cualquiera de los miles de millones de planetas de un universo generado de manera automática por el propio juego, explorar sus paisajes y formas de vida, y elegir si quiere combatir, comerciar o simplemente recorrer el espacio.
La versión móvil incluirá, según el propio estudio, todas las actualizaciones y expansiones gratuitas publicadas desde el estreno original, entre ellas Voyagers, lanzada el año pasado, y Cosmos, la más reciente, publicada en septiembre.
“Supongo que debería decir que esto no es No Man’s Sky Lite”, escribió el cofundador de Hello Games, Sean Murray, en la publicación oficial que anunció el lanzamiento.
El juego funcionará en dispositivos tan antiguos como el iPhone 11 y la tercera generación del iPad Air, y pesará apenas 5 GB, pese a generar universos completos de forma procedural dentro del propio dispositivo.
Qué quedó afuera de la versión móvil
Murray precisó que las únicas funciones ausentes al debutar serán el multijugador y los asentamientos planetarios, las bases que los jugadores construyen y comparten con otros usuarios.
El estudio comparó la estrategia con la que usó al llevar el juego a la Nintendo Switch original. “En Switch escuchamos a los jugadores y construimos a partir de ahí, incluso con una versión mucho más amplia en Switch 2”, señaló Murray. “Según la respuesta y la cantidad de jugadores, vamos a apoyar iOS de manera similar”, agregó.
La edición para iPhone y iPad tendrá controles táctiles diseñados específicamente para pantalla, además de compatibilidad con mandos físicos, transmisión a otras pantallas y manejo con mouse y teclado en el iPad.
Murray afirmó además que el estudio dedicó un trabajo considerable a la duración de batería y al manejo térmico del dispositivo, para permitir sesiones de juego largas sin que el teléfono se recaliente.
Una vuelta a origen marcada por el fracaso inicial
No Man’s Sky generó una enorme expectativa antes de su estreno en PC y PlayStation 4, pero decepcionó a buena parte de la crítica y los jugadores al faltarle funciones que Hello Games había prometido antes del lanzamiento.
El fracaso inicial derivó en una ola de pedidos de reembolso y en críticas tan duras que el propio Murray se alejó durante meses de las redes sociales antes de que el estudio empezara a reconstruir la reputación del juego a través de actualizaciones gratuitas sostenidas en el tiempo.
El estudio sostuvo el desarrollo del título durante una década a fuerza de esas actualizaciones, que fueron sumando multijugador, vehículos, bases, mascotas y, más recientemente, estaciones espaciales propias con la actualización Cosmos.
Según el sitio Polygon, parte de la tecnología que permite correr un universo generado de manera procedural en un teléfono proviene del desarrollo de Light No Fire, el próximo juego de Hello Games, que todavía no tiene fecha de lanzamiento.
El sitio especializado Ars Technica destacó que el logro técnico es inusual para un juego de este tipo, porque cada planeta no está guardado como un archivo en el dispositivo sino que se construye en el momento, a partir de una única semilla matemática común a todos los jugadores.
El medio agregó que los gráficos, aunque no son los más avanzados del género, mejoraron de forma notoria desde el lanzamiento original gracias a las sucesivas actualizaciones.
En los últimos años, otros títulos pensados originalmente para computadoras y consolas de escritorio llegaron también al teléfono, como Control, Resident Evil 7, Tomb Raider y Red Dead Redemption, de acuerdo con un relevamiento del sitio Digital Foundry.
La llegada a dispositivos de Apple se da en el marco de la Semana de Juegos Independientes que la propia compañía organiza en su tienda de aplicaciones, junto a otros títulos como Little Kitty, Big City, Dome Keeper, 9 Kings y Yes, Your Grace 2: Snowfall.
Según Engadget, No Man’s Sky es, por lejos, el nombre más conocido de esa selección, lo que convierte a su llegada en la pieza central de la promoción de Apple para esa semana.
El precio de la versión completa será de 19,99 dólares, aunque el estudio ofrecerá gratis el tramo inicial del juego para que los nuevos jugadores decidan si quieren comprarlo antes de avanzar.
Las reservas ya están disponibles en la App Store, a la espera del lanzamiento del 28 de octubre.

articles.title: Physicists discover “astonishing” property of light that defies expectations
articles.text:
Physicists discover “astonishing” property of light that defies expectations
- Date:
- October 13, 2026
- Source:
- University of East Anglia
- Summary:
- Scientists have uncovered a surprising hidden ability of light that allows it to develop spinning, twisting behavior as it travels through empty space, without special lenses, mirrors, or materials. Researchers discovered that light’s internal geometry can naturally produce left- and right-handed patterns, challenging long-standing assumptions about how light behaves. By carefully arranging a beam’s structure, scientists can control where and how these spinning patterns emerge, unlocking a new way to manipulate light.
- Share:
Scientists have discovered a surprising ability of light that allows it to develop spinning patterns as it moves through empty space, without relying on special lenses, mirrors, or materials. The finding reveals that light possesses a hidden geometric structure that can influence its behavior in ways researchers previously thought were difficult to achieve.
The discovery comes from an international team led by researchers at the University of East Anglia (UEA) in the United Kingdom, working with scientists in South Africa. Their experiments demonstrate that carefully prepared light can be controlled through its own internal geometry, offering a new approach to manipulating how light spins and twists.
The findings challenge long-standing assumptions about how different properties of light interact. They could eventually lead to more sensitive medical tests, faster and more secure communications, and advanced quantum technologies that use light to transmit and protect information.
Why the Direction of Light's Spin Matters
One of the most intriguing aspects of the discovery involves chirality, a scientific term describing the difference between left-handed and right-handed structures.
Human hands provide a familiar example. Although they are mirror images of each other, a left hand cannot be perfectly superimposed on a right hand. Many molecules have a similar property, including compounds used in medicines. Two versions of the same molecule can have nearly identical chemical structures yet produce very different effects in the body.
Scientists can distinguish these molecular forms by studying how they interact with light that has a particular rotational behavior. Traditionally, producing and controlling such light has often involved specialized materials, carefully designed surfaces, or powerful lenses that focus beams extremely tightly.
The research demonstrates that appropriately prepared light can develop this behavior naturally as it travels, without requiring those additional optical components.
"Our work shows that light can naturally develop this handed behavior all on its own," said Dr. Kayn Forbes from UEA's School of Chemistry, Pharmacy and Pharmacology.
"You just have to prepare it in the right way.
"Most people think of light as traveling in straight lines. But scientists can also create structured light -- light whose brightness, shape, and direction are carefully arranged.
"One extreme example is light that twists as it travels, forming a corkscrew shape known as an optical vortex. Each twist can carry information, making this kind of light valuable for high-speed internet, secure communications, and advanced sensors.
"Light can also spin as it travels, depending on how it is polarized. This spin can be left-handed or right-handed -- another form of chirality."
Scientists Discover How Light Develops a Hidden Spin
Light can exhibit different kinds of rotational behavior. An optical vortex, for example, has a wave pattern that twists around its direction of travel, much like a corkscrew. Light also has a property known as polarization, which describes how its electric field oscillates. Certain polarization patterns produce a form of rotation called spin.
Physicists have long studied the relationship between these two properties. However, the interactions responsible for the newly observed effect were generally considered extremely weak and difficult to detect without specialized experimental conditions.
The researchers found that the situation changes when a beam of light is prepared in a particular balanced configuration.
Under those conditions, the beam can initially have no spin, yet distinct regions with spinning behavior emerge as it travels through free space. The effect does not require the light to pass through engineered materials or additional optical devices.
"It starts off with no spin at all," explained MSc student Light Mkhumbuza, who carried out key experiments. "But as the beam travels forward, spinning regions appear and separate out -- almost as if the spin was hiding and then revealed itself."
Rather than creating spin through an external optical component, the researchers demonstrated how the beam's existing internal structure can determine where spinning regions develop during propagation.
The Hidden Geometry That Controls Light
To explain this unexpected behavior, the researchers turned to topology, a mathematical field concerned with properties that remain unchanged when objects are continuously stretched, bent, or reshaped.
Dr. Isaac Nape, from the University of the Witwatersrand in Johannesburg, South Africa, offered a simple way to understand the concept.
"To explain it, imagine a mug and a doughnut," he said. "You can morph one into the other without tearing it, because they both have one hole. That hole is a topological feature."
The researchers found that structured light possesses its own topological characteristics, encoded in the arrangement of its polarization.
This underlying pattern acts like a mathematical fingerprint. Even as the light beam changes shape while traveling, its topological structure remains, influencing how different regions of the beam evolve.
As a result, the arrangement of the light itself can determine where its left-handed and right-handed spinning patterns become visible.
The discovery gives scientists a way to guide this behavior by designing the beam's initial structure, rather than depending on specialized materials to produce the desired effect.
"This gives us a completely new tuning knob for light. By adjusting its topology, we can decide how and where chirality appears," said Dr. Nape.
Potential Breakthroughs in Medicine and Communications
The ability to control light through its geometry could eventually make several important optical technologies simpler, more affordable, and more versatile.
One particularly promising application involves medical diagnostics and pharmaceutical research. Because many biologically important molecules have left-handed and right-handed forms, carefully structured light could help scientists identify these differences with greater sensitivity. Such tools could be valuable for evaluating drug safety and detecting biological markers associated with disease.
The same principles could support smaller optical sensors capable of identifying chemicals or biological substances without requiring large, sophisticated laboratory instruments.
Communications technology could also benefit. By encoding information into different twisting and spinning patterns, researchers may be able to increase the amount of data carried by individual light beams. This could contribute to faster optical communications, improved information security, and future quantum networks.
Other potential uses include manipulating microscopic particles, cells, and molecules with light, as well as developing more resilient quantum systems. Topological properties may help protect delicate quantum information against certain forms of noise and interference.
"The implications are wide-ranging," said Dr. Forbes. "This work could lead to simpler and more sensitive medical tests, especially in drug development.
"It could also be used to pack more information into laser beams -- boosting data capacity for communications, including future quantum networks.
"And because the effect doesn't rely on fragile materials or precision-engineered surfaces, it could be easier and cheaper to use in real-world technologies.
"This research could lay the foundations for a new generation of light-based technologies, by showing that light's behavior can be controlled using its own internal geometry," he added.
These applications remain possibilities for future development, but the underlying discovery provides researchers with another way to design and control the behavior of light.
A Hidden Property of Light Finally Revealed
For decades, scientists have relied on increasingly sophisticated optical equipment to produce and manipulate unusual forms of light. The findings suggest that some of these behaviors can instead arise from carefully designed structures already encoded within a light beam.
By showing how topology governs the emergence of spinning regions during propagation, the team has revealed a previously underappreciated connection between light's geometry and its physical behavior.
The discovery also illustrates how much remains to be learned about something as familiar and extensively studied as light.
"For something so familiar, light is proving to be far richer, stranger and more powerful than anyone imagined," said Dr. Forbes.
"And astonishingly, this new behavior has been there all along -- just waiting to be seen."
The research, 'Topological Control of Chirality and Spin with Structured Light', was published in the journal Light: Science & Applications.
Story Source:
Materials provided by University of East Anglia. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Light Mkhumbuza, Pedro Ornelas, Angela Dudley, Isaac Nape, Kayn A. Forbes. Topological control of chirality and spin with structured light. Light: Science, 2026; 15 (1) DOI: 10.1038/s41377-026-02278-6

articles.title: CELOL Série A: faltam duas rodadas e três equipes disputam as últimas vagas nos playoffs
articles.text:
A fase de pontos do CELOL Série A está chegando ao fim, mas a disputa pelos playoffs ainda não terminou. Com nove das 11 rodadas concluídas, restam duas partidas para cada equipe antes da definição dos seis classificados à fase eliminatória do campeonato de League of Legends da Liga GG.
Na parte de cima da tabela, emBRAZA! Esports e Smoke Tram Esports dividem a liderança com oito vitórias e apenas uma derrota. NKZ Vorax e Marere E-Sports aparecem logo atrás, com sete vitórias cada.
As quatro equipes já estão matematicamente garantidas nos playoffs. A disputa pelas duas vagas restantes envolve LOS Academy, Neon Esports e Invictus Team.
Para as demais equipes, a classificação já não é possível, mas seus resultados ainda podem interferir na posição final dos adversários.
Como está a classificação após a nona rodada?
A emBRAZA! Esports segue na liderança, com 24 pontos, empatada com a Smoke Tram Esports. Ambas acumulam oito vitórias e uma derrota.
NKZ Vorax e Marere E-Sports somam 21 pontos, enquanto LOS Academy e Neon Esports completam o Top 6, com 18 pontos cada.
A Invictus Team ocupa a sétima posição, com quatro vitórias e cinco derrotas, e ainda pode alcançar as equipes imediatamente acima.
Confira a tabela completa:
Quais equipes já estão classificadas?
Quatro equipes já garantiram matematicamente uma vaga nos playoffs:
emBRAZA! Esports: oito vitórias e uma derrota.
Smoke Tram Esports: oito vitórias e uma derrota.
NKZ Vorax: sete vitórias e duas derrotas.
Marere E-Sports: sete vitórias e duas derrotas.
Com apenas duas rodadas restantes, a Invictus Team, sétima colocada, pode chegar a no máximo seis vitórias. Portanto, não consegue alcançar nenhuma dessas quatro equipes.
Embora já estejam classificadas, elas ainda disputam suas posições finais na tabela.
A liderança segue aberta, especialmente entre emBRAZA! e Smoke Tram, que chegam à reta final empatadas em pontos.
LOS Academy e Neon Esports: perto da classificação, mas ainda não garantidas
LOS Academy e Neon Esports chegam à décima rodada com campanhas idênticas: seis vitórias e três derrotas.
As duas equipes dependem apenas de seus próprios resultados para assegurar uma vaga nos playoffs.
Uma vitória nas duas rodadas restantes é suficiente para garantir a classificação, já que ambas chegariam a sete triunfos, número que a Invictus Team não pode alcançar.
Na décima rodada, a LOS Academy enfrenta a Marere E-Sports, quarta colocada. Já a Neon Esports encara a Sphere, que ainda não venceu na competição.
Caso ambas vençam, as seis vagas dos playoffs estarão matematicamente definidas antes da última rodada.
Por outro lado, se uma delas perder seus dois compromissos e a Invictus vencer suas duas partidas, haverá empate em número de vitórias, exigindo a aplicação dos critérios de desempate.
Invictus Team: a última esperança fora do Top 6
A Invictus Team é a única equipe atualmente fora da zona de classificação que ainda possui chances matemáticas de chegar aos playoffs.
Com quatro vitórias e cinco derrotas, o time precisa obrigatoriamente vencer seus dois últimos confrontos para alcançar seis vitórias.
Mas isso não será suficiente por si só.
A Invictus também precisa que LOS Academy ou Neon Esports perca as duas partidas restantes. Dessa forma, pelo menos uma das equipes terminaria com a mesma campanha de seis vitórias e cinco derrotas.
Nesse cenário, a definição dependeria dos critérios oficiais de desempate.
Se LOS Academy e Neon Esports conquistarem ao menos uma vitória cada, a Invictus estará eliminada, independentemente de seus próprios resultados.
Na décima rodada, a equipe enfrenta a Smoke Tram Esports, vice-líder do campeonato, em um confronto que pode definir seu futuro na competição.
Quais equipes já estão eliminadas?
Quatro equipes já não possuem chances matemáticas de alcançar os playoffs:
Shark Bite Furious Gaming Black
Shark Bite Furious Gaming White
Juventus Gaming Red
Smoke Tram Ascension
As quatro possuem duas vitórias e podem chegar a no máximo quatro.
Como LOS Academy e Neon Esports já somam seis vitórias, nenhuma dessas equipes consegue alcançar a zona de classificação.
Ainda assim, os resultados das últimas rodadas podem influenciar a disputa pelas primeiras posições e pela sexta vaga.
O que esperar da décima rodada?
A próxima rodada reúne confrontos importantes tanto para a liderança quanto para a definição dos classificados.
emBRAZA! Esports x Juventus Gaming Red
Marere E-Sports x LOS Academy
Smoke Tram Esports x Invictus Team
NKZ Vorax x Smoke Tram Ascension
Shark Bite Furious Gaming Black x Shark Bite Furious Gaming White
Lembrando que todos os times vencem de W.O. da Sphere até o final da fase.
A LOS Academy também pode assegurar sua vaga caso vença a Marere E-Sports.
Já a Invictus Team precisa superar a Smoke Tram Esports para continuar com chances de classificação até a 11ª rodada.
Se perder, estará matematicamente eliminada, independentemente dos outros resultados.
A 11ª rodada será a última oportunidade
Depois da décima rodada, cada equipe terá somente mais um confronto para disputar antes do encerramento da fase de pontos.
Nesse momento, as campanhas acumuladas determinarão a classificação final e, se necessário, os critérios de desempate decidirão as posições entre equipes com o mesmo número de vitórias.
Vale lembrar que o fim da 11ª rodada não representa o encerramento do CELOL Série A. As seis equipes classificadas avançarão para os playoffs, quando começará a disputa eliminatória pelo título.
Até lá, vamos descobrir se LOS Academy e Neon Esports confirmarão suas vagas ou a Invictus Team conseguirá levar a disputa até a última rodada.

Os jogos são transmitidos pelos canais oficiais da Liga GG e pelo YouTube do Olhar Digital.
